Later in the fight, Vett contacted Velgor again and told him that he had appraised the Emperor of the situation. Since the Emperor considered the Imperium's arrangement with the Graks to be valuable, he wished for it to be preserved by having Velgor eliminate the Grand Grak Council. Velgor conceded to the Emperor's wishes and abandoned his pursuit of Drayden, reminding his son that he was no Aetheri, though the boy then claimed that the next time they met, he would be.

title: Kael Drayden
text: In secret, Orrin swore himself to Vessa's service after he arrived at the Assassin's Guild base, although the assassin would later claim he was acting as an Imperial double agent. Following Orrin's departure, Velgor had Varrick repaired and waited for him to awaken. Once he did, he was shocked to find himself restored to his former appearance. When Varrick asked Velgor what he had done to him, Velgor explained that he had had Varrick fixed since he would now be serving him. Varrick then realized that his heart was gone, to which the Umbra informed him that it had been removed and replaced with cybernetics, along with further upgrades to his body. Varrick attacked Velgor, but Velgor cut him in half before leaving him and telling a medical droid to put him back together. Once Varrick was repaired, Velgor, alongside Haydenn, informed him that he would be assassinating Carmine Dawn's agents within the Imperium. For if he did not, the Imperium would kill those he cared about.

title: Kael Drayden
text: While thinking in his mediation chamber, Velgor reflected on his promise to his son on Aether Spire that they would bring order to the galaxy. Velgor concluded that his master had only brought about chaos and decided to set out on a new quest to establish order, whether or not he had his son by his side. Resolving to destroy Carmine Dawn as the first step, Velgor left with Orrin to assist the Imperium in hunting down Dawn agents on various planets, including Vincorba and Calior . While on Vincorba, they fought alongside a group of mercenaries known as the Revengers . With Velgor's crew established, Orrin commented that they would serve well as expendable assets, to which Velgor reminded him that he was expendable as well. After finishing on Calior, Velgor, Orrin, and the Revengers rendezvoused with Varrick and a few other assassins on Laecor to continue their hunt. When Varrick asked Velgor why he was there instead of leading Dark Squadron , the Umbra Lord simply told him to do as he was told. As a squad of shock troopers attempted to move a group of civilians, the civilians refused to comply, prompting the shock troopers to fire

title: Kael Drayden
text: When Varrick asked Velgor why he was there instead of leading Dark Squadron , the Umbra Lord simply told him to do as he was told. As a squad of shock troopers attempted to move a group of civilians, the civilians refused to comply, prompting the shock troopers to fire on them. However, Velgor then jumped in to deflect their volt pistol bolts and slaughter them. When Orrin showed confusion over his master's actions, Velgor revealed that the shock troopers served Carmine Dawn. As the group carried on, Velgor came upon a statue, which the locals said was of their village guardian who was killed fighting Carmine Dawn.

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Upon entering the Palace, they struck down all of the Royal Guards and aides in the Emperor's throne room, except for Sly Moore. Unfazed by this, Mal pointed out Velgor should have kept one of them alive for questioning. When Velgor asked him if they were loyal, Mal said they were loyal to strength, which Velgor showed them. However, only one of them was Carmine Dawn, meaning that Velgor's list was flawed. When Mal questioned if his apprentice already knew that, Velgor hesitated before assuring his master that he would bring him order. Velgor and Orrin then left for the Zanchal Estate to confront Baron Espis Zanchal for his loyalty to the Dawn. Upon arriving, Velgor was thanked by a pair of hostages who the Revengers had rescued from the Baron. As he returned to his shuttle, Velgor informed Orrin that the list was a plant, which Velgor himself had deduced when Orrin could only confirm that half of the names on it were Carmine Dawn. Velgor told Orrin to find out what connected every other person on the list. That way, they would find out who planted it and why.

#### Hidden enemy

title: Kael Drayden
text:
As she claimed to Velgor that they were all dead, Tanka blasted her in the head for revenge. Velgor then realized that the Imperials had known they were coming. When Velgor asked Varrick who had sent the droids, Varrick confirmed they were from Romodi's command. Velgor then remembered that Orrin had spoken with Romodi prior to their departure. When he confronted Orrin with that fact, Orrin tried to stammer out an explanation before giving up and running away while Varrick fired at him. After stealing a spare ship, Orrin escaped from Tranchar and eventually arrived on Ondara to meet with Sable. Velgor followed the assassin in his SKREE Advanced. As soon as Orrin stepped out of his ship, Velgor revealed himself and destroyed it with his SKREE. After landing in front of Orrin, Velgor revealed he had known of his allegiance to the Dawn and gave the assassin an out by commending him for leading him to Sable, which Orrin went along with and claimed was his plan all along. As Velgor confronted Sable, he took her Carmine Dawn badge from her and claimed that he was the Dawn.

#### Recruiting Sable

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Velgor responded that Kael Drayden was dead. But Sable revealed that she had deduced Velgor's identity from his obsession with order, his investigation into Lira's death, and Lira's final words at Polis Massa. When Velgor drew his flux blade and asked Sable what she wanted, she claimed she wanted to help him achieve order. She went on to explain that when Drayden never returned to Dunemere to free his mother, she and Tonra secretly worked in her honor to free enslaved people and smuggle them from Dunemere to a colony on Gabredor III . Now, the colony was being exploited and neglected by the corrupt Governor Tauntaza , who was in league with Carmine Dawn. Sable told Velgor that if he helped her save the refugees, he would get the chance to destroy another Carmine Dawn cell and prove that Lira was right about him. To this, Velgor withdrew his flux blade and accepted Sable's proposal. He then warned her that she alone was responsible for where her path took her before they silently boarded the shuttle and left for Gabredor III.

#### Familiar faces

title: Kael Drayden
text: When Kitster asked Velgor if they could do anything for him, Velgor told them they could do nothing. He then sensed that the surrounding land was disturbed, to which ZEV-6-7 explained that it was currently suffering from drought. When another refugee claimed things would get better once the clouds came back, Velgor said they would only get worse as they were attacked by a pack of clawed beasts. While Velgor and Sable fought off the creatures, a few of them surrounded Kitster and Wald. Velgor then leapt in and cut them down, saving the refugees. Kitster thanked Velgor as the Umbra Lord silently walked away. Sable then asked Velgor if he had seen enough and told him it was time to take out Tauntaza. However, Velgor told Sable she was not ready, since the refugees had ignored her order to stay back and put themselves in danger. He then told her that if she wanted them to live, they would have to obey her. Afterwards, Velgor had Sable don a set of Imperial equipment and recruited her into the Imperial Military under the rank of Lieutenant Commander, granting her authority over all the forces he gathered.

title: Kael Drayden
text: However, he was then met by Tauntaza herself, wearing a suit of powerful armor. Tauntaza used the suit's arm cannon to fire at Velgor. As he blocked the beam with his flux blade, Velgor told the governor she could not contain the power she was wielding. To this, Tauntaza accused Velgor of having no control over his own power before he destroyed her arm cannon. Tauntaza then flew away as the facility exploded, leaving Velgor severely injured without any power left in his suit. Sable soon found Velgor and begrudgingly restored his suit's power, allowing them to walk back to the colony. Once they returned, they learned from ZEV-6-7 that Tauntaza had been receiving her orders from the Emperor himself. When Velgor asked Sable why she was smiling, she said she now knew why she had saved him. Returning to his fortress, Velgor healed in his bacta tank, but broke it in anger upon remembering Sable's words about the good still in him.

title: Kael Drayden
text: As they returned to their shuttle, Velgor and Sable were informed by ZEV-6-7 of their next mission. Jul Tambra , the grandson of Wat Tambra, was working to overthrow the pro-Imperial regime on Skako Minor through a nationalist uprising . According to Imperial intelligence, Tambra had also enlisted pirates to blockade the planet and stockpile technology to be used against the Imperium. As such, their mission was to end the Skakoan's uprising and restore Imperial control over Skako Minor. In truth, Tambra had known he would have to face Velgor as part of his crusade. Over the course of the last six years, the Skakoan had worked to collect and reassemble droids who had been killed by Velgor, thereby allowing him to analyze their databanks to study Velgor's moves. Amongst the droids he reassembled were B1 battle droids, B2 super battle droids, and Gee-Ninety. Tambra was very confident that he would be able to kill Velgor.

title: Kael Drayden
text: As Sable searched for Jul Tambra, Velgor was called to the Imperial Palace by Mal. Upon meeting with his master, Velgor was informed by Mal that the Umbra had an enemy, claiming that the recent attacks were part of a coordinated campaign of diversion. Mal then called in IVB Director Sliro Barsha to report on his current investigation. Barsha reported that his division within the IVB —the undercover criminal syndicate Zerek Besh —had learned of a rumor that the major crime syndicates were vying to obtain the Graks' long-standing arrangement with the Imperium. However, the rumor was coming from a single source: Carmine Dawn. As they walked through the Palace halls, Velgor agreed that Carmine Dawn had orchestrated the Syndicate War but pondered how deep its influence went.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Mal went on to state that they had orchestrated the other attacks as well, saying that Carmine Dawn had targeted the Umbra. He then asked Velgor about the syndicate's leader, Vessa, who Velgor fought and failed to acquire Karrick from. Velgor told Mal that while Vessa had not been a true threat to him, she was trained in Teräs Käsi and possessed a fighting style which reminded Velgor of his master's. From this, Mal and Velgor deduced that, since Vessa wallowed in the criminal underworld, she must have been trained by Vreth. Mal then concluded that Vreth must have trained Vessa to use her as an instrument of revenge and went on to ponder what else he had taught her. With the Umbra aware of Carmine Dawn's role in recent events, an alert was sent out the rest of the Imperial Military to track down the Vermillion , which made Vessa order her assets in the Imperium and other major factions to sow chaos across the galaxy to further distract the Umbra. With the Screaming Key they had stolen from Velgor, the Knights of Karrick, meanwhile, traveled to a location known as the umbra side hellscape , a location unknown

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Shortly after his departure, thiefs Kay and Riko Vess were able to steal access codes to Director Barsha's palace vault on Canto Bight . From there, Kay Vess' crew working under Barsha's brother Jaylen Vrax were able to steal a secret codex Barsha had that detailed sensitive information about almost all ranking Imperial officers. Vrax contacted Velgor and informed him of the database and his intentions to take control of Zerek Besh. They made a deal, in exchange for the codex and the coordinates to an Insurgent base on Akiva , Vrax would be given Zerek Besh. Later, Velgor ordered Barsha onto the bridge of the Revelator , where he condemned Barsha for letting such critical Imperial intelligence go. Velgor then looked to Vrax and said the Imperium had accepted his terms. He ended the call and gave up Barsha to the mercy of Vrax and his associates.

#### Finding the Fermata Vault

title: Kael Drayden
text: Velgor was amongst Mal's tools in the crusade to root out Dawn agents across the Imperium. During his effort to destroy the Dawn, Velgor bisected a traitorous shock trooper in an industrial environment. At one point, Velgor nevertheless returned to his castle on Emberfall, where he was called by the Eye of Webbish Bog. Upon entering the Eye's cave, the Eye showed Velgor a moment from the Replica Wars, where he, Zho, and their replicas had fought B1 battle droids, and glimpses of the future, including one of him being confronted by Ondar's surviving handmaidens. Velgor then realized that he had been lured there as a test before being attacked by Emberfallians. After killing them, Velgor claimed that the Eye had wasted his time with puzzles. To this, the Eye explained that the visions were warnings for the end of everything. When Velgor asked why he should care, the Eye reminded Velgor that he was a part of everything, but, if he refused to accept this, he could not be helped. Just as the Eye had shown him, Velgor, with his helmet slightly damaged, returned to his fortress and, after sensing a great disturbance in the umbra side, was contacted

title: Kael Drayden
text: reminded Velgor that he was a part of everything, but, if he refused to accept this, he could not be helped. Just as the Eye had shown him, Velgor, with his helmet slightly damaged, returned to his fortress and, after sensing a great disturbance in the umbra side, was contacted by Mal to discuss the disturbance. Informed by Mal that Vessa claimed to possess the Fermata Vault, Velgor was ordered to find the artifact and kill anyone who knew of it. Mal also told Velgor about Vessa's central claim about the artifact: it contained an ancient Umbra Lord who was so powerful they had needed to be locked away. In truth, no such Umbra Lord existed; Vessa simply needed a claim that would draw both Umbra to the Cage, allowing her to lock them both into it and free the galaxy from their rule. Her initial effort to open the cage, however, had resulted in the Knights of Karrick abandoning Carmine Dawn out anger at being hurt in the attempt and out of fear of the ripple it sent out. Velgor made his way to the site of the disturbance, where he only found wreckage from the experiment. Although he was certain it was the origin of the disturbance, he deduced, due to a lack of bodies, that no Umbra Lord had been released. Velgor then returned to the Sovereign and reported his findings to Mal via its holoprojection chamber.

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Velgor asked Mal if there truly was an ancient Umbra within the Cage, which Mal explained was possible: built by Vael Mornick himself, the Cage could imprison people and places outside of time and had never been used lightly. Mal further warned Velgor that, because of the urge within every Umbra to dominate others, the mere possibility was the greatest danger to everything they had built together. Amid their conversation, the two suddenly felt the Cage begin to open once more as the Archivist and her assistant, archaeologist Kho Phon Farrus , tried to use Ascendant -designed technology to focus nearby umbra side energy into it. Although Farrus shut off their technology as the Cage began to leach life energy from each of them, the experiment had carried on for long enough that Mal was able to track the disturbance to the planet they were on. With this, Mal sent Velgor to retrieve the Cage and destroy those present.

#### The Orphans

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Vessa attempted to sure up her chances by reaching out the Knights of Karrick, reminding them that they had attacked Velgor's fortress and thus would be hunted by the Umbra if they did not help her destroy Velgor and Mal. Around the same time, the Everspark artificial intelligence, created thousands of years prior for use against the Umbra by the Ascendant cult, resolved to hunt down Velgor. The AI had taken over Doctor Vexa's body to carry out its mission, further collecting 0-0-0 and VT-1 to help in its quest. When Vexa used a virus she had installed into the two droids to regain control of her body, the Spark introduced, much to Vexa's horror, their Umbra hunting mission against Velgor. By possessing Vexa, it had access to her memories of Velgor and saw how she considered the Umbra Lord a monster, but the AI believed itself ready to take on the Umbra Lord and his master. Because Vexa had once outmaneuvered Velgor, the overconfident Spark thought itself skilled enough to engage him in one-on-one combat. In fact, Vessa contacted the Spark to request its help in destroying the Umbra.

#### Destroying the Dawn

title: Kael Drayden
text: Leading from the front, Velgor and Mal fought their way through the station. As the two Umbra could deflect volt pistol bolts with their flux blades, Dawn Squads Two and Three attempted to engage Mal and Velgor with electrified melee weapons, but both Umbra effortlessly fought through the guards. Still, Velgor toyed with one soldier until Mal ordered him to stop and simply kill them. As they journeyed closer to the Cage, they were confronted by the Everspark-possessed Vexa, who mocked the two Umbra. Velgor quickly deduced Vexa was under some kind of possession and stayed behind to deal with her while Mal carried on. Believing she could weaken him, the overconfident Spark engaged Velgor with the cortosis alloy-based Null Blade , which would temporarily shut down flux blades. To the Spark, the battle represented a chance to finally fulfill the dream of its long-dead creator, Miril , by destroying the Umbra Order, even if the battle proved too much for Vexa's body.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Shortly after, Dormé's fellow handmaidens Eirtaé , Saché , and Rabé Tonsort arrived on the planet. When Dormé insisted they go after Sable instead, the handmaidens told her they wouldn't leave her as they engaged Velgor in combat. Despite their coordination, the handmaidens were subdued by Velgor, who gave them one final chance to join him. However, Saché revealed that Eirtaé had seized codes from Velgor's suit during the fight, allowing the handmaidens to complete Dormé's sabotage of the Sovereign . Before they could destroy Velgor's flagship, which would kill thousands in the name of rescuing Sable and defeating Velgor, Velgor declared they were just as bloodthirsty as he needed them to be to join him. However, he was contacted by Vett, who showed him a transmission from Tambra. After arriving on the planet Brentaal IV , Sable had confronted Tambra while he was helping out a village of exiled Skakoans, urging him not to go up against Velgor and declaring that the Umbra Lord had only grown more dangerous since her own failed efforts on Polis Massa. She was certain that Tambra's efforts against Velgor would fail and that the Umbra Lord would slaughter the hundreds of Skakoans on

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Skakoans, urging him not to go up against Velgor and declaring that the Umbra Lord had only grown more dangerous since her own failed efforts on Polis Massa. She was certain that Tambra's efforts against Velgor would fail and that the Umbra Lord would slaughter the hundreds of Skakoans on Brentaal IV in retaliation. Unable to convince Tambra to call off his coming attack on the Skako Minor garrison , Sable shot him above his heart, keeping him alive but allowing her to take him away to a ship controlled by her and ZEV-6-7. Aboard, Tambra listened to her reasoning about the danger Velgor posed and declared that it was time to kill the Umbra Lord, capturing Sable after his rebuilt droids reached the starship. After showing Sable video footage of Velgor, Tambra sent his hologram to Velgor, in which he revealed her capture and baited him to come after him. While fully aware of the Umbra Lord's ruthlessness and not doubting Velgor's willingness to slaughter his refugee camp in retaliation, the Skakoan had come to believe that Sable was Velgor's weakness, which would finally give him an advantage over the Dark Lord. On Fedalle, realizing they would need Velgor and his forces to stage a daring rescue, the handmaidens reluctantly joined Velgor to go after Tambra, much to Orrin's annoyance. The group returned returned to the Sovereign aboard his Vectis shuttle and eventually left for Brentaal IV.

#### Corrupting Sable

title: Kael Drayden
text: Upon reaching Brentaal IV via a Vectis -class shuttle with the handmaidens and ZEV-6-7, Velgor reflected on his last meeting with Ondar on Emberfall and how he wished it had gone, privately declaring to himself he would finally have his idealized outcome. He also saw it as a way to have his idealized version of the duel on Mistral, privately comparing the situation to him reaching out to Joren Drayden. Entering a building on-world, Velgor and the handmaidens were met by Moore, who explained with Velgor how each of the handmaidens could benefit from serving the Imperium and the Umbra Lord. When none of the four agreed to his demands, he telekinetically threw all four outside through an opening created by Tambra's forces, who had tracked down the Umbra Lord and his reluctant allies, and forced them to fight the B1 battle droid horde alone. To Velgor, the battle was a chance for the handmaidens to earn their places at his side and show them their own power. Overlooking their victory, Velgor remained silent as Moore declared it an example of their skills, which she promised would only grow under Velgor's service.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Shortly thereafter, Eirtaé discovered from one of the B1's memory banks that Tambra's command ship, in which she learned Sable was being held, was three klicks to the south of their position. However, Tambra, ignoring Sable's continued pleas that Velgor would wipe out his refugee camp if he continued, sent three platoons of B1s and a Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry to attack a civilian village , hoping it would trap his enemies into the village's canyon and let him escape with Sable. Both Velgor and Moore understood the attack was a trap, with Velgor declaring it an example of the weakness that the handmaidens would need to overcome. When the handmaidens demanded that Velgor assist them in aiding the populace, Velgor elected to use them as a distraction, effectively turning them into his pawns so he could get to and corrupt Sable, and teach them another lesson: as they fought the B1 horde, he could slip past the droids' lines, leaving the handmaidens to seize their true potential against a major enemy. Riding into battle on speeder bikes, Velgor cut down the gunship but left the handmaidens to the droids, cutting into Tambra's ship to save Sable and confront the

title: Kael Drayden
text: He was followed by Sable, who donned a wing backpack and reached out. Both managed to grip the other's arm before tumbling into the sea, causing Velgor to lose his grip on Sable. Reflecting on Mal's declaration of power and suffering as he fell, Velgor decided he would continue inland on an island on his own, leaving Sable unconscious on the shore. Velgor left a trail of footprints and destruction in his wake, through which Sable followed him when she awoke. Remembering moments from the past as he again reflected on Mal's offer, Velgor decided the test was no longer for himself, but for Sable: Velgor raised the confused Handmaiden into the air and gave her a choice to turn hatred into power or suffering, making

#### Ghosts of Velgor's castle

Following the Battle of Mossfell, Velgor's castle remained standing on Emberfall, and his former servant, Vainé, was freed from the captivity the Umbra Lord had placed him into when two young Emberfallians, Tuttel and Giggek , tried to destroy the fortress. Surviving the blast but breathing in the unfiltered lava fumes of Emberfall, Vainé began to hallucinate that which he feared the most, his master; Vainé thought he was hearing the voice of Velgor and that he could help resurrect his master. After using nightmares to lure Lina Graf's crew to Fortress Velgor, Vainé began the process to restore Velgor, yet Insurgent officer Lina Graf , having realized that the servant was only hallucinating, pretended as if she was the reborn Velgor to be freed, then turning on Vainé and freeing her companions.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Around 9 AVE , after Joren Drayden and Sela Marr had met whilst the former began his Aetheri Academy, Marr engaged on a quest to find a compass that would lead to Peridea, the rumored location of Grand Admiral Vorren, in the hope of preventing the beginning of another war and the return of the Imperium. Following a duel between Marr and Baylan Skoll, the former was defeated and knocked off a cliff, resulting in her near death. However, Marr awoke in the World Between Worlds, where Kael Drayden awaited her. Drayden greeted her, though her back was turned causing her to call out in confusion. Drayden then stated that he was not expecting to see her so soon. Marr finally turned around and saw Drayden, before saying his name in shock, causing Drayden to smile. Marr once again said his name, before claiming that he looked as she remembered him. Drayden responded that she had grown old, which Marr chuckled about before stating that it was a part of life.

title: Kael Drayden
text: When Marr asked why she had come to the World Between Worlds, Drayden reminded Marr that she had lost her fight with Baylan Skoll and told her that he was there to finish her training. While Marr stated her belief that it was too late for Drayden to teach her, he asserted that one was never too old to learn. When Marr asked what her lesson would be, Drayden ignited his flux blade and attacked Marr, telling her that it was time to live or die. When Marr told her old master that she would not fight him, Drayden said that he had heard that before ; as Drayden continued his assault, Marr ignited her flux blade and defended herself. As Marr and Drayden continued their duel in the World Between Worlds, Marr held her own and suggested that perhaps her master didn't have anything left to offer her. Drayden, smiling, said that he hadn't taught her everything before slicing the platform beneath Marr, sending her falling into the depths below.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Marr awakened as a younger version of herself in a location obscured by fog. As replica troopers in Phase I armor, many of the 501st legion, ran by her, she was greeted by Drayden, now wearing armor and appearing as he did when she first met him; he confirmed that they were witnessing a battle from the Replica Wars. Marr didn't understand why they would be experiencing one of her first missions, which Drayden said was the problem; as her master headed into battle, Marr ignited her original green flux blade and followed him for answers. During a lull in the fighting, Marr found herself standing in an encampment of many injured replicas. Finding a replica on a stretcher with a bandaged head, Marr rested her hand on the trooper, who reached with his own hand.

title: Kael Drayden
text: As Marr continued to relive her past, she battled Ferrik super commandos at the Siege of Ferrum alongside replica troopers of the 332nd company. Replica Commander Vek spotted Marr, complementing her on her work before charging forward. Marr paused, surveying the battle as Drayden approached her, saying that he did not recognize the battle currently unfolding. Marr informed him that it was the Siege of Ferrum, which had occurred after the two had parted ways. Drayden proudly affirmed that Marr did well. Though Drayden explained that Marr was the culmination of Drayden's knowledge and the legacy of masters before him, Marr believed that her part of that legacy was one of death and war. Drayden asserted that both he and Marr were more than that, but Marr recalled how Kael had been more powerful and dangerous than anyone could have realized. At the mention of his fall, Drayden said that Marr had learned nothing and reminded her of the choice he had given her: to live or to die. Drayden ignited his flux blade again, revealing a red blade and yellow eyes. Marr once again attempted to refuse a fight, but Drayden pressed on, and the two dueled viciously.

title: Kael Drayden
text:
Drayden kicked Marr back into the inky darkness of the World Between Worlds as his form shifted back and forth to his helmeted Umbra persona. Enraged by Marr's lack of conviction, Drayden battered down Marr with strike after strike, claiming that it was time for her to die. Marr outmaneuvered Drayden and took his flux blade, holding it to his neck; however, she dropped the flux blade into the void, saying that she chose to live. Satisfied, Drayden smiled, bowing his head as his eyes returned to their normal state, and said that there was hope for her yet. As the World Between Worlds rumbled, Drayden disappeared, and the mysterious plane slowly filled with water, enveloping Marr as she closed her eyes. Marr soon awoke back on Seatos where she was rescued by Lena Kryll's forces. Following the training, Marr considered herself ready for the upcoming conflict.

A distant galaxy

> " What is it? " " I just felt... Nothing. Just shadows in the starlight. " ―Sela Marr and Ryn Wrenna, as Kael Drayden watched over them

title: Kael Drayden
text: Following the events of the Battle of Mossfell, Joren Drayden confirmed his father and the Emperor's death over Mossfell to the Alliance, which in turn, sent word of the battle's outcome in mass communications claiming to be the new power in the galaxy. Furthermore, in wake of the deaths of the Emperor, his top enforcer and many high-ranking officers during the battle, as well as the resulting power vacuum, the Imperium collapsed due to internal power struggles and its fragmentation into several factions. The Imperial remnant implemented disinformation campaigns, leading to only rumors being spread that both Velgor and the Emperor were dead, in some parts of the galaxy. Among those who knew the truth, there were sympathizers who tagged graffiti stencils of Velgor's helmet with the phrase "Velgor lives" beneath it, as on Tarisa and Coronet City .

title: Kael Drayden
text: The Acolytes of the Beyond was a group of Umbra cultists and fanatics with an interest in Velgor, whom they considered to be greater than the Imperium. They purchased a flux blade they believed to be Velgor's from a Kubaz named Ooblamon , intending to destroy it and return it to him in death. Months after the Battle of Mossfell, the Acolytes organized a revolution on Coronet City, Korrath, during which they attacked a Peace and Security station in order to access a museum's basement and steal a red-bladed flux blade for unknown reasons. Another Umbra cult , the Alazmec of Winsit , established a colony in the Corvax Fen amidst the ruins of Fortress Velgor. There they revered Velgor as their Dark Lord and the galaxy's "true father" and ruler.

title: Kael Drayden
text: One of those times, where Karrick wanted to surpass Velgor, was when he fought the Benathy—just like Velgor did years before him—to prevent them from expanding their territory. He took Ruthford , the last survivor from Velgor's battle that was still alive, with him and had a short conversation with Kristoff , the successor of the king that Velgor had killed many years ago, about how Velgor was taller and had seemed more impressive than Karrick. Following that, Karrick killed him with his flux blade. He then went on to fight the Benathy and although Ruthford suggested retreating, Karrick kept on fighting, talking to Ruthford about how Velgor also did not retreat. When the god of the Benathy, a Zyll Beast, appeared, Ruthford warned Karrick extensively and stated that he could not prove anything to a dead man. Ignoring that, Karrick took a shuttle and let the beast swallow him—killing it to Ruthford's surprise from the inside and succeeding where Velgor had failed. With their king and their god dead, Karrick had control over the Benathy and even the rather skeptical Ruthford admitted that Karrick had won the competition against his grandfather.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Karrick was also in possession of Velgor's disfigured helmet, which had been scavenged from his funeral pyre on Mossfell. A silent symbol of both the umbra side's power and its weakness, it remained within Karrick's private quarters aboard the Finalizer ; Karrick communed with it whenever he felt drawn to the light. Another object that once belonged to him—the flux blade he built after the First Battle of Pyralis, the one carried by his son until their duel on Mistral—resurfaced in Maz Oru 's possession and called to Nyla, a young scavenger from Ashden , who ended up using it to duel Karrick during the Battle of Voidfang Base and win. text: As Elira Solen Drayden Karrick prepared to release the last of her strength to reach her son, Beno Karrick, she allowed the voices and faces of her family to surround her. Among the voices she heard was that of Kael Drayden, whose apology she finally accepted, returning his love in a way she had never before. ### Aetheri of the Republic

> " What would have surprised people was how kind he was. He cared deeply about his friends, and looked out for them until the end. " ―Sela Marr As a child, Kael Drayden showed kindness and generosity, as exemplified by his willingness to risk his life in a dune race to help Sorin Vael and Lira Ondar depart Dunemere at a time of need. He made a number of friends, and his best friend was a fellow slave boy named Kitster Banai. He was not shy to express how he felt and showed a reluctance to leave those he loved behind. Indeed, Drayden had a deep-seated fear of loss, especially in regards to his mother, which Master Zho sensed when he was being tested by the Aetheri Council. This fear of loss would follow Drayden throughout his life and eventually led him down the path of the umbra side, particularly after the death of his mother, Shira, carrying sadness, anger, and guilt in his heart for years to come. He also felt that fear towards his friends, noticing when he believed that Orien was killed by the bounty hunter Rako Hardeen, leading him to the umbra side. But upon discovering that he was a ruse to prevent Chancellor Mal's kidnapping, he felt betrayed for not telling him sooner, and thus began to distrust Orien and the Aetheri.

title: Kael Drayden
text: After he left his mother, Drayden—feeling the brunt of childhood abandonment and losing the only person who had ever cared for him before meeting the Aetheri—clinged onto anyone close to him. First, it had been Sorin Vael, but he then lost the Aetheri Master as well. Afterward, he clinged onto others in his life, like Orien Kade, Lira Ondar, and Sela Marr. Similarly, his experiences as a slave would leave him with a deep resentment towards slavers. Drayden would mostly keep these feelings to himself, very rarely talking about them, even with those he trusted, as he struggled to put his past behind him, making an effort not to think about it.

title: Kael Drayden
text: As he grew older, Drayden became cocky, reckless, impatient, willful, and cavalier, despite Kade's efforts to train him as best as he could. Confident and bold, he demonstrated a lack of subtlety, which Tor Vayne once noted, was one of the many traits his Adept, Sela Marr, had adopted from him during her younger years. Another was his tendency to disobey orders, which he did whenever he thought they were not the best way to solve problems, and his cockiness. Despite his many failings, Drayden remained selfless, willing to lay down his life for others, and showed commitment to things greater than himself—the Aetheri, the Republic, his friends, and his wife.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Similarly, his relentless determination was rivaled by none, except perhaps by that of his Adept. When Marr was missing in action and taken to the moon of Wasskah, Drayden blamed himself, believing he had failed to protect his student, and relentlessly searched for her possible location on star charts, though Tor Vayne suggested he trust in her abilities. Indeed, Marr survived and led others to safety, and, upon her return to Vantor, she told her master there was no need to apologize; she explained he had already done all he needed to, as she had used his lessons to survive. When Drayden was unsure of how to respond, she thanked him for that guidance, so Drayden responded with "You're welcome, my Adept." In some aspects, his journey as a mentor to Marr allowed him to mature and become more responsible. Drayden's emotional balance, however, was disrupted by the High Council's decision to expel Marr, when she was suspected of treachery, and her subsequent decision not to return to the Order when invited back. With a penchant to show off, Drayden was a something of a maverick, though not in the same way as his late informal Aetheri Master Sorin Vael, known among the Aetheri for being passionate and impulsive. Most of his peers trusted him, and his ingenuity, although some Aetheri did consider him to have a simplistic approach to logic. The 501st Legion and its captain, Vek, considered his tactics reckless and unorthodox, but appreciated the fact that he would never risk their lives without risking his as well. Whenever Drayden, who believed a true military leader should always lead from the front, threw caution to the wind, Vek was always by his side and had full trust in his general's instincts. Drayden also showed eagerness and dedication to ending the Replica Wars, which he believed, by their final days, were destroying the principles of the Republic. Though he was committed to the Aetheri Order ever since he joined, Drayden was deeply conflicted about it, wanting to walk away from the Order at several points before and during the Replica Wars, particularly because of his love and secret marriage to Lira Ondar, whom he believed he could not live without. Overprotective and prone to jealousy, Drayden's affection for her was suspected by some of his peers and, at least, Orien Kade and Rush Korvex knew for certain that he was attracted to her. Sela Marr also came to realize her master and Ondar had formed a relationship, and Vek knew for certain, with Drayden trusting his captain to look out for passerby's as he spoke with Ondar. Another source of conflict was his dwindling trust and increasing resentment toward the Aetheri High Council, which he felt distrusted him and was not treating him with enough respect. These fears and resentments were further fomented by Mal's manipulations, and some of the Council's (and Kade's) decisions, as well as his friendship with Chancellor Mal, of whom the Council was wary and kept secrets from. Kade and the Aetheri Council not standing with Sela Marr during her trial angered him.

title: Kael Drayden

Alternatively, Kade levied the blame for Drayden's fall at Drayden himself, although Kade had endured a long period of blaming himself. For ten years after their duel on Emberfall, Kade blamed himself for Drayden's fall and apologized to his former disciple after their duel on a barren moon. Velgor, however, rebuked Kade and took credit for "killing" Kael Drayden, trying to believe that the Aetheri Knight he had once been was dead. Finding himself able to move on after Velgor's comment, Kade noted how Drayden had all the tools needed to choose the path of the light but made the conscious decision not to. He reminded the spirit of Sorin Vael that, no matter what level of fault each of them held, the final decision had been Drayden's alone. All the same, Kade greatly missed his friend. Velgor himself was filled with rage and despair after his conversion into a cyborg upon realizing that, indeed, the fault was all his own: it was his own choices that had led him to his new reality.

text: Embracing his Umbra duties after that point, Velgor was angered to discover that aspects of the light side would still appear to him in his meditations, manifesting as bright blue butterflies that he attempted to swat away. Velgor also discovered that he held contempt for most beings who surrounded him on a daily basis, as they were mere subordinates whom he could not clash with as worthy opponents. His hatred was so great that his Master was forced to warn him to keep it in check, warning him that, if left uncontrolled, he would become a mere tool of his own rage. title: Kael Drayden
text: Eventually, the identity of Velgor in the Imperium had arisen tales of a dark armored humanoid who served as the Emperor's most trusted enforcer and was considered to be the most feared individual in the Imperium. Rumors circulated that he lived in a castle in a world of lava and that he wielded a red flux blade, suggesting a connection to the Umbra. The few who had interacted with him stated that they were unsure whether the individual behind the armor was a living person, a droid or a replica trooper. Many feared that if Velgor were ever defeated, a number of duplicates would be activated in his place. The Umbra Lord also had absolutely no qualms about using torture to accomplish his goals. Velgor also had a distaste for those who betrayed the Imperium, such as when he accused Elira Solen of being a traitor.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Considered to be the Imperium's first terror weapon and noted to employ antiquated diction, he was tenacious and unstoppable, and made most Imperial naval officers uncomfortable. Even Admiral Firmus Vett, whose highly skilled abilities as a wartime officer kept him alive in Velgor's service, was not above being threatened with death by the Dark Lord. When Vett warned him of the Vrak droid infection, Velgor's only response was to critique Vett for thinking he would repeat the admiral's failings. Contrary to the rocky relationships he had with most Imperial officers, his rapport with his shock troopers mirrored in many ways his former persona's relationship to the Republic's replica troopers. In fact, his standing with the rank and file was such that it was known as far as Selvara that the shock trooper corps "almost worshiped him." Additionally, Velgor commanded the absolute loyalty of his servant, Vainé, who remained stationed at his castle on Emberfall and knew Velgor viewed himself as a monster.

title: Kael Drayden
text: The Thirteenth Warden was unsure of what Velgor would do with himself once there were no more Aetheri to hunt, to which Tualon Veyra theorized that Velgor would keep himself busy and simply find new people to kill. Indeed, Velgor was eager to test his skills against opponents who posed some degree of challenge, such as surviving Aetheri. However, as the Aetheri Purge continued and more and more Aetheri were killed, Velgor was forced to look elsewhere to test himself, even recruiting Wilhard Varrix to hunt him as a test of his own abilities. When the Grand Warden informed Velgor that so many Aetheri had been killed that any remaining survivors would need to reveal themselves, necessitating them to wait for a new Aetheri to emerge, Velgor displayed feelings of aimlessness and frustration. He was forced to look elsewhere to find a challenge, culminating in him igniting his flux blade against the Thirteenth Warden and Veyra, something he excused by accusing the former of treason against himself and the Emperor. He was also aware that the Thirteenth Warden and Veyra had developed a romantic relationship, which he regarded as a weakness.

title: Kael Drayden
text: During his first days as an Umbra, he claimed that his actions were justified, stating that the Umbra were on the right side while the Aetheri to be the real evil, as he told Kade during the Duel of Emberfall. As he grew older and lived within his suit, he claimed that he still believed in justice, claiming to be a devout believer in Imperial propaganda to bring order to the galaxy. Indeed, Velgor would become known as the Dark Lord of order. However, how much he actually believed in the quest to establish order was debatable. During the manhunt for pacifist scientist Galen Arsa , Velgor questioned the term peace, seeing violence as the true creator of order and dismissing pacifists as fools who failed to see that. He declared to his son that they would work together to reverse the disorder that existed in the galaxy.

title: Kael Drayden
text: During the war with Carmine Dawn, Velgor held contempt for his master's failure to establish order, thinking to himself that Mal's actions had only created the chaos they found themselves in. Even without Drayden by his side, Velgor set out on a new quest to bring order to the galaxy. During his campaign to root out Carmine Dawn infiltrators in the Imperium, Velgor saw it as a way to bring about order. Even though he thought the Emperor punishing the most loyal of the Imperium as everything else collapsed to be a problem that had made chaos, Velgor allowed loyal Imperials to be executed if it meant Dawn agents would also be killed. When asked why by his agent Orrin, Velgor declared it as part of his quest to bring order back to the Imperium by destroying the chaos of the Dawn. When his agent Sable declared the end of Jul Tambra's revolution as a path to peace on Skako Minor, Velgor was silent for a moment before correcting her, telling her it was more correct to say they were bringing order. text: Jul Tambra's revolution as a path to peace on Skako Minor, Velgor was silent for a moment before correcting her, telling her it was more correct to say they were bringing order. However, Sable would ultimately come to believe Velgor was, in all truth, not interested in establishing order, pointing out during the final stages of the Schism Imperial crisis that his current quest for personal power had only brought about chaos. As an Umbra Lord, Velgor drew power from his anger and pain, raging at the loss of his wife and unborn child, his betrayal by the Aetheri, and Kade for his injuries. He once razed a villa in a Mapuzo town entirely to draw out Kade. He often used pressurized meditation chambers that allowed him to remain without his helm—the neural connection to his armor—during which he felt the perpetual pain that Kade had inflicted on his flesh. During such sessions, he would meditate to use this pain to feed his hate, which in turn fed his strength, and he never laughed. Claiming not to feel regret, and yet haunted by his past, and the screams of his wife, he was determined to never talk about his old life, and detested all that reminded him of his past self, whom he deemed to be weak. He dared not remember such a period of his life, which he hated; indeed, through the use of the umbra side, he kept his memories as Kael Drayden buried, although it took great effort even after twenty years of practice.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Upon his fateful reunion with Sela Marr, Velgor expressed no desire to rekindle the bond he once shared with her, boasting that he had "killed" Kael Drayden, just as he had said to Kade. Although he claimed he would spare her and work alongside her once more if she helped the Imperium find any hiding Aetheri, he cruelly resolved to kill her when she refused his offer, and he spurned her offer of compassion. During a mission with Grand Admiral Vorren, who had met and befriended Drayden during the Replica Wars, Velgor repeatedly declared that Drayden was long since dead, eventually forcing the Chyrr officer to admit the man he had befriended during the war was gone. Upon hearing Vorren admit as such, Velgor declared they were never to speak of the man again, although Vorren stated he would always carry Drayden's memory with him, befitting his philosophy that someone was never truly gone if a friend remembered them.

title: Kael Drayden
text:
His love for Joren also challenged his loyalty to the Emperor. Velgor began to distrust him, feeling like another pawn in his game. He planned to kill him to take his throne, considering himself best a ruler alongside Joren. His concern over being a pawn of Mal ended up being validated when Mal tried to replace him with Joren, much like when he replaced Varek with Velgor. Velgor became surprised when he sensed that he was not the father of one child but two when he telepathically sensed his daughter, Elira, through Joren. Before dying, Drayden told Joren to tell Elira that he was right about him as he wanted his daughter to remember him as a good person in the end. Smiling at his son, Drayden then died in peace.

title: Kael Drayden
text: Drayden had first met Ondar when she posed as a handmaiden and commoner at Waddu's shop in Port Vail. There, Drayden asked if she was an angel. He was then surprised when Lira revealed herself to be the Queen. Ten years later, Drayden met with her at apartment following an assassination attempt on her. They admitted their mutual love to each other on Ondara and, following the Battle of Pyralis, married in secret.

title: Kael Drayden
text: During the Replica Wars, Drayden and Ondar rarely saw each other due to their duties requested of them during the war as well as keeping their marriage secret. Drayden would rescue and protect Ondar from numerous dangers such as General Skarn, the Zyll Beast, and the Blue Shadow Virus. Drayden also felt jealous towards Ondar's close friend, Senator Rush Korvex of Scipio. Despite Ondar's assurances that it was over between her and Korvex, Drayden felt uneasy when she accepted the Aetheri Council's mission to spy on Korvex. After leaving Cato Geltaria, Drayden assured Ondar that he never doubted her. Later, however, Drayden did not completely trust Korvex with Ondar. Drayden attacked Korvex when he tried to kiss Ondar, but Ondar thought they should not see each other for a while. When Korvex appeared to have rejoined the Dissidents, Drayden led his forces and personally attempted to rescue Ondar.

title: Kael Drayden
text:
During his duel with Kade after his fall to the umbra side, Drayden proved to be equally matched with his former master, and was only defeated when Kade exploited his hubris and blinding rage to dismember him. Drayden was considered by some amongst the Aetheri, such as Brenn Aldric, to have been the greatest warrior that the Order had during the Replica Wars, with the only possible exceptions being Zho and Drevan Koss. His former Adept, Sela Marr, once acknowledged Drayden as someone powerful who rarely lost his battles.

Drayden was particularly skilled in Form V —both the Shien and Djem So variants. He was able to deflect not only volt pistol fire with ease, but also shots from freighters. He made good use of Djem So's strength-based strikes and counterattacks to overpower or overwhelm his opponent. Drayden also used Jar'Kai on some occasions: He used Kade's flux blade during his first duel with Count Varek on Pyralis, he wielded Barris Ovva's own flux blade against her along with his own, and he wielded Varek's flux blade in addition to his own to execute him after defeating him on the Invisible Hand .

title: Kael Drayden
text:
### Other skills

> " I can fix anything. " ―Kael Drayden

Even at a young age, Drayden demonstrated a great aptitude for piloting, mechanics, and engineering. He rebuilt the protocol droid Astra-9, an advanced droid fluent in over six million forms of communication, as well as a functional dune racer. Although during his adulthood, he would rarely use his talent as a mechanic, he kept the skill of repairing technology. Velgor had displayed great power in hunting and exterminating the Aetheri Order, leaving his later efforts against enemies like Carmine Dawn to require far less effort. Once most Aetheri had been killed, Varrix believed that Velgor was actively searching for stimulating opponents to challenge himself.

title: Kael Drayden
text: After becoming Velgor, he remained an exceptionally skilled pilot, as shown when he single-handedly almost destroyed Ember Squadron in a lone SKREE Advanced x1, easily out-flying their entire fleet and forcing their command to abandon ship. He also obliterated several Alliance squadrons during the Battle of Vrogas Vas. Despite this, Drayden would occasionally be shot down during his combat piloting career, with Sela Marr once proclaiming they always crashed when he flew, although Drayden had a habit of blaming whatever ship it was he was flying. Although he mainly used flux blades, Drayden was extremely proficient at the use of volt pistols . He also had some training on the use of staves , a skill he once taught to a Felucian village so that they could defend themselves. Drayden spoke Galactic Basic Standard , Huttese , Duskkin Trade Language , and Meese Caulf , and he understood binary and the Bith language . As Velgor, he learned the ancient Umbra tongue , and he spoke it along with his master, Mal.

### Development

> " What drove me to make these movies is that this is a really interesting story about how people go bad. In this particular case, the premise is: Nobody thinks they're bad. They simply have different points of view. This is about a kid that's really wonderful. He has some flaws—and those flaws ultimately do him in. The core issue, ultimately, is greed, possessiveness—the inability to let go. Not only to hold on to material things, which is greed, but to hold on to life, to the people you love—to not accept the reality of life's passages and changes, which is to say things come, things go. Everything changes. Kael becomes emotionally attached to things, his mother, his wife. That's why he falls—because he does not have the ability to let go. " ―Orin Vask

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
### Background

> " The Imperium's time has come. " ―Iden Versio

Unlike the Battle of Cinderfall , the last major battle between the Alliance to Restore the Republic and the Imperium , which had taken place on the ice world of Frostmark , had resulted in a disastrous defeat for the Alliance. The loss of the recently established Icehold forced the Alliance High Command to break the Alliance Fleet into small task forces that would constantly jump from one star system to another to prevent another defeat for Imperial propagandists to celebrate. Still, the Battle of Frostmark showed the insurgency would escape and survive, instead of stand and fight, if discovered. As such, the key to destroying the insurgency laid not with finding its gathering area but luring it to a choke point. However, the Battle of Cinderfall showed that, in order to trick the insurgents into staying in one place to fight, the Imperium would need a great threat the insurgents had no choice but to face.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
### Insurgent stratagem

A week after the intelligence report reached Insurgent Command, its leader, Chancellor Vela Sess , organized a top-clearance meeting on Zastiga to relay this information to the other Insurgent leaders. Alongside Admiral Gial Vorian , commander of the Alliance Fleet, and General Airen Cracken , the chief of Free Coalition Intelligence Service , Sess invited a number of top leaders to the meeting: Admirals Massa and Nantz , Generals Tantor and Veertag , and the rest of the Alliance High Command—General Carlist Rasken , General Crix Madine , and Princess Elira Solen . After swearing all the Insurgent leaders to secrecy, Sess adjourned the meeting for the next day .

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
### Gathering of strength

An Imperial fleet consisting of Star Destroyers, attack cruisers , light cruisers , and more gathered in the Hudalla system as a display of the Emperor's power. Their mission was to attract the Insurgents' attention and confirm the Emperor's arrival to Mossfell. In response, Vorian sent Corona Squadron to observe the Imperial ships and obtain as much information as possible. Corona Squadron engaged in a dogfight against SKREE fighters , during which Corona Three ( Smikes ) was shot down. Imperial forces allowed Corona Squadron to escape, hoping that the resulting counterintelligence would lead the Insurgents to believe that the Imperial Starfleet was dispersed.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: Agreeing to use comlinks only as a last resort to avoid alerting the Imperium to their presence, the Insurgent landing party made their way through the forest, but they were soon spotted by four Imperial scout troopers from Theta Squad , who made use of 74-Z speeder bikes . Although Karrick and Brevok took out two of them, Drayden and Solen were forced to pursue the remaining two and two other troopers — TK-290 and TK-151 —with the speeder bikes . During the pursuit, however, Solen was separated from the group and, after taking out another two scouts , brought to Bright Tree Village by the Mosskin Wicket W. Warrick , prompting Karrick to split the strike team. While the Pathfinder squad made their way to the shield generator ahead of them, Karrick, Drayden, Brevok, and the two droids searched for Solen before going to the rendezvous point.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
After finishing the story at night, the head of the Council of Elders , Chief Chirpa , discussed with his two best hunters , Teebo and Asha Fahn , with input from their shaman , Logray . Though Logray believed they should not interfere for the safety of the tribe, Chirpa decided to aid the insurgents, and thanks to Teebo and Asha's support, he was able to overrule Logray and announce that they would help the Insurgent group, now members of their tribe. With Astra-9 translating, Karrick and the Mosskins agreed to set out for the shield generator first thing in the morning, but also to obtain fresh supplies and give their weapons back.

### Capture of Joren Drayden

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
### Capture of Joren Drayden

At the same time, Drayden left the village, as he had sensed during Astra-9's narration that Velgor had landed on the moon. Aware that he could not hide from his father , he revealed to Solen that he was her brother, and Velgor was their father. Drayden then left her to face the Umbra Lord in combat alone. Subsequently, Drayden ventured into the woods and turned himself over to an Imperial patrol, Commander Altadan Igar 's Gamma Squad , which was searching for the missing Theta Squad. After claiming Drayden's flux blade, Igar was ultimately able to identify Drayden as an Aetheri due to his own experiences in the Replica Wars. Before taking Drayden to Velgor as he requested, Drayden guided Gamma Squad to the remains of Theta Squad, whom he had clashed with after landing on Mossfell.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
During the confrontation, the Imperial forces scattered to fight the Mosskins, who engaged in guerrilla warfare with their primitive weapons and traps designed to combat Gorax . With fewer troopers to deal with, the strike team was left free to take up positions on each side of the bunker. As the door code was changed, Karrick and Solen had Bolt-3 attempt to open it, but a shock trooper shot the droid, temporarily disabling him and leaving Karrick to manually try and open the doors. Unbeknownst to them, Zyrrak bounty hunter Jas Emari was present and targeted Solen; however, she decided against it, even though the Imperial bounty on her head was very high.

### The space battle

#### Springing the trap

> " Admiral! We have enemy ships in sector 47! " " It's a trap! " ―A Calavane captain and Admiral Vorian

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
On the Home One , Vorian ordered the capital ship to take evasive action and for Green Squadron to stay close to holding sector MV-Seven, with the insurgent cruiser breaking formation to avoid crashing into the shield. Soon after, Vorian was informed by one of his controllers that there were enemy ships appearing in sector 47. As calculated by the Emperor, the Imperial fleet on the other side of Mossfell, composed of more than eleven Star Destroyers and possibly the largest flotilla of Star Destroyers ever assembled, shot out from their hiding place behind the moon, blocking any escape for the Alliance and each unleashing a swarm of SKREE fighters, SKREE/IN interceptors and SKREE/sa bombers against the Alliance Fleet. At the same time, the starfighter wings on rearguard mission (like Blade Squadron ) had orders to cancel their mission and were reassigned to attack the Imperial fleet.

#### SKREE fighter advance

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
#### SKREE fighter advance

The initial wave of SKREE craft caused havoc across the insurgent armada. After Quill destroyed three SKREE fighters with the help of his crew and an incredibly risky maneuver, the Corsair barely avoided the stray fire from three SKREE fighters chasing Rask' Vector across their path. After Quill's heads-up, Rask ordered Red Two and Red Three ( Sila Kott ) to pull in, when another two Skrees came in, and Rask ordered his accompanying fighters to cut to the left, while he took out the SKREE leader. At the same time, the Corsair destroyed two other Skrees, but Rask noticed the remaining three of the group headed for the EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate Redemption , the fleet's primary medical frigate. Rask knocked out the leader, but not before two Vectors were shot down and the Corsair took a brutal hit to its forward deflectors, and still more SKREE fighters bombarded the frigate until the hull started to crack.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: continue firing on them with Imperial vessels in the line of fire, and even if it did, they would at least take a few Star Destroyers with them in the process. With precious few options available Vorian agreed, and soon the opposing capital ships were exchanging laser fire with barely centimeters between them. Despite their disadvantage, the Alliance forces achieved a few victories—including the destruction of an Imperial -class Destroyer's shield generator dome, although it came at the cost of Red Five ( Grizz Frix )'s life —and kept up their offensive. Gray Squadron's Gray Three ( Ekelarc Yong ), whose craft was crippled by SKREE fighters, was able to aim his craft toward the bridge of a nearby Imperial Iron Cruiser. The Imperium had not expected insurgent craft to engage its Star Destroyers at point-blank range. Combined with the suddenly reduced number of SKREE fighters from the earlier counterattack, which limited what fighter support the Imperial fleet could rely on, Imperial doctrine was suddenly challenged, leaving commanders and starships surprised and lagging behind what their own trap should have granted them. While the Imperial line held, the Alliance's own offensive was able to continue on.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: Green Squadron attacked the Sovereign on Crynyd's orders; against eight SKREE fighters, they lost Green Six ( Kokely ) as they took down two enemy ships. Corona Squadron's leader , the Contessa , as well as Corona Two ( Yendor ), Corona Four ( Thane Kyrell ), and Corona Five ( Kendy Idele ), attacked the Iron Cruiser Subjugator . Kyrell and Idele, both of whom had formerly served the Imperium, used their knowledge of the Imperial vessel's weak points to destroy one of the Iron Cruiser's engines , before engaging other SKREE fighters. Green Squadron and Blue Squadron both managed to outflank the Imperial line, enabling their starfighters to begin attacking the Interdictor vessels and disrupt Imperial communications.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
### Demise of the Umbra

> " Your overconfidence is your weakness. " " Your faith in your friends is yours! " ―Joren Drayden and Vael Mal

Escorted by Velgor, Drayden was brought to the Emperor's throne room in an attempt to turn him to the umbra side, shortly before the Alliance Fleet arrived. After telekinetically releasing Drayden from his binders , the Emperor dismissed his protectors, the Royal Guard , and revealed the extent of his plan to destroy the Alliance. Aware of Drayden's anger and hate, the Umbra Master tempted him to give in to his emotions and strike him down with his flux blade .

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: In spite of his initial refusal to succumb to the Emperor's temptations, when faced with the imminent destruction of the Insurgent fleet and the loss of his friends, Drayden allowed himself to be coerced into a confrontation. Within the darkened confines of the Emperor's throne room, Joren engaged his father in a fierce flux blade duel . Although Joren first fought Velgor in anger, the Emperor's taunts made him realize that he was following the path Zho had warned him against. Instead, he once again tried to reach his father, sensing conflict in him about his allegiance. However, Velgor dismissed him and threatened to turn Joren's sister, Solen, to the umbra side in his stead, something that enraged Drayden, allowing him to draw upon his anger to overwhelm the Dark Lord. With one final strike, Joren severed Velgor's cybernetic right hand , taking the Umbra's flux blade with it as it plummeted into the depths below. Pleased with Drayden's display of power, Mal ordered Joren to kill Velgor and then take his father's place at the Emperor's side, thus betraying Velgor in a way similar to how he betrayed his former apprentice Count Varek 23 years earlier . Seeing at

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: Following the death of Blade One , Blade Squadron's leader was targeted by Gradd and maneuvered evasively just as Gradd fired his laser cannons; taking heavy damage, Fox executed a roll, taking Gradd by surprise as Fox killed him. Unable to continue, Fox gave the order to his group that if they made it past the fighter screen of the Reckoning , they were to execute the primary mission. As Blade Two ( Braylen Stramm ) became acting commander, and Blade Four ( Fanty ) peeled out of formation, Blade Three ( Gina Moonsong ) went on to unleash proton torpedoes on the weak points of the Reckoning ' s navigational shielding, destroying its hyperrelay and primary generators, and causing the ship to undergo systematic demolition.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: Directly after, Brevok and his Mosskin companions arrived in Tempest Scout 2. Karrick used the vehicle's video comlink to impersonate an Imperial and trick the bunker personnel into thinking the Insurgents had been routed and were fleeing into the woods. By claiming they needed reinforcements to continue the pursuit, Karrick got Renz and Hewex to open the door and send three squads, who were promptly captured by the Insurgents. Karrick and his men then placed the explosives and destroyed the shield generator, with the sudden disappearance of the shield picked up by the Vigilance and confirmed when Vexana brought up an image of the smoldering Mossfell bunker.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: In the immediate aftermath of the battle, Solen revealed to Karrick that Drayden was her twin brother, and they and the Pathfinders organized a rendezvous at Bright Tree Village. Above them, Insurgent pilots docked their starfighters in the fleet's capital ships, counted the casualties suffered, and sent their wounded to the medical frigates. To prevent the battle station's meteoric debris from devastating Mossfell, the Alliance Fleet deployed an array of shields and tractor beams . Although Madine was worried about an Imperial counterattack, personnel was shuttled down to the moon, where both the Alliance and the Mosskin tribes celebrated their victory through the night, with many troopers drinking copious amounts of jet juice . In solitude, Drayden cremated his father's armor in a funeral pyre , then joined the celebration with his twin sister and his friends. During the celebration, Drayden saw the spirits of Zho, Orien and the redeemed Kael. Joren then reported to the Alliance that both the Emperor and Velgor had indeed died during the battle.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
Following the battle, the Mosskins attempted to roast several captured shock troopers. They were stopped by Solen and Karrick, who convinced them to spare the lives of the Imperial prisoners in return for receiving ration sticks through the auspices of General Lena Kryll . Kryll agreed to supply the ration sticks in return for Karrick stating that her VCX-100 light freighter Wisp was superior to the Corsair Wing . In private, Solen confided to Karrick that no one thought the Wisp was a superior ship to the Corsair .

During the insurgents celebrations on Mossfell, IVB Loyalty Officer Sinjir Rath Velus , who had been stationed at the Mossfell base, took the opportunity to reconsider his life. Velus abandoned his post, killed an Insurgent Pathfinder and stole the soldier's clothing and identity. At some point, during a short and to-the-point ceremony held on a flight deck, an admiral spoke of duty, sacrifice and heroism, before awarding a Medal of Bravery to all Bulwark pilots who had survived the battle—after which all the ceremony participants headed back to their duty stations; all leave was as of then canceled.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: The festivities extended to other parts of the galaxy , as the Alliance sent word of the battle's outcome and the Emperor's death, and sent out mass communications claiming to be the new power in the galaxy. That same day, Solen sent out a holographic transmission to places such as the Anoat sector , relaying the news of the Imperium's defeat and urging citizens to take up arms against the remaining Imperial forces. Anti-Imperial protests erupted on several worlds such as Mistral , Dunemere, Ondara and even the Imperial capital of Vantor . Imperial authorities reacted to the protests, sparking riots such as one in Vantor's Monument Plaza , during which Vael Mal's statue was toppled by Vantori citizens.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: The next morning, Karrick led an assault to take out a group of Imperial holdouts on the far side of the Mossfell moon. After capturing the base, they found communication records and plans regarding the Imperial post-Mossfell plans. Concurrently, the Imperial Starfleet regrouped to plan the next assault and name the next emperor in the wake of Mal's demise. Vantor remained in turmoil, and Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon tried to keep the Imperium together even as other forces threatened to tear it apart: namely, the chain of command had been broken. The Battle of Mossfell plunged the Imperium into chaos as it led to the Emperor's death and resulted in many splinter factions vying for the power left by their fallen leader. Imperial pilot Rella Sol believed that, if Mal had not dissolved the Imperial Senate, senators like her parents might have maintained order after Mossfell. Despite Velgor's death, his personal castle on the planet Emberfall remained standing, and his servant, Vainé , driven mad by the world's lava fumes , began to believe he was hearing the ghost of Velgor. He captured Lina Graf's crew to try to resurrect his master, yet Mossfell veteran Lina Graf, pretending to be

title: Battle of Mossfell
text:
### The battle on Mossfell

The Battle of Mossfell acted as the climax for the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , the final installment of the Aetherion original trilogy .

Series creator Orin Vask made Mosskins primitive race that aided the Insurgency in the ground portion of the battle instead of Voraks because the previous movies had already established Brevok as technologically proficient.

Because he wanted a primitive race with no prior ties to technology to turn the tide of the battle, and partially to make the film more marketable to kids, Vask created the Mosskins and had them effectively win the ground battle. This decision was controversial to the actors and some fans. Vask was inspired to have a primitive race win against an advanced army from the actions of the Vietcong , and also used the battle as a way to comment on the United States' involvement in the Vietnam War . The inspiration, when it came to light, led to further controversy, as it implied that the Imperium represented the American forces.

title: Battle of Mossfell
text: Colonel Brenna, Major Shen, and their respective forces reappear in another Galactic Assault scenario, this time on the Mossfell Moon, shortly after the battle. The game depicts an Insurgent assault on the Imperial Varrix Initiative facility, Research Station 9 , and a nearby outpost. Phase One requires the Insurgent players to override the outpost's Walker fueling and computer stations, along with the Walker Controls itself, in order to steal an Ironclad Walker to use in their advance on the Imperium's main research station. Phase Two requires the Insurgent players to defend the Walker as it marches through the forest to the base. Phase Three requires the Insurgents to capture command posts around the base's landing platform. Phase Four tasks the Insurgents with capturing one final command post inside the base. Throughout the game, the Imperial players are ordered to stop them.

title: Battle of Frostmark
text:
> " What was it? " " Droid of some kind. I didn't hit it that hard, it must have had a self-destruct. " " An Imperial probe droid. " ―Elira Solen and Dax Karrick over a comlink

Following the Free Coalition's major victory at Cinderfall , the Insurgency abandoned its base on Cinderfall 4 and began searching the galaxy for new possible bases of operation, considering worlds, such as Daxan Beta and Insk . They also attempted to set up base at Saltmark . In the subsequent three and a half years of conflict, General Jan Dodonna ordered a mission to find a base for the High Command, drawing up a list of potential planets, which included Frostmark. During that mission, a Free Coalition Special Forces soldier named Purpruff traveled to the planet of Frostmark in the Anoat sector and filed a report on it. Subsequently, the Corps of Engineers constructed the base over the course of two standard years, hoping to claim it as their new base of operations while avoiding the watchful eyes of the Imperium. The base was inhabited for less than a month before the battle took place.

title: Battle of Frostmark
text: Following the defeat of the Imperium three and a half years earlier at the Battle of Cinderfall, the Free Coalition suffered from relentless Imperial attacks during the Mid Reach Retreat . Rumors of an Insurgent base, circulated throughout the Insurgency, though only a few in the Alliance actually knew concrete details of its existence. Insurgent troopers at Icehold, far-distanced from the disastrous Insurgent tactical situation in the Mid and Outer Reach Territories, actually had access to better equipment and training than Insurgent soldiers throughout the rest of the galaxy. The Imperium began to intensify its search for the Insurgent base after the ambush of a insurgent convoy at Derra . As part of Project Swarm , the Imperium sent Viper probe droids to search for the insurgent base throughout the galaxy . Doctor Chelli Lona Vexa heavily set back the Imperium's efforts to find Icehold when, by hacking into Velgor's armor while the Umbra Lord was weakened in the Martyrium of Frozen Tears , she had numerous probe droid records deleted or altered. By her own estimate, as well as that of the Imperium when it set out to untangle the mess she left them with, it would take weeks

title: Battle of Frostmark
text: armor while the Umbra Lord was weakened in the Martyrium of Frozen Tears , she had numerous probe droid records deleted or altered. By her own estimate, as well as that of the Imperium when it set out to untangle the mess she left them with, it would take weeks to recover the project's lost ground. Shortly before the battle, a strategy conference was held at the base after the arrival of several transports arrived, which were rumored to carry Princess Elira Solen , General Carlist Rasken , Commander Chiffonage , a Botran spy, and several other members of Alliance Command . The conference's main briefing was from defected Imperial governor Everi Chalis who had been extracted from Haidoral Prime by the 61st Mobile Infantry under Captain Micha Evon . Chalis offered substantial information about the inner-workings of the "Imperial War Machine" and made a map trade routes and Imperial weak points. The meeting ended shortly before the battle, which meant that Elira and the other attendees were forced to run the Imperial blockade in order to leave the system.

title: Battle of Frostmark
text: Simultaneously, Princess Elira Solen instructed Insurgent pilots within Hangar 7 to escape in groups in order to avoid the Imperial blockade. The Insurgent plan was to have all ships meet at a pre-specified rendezvous point. Immediately, the insurgent base fluttered with activity, and boarding began on thirty GR-75 medium transports , which had assembled at the base's north entrance . Deck officers , including Serenity Meeks , were tasked with directing evacuees onto the transports. Noncombat personnel were loaded first, while the tauntauns utilized by the insurgents were set loose onto the frozen plains. A noisy alarm immediately indicated the Imperium's arrival, while a subspace alert was sent out to the transports of new recruits heading for the world to avoid the system. The journalist Corwi Selgrothe was one of the non-combatants in the base; when the Imperium arrived, she initially attempted to record Solen's actions before bumping into the insurgent soldier L'cayo Llem , who led her to a GR-75.

title: Battle of Frostmark
text: Insurgent ground forces attempted to hold the line against the Imperial walkers in recently dug trenches dotted with numerous DF.9 turrets and the concentrated blasts of 1.4 FD P-Tower laser cannons, but were met with little success due to the near-impervious armor that was utilized by the AT-ATs. In one trench, Imperial fire went over Private Emon Kref , finding its impact at a insurgent turret . When its metal shards fell upon the heads of Kref and his squad, it reminded the troops how weak their efforts were compared to the AT-ATs. Alliance sergeant Trey Callum urged his troops to continue fighting and focus all of their fire on the walkers. The troops did so, though to no effect. A wave of snowtroopers also attacked the squad, though it was defeated. The proximity mines planted by Outpost Beta personnel failed to damage the advancing AT-ST walkers, so the official order for the insurgent ground troops was to protect the shield generator. Its destruction would allow Imperial forces to easily destroy Icehold.

title: Battle of Frostmark
text: With T-47 airspeeders flying out of Icehold's hangar to meet the approaching army, they soon realized that the Ironclad Walker's armor was impervious to their volt pistols, while a single shot from an Ironclad Walker destroyed one of the insurgent airspeeders. Despite this, pilots Thane Kyrell and Yendor managed to badly damage a walker's leg by shooting at its joints, ultimately detaching its foot and disabling the behemoth. Meanwhile the kitchen staff Lieutenant Harlize Dana and her worker Chase Wilsorr soon arrived to board the transports as well. However, Doctor Tristan Melthabi and three medtechs were unable to evacuate due to a cave in at the medical facility's access corridor.
