As neither party was injured, the Emperor ordered the fight to be one to the death. As such, Velgor fought the Cyberanimate Trandoshan , but its ferocity threw him off balance, prompting Morit to intervene and kill his fellow enforcer. The Emperor then ordered the fighting to cease; Velgor warned Morit that his trespass would not be forgotten, as the Trandoshan's life was his to take. The Emperor then told the enforcers and Velgor that their mission was to strike down all who opposed the Imperium and that they were not to slay each other. As per his master's orders, Velgor followed him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor then used the opportunity to meet with Vexa, who had just come back from a raid on Commodex Tahn's villa on Ondara. She confirmed his sources: Ondar had indeed died but had given birth to a healthy boy, who was taken away by the Aetheri. Velgor then tasked Vexa with finding Joren before Karbin could; subsequently, she resorted to The Ante . Velgor then returned to the Iron Cruiser, where Thanoth they would travel to the Spire to find The Ante. When they found him, he told them the location of the Plasma Devils to show cooperation and pointed at the one responsible for the theft, Vexa. Before the Givin could identify her by name, Velgor telekinetically forced an unlucky stray shot and killed him. Velgor then went to find Vexa before anyone else.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: After sending a broadcast to the barons, Velgor, Triova, and Silvar and his enforcers went, per the queen's suggestion, to the ancestral retreat of the Shu-Torun royalty. There, they were soon attacked by Baron Rubix 's Lava Leviathan , and Velgor used Triova' escape vessel to reach the Leviathan and dared the twins to follow him. With their flux blades, they boarded it, and from the inside, the three cut large holes that allowed the ship to flood with magma and be destroyed. Upon returning, Triova suggested that they attack Rubix next (as she had identified the ship's owner) and so, Velgor told Silvar to prepare his enforcers. In the meantime, he killed Beebox for trying to deceive him with a stranger's disintegrated body, and refused Aiolin's request to train her.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Soon enough, they carried out the siege to Rubix's delving citadel , using the Shu-Torun Loyalist/Imperial Delving Fleet 's combat drills , with Velgor heading the first wave alongside the Astarte. However, he was betrayed by Silvar, and his drill was redirected into a lithoporoite seam, where they were surrounded by Rubix's elite forces. With their outbound communications jammed, Velgor left his troops as well as droid platoons to protect the drill and had the Astarte twins follow him as to use the enemy's lines to tell the rest of the assault fleet to resume the attack. On the way there, the twins attacked him, but Aiolin saw they could not win against Velgor and destroyed the pathway between them. She was then betrayed by her brother who pushed her into the lava and fled back to Silvar; Velgor then took the dying Aiolin out of the lava and had her reveal Silvar's deceit before finishing her off.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Outside and ignoring the droids' request to dispose of Thanoth's corpse, Velgor ordered 0-0-0 and VT-1, who were joined by Zazzik and his commando droids, to return Vexa to the Sovereign or kill her as their priority orders. Velgor also made it clear to wipe out anyone else they found at the Cosmatanic Steppes to eliminate all witnesses present, ensuring that, if Vexa had told anyone about her work with Velgor, they were silenced. Velgor then departed aboard his SKREE Advanced x1, with 0-0-0 realizing he would not be taking Silvar back alive, and returned to the Sovereign . Aboard, he confronted Professor Thlu-Ry , a colleague of Silvar's, whom he threatened to learn the traitor's location in the Crushank Nebulae . Velgor took the Reckoning to the nebulae, where his crew confirmed Silvar's whale fleet was present. After ordering that Thlu-Ry be thanked and then, for fraternizing with a traitor, executed, Velgor led the assault on Silvar's fleet from his SKREE Advanced. After Silvar's flagship fired an ion pulse to disable the Reckoning and moved to escape, Velgor fired into the whale ship and crashed into the opening he'd made, boarding the enemy ship just before it jumped to

title: Xarn Velgor
text: traitor, executed, Velgor led the assault on Silvar's fleet from his SKREE Advanced. After Silvar's flagship fired an ion pulse to disable the Reckoning and moved to escape, Velgor fired into the whale ship and crashed into the opening he'd made, boarding the enemy ship just before it jumped to hyperspace Moving past the personnel he'd left to be sucked into hyperspace and entering the labs, Velgor was confronted by Voidgazer, who pitted him against a cyberanimate rancor as a test of her technology just as Silvar's fleet arrived at Kuat. Although the creature gave him some difficulty, Velgor killed it by throwing his flux blade through its skull, severing the neural link, and turned one of Voidgazer's defense droids against her, fatally wounding her. As she lay dying, Voidgazer revealed that she had tampered with the Sovereign ' s systems to incapacitate the crew; Velgor finished her off and went to the empty bridge, which had been abandoned by Silvar and Morit as they had fled in the escape pods, to find that Silvar's flagship was to collide with the Sovereign . Before it did, he ejected and landed on the Sovereign ' s outer hull, where he soon encountered Morit. He easily killed him and then made his way to the Sovereign ' s bridge, where he confronted Silvar. The scientist simply disabled Velgor's cybernetics with a device he had kept for twenty years, forcing Velgor to kneel and drop his flux blade.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: was dead, Velgor used his flux blade to impale Silvar, who was astounded that Velgor was moving while his suit was deactivated. Thus, Velgor had regained the ship from his control. The Dark Lord then informed his master of his success. The Emperor then ordered Velgor to finish his mission then return to him, stating there was much to discuss. Velgor took control of his SKREE Advanced, flying into Silvar's command ship. After cutting his way through Silvar's forces, the Dark Lord found his way to the doctor's replication room. After destroying Silvar's spare bodies, Velgor made it to the command bridge. Velgor then confronted the doctor one last time. He mind-tricked the whale-ship into flying into a nearby star, destroying Silvar once and for all. After returning to the Sovereign , Velgor met with his master, whom had been awaiting a full report, only to reveal it was no longer needed because Vexa was present: while 0-0-0 and VT-1 had successfully brought Vexa to the Sovereign and were planning on giving Velgor suggestions on how to kill the doctor, should they have found his planned execution too boring for their tastes, Vexa realized Velgor's priority order only mandated the droids bring her to the Sovereign . As she realized as such and was dragged away by two shock troopers to await Velgor's wrath, she gave a new priority order: help her escape. Reaching Mal's chamber, Vexa told Mal all of Velgor's secret missions and plans, although she did chose to leave out the details surrounding Joren Drayden.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Instead of being angry with Velgor, however, the Emperor was pleased with his apprentice's ability to operate in the shadows, stating he was everything he could have hoped for. The Emperor then left his apprentice to deal with Vexa as he pleased. Velgor then ordered Vexa to follow him. Despite her pleas for a quick death, he forced her out the airlock, although she secretly survived; having deduced Velgor would never honor her wish to avoid execution via airlock, she was rescued in time by Zazzik, 0-0-0, and VT-1. Making his way to the bridge, the Emperor informed him that Grand General Targ was to be demoted and that command of the Sovereign and the fleet would be transferred to Velgor, who Mal named supreme commander of the Imperial fleet . The Emperor then left his apprentice to "educate" his subordinates of this new era. Velgor then executed Targ and ordered Admiral Kendal Ozzel to have the ship ready in two weeks. Velgor then thought of his son, content that he would soon have him.

#### Slaying the unworthy

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Soon after, Velgor was contacted by Kreel and informed that Astra-9 had told them everything they needed to know and that they could not get him to stop talking. Velgor then told him that the droid was a piece of worthless junk and to dispose of him. Shortly after, Bolt-3 managed to infiltrate the Iron Cruiser where Astra-9 was held and broke the droid out. Velgor was notified of this and intercepted their Vector in his SKREE advanced. Bolt-3 knew they could not escape alone and sent out a distress call to their friends. To Velgor's frustration, Bolt-3 gained the support of Joren, the Corsair Wing and the Volt Cobra , who gave enough covering fire to help them all escape.

#### Confronting Kreel

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Sometime later, Velgor approached Kreel, who was training with half a dozen training droids . Velgor told him he could try all he wanted but he would never become an Umbra. Kreel said he was not asking to be, saying that it was not an Umbra who saved him from the pits of Chagar IX , but the 501st Legion. Claimed to be a shock trooper to the core and that he was just appreciating the value of a flux blade. Velgor then took his flux blade and threatened to get rid of him and his squad for failing him aboard the Harbinger . Kreel told Velgor that if he failed him again, he would kneel down to Velgor and bury that flux blade in his chest himself, after killing his men with it. Velgor gave Kreel a mission to destroy a possible insurgent outpost on Horox III , bringing back Joren if he was present. Velgor then handed back Kreel's flux blade and told him to be worthy of it. Mal then entered the room and summoned Velgor. Kreel knelt down and in honor of Mal's presence and he thanked him. Mal then brought Velgor out of the room.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
back Joren if he was present. Velgor then handed back Kreel's flux blade and told him to be worthy of it. Mal then entered the room and summoned Velgor. Kreel knelt down and in honor of Mal's presence and he thanked him. Mal then brought Velgor out of the room. Kreel then traveled to the Horox system and destroyed the insurgent outpost there, killing all insurgents present. #### Sculpting a trap

Sometime later, Velgor was at his castle with Admiral Kendal Ozzel and General Maximilian Veers . There, he asked Ozzel of the excuses he had for the slowing progress of Imperial projects, which Ozzel blamed on the growing coalition. He argued that, although he could strike back, the insurgents were too spread out. Ozzel suggested that scrounging more worlds with constant bombardments via Velgor's new Death Squadron, but Veers intervened and came up with a theory; Veers claimed that the insurgency was like weeds, while the Imperium was like a storm; when a storm passed, weeds would bend and come out unharmed, whereas a tree could not withstand the onslaught. Until the insurgency was a solid singular unit, Veers argued, it would slip through their fingers. This triggered a memory in Velgor of when Elira Solen told Varrix: "The more you tighten your grip, the more star systems will slip through your fingers." Velgor told his subordinates that Veers made an interesting point and set out with a new strategy: give the Alliance time to gather its forces and assemble its might in one location, where they could be crushed.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Velgor traveled to Shu-Torun and approached Queen Triova in her meeting room. She was surprised at his arrival and assumed it was not on good terms. She pleaded that she had done nothing against him and that she had been a loyal servant. She then told her guards to lower their weapons. Triova asked Velgor how she could help him. Velgor revealed his plan for her specialists to mine the ruins of Embermoor. After she was to supply information to the insurgents that would be sufficient to entirely sabotage the mining efforts. Finally, she had to infiltrate the insurgency, which was trying to build a fleet, and do everything she could to help them. Velgor said to her that when they had built their armada, and before they hid it, he would show them how weak they truly were. Velgor then threatened her that he'd make Cindervale look like a dream to Shu-Torun if she tried anything. A Shu-Torun guard stepped forward and told Velgor that he could not threaten Triova like that. Triova shot him as Velgor was their honored guest. She then allowed Velgor to kill the rest of the people in the room.

#### Velgor's master stroke

title: Xarn Velgor
text: To Velgor's pleasure, Triova was successful in her mission, being able to earn Elira Solen's trust at Embermoor and helping them prompt a mass mutiny of Calavane merchant ships. As the insurgents armed their new cruisers at the Mako-Ta Space Docks , she gave Velgor the go-ahead to attack, telling him that they expected nothing. As the insurgents prepared to scatter their new fleet, their hyperrelays failed to work, rendering the cruisers immobile from the system. Velgor arrived soon after with Death Squadron and Ozzel asked Velgor if they should begin a bombardment. Velgor told him to wait, saying he sensed their fear and that it was insufficient. He told Ozzel to give them time to understand. As the insurgent fighters prepared to deploy, they realized that not only were the hanger doors not opening, but neither were the defense turrets able to fire or were their engines able to activate. This was because Solen had ensured that the cruisers were outfitted with Shu-Torun technology, meaning Triova could sabotage them. The cruisers were useless against Velgor's fleet, and Velgor ordered the nearest cruiser be destroyed. The fleet subsequently fired on General Vanden Willard's flagship Cinderfall's Hope and destroyed it with

title: Xarn Velgor
text: activate. This was because Solen had ensured that the cruisers were outfitted with Shu-Torun technology, meaning Triova could sabotage them. The cruisers were useless against Velgor's fleet, and Velgor ordered the nearest cruiser be destroyed. The fleet subsequently fired on General Vanden Willard's flagship Cinderfall's Hope and destroyed it with ease, killing Willard. Ozzel then asked Velgor of their next target, and Velgor said hope. The Star Destroyers began engaging the other Calavane cruisers, and Triova attempted to get off the spacedocks on her ship. However, insurgent forces boarded the vessel, and she was forced to escape in an escape pod. The insurgents discovered they could get the cruiser's hangar doors to open by flying a ship towards it. Bandwin Cor volunteered to do so and flew a shuttle towards the cruisers. The shuttle was reported to Velgor, but the SKREE fighters dealt with it before Velgor could make any decisions. Velgor's fleet soon destroyed another cruiser, sending it into a fireball. The Corsair Wing then arrived at the system, and Dax Karrick was told to attempt the same thing by Solen. Velgor was notified of the Corsair ' s arrival and quickly went to his SKREE advanced. Karrick flew the Corsair through the fleet and took on Skrees before flying towards General Jan Dodonna 's Republic . Velgor then engaged the Corsair and hit the ship's stabilizer, sending it spiraling. Karrick set it to manual, and Velgor prepared to fire on the Corsair when it got back on course.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Three years after the Battle of Cinderfall, Velgor was still in command of the Sovereign , under the admiralty of Ozzel, and Death Squadron. At Velgor's request, Lieutenant Commander Ciena Ree was transferred from the Reckoning to the Sovereign ; Ree believed, however, that Velgor's request had been more threat than reward, as she remained forever vulnerable to him for seeing him during Cinderfall's immediate aftermath. Obsessed with finding Joren, Velgor dispatched thousands of Viper probe droids as Project Swarm into the far reaches of space in order to find the insurgent base and, by extension, his son. Amongst the project on the Sovereign were a number of archaeological consultants, who were brought in due to the insurgency's prior history of hiding in historical sites. The archaeological supervisor, Professor Rupo Ud , secretly only saw the operation as a way to study historical sites and disliked the Umbra Lord, but he knew to stay quiet, having seen Velgor execute gifted individuals on little pretext. Imperial forces also found 0-0-0 and VT-1 on the Ring of Kafrene and installed restraining bolts on both, suppressing their memories and returning them to Velgor's service. Both were stationed on the Sovereign as interrogation specialists.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor burst through a wall into Vexa and the droids' hiding place with several snowtroopers, including members of First squad , whom he ordered to move eastward but to leave Vexa for him. However, Vexa activated a trap that unleashed a flame, which Velgor defended himself against but engulfed several surrounding troops. Contacting Bryce and ordering him to withdraw their forces, only for 0-0-0 to kill Bryce before the colonel could issue a retreat, Velgor embarked on his hunt alone despite a few snowtroopers remaining close. He tracked Vexa to the other side of another wall, which he began to cut through until VT-1 tripped another trap, separating Velgor from his troops, all of whom were soon massacred by the droid. Velgor, however, quickly freed himself from the trap and came face-to-face with Vexa, whom he demanded kneel as he prepared to cut her down. When 0-0-0 suddenly attacked, Velgor cut the droid down into several parts but was distracted for long enough that several explosive darts could hit his armor and knock him back. With Velgor trapped under the kyberite confessional, Vexa activated it and trapped Velgor within. Under the weight of the many sinners who had confessed their

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
regret when Vexa called him the "lost boy," Velgor was hit by a cord fired by Vexa, who used it to hack into Velgor's suit and contact a comms jockey on the Sovereign . Using Velgor's voice, she scared the officer and ordered him to alter and delete numerous probe droid records, which she hoped would hold back Velgor's search for Icehold by several weeks. While Vexa knew Velgor would one day find the insurgents, she was certain she had done something good and bid goodbye to Velgor, who promised he would find her again one day. While she was still terrified of him and knew he would never stop his hunt for her, Vexa left Velgor with the hope he, too, would one day "do something good" and declared he had, from a certain point of view, been the best thing that had ever happened to her. Vexa soon escaped Tython aboard one of the SKREE/rp Reaper attack landers with the remains of 0-0-0 and VT-1, both of whom would be rebuilt and dropped off by Vexa on the planet Birukay outside of Imperial notice. As Vexa made her escape, Velgor broke out of the confessional by destroying it in a burst of rage. The Imperium put out an arrest warrant for Vexa and tried to keep the damage she caused their search a secret, but the mess she left behind was set to keep Velgor from his son and the insurgents for long enough that the insurgents—Tolvan, Korin, and Klam among them—could finalize their defenses and set up an escape plan.

#### Frostmark

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Only the Corsair Wing remained at the base's hangar, but the light freighter was able to escape before Velgor could capture it. With the Alliance's forces on Frostmark in complete retreat and the various transports scattered throughout the galaxy, Velgor and his troops had secured a great victory for the Imperium. Rather than pursuing the Insurgent transports which had gotten away, Velgor redirected his Death Squadron's efforts to capturing the Corsair Wing , which had evaded Imperial forces in the Frostmark asteroid belt due to its faulty hyperrelay. Despite Vett's reservations, Velgor ordered the fleet to pursue the ship into the asteroid field, and told the Sovereign ' s crew that he wanted the freighter towed aboard and its passengers taken alive. Even though the asteroids heavily damaged the Star Destroyers, Velgor instructed every ship to sweep the field until the Corsair was found.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When the Corsair arrived, Joren was not among them, but Velgor knew he could use his friends to lure his son to Mistral. Escorted by Vark, Velgor waited for Karrick, Solen, Brevok, and Quill. Whilst waiting in the Rinetta dining room , he was barged in upon by the Lepi smuggler Jaxxon T. Tumperakki , who quickly left after the Dark Lord and the smuggler stared at each other. A team of shock troopers was then dispatched to arrest Tumperakki. When the Insurgents arrived, Velgor had them surrounded by shock troopers, imprisoned—and, in the case of Captain Karrick, tortured. Much to Quill's displeasure, Velgor altered their deal, agreeing to let Vark take Karrick and collect Grukk's bounty on him. Afterward, he inspected one of the city's carbon-freezing chambers , and deemed it adequate if crude, to freeze Joren for his journey to the Emperor, but at the danger of it being fatal, he had the facility tested on Captain Karrick.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: On his orders, Karrick was frozen in carbonite ; as he survived, Velgor handed Karrick over to Vark and ordered Solen, Brevok, and Astra-9 taken to his ship, while he awaited Joren at the facility. Once his son was separated from Bolt-3 and made his way to the carbon-freezing chamber, Velgor appeared before him, and the two dueled . Joren held his own for much of the duel, but he was ultimately no match for Velgor: as they moved to a reactor shaft and a catwalk, Joren managed to cut Velgor's shoulder, only for Velgor to slice off his right hand, which along with his old flux blade fell through the shaft.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor beckoned Joren to join him in the umbra side, but Joren vehemently refused. Velgor then told Joren that Kade had hidden from him the truth about his father, Kael Drayden, before revealing that he was, in fact, his father. Joren refused to believe the truth, but Velgor continued to tempt his weakened son, offering Joren the chance to destroy the Emperor and "bring order to the galaxy," just as he tried to do with Lira on Emberfall. He even pleaded with his son to come with him. In Velgor's ideal world, his son would have taken his hand, accepting him as his father. However, Drayden instead chose to throw himself into the shaft, possibly facing death to avoid joining Velgor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: At some point, Velgor also returned to the Imperial Palace and met with Mal, who ordered him to hunt down the remnants of the Insurgent fleet while it was scattered, believing he may be the only officer in the Imperium who could lead such a hunt despite it interrupting his quest to find his son. Unwilling to abandon that search, Velgor instead proposed they give the mission to Varrix's protégé, Ellian Zahra . Contacting her via hologram, Velgor granted her permission to return to active duty to try and redeem herself for a past failure under Varrix, making it clear she had no room to fail him and the Emperor. Shortly after the Corsair ' s escape and its vital role in the Battle at Rendezvous Point Delta-Three , Velgor chastised Zahra for attempting to destroy the vessel during the engagement, stating that while Elira Solen would be an acceptable casualty, another passenger was of value to him. Velgor further threatened consequence to Zahra should she report further of "partial success" before dismissing her.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Before journeying to Vendaxa, the Umbra Lord traveled to a cantina and confronted a man who claimed to be his son Joren Drayden. Velgor quickly found that the man was a liar, telling him that it did not matter who the man was. Because by tomorrow, no one would remember that he ever lived. Velgor then killed the impostor and told the people who were about to hire him that he would let them live. That way, they would be witnesses for what the man had done. The Umbra then stated that whoever claimed the name of Joren Drayden would also claim the crimes he had committed against the Imperium. After leaving the cantina, Velgor admonished the Imperial officer who had given him the information on the alleged Joren Drayden, telling him his information was worthless and that he had simply wasted his time.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Upon arriving on Vendaxa, Velgor was confronted by " Lira Ondar ." Ondar, revealed to be former Ondara Royal Handmaiden Sable, was briefly choked by Velgor before they came under attack by several Vendaxan land squids . Together, they eliminated the squids, allowing Sable to give her slain soldiers a proper burial. Sable also revealed her true motives; to investigate the death of her former queen. Velgor agreed to assist her in her mission so long as she obeyed him. Following Sable's guidance, Velgor returned to the planet Ondara to retrieve security recordings stolen from Ondar's quarters on Vantor. Upon entering the Naberri Lake Retreat, they were met by Gregar Typho and Tonra , who agreed to help them retrieve the stolen recordings. Taking a submarine , the four of them left for the recordings' location, while Sable expressed regret at her inability to save either her queen or Kael Drayden's mother. After surviving an attack by a colo claw fish , they reached their destination and found the recordings, which showed Sable forming the Amidalans and swearing to find and destroy their queen's murderers. She then accused Velgor of murdering Ondar himself, to which Velgor said he did before attacking the Amidalans.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: However, the fight was quickly interrupted by a sando aqua monster , which attacked Velgor and allowed the Amidalans to escape. After slaying the monster along with his death troopers, Velgor found the rest of the Amidalans in the jungles of Ondara, where they were led into battle by Ric Olié. In the battle at Lira's tomb , Velgor and his death troopers eliminated most of the Amidalans and incapacitated Olié before moving onto their next destination: the Tomb of Lira Ondar . But before they could enter the tomb, they were surrounded by Sable and other members of Ondar's surviving handmaidens: Eirtaé , Rabé Tonsort , Saché , and Dormé . The handmaidens fought bravely, but were easily defeated by Velgor, who then opened the door to Ondar's tomb. In truth, the handmaidens had known they would be unable to defeat the Umbra Lord, but instead made sure Eirtaé could tap into his armor with her staff. Doing so got Eirtaé an incomplete set of code, which the handmaidens hoped would one day get them the Sovereign ' s self-destruct codes.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
In the meantime, unaware of Eirtaé's success and ignoring Sable's protests, Velgor proceeded into the tomb and allowed ZEV-6-7 to scan Ondar's sarcophagus. The droid then discovered a med implant , which he traced back to the asteroid field Polis Massa . Upon reaching the asteroid field, they entered the Polis Massa Base and uncovered data that Ondar had been flown to the base by Orien Kade in an effort to save her life. However, Velgor and his forces were then attacked once more by the Amidalans, whom he managed to defeat once and for all. Along with ZEV-6-7, Velgor entered the base's maternity ward and allowed the droid to access the memory bank of a damaged Chroon-Tan B-Machine . He then watched a recording of Ondar speaking with Kade in her final moments of life. When ZEV-6-7 commented that Kade must have been important to her, Velgor promptly destroyed the droid in one-thirtieth of a second. The recording then ended with Ondar stating that she knew there was still good in Velgor, leaving the Umbra to mull over his wife's last words.

#### Test on Emberfall

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
by the Emperor to test his apprentice. With his new limbs, Velgor fought the assassin and bested him. He then demanded to know what his master's greater plan was before being interrupted by a distant voice. Velgor followed the voice into a cave, which Orrin trapped him inside of after stealing his flux blade. As Velgor fought his way through the cave, the voice taunted him with riddles about what he wanted and who he truly was. Eventually, Velgor reached the source of the voice; an ancient being known as the Eye of Webbish Bog . Velgor demanded the answers to his questions about his master, to which the Eye granted him an Umbra wayfinder . After leaving the cave, Velgor came upon his old Aetheri interceptor, where he was then met by Orrin and his Droid Crush Pirates .

While fighting off the pirates, Velgor cornered Orrin and knocked him out before reclaiming his flux blade. He then finished off the pirates and used their parts to repair the damaged interceptor. Once the ship was repaired, Velgor used the now captured Orrin to access the wayfinder, which showed the way to a planet called Umbrale . With Orrin trapped in a escape pod beneath the ship, Velgor flew the interceptor away from Emberfall and used a hyperspace transport ring to journey toward his next destination.

#### Finding Umbrale

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Grak named Bokku . When Orrin asked for the whereabouts of Dax Karrick, Bokku reported that he had been stolen and assured the assassin that Grukk would recover him. However, Orrin then told Bokku that he would recover Karrick himself in exchange for power. Bokku then asked Orrin if he served the Emperor, to which Orrin replied that they both served Velgor now. Velgor was then attacked by a group of Gamorrean guards, which the Umbra Lord slew with ease. Bokku quickly apologized for not recognizing Velgor and reiterated that he did not know where Karrick was. From this, Orrin determined that Grukk had likely hired someone to find Karrick and asked Bokku for their identity. Bokku expressed fear at the idea of betraying Grukk until Orrin pried into Bokku's willingness to take over the Grand Grak Council . Bokku then revealed that he had been tracking the hunters who had taken Grukk's bounty and that one crew of droids had gone in a different direction from the others. Bokku told Velgor the droids were deep in the heart of Grak Space and that it would be better to go in Bokku's barge so as not to scare them away. On their way to the droids' location, Bokku inquired as to his compensation for his assistance, to which Velgor assured him that he would be rewarded. Under the piloting of Bokku's nav droid Gak-Sixtoo , they arrived at Zee-Nine City Seven while Velgor and Orrin boarded their Vectis shuttle. But as they approached the city, their ship's engines were shut down, causing them

title: Xarn Velgor
text: for his assistance, to which Velgor assured him that he would be rewarded. Under the piloting of Bokku's nav droid Gak-Sixtoo , they arrived at Zee-Nine City Seven while Velgor and Orrin boarded their Vectis shuttle. But as they approached the city, their ship's engines were shut down, causing them to crash. After escaping the wreckage, Velgor and Orrin were confronted by the Droid Crush Pirates, who expressed shock at Orrin's service to Velgor. When Orrin claimed he had picked the winning side, the droid captain told him he had picked wrong as VX-88 revealed himself and fired upon both Orrin and Velgor. As Velgor deflected VX-88's attacks, the droid reminded his target that he had sustained damages while VX-88 himself had not. Velgor informed the droid that he had information he required and commanded him to lay down his weapons, to which VX-88 replied that Velgor would only access his information by downloading it from his severed head. Velgor went to attack VX-88, but the droid then took out a remote and used it to slice into Velgor's armor, taking control of the Umbra Lord. As VX-88 forced Velgor to hold his own blade to his head, Velgor demanded to know who had given the droid the code to breach his armor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As Velgor ordered the death troopers to transport Karrick to his flagship, Grukk pointed out that he had already laid claim to the smuggler. Moore attempted to explain the situation, but Velgor chastised her for her failure and warned her that the Emperor would hear of it. The Umbra Lord then told Grukk that he and everyone else within the Imperium belonged to the Emperor, to which Grukk feigned amusement. Velgor went on to point out that the Imperium could easily replace the Graks, while also pointing out the fear he could sense in Grukk and the rest of the attending Graks. When Bokku angrily interrupted, Velgor asked Grukk who he was, to which Grukk said that he was no one. Grukk then finally conceded and allowed Karrick to be taken with his compliments and regards to the Emperor. As Velgor approached Karrick, Lady Vessa informed him that she would not get in his way, but also still required the one million credits she was promised. When Velgor told her she was owed nothing, Vessa inquired if the Imperium was too poor or cheap to pay its debts. Out of patience, Velgor drew out his flux blade, to which Vessa

title: Xarn Velgor
text: After causing some damage to the Umbra's fighter, the pirates fell onto Drayden's Vector and quickly repaired it for him, allowing him to take off from the planet. As Velgor continued his chase while fending off the pirates, he was informed by Orrin that the Graks were going after the Imperial shuttle transporting Karrick. Velgor was then contacted by Admiral Vett, who informed him of the Graks' attack on the Sovereign . However, Velgor chastised Vett for disturbing him, claiming that the activities of the Graks were irrelevant to him. He then warned Vett that if Karrick was not aboard his flagship by the time he returned, he would require an explanation in person. Later in the fight, Vett contacted Velgor again and told him that he had appraised the Emperor of the situation. Since the Emperor considered the Imperium's arrangement with the Graks to be valuable, he wished for it to be preserved by having Velgor eliminate the Grand Grak Council. Velgor conceded to the Emperor's wishes and abandoned his pursuit of Drayden, reminding his son that he was no Aetheri, though the boy then claimed that the next time they met, he would be.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In secret, Orrin swore himself to Vessa's service after he arrived at the Assassin's Guild base, although the assassin would later claim he was acting as an Imperial double agent. Following Orrin's departure, Velgor had Varrick repaired and waited for him to awaken. Once he did, he was shocked to find himself restored to his former appearance. When Varrick asked Velgor what he had done to him, Velgor explained that he had had Varrick fixed since he would now be serving him. Varrick then realized that his heart was gone, to which the Umbra informed him that it had been removed and replaced with cybernetics, along with further upgrades to his body. Varrick attacked Velgor, but Velgor cut him in half before leaving him and telling a medical droid to put him back together. Once Varrick was repaired, Velgor, alongside Haydenn, informed him that he would be assassinating Carmine Dawn's agents within the Imperium. For if he did not, the Imperium would kill those he cared about.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: While thinking in his mediation chamber, Velgor reflected on his promise to his son on Aether Spire that they would bring order to the galaxy. Velgor concluded that his master had only brought about chaos and decided to set out on a new quest to establish order, whether or not he had his son by his side. Resolving to destroy Carmine Dawn as the first step, Velgor left with Orrin to assist the Imperium in hunting down Dawn agents on various planets, including Vincorba and Calior . While on Vincorba, they fought alongside a group of mercenaries known as the Revengers . With Velgor's crew established, Orrin commented that they would serve well as expendable assets, to which Velgor reminded him that he was expendable as well. After finishing on Calior, Velgor, Orrin, and the Revengers rendezvoused with Varrick and a few other assassins on Laecor to continue their hunt. When Varrick asked Velgor why he was there instead of leading Dark Squadron , the Umbra Lord simply told him to do as he was told. As a squad of shock troopers attempted to move a group of civilians, the civilians refused to comply, prompting the shock troopers to fire

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When Varrick asked Velgor why he was there instead of leading Dark Squadron , the Umbra Lord simply told him to do as he was told. As a squad of shock troopers attempted to move a group of civilians, the civilians refused to comply, prompting the shock troopers to fire on them. However, Velgor then jumped in to deflect their volt pistol bolts and slaughter them. When Orrin showed confusion over his master's actions, Velgor revealed that the shock troopers served Carmine Dawn. As the group carried on, Velgor came upon a statue, which the locals said was of their village guardian who was killed fighting Carmine Dawn.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Upon entering the Palace, they struck down all of the Royal Guards and aides in the Emperor's throne room, except for Sly Moore. Unfazed by this, Mal pointed out Velgor should have kept one of them alive for questioning. When Velgor asked him if they were loyal, Mal said they were loyal to strength, which Velgor showed them. However, only one of them was Carmine Dawn, meaning that Velgor's list was flawed. When Mal questioned if his apprentice already knew that, Velgor hesitated before assuring his master that he would bring him order. Velgor and Orrin then left for the Zanchal Estate to confront Baron Espis Zanchal for his loyalty to the Dawn. Upon arriving, Velgor was thanked by a pair of hostages who the Revengers had rescued from the Baron. As he returned to his shuttle, Velgor informed Orrin that the list was a plant, which Velgor himself had deduced when Orrin could only confirm that half of the names on it were Carmine Dawn. Velgor told Orrin to find out what connected every other person on the list. That way, they would find out who planted it and why.

#### Hidden enemy

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
As she claimed to Velgor that they were all dead, Tanka blasted her in the head for revenge. Velgor then realized that the Imperials had known they were coming. When Velgor asked Varrick who had sent the droids, Varrick confirmed they were from Romodi's command. Velgor then remembered that Orrin had spoken with Romodi prior to their departure. When he confronted Orrin with that fact, Orrin tried to stammer out an explanation before giving up and running away while Varrick fired at him. After stealing a spare ship, Orrin escaped from Tranchar and eventually arrived on Ondara to meet with Sable. Velgor followed the assassin in his SKREE Advanced. As soon as Orrin stepped out of his ship, Velgor revealed himself and destroyed it with his SKREE. After landing in front of Orrin, Velgor revealed he had known of his allegiance to the Dawn and gave the assassin an out by commending him for leading him to Sable, which Orrin went along with and claimed was his plan all along. As Velgor confronted Sable, he took her Carmine Dawn badge from her and claimed that he was the Dawn.

#### Recruiting Sable

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Velgor responded that Kael Drayden was dead. But Sable revealed that she had deduced Velgor's identity from his obsession with order, his investigation into Lira's death, and Lira's final words at Polis Massa. When Velgor drew his flux blade and asked Sable what she wanted, she claimed she wanted to help him achieve order. She went on to explain that when Drayden never returned to Dunemere to free his mother, she and Tonra secretly worked in her honor to free enslaved people and smuggle them from Dunemere to a colony on Gabredor III . Now, the colony was being exploited and neglected by the corrupt Governor Tauntaza , who was in league with Carmine Dawn. Sable told Velgor that if he helped her save the refugees, he would get the chance to destroy another Carmine Dawn cell and prove that Lira was right about him. To this, Velgor withdrew his flux blade and accepted Sable's proposal. He then warned her that she alone was responsible for where her path took her before they silently boarded the shuttle and left for Gabredor III.

#### Familiar faces

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When Kitster asked Velgor if they could do anything for him, Velgor told them they could do nothing. He then sensed that the surrounding land was disturbed, to which ZEV-6-7 explained that it was currently suffering from drought. When another refugee claimed things would get better once the clouds came back, Velgor said they would only get worse as they were attacked by a pack of clawed beasts. While Velgor and Sable fought off the creatures, a few of them surrounded Kitster and Wald. Velgor then leapt in and cut them down, saving the refugees. Kitster thanked Velgor as the Umbra Lord silently walked away. Sable then asked Velgor if he had seen enough and told him it was time to take out Tauntaza. However, Velgor told Sable she was not ready, since the refugees had ignored her order to stay back and put themselves in danger. He then told her that if she wanted them to live, they would have to obey her. Afterwards, Velgor had Sable don a set of Imperial equipment and recruited her into the Imperial Military under the rank of Lieutenant Commander, granting her authority over all the forces he gathered.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: However, he was then met by Tauntaza herself, wearing a suit of powerful armor. Tauntaza used the suit's arm cannon to fire at Velgor. As he blocked the beam with his flux blade, Velgor told the governor she could not contain the power she was wielding. To this, Tauntaza accused Velgor of having no control over his own power before he destroyed her arm cannon. Tauntaza then flew away as the facility exploded, leaving Velgor severely injured without any power left in his suit. Sable soon found Velgor and begrudgingly restored his suit's power, allowing them to walk back to the colony. Once they returned, they learned from ZEV-6-7 that Tauntaza had been receiving her orders from the Emperor himself. When Velgor asked Sable why she was smiling, she said she now knew why she had saved him. Returning to his fortress, Velgor healed in his bacta tank, but broke it in anger upon remembering Sable's words about the good still in him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As they returned to their shuttle, Velgor and Sable were informed by ZEV-6-7 of their next mission. Jul Tambra , the grandson of Wat Tambra, was working to overthrow the pro-Imperial regime on Skako Minor through a nationalist uprising . According to Imperial intelligence, Tambra had also enlisted pirates to blockade the planet and stockpile technology to be used against the Imperium. As such, their mission was to end the Skakoan's uprising and restore Imperial control over Skako Minor. In truth, Tambra had known he would have to face Velgor as part of his crusade. Over the course of the last six years, the Skakoan had worked to collect and reassemble droids who had been killed by Velgor, thereby allowing him to analyze their databanks to study Velgor's moves. Amongst the droids he reassembled were B1 battle droids, B2 super battle droids, and Gee-Ninety. Tambra was very confident that he would be able to kill Velgor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As Sable searched for Jul Tambra, Velgor was called to the Imperial Palace by Mal. Upon meeting with his master, Velgor was informed by Mal that the Umbra had an enemy, claiming that the recent attacks were part of a coordinated campaign of diversion. Mal then called in IVB Director Sliro Barsha to report on his current investigation. Barsha reported that his division within the IVB —the undercover criminal syndicate Zerek Besh —had learned of a rumor that the major crime syndicates were vying to obtain the Graks' long-standing arrangement with the Imperium. However, the rumor was coming from a single source: Carmine Dawn. As they walked through the Palace halls, Velgor agreed that Carmine Dawn had orchestrated the Syndicate War but pondered how deep its influence went.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Mal went on to state that they had orchestrated the other attacks as well, saying that Carmine Dawn had targeted the Umbra. He then asked Velgor about the syndicate's leader, Vessa, who Velgor fought and failed to acquire Karrick from. Velgor told Mal that while Vessa had not been a true threat to him, she was trained in Teräs Käsi and possessed a fighting style which reminded Velgor of his master's. From this, Mal and Velgor deduced that, since Vessa wallowed in the criminal underworld, she must have been trained by Vreth. Mal then concluded that Vreth must have trained Vessa to use her as an instrument of revenge and went on to ponder what else he had taught her. With the Umbra aware of Carmine Dawn's role in recent events, an alert was sent out the rest of the Imperial Military to track down the Vermillion , which made Vessa order her assets in the Imperium and other major factions to sow chaos across the galaxy to further distract the Umbra. With the Screaming Key they had stolen from Velgor, the Knights of Karrick, meanwhile, traveled to a location known as the umbra side hellscape , a location unknown

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Shortly after his departure, thiefs Kay and Riko Vess were able to steal access codes to Director Barsha's palace vault on Canto Bight . From there, Kay Vess' crew working under Barsha's brother Jaylen Vrax were able to steal a secret codex Barsha had that detailed sensitive information about almost all ranking Imperial officers. Vrax contacted Velgor and informed him of the database and his intentions to take control of Zerek Besh. They made a deal, in exchange for the codex and the coordinates to an Insurgent base on Akiva , Vrax would be given Zerek Besh. Later, Velgor ordered Barsha onto the bridge of the Revelator , where he condemned Barsha for letting such critical Imperial intelligence go. Velgor then looked to Vrax and said the Imperium had accepted his terms. He ended the call and gave up Barsha to the mercy of Vrax and his associates.

#### Finding the Fermata Vault

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor was amongst Mal's tools in the crusade to root out Dawn agents across the Imperium. During his effort to destroy the Dawn, Velgor bisected a traitorous shock trooper in an industrial environment. At one point, Velgor nevertheless returned to his castle on Emberfall, where he was called by the Eye of Webbish Bog. Upon entering the Eye's cave, the Eye showed Velgor a moment from the Replica Wars, where he, Zho, and their replicas had fought B1 battle droids, and glimpses of the future, including one of him being confronted by Ondar's surviving handmaidens. Velgor then realized that he had been lured there as a test before being attacked by Emberfallians. After killing them, Velgor claimed that the Eye had wasted his time with puzzles. To this, the Eye explained that the visions were warnings for the end of everything. When Velgor asked why he should care, the Eye reminded Velgor that he was a part of everything, but, if he refused to accept this, he could not be helped. Just as the Eye had shown him, Velgor, with his helmet slightly damaged, returned to his fortress and, after sensing a great disturbance in the umbra side, was contacted

title: Xarn Velgor
text: reminded Velgor that he was a part of everything, but, if he refused to accept this, he could not be helped. Just as the Eye had shown him, Velgor, with his helmet slightly damaged, returned to his fortress and, after sensing a great disturbance in the umbra side, was contacted by Mal to discuss the disturbance. Informed by Mal that Vessa claimed to possess the Fermata Vault, Velgor was ordered to find the artifact and kill anyone who knew of it. Mal also told Velgor about Vessa's central claim about the artifact: it contained an ancient Umbra Lord who was so powerful they had needed to be locked away. In truth, no such Umbra Lord existed; Vessa simply needed a claim that would draw both Umbra to the Cage, allowing her to lock them both into it and free the galaxy from their rule. Her initial effort to open the cage, however, had resulted in the Knights of Karrick abandoning Carmine Dawn out anger at being hurt in the attempt and out of fear of the ripple it sent out. Velgor made his way to the site of the disturbance, where he only found wreckage from the experiment. Although he was certain it was the origin of the disturbance, he deduced, due to a lack of bodies, that no Umbra Lord had been released. Velgor then returned to the Sovereign and reported his findings to Mal via its holoprojection chamber.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Velgor asked Mal if there truly was an ancient Umbra within the Cage, which Mal explained was possible: built by Vael Mornick himself, the Cage could imprison people and places outside of time and had never been used lightly. Mal further warned Velgor that, because of the urge within every Umbra to dominate others, the mere possibility was the greatest danger to everything they had built together. Amid their conversation, the two suddenly felt the Cage begin to open once more as the Archivist and her assistant, archaeologist Kho Phon Farrus , tried to use Ascendant -designed technology to focus nearby umbra side energy into it. Although Farrus shut off their technology as the Cage began to leach life energy from each of them, the experiment had carried on for long enough that Mal was able to track the disturbance to the planet they were on. With this, Mal sent Velgor to retrieve the Cage and destroy those present.

#### The Orphans

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Vessa attempted to sure up her chances by reaching out the Knights of Karrick, reminding them that they had attacked Velgor's fortress and thus would be hunted by the Umbra if they did not help her destroy Velgor and Mal. Around the same time, the Everspark artificial intelligence, created thousands of years prior for use against the Umbra by the Ascendant cult, resolved to hunt down Velgor. The AI had taken over Doctor Vexa's body to carry out its mission, further collecting 0-0-0 and VT-1 to help in its quest. When Vexa used a virus she had installed into the two droids to regain control of her body, the Spark introduced, much to Vexa's horror, their Umbra hunting mission against Velgor. By possessing Vexa, it had access to her memories of Velgor and saw how she considered the Umbra Lord a monster, but the AI believed itself ready to take on the Umbra Lord and his master. Because Vexa had once outmaneuvered Velgor, the overconfident Spark thought itself skilled enough to engage him in one-on-one combat. In fact, Vessa contacted the Spark to request its help in destroying the Umbra.

#### Destroying the Dawn

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Leading from the front, Velgor and Mal fought their way through the station. As the two Umbra could deflect volt pistol bolts with their flux blades, Dawn Squads Two and Three attempted to engage Mal and Velgor with electrified melee weapons, but both Umbra effortlessly fought through the guards. Still, Velgor toyed with one soldier until Mal ordered him to stop and simply kill them. As they journeyed closer to the Cage, they were confronted by the Everspark-possessed Vexa, who mocked the two Umbra. Velgor quickly deduced Vexa was under some kind of possession and stayed behind to deal with her while Mal carried on. Believing she could weaken him, the overconfident Spark engaged Velgor with the cortosis alloy-based Null Blade , which would temporarily shut down flux blades. To the Spark, the battle represented a chance to finally fulfill the dream of its long-dead creator, Miril , by destroying the Umbra Order, even if the battle proved too much for Vexa's body.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Shortly after, Dormé's fellow handmaidens Eirtaé , Saché , and Rabé Tonsort arrived on the planet. When Dormé insisted they go after Sable instead, the handmaidens told her they wouldn't leave her as they engaged Velgor in combat. Despite their coordination, the handmaidens were subdued by Velgor, who gave them one final chance to join him. However, Saché revealed that Eirtaé had seized codes from Velgor's suit during the fight, allowing the handmaidens to complete Dormé's sabotage of the Sovereign . Before they could destroy Velgor's flagship, which would kill thousands in the name of rescuing Sable and defeating Velgor, Velgor declared they were just as bloodthirsty as he needed them to be to join him. However, he was contacted by Vett, who showed him a transmission from Tambra. After arriving on the planet Brentaal IV , Sable had confronted Tambra while he was helping out a village of exiled Skakoans, urging him not to go up against Velgor and declaring that the Umbra Lord had only grown more dangerous since her own failed efforts on Polis Massa. She was certain that Tambra's efforts against Velgor would fail and that the Umbra Lord would slaughter the hundreds of Skakoans on

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Skakoans, urging him not to go up against Velgor and declaring that the Umbra Lord had only grown more dangerous since her own failed efforts on Polis Massa. She was certain that Tambra's efforts against Velgor would fail and that the Umbra Lord would slaughter the hundreds of Skakoans on Brentaal IV in retaliation. Unable to convince Tambra to call off his coming attack on the Skako Minor garrison , Sable shot him above his heart, keeping him alive but allowing her to take him away to a ship controlled by her and ZEV-6-7. Aboard, Tambra listened to her reasoning about the danger Velgor posed and declared that it was time to kill the Umbra Lord, capturing Sable after his rebuilt droids reached the starship. After showing Sable video footage of Velgor, Tambra sent his hologram to Velgor, in which he revealed her capture and baited him to come after him. While fully aware of the Umbra Lord's ruthlessness and not doubting Velgor's willingness to slaughter his refugee camp in retaliation, the Skakoan had come to believe that Sable was Velgor's weakness, which would finally give him an advantage over the Dark Lord. On Fedalle, realizing they would need Velgor and his forces to stage a daring rescue, the handmaidens reluctantly joined Velgor to go after Tambra, much to Orrin's annoyance. The group returned returned to the Sovereign aboard his Vectis shuttle and eventually left for Brentaal IV.

#### Corrupting Sable

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Upon reaching Brentaal IV via a Vectis -class shuttle with the handmaidens and ZEV-6-7, Velgor reflected on his last meeting with Ondar on Emberfall and how he wished it had gone, privately declaring to himself he would finally have his idealized outcome. He also saw it as a way to have his idealized version of the duel on Mistral, privately comparing the situation to him reaching out to Joren Drayden. Entering a building on-world, Velgor and the handmaidens were met by Moore, who explained with Velgor how each of the handmaidens could benefit from serving the Imperium and the Umbra Lord. When none of the four agreed to his demands, he telekinetically threw all four outside through an opening created by Tambra's forces, who had tracked down the Umbra Lord and his reluctant allies, and forced them to fight the B1 battle droid horde alone. To Velgor, the battle was a chance for the handmaidens to earn their places at his side and show them their own power. Overlooking their victory, Velgor remained silent as Moore declared it an example of their skills, which she promised would only grow under Velgor's service.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Shortly thereafter, Eirtaé discovered from one of the B1's memory banks that Tambra's command ship, in which she learned Sable was being held, was three klicks to the south of their position. However, Tambra, ignoring Sable's continued pleas that Velgor would wipe out his refugee camp if he continued, sent three platoons of B1s and a Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry to attack a civilian village , hoping it would trap his enemies into the village's canyon and let him escape with Sable. Both Velgor and Moore understood the attack was a trap, with Velgor declaring it an example of the weakness that the handmaidens would need to overcome. When the handmaidens demanded that Velgor assist them in aiding the populace, Velgor elected to use them as a distraction, effectively turning them into his pawns so he could get to and corrupt Sable, and teach them another lesson: as they fought the B1 horde, he could slip past the droids' lines, leaving the handmaidens to seize their true potential against a major enemy. Riding into battle on speeder bikes, Velgor cut down the gunship but left the handmaidens to the droids, cutting into Tambra's ship to save Sable and confront the

title: Xarn Velgor
text: He was followed by Sable, who donned a wing backpack and reached out. Both managed to grip the other's arm before tumbling into the sea, causing Velgor to lose his grip on Sable. Reflecting on Mal's declaration of power and suffering as he fell, Velgor decided he would continue inland on an island on his own, leaving Sable unconscious on the shore. Velgor left a trail of footprints and destruction in his wake, through which Sable followed him when she awoke. Velgor pushed the Handmaiden back when she approached and demanded he be left alone because of his out-of-control powers. When Sable—who called Velgor "Kael" once more in the process—offered the astronomical object as a chance for Velgor to take control of his powers and life as a whole, reasoning that he had never truly controlled his own destiny, another blast of his power ripped apart the land around her and forced her to run. Remembering moments from the past as he again reflected on Mal's offer, Velgor decided the test was no longer for himself, but for Sable: Velgor raised the confused Handmaiden into the air and gave her a choice to turn hatred into power or suffering, making

text: and forced her to run. Remembering moments from the past as he again reflected on Mal's offer, Velgor decided the test was no longer for himself, but for Sable: Velgor raised the confused Handmaiden into the air and gave her a choice to turn hatred into power or suffering, making Sable experience a vision before asking her to choose. Sable ignored the question and tried to focus their efforts to regaining control of Velgor's powers, only for Velgor to pull her close as a way of showing that the only safe place was to stand at the center of the storm. Velgor then showed Sable what he claimed to be her own desires, whereas she believed they were his, in a vision where she joined the Imperium and brought order to the galaxy by turning suffering into power. As Sable rejected the possible future and demanded to know what "Kael" wanted, a vision of one of the Handmaidens—as Saché, Tonsort, Rabé Dormé and Eirtaé were all present in the vision—tried to argue Velgor and Drayden were different, which she vehemently denied before chasing after Velgor in the vision: within the vision, Velgor appeared in the shadows of the forest where they stood, with Drayden's face visible when he turned back to her. Chasing after Velgor brought Sable into contact with visions of Ondar and Joren Drayden, which Sable took as proof that the light did indeed still exist in Velgor, before the Umbra Lord emerged and cut down both his wife and son, claiming once more the vision was

title: Xarn Velgor
text: to kill Velgor once and for all with the Vrak as a convenient excuse. Velgor, however, ordered Vett to stand his ground before re-engaging the attacking droids. Fortunately for the Sovereign ' s crew, the outside fleet was under the command of Admiral Corleque, the very same admiral Velgor had clashed with during his race to Umbrale, who delayed the order to destroy the Sovereign to instead rescue Vett and company, intending to fire on the Sovereign once his former commanding officer was clear. Corlque's rescue team, however, only succeeded in supplying the Vrak with a supply of KX-series security droids, which the Vrak used to murder the rescuers as Velgor picked off the last of the corrupted battle droids. After wiping out the last battle droids with a blast from the Zaly Shield, Velgor took a moment to recompose himself before requesting an update from ZED and Ought-Six, who were nearly finished with the failsafe. Suddenly, however, the Vrak used a surviving RA-7 series droid to taught Velgor and offer him a chance at assimilation, distracting the Umbra Lord while a spider-droid tried to drop on Velgor. After ZED destroyed the spider-unit, the Vrak attacked Velgor and his droids its KX-series droid bodies until the ZED activated the signal on Velgor's order, shutting down all droids aboard the Sovereign , including themselves. Velgor took the moment to survey the battlefield his ship had become. While Vett and his crew contacted Corleque, who expressed surprise at Velgor's survival, the Umbra Lord departed for Emberfall aboard his SKREE Advanced with the heads of ZED, Ought-Six, Arekso, and Gee-Ninety, intending to rebuild them once more. Just as Corleque tried to confirm Velgor's destination for Veldon, the

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
At another stage, Velgor, seemingly on a mission to wipe out all knowledge of his deceased wife, made his way back to Ondara, entering and destroying the lake side retreat where Ondar had once lived and that he had visited with Sable during their post-Aether Spire journey together. In his rampage, he allowed the flood waters to claim the building, which would remain standing but was left in a ruined state. Velgor then made his way across Ondara and slaughtered any who dared to invoke Ondar's memory. The people of Ondara would go onto remember Velgor as a spirit of death who had descended upon their world, with many choosing to abandon the entire segment of Ondara where the lakeside retreat stood, lest they bring back the "demon," which left the old building totally abandoned. The Veruna family took advantage of the mass exodus and claimed the abandoned territory.

### Redemption

#### Gambit in the Mossfell system

title: Xarn Velgor
text: With his designs against his master having failed, Velgor resigned himself to servitude: to Velgor, Mal was simply too powerful for him to overthrow, which the defeated Velgor felt left him no choice but to obey his Umbra Master. Velgor and Mal also plotted to turn Drayden to the umbra side; as Velgor understood the current plan, Drayden was to be turned to the umbra side as a third member of the Umbra Order, who was to be trained by Mal. In truth, however, Mal hoped to replace Velgor as his apprentice with Drayden. Velgor was eager to search for his son and believed his son had no choice but to serve the Emperor, just as he thought about himself.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Drayden then asked his two mentors whether Joren would end up alright. Kade responded, noting that it was possible, given that he had been alright thus far. For the next years, Kael's spirit, alongside Orien and Zho, continued to guide Joren.

#### Ghosts of Velgor's castle

Following the Battle of Mossfell, Velgor's castle remained standing on Emberfall, and his former servant, Vainé, was freed from the captivity the Umbra Lord had placed him into when two young Emberfallians, Tuttel and Giggek , tried to destroy the fortress. Surviving the blast but breathing in the unfiltered lava fumes of Emberfall, Vainé began to hallucinate that which he feared the most, his master; Vainé thought he was hearing the voice of Velgor and that he could help resurrect his master. After using nightmares to lure Lina Graf's crew to Fortress Velgor, Vainé began the process to restore Velgor, yet Insurgent officer Lina Graf , having realized that the servant was only hallucinating, pretended as if she was the reborn Velgor to be freed, then turning on Vainé and freeing her companions.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Around 9 AVE , after Joren Drayden and Sela Marr had met whilst the former began his Aetheri Academy, Marr engaged on a quest to find a compass that would lead to Peridea, the rumored location of Grand Admiral Vorren, in the hope of preventing the beginning of another war and the return of the Imperium. Following a duel between Marr and Baylan Skoll, the former was defeated and knocked off a cliff, resulting in her near death. However, Marr awoke in the World Between Worlds, where Kael Drayden awaited her. Drayden greeted her, though her back was turned causing her to call out in confusion. Drayden then stated that he was not expecting to see her so soon. Marr finally turned around and saw Drayden, before saying his name in shock, causing Drayden to smile. Marr once again said his name, before claiming that he looked as she remembered him. Drayden responded that she had grown old, which Marr chuckled about before stating that it was a part of life.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When Marr asked why she had come to the World Between Worlds, Drayden reminded Marr that she had lost her fight with Baylan Skoll and told her that he was there to finish her training. While Marr stated her belief that it was too late for Drayden to teach her, he asserted that one was never too old to learn. When Marr asked what her lesson would be, Drayden ignited his flux blade and attacked Marr, telling her that it was time to live or die. When Marr told her old master that she would not fight him, Drayden said that he had heard that before ; as Drayden continued his assault, Marr ignited her flux blade and defended herself. As Marr and Drayden continued their duel in the World Between Worlds, Marr held her own and suggested that perhaps her master didn't have anything left to offer her. Drayden, smiling, said that he hadn't taught her everything before slicing the platform beneath Marr, sending her falling into the depths below.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Marr awakened as a younger version of herself in a location obscured by fog. As replica troopers in Phase I armor, many of the 501st legion, ran by her, she was greeted by Drayden, now wearing armor and appearing as he did when she first met him; he confirmed that they were witnessing a battle from the Replica Wars. Marr didn't understand why they would be experiencing one of her first missions, which Drayden said was the problem; as her master headed into battle, Marr ignited her original green flux blade and followed him for answers. During a lull in the fighting, Marr found herself standing in an encampment of many injured replicas. Finding a replica on a stretcher with a bandaged head, Marr rested her hand on the trooper, who reached with his own hand.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As Marr continued to relive her past, she battled Ferrik super commandos at the Siege of Ferrum alongside replica troopers of the 332nd company. Replica Commander Vek spotted Marr, complementing her on her work before charging forward. Marr paused, surveying the battle as Drayden approached her, saying that he did not recognize the battle currently unfolding. Marr informed him that it was the Siege of Ferrum, which had occurred after the two had parted ways. Drayden proudly affirmed that Marr did well. Though Drayden explained that Marr was the culmination of Drayden's knowledge and the legacy of masters before him, Marr believed that her part of that legacy was one of death and war. Drayden asserted that both he and Marr were more than that, but Marr recalled how Kael had been more powerful and dangerous than anyone could have realized. At the mention of his fall, Drayden said that Marr had learned nothing and reminded her of the choice he had given her: to live or to die. Drayden ignited his flux blade again, revealing a red blade and yellow eyes. Marr once again attempted to refuse a fight, but Drayden pressed on, and the two dueled viciously.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Drayden kicked Marr back into the inky darkness of the World Between Worlds as his form shifted back and forth to his helmeted Umbra persona. Enraged by Marr's lack of conviction, Drayden battered down Marr with strike after strike, claiming that it was time for her to die. Marr outmaneuvered Drayden and took his flux blade, holding it to his neck; however, she dropped the flux blade into the void, saying that she chose to live. Satisfied, Drayden smiled, bowing his head as his eyes returned to their normal state, and said that there was hope for her yet. As the World Between Worlds rumbled, Drayden disappeared, and the mysterious plane slowly filled with water, enveloping Marr as she closed her eyes. Marr soon awoke back on Seatos where she was rescued by Lena Kryll's forces. Following the training, Marr considered herself ready for the upcoming conflict.

A distant galaxy

> " What is it? " " I just felt... Nothing. Just shadows in the starlight. " ―Sela Marr and Ryn Wrenna, as Kael Drayden watched over them

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Following the events of the Battle of Mossfell, Joren Drayden confirmed his father and the Emperor's death over Mossfell to the Alliance, which in turn, sent word of the battle's outcome in mass communications claiming to be the new power in the galaxy. Furthermore, in wake of the deaths of the Emperor, his top enforcer and many high-ranking officers during the battle, as well as the resulting power vacuum, the Imperium collapsed due to internal power struggles and its fragmentation into several factions. The Imperial remnant implemented disinformation campaigns, leading to only rumors being spread that both Velgor and the Emperor were dead, in some parts of the galaxy. Among those who knew the truth, there were sympathizers who tagged graffiti stencils of Velgor's helmet with the phrase "Velgor lives" beneath it, as on Tarisa and Coronet City .

title: Xarn Velgor
text: The Acolytes of the Beyond was a group of Umbra cultists and fanatics with an interest in Velgor, whom they considered to be greater than the Imperium. They purchased a flux blade they believed to be Velgor's from a Kubaz named Ooblamon , intending to destroy it and return it to him in death. Months after the Battle of Mossfell, the Acolytes organized a revolution on Coronet City, Korrath, during which they attacked a Peace and Security station in order to access a museum's basement and steal a red-bladed flux blade for unknown reasons. Another Umbra cult , the Alazmec of Winsit , established a colony in the Corvax Fen amidst the ruins of Fortress Velgor. There they revered Velgor as their Dark Lord and the galaxy's "true father" and ruler.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: One of those times, where Karrick wanted to surpass Velgor, was when he fought the Benathy—just like Velgor did years before him—to prevent them from expanding their territory. He took Ruthford , the last survivor from Velgor's battle that was still alive, with him and had a short conversation with Kristoff , the successor of the king that Velgor had killed many years ago, about how Velgor was taller and had seemed more impressive than Karrick. Following that, Karrick killed him with his flux blade. He then went on to fight the Benathy and although Ruthford suggested retreating, Karrick kept on fighting, talking to Ruthford about how Velgor also did not retreat. When the god of the Benathy, a Zyll Beast, appeared, Ruthford warned Karrick extensively and stated that he could not prove anything to a dead man. Ignoring that, Karrick took a shuttle and let the beast swallow him—killing it to Ruthford's surprise from the inside and succeeding where Velgor had failed. With their king and their god dead, Karrick had control over the Benathy and even the rather skeptical Ruthford admitted that Karrick had won the competition against his grandfather.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Karrick was also in possession of Velgor's disfigured helmet, which had been scavenged from his funeral pyre on Mossfell. A silent symbol of both the umbra side's power and its weakness, it remained within Karrick's private quarters aboard the Finalizer ; Karrick communed with it whenever he felt drawn to the light. Another object that once belonged to him—the flux blade he built after the First Battle of Pyralis, the one carried by his son until their duel on Mistral—resurfaced in Maz Oru 's possession and called to Nyla, a young scavenger from Ashden , who ended up using it to duel Karrick during the Battle of Voidfang Base and win. When Karrick changed quarters from the Finalizer to Vorr's flagship the Supremacy , he left Velgor's charred helmet behind him because he was not ready to face Velgor's "visage" until he recovered from his failure on Voidfang Base . Karrick's master, Vorr, owned a ring with obsidian taken from Velgor's castle. Captured by Graska Besadii the Elder on Dunemere and under the influence of hallucinogens, Karrick had a vision of Velgor cutting down Insurgent soldiers. Karrick admired Velgor as magnificent and asked for his help. Velgor turned to Karrick

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As Elira Solen Drayden Karrick prepared to release the last of her strength to reach her son, Beno Karrick, she allowed the voices and faces of her family to surround her. Among the voices she heard was that of Kael Drayden, whose apology she finally accepted, returning his love in a way she had never before. Drayden's voice was later heard by Nyla among the voices of many Aetheri of the past who aided her with destroying Vael Mal during the Battle of Umbrale , telling Nyla to restore the balance as he did. He and the many Aetheri used their eternal power to help Nyla bring Mal down once and for all and the balance Kael had created was maintained. Karrick, who had assumed the identity of Beno Karrick once again, sacrificed himself to save Nyla, following in his grandfather, Kael's path of redemption. While Karrick was the last of the Drayden bloodline, Nyla took on the name Drayden, and Kael was reunited with his family in the afterlife at long last.

### Aetheri of the Republic

> " What would have surprised people was how kind he was. He cared deeply about his friends, and looked out for them until the end. " ―Sela Marr As a child, Kael Drayden showed kindness and generosity, as exemplified by his willingness to risk his life in a dune race to help Sorin Vael and Lira Ondar depart Dunemere at a time of need. He made a number of friends, and his best friend was a fellow slave boy named Kitster Banai. He was not shy to express how he felt and showed a reluctance to leave those he loved behind. Indeed, Drayden had a deep-seated fear of loss, especially in regards to his mother, which Master Zho sensed when he was being tested by the Aetheri Council. This fear of loss would follow Drayden throughout his life and eventually led him down the path of the umbra side, particularly after the death of his mother, Shira, carrying sadness, anger, and guilt in his heart for years to come. He also felt that fear towards his friends, noticing when he believed that Orien was killed by the bounty hunter Rako Hardeen, leading him to the umbra side. But upon discovering that he was a ruse to prevent Chancellor Mal's kidnapping, he felt betrayed for not telling him sooner, and thus began to distrust Orien and the Aetheri.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: After he left his mother, Drayden—feeling the brunt of childhood abandonment and losing the only person who had ever cared for him before meeting the Aetheri—clinged onto anyone close to him. First, it had been Sorin Vael, but he then lost the Aetheri Master as well. Afterward, he clinged onto others in his life, like Orien Kade, Lira Ondar, and Sela Marr. Similarly, his experiences as a slave would leave him with a deep resentment towards slavers. Drayden would mostly keep these feelings to himself, very rarely talking about them, even with those he trusted, as he struggled to put his past behind him, making an effort not to think about it.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As he grew older, Drayden became cocky, reckless, impatient, willful, and cavalier, despite Kade's efforts to train him as best as he could. Confident and bold, he demonstrated a lack of subtlety, which Tor Vayne once noted, was one of the many traits his Adept, Sela Marr, had adopted from him during her younger years. Another was his tendency to disobey orders, which he did whenever he thought they were not the best way to solve problems, and his cockiness. Despite his many failings, Drayden remained selfless, willing to lay down his life for others, and showed commitment to things greater than himself—the Aetheri, the Republic, his friends, and his wife.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Similarly, his relentless determination was rivaled by none, except perhaps by that of his Adept. When Marr was missing in action and taken to the moon of Wasskah, Drayden blamed himself, believing he had failed to protect his student, and relentlessly searched for her possible location on star charts, though Tor Vayne suggested he trust in her abilities. Indeed, Marr survived and led others to safety, and, upon her return to Vantor, she told her master there was no need to apologize; she explained he had already done all he needed to, as she had used his lessons to survive. When Drayden was unsure of how to respond, she thanked him for that guidance, so Drayden responded with "You're welcome, my Adept." In some aspects, his journey as a mentor to Marr allowed him to mature and become more responsible. Drayden's emotional balance, however, was disrupted by the High Council's decision to expel Marr, when she was suspected of treachery, and her subsequent decision not to return to the Order when invited back. Though he greatly missed her, Drayden respected her wish to stay away from the Order when he sensed her aboard the Silver Angel by allowing the ship

With a penchant to show off, Drayden was a something of a maverick, though not in the same way as his late informal Aetheri Master Sorin Vael, known among the Aetheri for being passionate and impulsive. Most of his peers trusted him, and his ingenuity, although some Aetheri did consider him to have a simplistic approach to logic. The 501st Legion and its captain, Vek, considered his tactics reckless and unorthodox, but appreciated the fact that he would never risk their lives without risking his as well. Whenever Drayden, who believed a true military leader should always lead from the front, threw caution to the wind, Vek was always by his side and had full trust in his general's instincts. Overprotective and prone to jealousy, Drayden's affection for her was suspected by some of his peers and, at least, Orien Kade and Rush Korvex knew for certain that he was attracted to her. Sela Marr also came to realize her master and Ondar had formed a relationship, and Vek knew for certain, with Drayden trusting his captain to look out for passerby's as he spoke with Ondar.
