These fears and resentments were further fomented by Mal's manipulations, and some of the Council's (and Kade's) decisions, as well as his friendship with Chancellor Mal, of whom the Council was wary and kept secrets from. Kade and the Aetheri Council not standing with Sela Marr during her trial angered him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Alternatively, Kade levied the blame for Drayden's fall at Drayden himself, although Kade had endured a long period of blaming himself. For ten years after their duel on Emberfall, Kade blamed himself for Drayden's fall and apologized to his former disciple after their duel on a barren moon. Velgor, however, rebuked Kade and took credit for "killing" Kael Drayden, trying to believe that the Aetheri Knight he had once been was dead. Finding himself able to move on after Velgor's comment, Kade noted how Drayden had all the tools needed to choose the path of the light but made the conscious decision not to. He reminded the spirit of Sorin Vael that, no matter what level of fault each of them held, the final decision had been Drayden's alone. All the same, Kade greatly missed his friend. Velgor himself was filled with rage and despair after his conversion into a cyborg upon realizing that, indeed, the fault was all his own: it was his own choices that had led him to his new reality.

### Dark Lord of the Umbra

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Embracing his Umbra duties after that point, Velgor was angered to discover that aspects of the light side would still appear to him in his meditations, manifesting as bright blue butterflies that he attempted to swat away. Velgor also discovered that he held contempt for most beings who surrounded him on a daily basis, as they were mere subordinates whom he could not clash with as worthy opponents. His hatred was so great that his Master was forced to warn him to keep it in check, warning him that, if left uncontrolled, he would become a mere tool of his own rage. From the perspective of the Wardens he trained, however, Velgor was already a master of the umbra side, whom they were to fear, respect, and learn from. When the Thirteenth Warden first encountered Velgor, she felt as if his mere presence sucked the air from the room and ushered her towards certain death. Immediately, she understood that she had no hope of defeating Velgor in real combat and regarded him as a unholy monster birthed from her own nightmares. While being around Vael Mal made her want to run away, Velgor's presence threatened to drown her as if

The Thirteenth Warden once claimed that Velgor did not need a reason to kill people and would just do so as it suited him. However, according to an Imperial captain who worked with Velgor, the Umbra Lord was always violent but would "mature" over the years. Velgor at first simply murdered those who annoyed him. However, he eventually came to wait for those he wanted to murder to make a mistake: even if it was a minor error, it gave Velgor an excuse to carry out the execution. Indeed, over the years since his fall to darkness, Velgor developed a new, more hardened and disciplined persona. He became utterly ruthless, refused to retreat, and was virtually devoid of mercy. Even though he once thought to himself that his master's punishment of the most loyal Imperials only hurt their efforts to establish order, Velgor was known to occasionally kill his own officers for their failures. The fear felt by members of the Imperial ranks was so great that some chose death rather than face the wrath of the Umbra Lord. title: Xarn Velgor
text: Eventually, the identity of Velgor in the Imperium had arisen tales of a dark armored humanoid who served as the Emperor's most trusted enforcer and was considered to be the most feared individual in the Imperium. Rumors circulated that he lived in a castle in a world of lava and that he wielded a red flux blade, suggesting a connection to the Umbra. The few who had interacted with him stated that they were unsure whether the individual behind the armor was a living person, a droid or a replica trooper. Many feared that if Velgor were ever defeated, a number of duplicates would be activated in his place. The Umbra Lord also had absolutely no qualms about using torture to accomplish his goals. Velgor also had a distaste for those who betrayed the Imperium, such as when he accused Elira Solen of being a traitor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Considered to be the Imperium's first terror weapon and noted to employ antiquated diction, he was tenacious and unstoppable, and made most Imperial naval officers uncomfortable. Even Admiral Firmus Vett, whose highly skilled abilities as a wartime officer kept him alive in Velgor's service, was not above being threatened with death by the Dark Lord. When Vett warned him of the Vrak droid infection, Velgor's only response was to critique Vett for thinking he would repeat the admiral's failings. Contrary to the rocky relationships he had with most Imperial officers, his rapport with his shock troopers mirrored in many ways his former persona's relationship to the Republic's replica troopers. In fact, his standing with the rank and file was such that it was known as far as Selvara that the shock trooper corps "almost worshiped him." Additionally, Velgor commanded the absolute loyalty of his servant, Vainé, who remained stationed at his castle on Emberfall and knew Velgor viewed himself as a monster.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: The Thirteenth Warden was unsure of what Velgor would do with himself once there were no more Aetheri to hunt, to which Tualon Veyra theorized that Velgor would keep himself busy and simply find new people to kill. Indeed, Velgor was eager to test his skills against opponents who posed some degree of challenge, such as surviving Aetheri. However, as the Aetheri Purge continued and more and more Aetheri were killed, Velgor was forced to look elsewhere to test himself, even recruiting Wilhard Varrix to hunt him as a test of his own abilities. When the Grand Warden informed Velgor that so many Aetheri had been killed that any remaining survivors would need to reveal themselves, necessitating them to wait for a new Aetheri to emerge, Velgor displayed feelings of aimlessness and frustration. He was forced to look elsewhere to find a challenge, culminating in him igniting his flux blade against the Thirteenth Warden and Veyra, something he excused by accusing the former of treason against himself and the Emperor. He was also aware that the Thirteenth Warden and Veyra had developed a romantic relationship, which he regarded as a weakness.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: During his first days as an Umbra, he claimed that his actions were justified, stating that the Umbra were on the right side while the Aetheri to be the real evil, as he told Kade during the Duel of Emberfall. As he grew older and lived within his suit, he claimed that he still believed in justice, claiming to be a devout believer in Imperial propaganda to bring order to the galaxy. Indeed, Velgor would become known as the Dark Lord of order. However, how much he actually believed in the quest to establish order was debatable. During the manhunt for pacifist scientist Galen Arsa , Velgor questioned the term peace, seeing violence as the true creator of order and dismissing pacifists as fools who failed to see that. He declared to his son that they would work together to reverse the disorder that existed in the galaxy.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: During the war with Carmine Dawn, Velgor held contempt for his master's failure to establish order, thinking to himself that Mal's actions had only created the chaos they found themselves in. Even without Drayden by his side, Velgor set out on a new quest to bring order to the galaxy. During his campaign to root out Carmine Dawn infiltrators in the Imperium, Velgor saw it as a way to bring about order. Even though he thought the Emperor punishing the most loyal of the Imperium as everything else collapsed to be a problem that had made chaos, Velgor allowed loyal Imperials to be executed if it meant Dawn agents would also be killed. When asked why by his agent Orrin, Velgor declared it as part of his quest to bring order back to the Imperium by destroying the chaos of the Dawn. When his agent Sable declared the end of Jul Tambra's revolution as a path to peace on Skako Minor, Velgor was silent for a moment before correcting her, telling her it was more correct to say they were bringing order. However, Sable would ultimately come to believe Velgor was, in all truth, not interested in establishing order, pointing

text: Jul Tambra's revolution as a path to peace on Skako Minor, Velgor was silent for a moment before correcting her, telling her it was more correct to say they were bringing order. However, Sable would ultimately come to believe Velgor was, in all truth, not interested in establishing order, pointing out during the final stages of the Schism Imperial crisis that his current quest for personal power had only brought about chaos. As an Umbra Lord, Velgor drew power from his anger and pain, raging at the loss of his wife and unborn child, his betrayal by the Aetheri, and Kade for his injuries. He once razed a villa in a Mapuzo town entirely to draw out Kade. He often used pressurized meditation chambers that allowed him to remain without his helm—the neural connection to his armor—during which he felt the perpetual pain that Kade had inflicted on his flesh. During such sessions, he would meditate to use this pain to feed his hate, which in turn fed his strength, and he never laughed. Claiming not to feel regret, and yet haunted by his past, and the screams of his wife, he was determined to never talk about his old life, and detested all that reminded him of his past self, whom he deemed to be weak. He dared not remember such a period of his life, which he hated; indeed, through the use of the umbra side, he kept his memories as Kael Drayden buried, although it took great effort even after twenty years of practice.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Upon his fateful reunion with Sela Marr, Velgor expressed no desire to rekindle the bond he once shared with her, boasting that he had "killed" Kael Drayden, just as he had said to Kade. Although he claimed he would spare her and work alongside her once more if she helped the Imperium find any hiding Aetheri, he cruelly resolved to kill her when she refused his offer, and he spurned her offer of compassion. During a mission with Grand Admiral Vorren, who had met and befriended Drayden during the Replica Wars, Velgor repeatedly declared that Drayden was long since dead, eventually forcing the Chyrr officer to admit the man he had befriended during the war was gone. Upon hearing Vorren admit as such, Velgor declared they were never to speak of the man again, although Vorren stated he would always carry Drayden's memory with him, befitting his philosophy that someone was never truly gone if a friend remembered them.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
His love for Joren also challenged his loyalty to the Emperor. Velgor began to distrust him, feeling like another pawn in his game. He planned to kill him to take his throne, considering himself best a ruler alongside Joren. His concern over being a pawn of Mal ended up being validated when Mal tried to replace him with Joren, much like when he replaced Varek with Velgor. Velgor became surprised when he sensed that he was not the father of one child but two when he telepathically sensed his daughter, Elira, through Joren. Before dying, Drayden told Joren to tell Elira that he was right about him as he wanted his daughter to remember him as a good person in the end. Smiling at his son, Drayden then died in peace.

### Relationship with Lira Ondar

> " The thought of not being with you— I can't breathe. […] You are in my very soul, tormenting me. […] " " We can't. It's… just not possible. " " Anything is possible, Lira, listen to me. " " No, you listen! We live in the real world. Come back to it. […] If you follow your thoughts through to conclusion, it'll take us to a place we cannot go—regardless of the way we feel about each other. " " You're asking me to be rational. That is something I know I cannot do. " ―Kael Drayden and Lira Ondar

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Drayden had first met Ondar when she posed as a handmaiden and commoner at Waddu's shop in Port Vail. There, Drayden asked if she was an angel. He was then surprised when Lira revealed herself to be the Queen. Ten years later, Drayden met with her at apartment following an assassination attempt on her. As Drayden continued to protect Ondar from further attempts, he tried to impress her and flirt with her in ways he later cringed at. However, the mistakes he and Ondar made during that time revealed who each truly was to the other, and Ondar fell in love with him. They admitted their mutual love to each other on Ondara and, following the Battle of Pyralis, married in secret.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: During the Replica Wars, Drayden and Ondar rarely saw each other due to their duties requested of them during the war as well as keeping their marriage secret. Drayden would rescue and protect Ondar from numerous dangers such as General Skarn, the Zyll Beast, and the Blue Shadow Virus. Drayden also felt jealous towards Ondar's close friend, Senator Rush Korvex of Scipio. Despite Ondar's assurances that it was over between her and Korvex, Drayden felt uneasy when she accepted the Aetheri Council's mission to spy on Korvex. After leaving Cato Geltaria, Drayden assured Ondar that he never doubted her. Later, however, Drayden did not completely trust Korvex with Ondar. Drayden attacked Korvex when he tried to kiss Ondar, but Ondar thought they should not see each other for a while. When Korvex appeared to have rejoined the Dissidents, Drayden led his forces and personally attempted to rescue Ondar.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
During his duel with Kade after his fall to the umbra side, Drayden proved to be equally matched with his former master, and was only defeated when Kade exploited his hubris and blinding rage to dismember him. Drayden was considered by some amongst the Aetheri, such as Brenn Aldric, to have been the greatest warrior that the Order had during the Replica Wars, with the only possible exceptions being Zho and Drevan Koss. His former Adept, Sela Marr, once acknowledged Drayden as someone powerful who rarely lost his battles.

Drayden was particularly skilled in Form V —both the Shien and Djem So variants. He was able to deflect not only volt pistol fire with ease, but also shots from freighters. He made good use of Djem So's strength-based strikes and counterattacks to overpower or overwhelm his opponent. Drayden also used Jar'Kai on some occasions: He used Kade's flux blade during his first duel with Count Varek on Pyralis, he wielded Barris Ovva's own flux blade against her along with his own, and he wielded Varek's flux blade in addition to his own to execute him after defeating him on the Invisible Hand .

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
### Other skills

> " I can fix anything. " ―Kael Drayden

Even at a young age, Drayden demonstrated a great aptitude for piloting, mechanics, and engineering. He rebuilt the protocol droid Astra-9, an advanced droid fluent in over six million forms of communication, as well as a functional dune racer. Although during his adulthood, he would rarely use his talent as a mechanic, he kept the skill of repairing technology. Velgor had displayed great power in hunting and exterminating the Aetheri Order, leaving his later efforts against enemies like Carmine Dawn to require far less effort. Once most Aetheri had been killed, Varrix believed that Velgor was actively searching for stimulating opponents to challenge himself.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: After becoming Velgor, he remained an exceptionally skilled pilot, as shown when he single-handedly almost destroyed Ember Squadron in a lone SKREE Advanced x1, easily out-flying their entire fleet and forcing their command to abandon ship. He also obliterated several Alliance squadrons during the Battle of Vrogas Vas. Despite this, Drayden would occasionally be shot down during his combat piloting career, with Sela Marr once proclaiming they always crashed when he flew, although Drayden had a habit of blaming whatever ship it was he was flying. Although he mainly used flux blades, Drayden was extremely proficient at the use of volt pistols . He also had some training on the use of staves , a skill he once taught to a Felucian village so that they could defend themselves. Drayden spoke Galactic Basic Standard , Huttese , Duskkin Trade Language , and Meese Caulf , and he understood binary and the Bith language . As Velgor, he learned the ancient Umbra tongue , and he spoke it along with his master, Mal.

text:
### Development

> " What drove me to make these movies is that this is a really interesting story about how people go bad. In this particular case, the premise is: Nobody thinks they're bad. They simply have different points of view. This is about a kid that's really wonderful. He has some flaws—and those flaws ultimately do him in. The core issue, ultimately, is greed, possessiveness—the inability to let go. Not only to hold on to material things, which is greed, but to hold on to life, to the people you love—to not accept the reality of life's passages and changes, which is to say things come, things go. Everything changes. Kael becomes emotionally attached to things, his mother, his wife. That's why he falls—because he does not have the ability to let go. " ―Orin Vask

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In order to keep the "big secret" of Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium under wraps from potential film spies, Vask actually used a diversion technique: actor David Prowsko was instructed to say, "Orien killed your father" during filming. Later, James Earl Jonis ' voice was dubbed in, revealing the actual truth of Velgor's progeny in the famous line, " I am your father." The only ones who knew this big secret were the writers, Mark Hamill (who was told in secret moments before shooting the scene), and Jonis. There have been claims that Orin Vask took the name "Kael" from his friend and fellow film director Ken Annakin. However, Vask denied this via his publicist following Annakin's death in 2009.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In Fury of the Umbra , Kristano briefly wore the Velgor suit, which the costume department specifically designed to fit his body. The actor had a difficult time moving around in the suit, and it was extremely rigid. When he told Vask about this, the director suggested that wearing the suit should feel very mechanical and unnatural. His stand-in double for the UK shoot was Christian J Simpson , who also played alongside the young Drayden in Episode I as Bravo Six , Lt. Gavyn Sykes . The few lines of the suited Velgor speaking are of Jonis, but at one time, there was some debate over this. Some fans believed that he did not participate at all, since his name does not appear in the credits of Fury of the Umbra , and the voice heard in the first trailer for the movie was Kristano's, albeit altered digitally. The matter was settled with the Summer 2005 issue of Starlog , in which producer Rick McCallum stated they had Jonis for a partial day of work on Fury of the Umbra .

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor returning would be highly scrutinized. Eventually, it was decided that Velgor would appear in the series and he would be played by Kristano again. Writer Jovet Harlo thought it was important to have Kristano be a part of the project because he was a massive part of the character. Harlo said that the whole crew made it a priority to handle Velgor with as much care as possible "to honor one of the greatest villains and antagonists in the history of entertainment." When Harlo was writing Velgor, he wanted to trump Velgor's scene in the ending of Renegade One: A Aetherion Story . At one point, Velgor was a lot more extreme, though Harlo got pulled back a little bit. For the scenes on Mapuzo, Harlo decided that Velgor had to express his feelings in action to reveal the character beneath. During the writing process, Harlo thought of having Kade learn that Kael Drayden survived their duel on Emberfall to get the series to a place of intense drama for Kade. He first had to ask Aetherion lore advisor Pablo Hidra how much Kade knows during the show's time period, and Harlo was given permission to use the scene. Harlo had Kade and Velgor duel in the series because he found that there was no line in a First Dawn that said they could not. Harlo said the key to the duel on Mapuzo and Velgor is feeling and articulating the range and anger under it all. He also wanted to find ways to feel the rivalry between the characters and to define the opportunities that are present in the fight.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In the fall of 2019 , director Deborah Chova went to Kristano's farm to make her pitch in person. Chova talked about the project and her vision for it. She promised that Velgor would add a new dimension that could reframe the way fans look at their duel in First Dawn . Kristano thought it sounded wonderful and was excited to return to Aetherion . When Kristano first came on the set, Chova thought it was intense to have an iconic character and that she was able to direct and film new scenes with him. When Chova became the showrunner, she championed a rematch between Kade and Velgor as Vask Pictures contemplated going that route. In March , 2020 , Velgor's return was finalized.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor was played by Kristano, Dmitrious Bistrevo , and Tom O'Connell . Kristano wore a Velgor costume that was very hot and heavy, but there was an under-layer with cooling liquid in it. Between takes, Kristano was plugged into a device that circulated the liquid and helped him cool down. Kristano said that the mechanical element made him feel more like Velgor. The costume also had tinted helmet lenses. Olga Sokolova , a choreographer and "Velgor movement specialist," made sure that Kristano moved and walked correctly in the suit. This was done because the actor wanted to stay true to how Velgor moves and how he is perceived by fans. It took Kristano nine months to gain 25-30 pounds to fit in the suit. Bistrevo wore the suit during full body shots with the helmet on while O'Connell wore the suit during fighting scenes. Bistrevo spent five months of training for the role and he learned all of his lines. He said that it was dark and heavy in the suit. While on set, he used meditation to stay in Velgor's mindset. Some scenes required switching back and forth between multiple actors. Sokolova worked as Bistrevo's movement coach and consultant,

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When Kristano spoke Velgor's lines on set, he pulled aspects from James Earl Jonis' delivery and intonation. Drayden Sound hired the Ukrainian start-up company Voxcraft to artificially create Velgor's voice for the series, which uses archival recordings and a proprietary A.I. algorithm to create new dialogue with the voices of performers. Voxcraft, which also created the voice of young Joren Drayden for Aetherion: The Book of Vex Vark , was used because Jonis's voice has altered with age and he has stepped back from the role. After The Rise of Drayden , Jonis had mentioned he was looking into winding down Velgor. Matthew Wooda presented Jonis with Voxcraft's work, and the actor signed off on using his archival voice recordings to keep Velgor alive and vital even by artificial means.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Jonis is credited for guiding the performance on Orien Kade . Wooda described his contribution as "a benevolent godfather." They informed the actor about their plans for Velgor and heeded his advice on how to stay on the right course. Voxcraft finished work on the series amid the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine . While he stated the alternatives "wouldn't be as good" as Voxcraft's work, Wooda confirmed Vask Pictures's main concern was always with their wellbeing and would have pursued other options to prevent putting the Voxcraft team in additional danger, but they wanted to persevere with their work despite Russian bombardments. One synthetic-speech artist, Bogdan Belyaev, subsequently volunteered to help fellow Ukrainians displaced by Russia's war.

title: Theron Mal
text: In his public persona as Theron Mal, Mal took a great interest in politics and the public life of Ondara. In 65 BVE he was part of the officials attending the opening ceremony of the Serath power generator , with attendees noting his interest in the complex's deep-pit design. His embarkment on a career in politics was further aided by his master, who arranged for him to be raised to the position of senator for his homeworld in the Vantor Republic Senate as part of the Ondara delegation , being elected in 52 BVE . His role also made him the senator for the rest of the Chommell sector , meaning he represented a total of thirty-six planets. Once elected, Mal quickly joined incumbent Supreme Chancellor Skor Kalpana 's ruling party. He was followed by a grouping of aides who loyally followed him since his days on Ondara. He noticed the fervent bickering and corruption that mired the Republic. He began to establish relations with those who would become his future collaborators, such as Wilhard Varrix . The duo met for the first time when Varrix was still a cadet of the Garnethex Sector Spacefarers Academy , and while Mal

title: Theron Mal
text: the fervent bickering and corruption that mired the Republic. He began to establish relations with those who would become his future collaborators, such as Wilhard Varrix . The duo met for the first time when Varrix was still a cadet of the Garnethex Sector Spacefarers Academy , and while Mal was still apprenticed to Plagueis. Taking an interest in the younger man, Senator Mal resolved to help him to join the Judicial Department , according to Varrix's desire but advised him to also consider a political career. In the following years, their relationship became more and more confidential. Mal often lauded Varrix for his talents and skills and remarked they were very similar: they both came from planets at the edge of the galaxy but were destined to have great repercussions on the history of the galaxy itself. Varrix eventually became one of the few people who called Mal by his first name.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Keeping his Umbra identity a secret from the public eye while infiltrating the Senate and Republic, Mal took it upon himself to execute the Umbra's long-percolating plan of supplanting the Republic with a new Umbra Imperium , as well as destroying the Aetheri Order . In the process, he would deceive the Senate, Republic and Aetheri. In his days as a senator, Mal was known to have the backing of mysterious friends and allies who he might reference but never name; for example, even Varrix did not know who specifically worked with Mal in the shadows, even if Mal often referenced them. Trying to speculate as to who his secret supporters were, Mal's political enemies knew he had secret contacts aside from his loyal Ondara followers and the senatorial cabal he was often grouped within. Rumors swirled that shadowy organizations and figures who worked out of the public eye—including industrialists, financiers and bankers from the galaxy's most major sectors—were linked to the senator of Ondara.

#### Training an Umbra apprentice

title: Theron Mal
text: According to legend, when Mal visited Talzin, Vreth always hid in his room, afraid of the man and worried about Talzin's increasing bond with him. However, Mal one day ordered Talzin to give up Vreth to a keeper , threatening to not follow through on his promise to make her his apprentice. She reluctantly agreed, and Vreth ran into the forest angrily, overhearing the conversation from behind his door. When he returned the next morning, a Nightbrother took him and threw him in a pit, not allowing him to say goodbye to his own mother. Over the course of months, Vreth was put through relentless domestic abuse, all orchestrated by Mal as a test. With the influence of his keeper's sons beating him and the abuse, Mal' wish for Vreth came true; Vreth's perceptions, and his love for his mother eventually turned into resentment and hatred for abandoning him.

title: Theron Mal
text:
At some point while training Vreth, Mal took his apprentice to Searmark to bear witness to a great battle that had occurred there between the Aetheri and the Umbra. He forced Vreth to breathe in the ashes of Umbra warriors , slain when an ancient weapon was activated in the Umbra temple on the planet. While breathing in this ash, Vreth had visions of members of the Umbra order being struck down by the Aetheri. He felt the slash of blade after blade as he felt the death of his Umbra brethren. These visions, in tandem with his training, made Vreth long for revenge against the Aetheri Order, which had defeated the Umbra a millennium earlier. Thus motivated, Vael Vreth would serve as a powerful weapon in Mal' plans to destroy the Aetheri and restore the Umbra to galactic power.

#### Preparations and manipulation

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### Preparations and manipulation

> " Because something dangerous is brewing in our little corner of the Outer Reach. Discontent is on the rise, as are criminal enterprises and mercenary groups in the employ of self-serving corporations. In the Seswenna sector, several lommite mining concerns are vying for the attention of the Commerce Combine, which is determined to forge a monopoly in the free trade zones. Even on my own Ondara, the king finds himself embroiled with the Commerce Combine and off world bankers with regard to our plasma exports. Ours are remote worlds, but what transpires in those sectors of the Outer Reach could very well have galactic repercussions. " ―Senator Theron Mal, to Governor-to-be Wilhard Varrix

title: Theron Mal
text: In 42 BVE , Mal was introduced to Varek , an Aetheri Master , by the latter's former Adept Rael Averross , after the former Aetheri Master delivered an address to the Galactic Senate on Vantor. Following the invasion of Sireno , Varek left the Aetheri Order to claim the title of planetary count , but Mal eventually recruited Varek to the Umbra by exploiting his anger with the Republic despite also having Vreth under his wing. Indeed, Varek would not yet become an Umbra apprentice. Around the time of the Invasion of Ondara or shortly after it in 32 BVE , Mal discovered that Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen contacted the replicators on the planet Gelvaris and placed an order for a Replica army for the Republic. Realizing that this army could be used as part of his plot to destroy the Aetheri, Mal knew he needed him silenced so the Umbra could secretly take control of the army. As such, Mal ordered Varek to kill his friend. Obeying, Varek betrayed and orchestrated Dyas's death and took over his clientele for the commission of the replica army; the event was subsequently covered up when Varek erased all records of Gelvaris from the Aetheri Archives .

title: Theron Mal
text: In need of pawns for his plans but preferring a mysterious, hooded presence through holographic transmissions rather than direct communication, Mal contacted the galaxy's most powerful beings and convinced them to do his bidding with promises and threats. To that end, Mal was also able to manipulate Nutis Gunray 's rise to the position of Viceroy of the Commerce Combine . Gunray was able to arise to that position thanks to the Eriadu Conference , where an effort to end the squabbles between the Commerce Combine and Republic ended in disaster; the Nebula Front attacked the conference and successfully wiped out the Federation directorate , creating a power vacuum for Gunray to step into, while Valorum escaped and was able to secure a brief boost in popularity, with which he pushed through taxation legislation. Convincing the Commerce Combine to obey him by promising wealth, Mal odered the Federation to construct a droid army , Mal also helped the Pyralian Poggle the Lesser rise to the position of Archduke of Pyralis and controller of their droid foundries . With Mal' backing, Poggle produced millions of B1-series battle droids for the Commerce Combine military .

title: Theron Mal
text: In need of someone to lead the the Droid Army for their planned war, Mal and Varek eventually took notice of and realized the promise in Skarn , a Kaleesh warlord once known as Qymaen jai Sheelal who led his fellow Kaleesh warriors in the war against the neighboring and technologically superior Yam'rii species. After the Republic and the Aetheri intervened to support the Yam'rii, the Kaleesh had been punished, with hundreds of thousands dying of starvation. Mal and Varek, who had important plans for Skarn, took notice of his exploits as he became one of IGBC's most valuable resources. Also interested in how technologically advanced beings could be deployed, the Umbra offered Skarn a chance to be converted into a cyborg and hoped to recruit Skarn to command the droid armies.

title: Theron Mal
text:
After Skarn agreed to the surgeries to boost his own power and underwent his transformation over a period of time, Varek orchestrated a shuttle crash that destroyed whatever remained of Skarn's organic body. Extensive surgery performed by cybernetics experts and Pyralian biotechnicians , with assistance from medical droids, including the FX-9 surgical assistant FX-6 , was required to save Skarn's life. The operation resulted in Skarn physically being drastic changed.

#### Holding back Vreth

> " Remember that your anger is a tool. It is not your master." "No. You are. " ―Vael Mal and Vael Vreth

In 33 BVE , Mal met with Vreth in his hideout, the old LiMerge Power Building in the Works industrial zone of Vantor, to chide him on allowing Aetheri to sense his presence. Mal told his apprentice he did not care about his impatience, warning Vreth that ruining his master's long-term plans would have severe consequences. Mal then sent Vreth to deal with a group of pirates harassing their secret mining facilities in the Kellux system . Mal was secretly testing Vreth's loyalty by setting him up with the opportunity to face an Aetheri Adept . Vreth proceeded to unwittingly follow the path laid out for him and slew the Aetheri. After his apprentice's return to Vantor, Mal revealed his knowledge of all of Vreth's actions, asking if his apprentice was satisfied with having killed an Aetheri. Mal was pleased when Vreth replied that he was not.

title: Theron Mal
text:
learned the value of patience since rage alone was not enough for he and and his master to defeat the combined might of the Aetheri Order. Pleased, Mal pointed out that a combination of patient planning with the power granted by the umbra side would, in time, see them successfully destroy the Aetheri. #### Meeting with the Aetheri

> " Why this shade of blue?" "There's no accounting for taste. I sometimes wonder what it would look like in red. " ―Adi Gallia and Theron Mal

Around this time, Mal met, as he frequently did, with Chancellor Valorum and Aetheri Masters Zho and Adi Gallia to discuss diplomatic matters of relevance to the Republic and the Aetheri Order. One item of interest were the labor strikes on Garqi and Chamble ; for the latter, Mal suggested that the Aetheri stage a training mission there. Another topic was how to handle a shipment of garish boots sent by the new member world Hafernia as a gift for the Order. Gallia was uncomfortable at the idea of accepting them, stating that Aetheri did not endorse products. Mal replied that they did endorse the Republic and good governance. Ultimately, the group decided that the Order would accept the boots in name only.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Gallia was then briefly called away to speak with Aetheri Master Sorin Vael . When she returned, Mal handed her a datapad outlining the actions he and Valorum had proposed thus far. Before rejoining the main conversation, the two covertly discussed their aesthetic disagreement with the deep shade of blue that Valorum had chosen post-reelection, with Mal wondering what the room would look like in red. Shortly after, Mal and Valorum became aware of the Aetheri Council 's plan to visit Kwenn and contacted Master Drevan Koss to discuss the matter.

#### Eliminating a pawn

> " You are old. Too old, to be of much further service to the Aetheri—or me. And besides, my interests have changed." "What do you mean?" "The pieces are almost in place for the grand game. The Republic, the Commerce Combine, the rest—all are poised to play their roles. It serves me to have the Aetheri Order constantly moving around, following the whims of commerce and the Senate. Shuffling forces and dividing their attention. " ―Vael Mal and Voh

title: Theron Mal
text: After the Aetheri Council's defense of Kwenn from pirate forces commanded by the Riftwalker leader Zilastra and the destruction of the Order's Sanctuary Mount outpost , Mal contacted the installation's former Seneschal , an elderly Bimm named Voh , by holocomm. Mal had, in the guise of Senator Mal, made an arrangement with Voh to maintain the Senate's interest in Kwenn, such that the Aetheri kept the outpost open, in exchange for Aetheri texts from its library that Mal considered important. They had also agreed that anything Mal was not interested in would be destroyed to help obscure the fact that they were missing. However, Mal discovered that Voh had instead sold off the remaining material, unable to bring himself to eradicate historical documents; and that during the Council's time on Kwenn, Master Etha Korrin had discovered items were missing from the library and located some of the minor ones in a local shop . When presented with this, Voh argued that the evidence of the theft was gone with the outpost and that he could finagle his way into a position at another outpost and continue supplying Mal with Aetheri works.

title: Theron Mal
text:
However, Mal was not interested in continuing to deal with Voh and stated as much. The Umbra Lord explained to the confused Bimm that he was no longer interested in Kwenn, in fact that he was pleased to see the Aetheri closing outposts and moving around the galaxy in a reactionary manner, all of which would benefit plans he would soon put into effect involving the Republic and the Commerce Combine. Mal stated that Zilastra's scheme had impressed him and that she would be of further interest, although he was not surprised that she had ultimately failed in her endeavor against the Aetheri. The Umbra Lord also pointed out that Voh was too old to be of much further use to himself or the Aetheri. When the bewildered Bimm asked why Mal had so radically changed his attitude and why he was telling him all of this, Mal replied that it was for another being's ears, indicating his apprentice Vael Vreth, who had entered the room and proceeded to deal with the former Seneschal.

title: Theron Mal

#### The Senate

> " Enter the bureaucrats, the true rulers of the Republic, and on the payroll of the Commerce Combine, I might add. This is where Chancellor Valorum's strength will disappear. " ―Theron Mal, to Lira Ondar

While waiting for Ondar to reach Vantor, Mal found he had little to do, although he made sure to go to the Senate to vote on its current matters, even though he did not care for them. With nothing else to do, Mal took to looking through his catalogue of art, having run out of space in his office to store the rest of his collection. He stopped his scrolling when he saw a black statue known as the Yonta Prime , which, despite being one of his favorite pieces, he found he could not fit into his office without looking careless. He resolved to take it out of storage, ordering it to be taken to his apartment , so he could place it into the Supreme Chancellor's office when his current plan had finished.

title: Theron Mal
text: Despite these setbacks, Mal was able to convene with Ondar on Vantor , where she intended to plead her case to Chancellor Valorum before the Galactic Senate. Bringing Ondar to his apartment for an audience as part of his plan, Mal told the queen that the senate was long past caring about the common good, while Valorum was essentially powerless against them. With both the Senate and Valorum closed off to her as options, Mal offered her two choices: she could move for a Vote of No Confidence in Chancellor Valorum, and push for the election of a more effective leader; or she could take the matter to the courts, which would take even longer. Hoping still to reach some resolution to the matter in the Senate, Ondar opted to attend the special session of the body the next day.

title: Theron Mal
text: During the awaited Senate session, Ondar attempted to make her case for Republic intervention to stop the Commerce Combine's occupation of her world. However, the Federation representative Lott Dod fervently objected to the "accusations" levied against the Federation, citing that there was no proof that an invasion or occupation had even occurred. He recommended that a commission be sent to Ondara to ascertain the truth of the situation, a motion that was seconded by the senator from Malastare , Aks Moe . Vice Chair Mazan Veldon conferred quietly with Valorum for a few moments, and Mal took the opportunity to further manipulate and deceive the Queen by predicting that the Chancellor, shackled to Senatorial procedure at the behest of bureaucrats who were more than likely on the payroll of the Federation, would fail to help Ondara. When Valorum reluctantly admitted that the Federation was within their rights to request a commission, an outraged Ondar realized that Mal was right; Valorum was too weak and ineffectual to provide her world with the help it needed. As such, she took Mal's deceptive advice and publicly moved for a Vote of No Confidence in the Chancellor, unknowingly falling for Mal's plot and giving

title: Theron Mal
text:
commission, an outraged Ondar realized that Mal was right; Valorum was too weak and ineffectual to provide her world with the help it needed. As such, she took Mal's deceptive advice and publicly moved for a Vote of No Confidence in the Chancellor, unknowingly falling for Mal's plot and giving him what he wanted. Having learned of Vael's death, Count Varek traveled to their meeting place, the LiMerge Power Building in the Works, to confront Mal, infuriated that his ally's schemes had resulted in the death of his former apprentice.

title: Theron Mal
text: As Varek accused Mal of making him betray everything and everyone he had known, Mal affirmed that Varek's actions had been in the service of a greater good, and the galaxy required sacrifices in order to be remade. Varek pondered that Sorin Vael could have been a powerful ally, in which Mal acknowledged the truth, conceding that it would have indeed been advantageous for Varek. Despite everything Varek has done for him, Mal admitted that he always questioned his loyalty, much to Varek's disturbance. Defending his commitment, Varek pointed out that he had carried out every task entrusted to him. Mal then revealed that even greater demands lay ahead if they were to achieve their goals.

title: Theron Mal
text: Unbeknownst to them, Yaddle had followed Varek in secret, and urged Varek to surrender and help her defeat Mal. Varek hesitated initially but then, on Mal' orders, engaged Yaddle in a flux blade duel as a final test of loyalty. In spite of Yaddle's great effort, Varek's unrivaled dueling capabilities quickly began to overwhelm her. Yaddle called out to Varek, admitting that the Aetheri High Council had been wrong and informing him that as a result, she had stepped down from her position on the Council. Her last attempt at persuading Varek failed as he push Mal' H-2 executive shuttle , and they dueled once more, as Mal watched and cackled manically.

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### Preparing for war

> " They said Master Sifas Dyen placed an order for a replica army at the request of the Senate almost ten years ago. I was under the impression that he was killed before that. " ―Orien Kade, to Drevan Koss and Zho regarding the Gelvarians

Over the next ten years, Supreme Chancellor Mal amassed a favorable reputation as a mild-mannered servant of the common good, and the public remained oblivious to his true, insidious persona. He kept one of his flux blades hidden in a statue of Sistros Nevet , which was coated in neuranium and thus protected from scans, while the other was kept in an unknown hiding place. As Kael Drayden grew older, his relationship with Mal deepened; on many occasions, Mal lauded Drayden as the most gifted Aetheri he had ever encountered, one who would surpass even Zho, the Grand Master of the Aetheri Council. Drayden, who grew increasingly frustrated with the strict lifestyle of the Aetheri under his master Kade's guidance, appreciated Mal's praise and greatly took to his counsel. In truth, this was all part of Mal' plan to gain Drayden's trust and groom him into his eventual Umbra apprentice.

title: Theron Mal
text: However, Mal was well aware that his plan to turn Drayden to the umbra side could not bear fruit for many years to come, and with Vreth presumed dead, Mal needed an apprentice in the interim. As such, he turned to Varek to fill that role, making the former Aetheri his interim apprentice under the name Vael Varek, although the latter was unaware that he was just a temporary apprentice. Mal and Varek gained control of a behavioral modification biochip that Sifas Dyen wanted instilled in each replica as a safeguard against rogue Aetheri , and the two then reprogrammed the chip for Mal' purpose. Subsequently, bounty hunter Garrick Vark was hired as the genetic template for the replica army on Gelvaris, and the replicas were fitted with the Umbra's reprogrammed biochip, the latter containing a protocol that would ensure their total obedience to Mal when the time came for it.

title: Theron Mal
text:
In 26 BVE , Mal sent Varek to Garnethex to negotiate with the SoroSuub Corporation . Varek soon reported back that an Aetheri Knight was present on the planet. Uncertain as to what the Aetheri's purpose there was, Mal told his apprentice to uncover the reason for his presence and to keep the Aetheri from discovering the alliances Count Varek was forging on behalf of the Umbra, ostensibly for Sireno. Varek was successful in this endeavor and also covertly eliminated the Aetheri, under the guise of helping him investigate the Kaldana Syndicate .

#### Galli and the Contingency

> " You will go back to Ashden. The spot there in the dirt where my droids were operating is precious. Not just to me, but to the galaxy at large. It is significant… You will go back there and you will monitor my droids excavating the ground. Then I will send more droids and they will build something there below the ground. I want you to guard this space. Can you do that? " ―Vael Mal, to Galli

title: Theron Mal
text: In 25 BVE , Mal and his Adviser Yupe Tashu traveled to the barren Inner Reach planet of Ashden , which lay at the edge of the Unknown Regions . After landing his yacht Imperialis in the Plaintive Hand plateau , Tashu ordered a detachment of six droids to begin excavating. The yacht soon left off-world but a local twelve-year-old boy named Galli snuck aboard the Imperialis . Mal easily sensed his presence and found the boy, giving him the choice of dying or serving him. Galli chose the latter. Mal then instructed him to return to the excavation site and guard it against any intruders. He stressed that intruders should not be allowed to taint the site and ordered Galli to kill them. Mal then introduced himself on a first-name basis as Theron.

title: Theron Mal
text: As Kael Drayden grew older, the relationship between Mal and the young Aetheri greatly deepened. On many occasions, the Chancellor attended the boy's training at the Aetheri Sanctum , expressing appreciation for the progress reached by the young Adept in flux blade combat . Seeing that the boy was deeply conditioned by his emotions, Mal asked Master Drevan Koss to send Drayden to him, saying he could help with the boy's formation. When Drayden arrived in the company of his Master Orien Kade, Mal asked to be accompanied by Drayden for an errand in the lower levels of Vantor. Dismissing Master Kade's reminder that Drayden was not yet an Aetheri and dangers could lie ahead, the Chancellor brought Drayden to Level 2685 . Both disguised as travellers, Mal told the youth that he himself frequented the area when his duties permitted it—to try to do some good. Eventually, the duo arrived at Club Kasakar .

title: Theron Mal
text: There, Mal expressed some form of envy in the life of young Aetheri Adepts, that was already decided from an early age, in difference with his political life, one of troubling choices and difficult decisions. He also explained that the Club was full of Senators. In particular, he pointed out Senator Colandrus , a Tarsunt who often went there for gambling. While the Tarsunt senator was betting at a game table, Mal said that Colandrus was corrupt, but there were no proofs of it. Inspired by the unflattering description, Kael used Aetheri telekinesis to rig Colandrus' last die , making him lose large sums of money . Hearing the disguised Mal laugh at his misfortune, Colandrus sicced his bodyguard on him, but the Chancellor defused the situation by explaining that "his son" had just made a joke, and promised that they would leave at once. Still unconvinced, Colandrus nevertheless allowed the cloaked nuisances to go freely.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Mal continued to act as a confidant to Drayden, providing guidance to the young Adept who trained to become a true Aetheri. Drayden was grateful to Mal, and viewed the chancellor as a mentor as well as a friend. In private, Mal expressed to Drayden his confidence in him, including his belief that Drayden's power would eventually eclipse the combined strength of the Aetheri Order, including Grand Master Zho.

### The Replica Wars

#### Early campaigns

Dissident crisis

> " I love democracy. I love the Republic. The power you give me I will lay down when this crisis has abated. And as my first act with this new authority, I will create a grand army of the Republic to counter the increasing threats of the dissidents. " ―Theron Mal

title: Theron Mal
text: Under Mal' direction, Varek rallied several thousand solar systems into declaring independence from the Vantor Republic, instead joining the Fractio of Independent Systems with himself as its leader. The Fractio was established in 24 BVE with the Raxun Address , in which Varek blasted the Republic for its corruption and Core Reaches favoritism. Within two years, as more and more systems left the Republic to join Varek's new state, civil war seemed to be imminent and the Aetheri's numbers were too few to maintain galactic peace. Around 23 BVE , Varek's sister Jenza , who had become aware of his dealings with Mal but only knew him as "the hooded man," urged her brother to abandon his plans, warning him that Mal was corrupting him. Varek instead ordered his assassin and apprentice Kessa Vray , who at that time was unaware of Mal's existence, to kill his sister, which she reluctantly followed through with.

title: Theron Mal
text: In response to the beginning of the Dissident Crisis, the Senate passed the Emergency Powers Act , which allowed Mal to remain in office past the end of his term and remain for as long as the crisis lasted. Afterwards, Mal established the Loyalist Committee with the claim that they would act as his personal advisors, bringing in senators such as former Queen Lira Ondar, who was by that time the Senator of Ondara, Bael Solen, Ask Aak , and Orn Free Taa . As the crisis continued and the Senate grew fearful, many in the Senate pushed for a vote to create a Grand Army of the Republic , proposing the idea in 24 BVE. Keeping his true motives a secret, Mal resisted all of the Senate's attempts to create an army and the push to go to war with the Fractio. Debate over the Military Creation Act continued for a further two years.

title: Theron Mal
text: However, when it was revealed that the Dissidents were secretly building a battle droid army with the support of many commercial organizations, including the Commerce Combine. Mal used the situation to have himself granted emergency powers from the Senate by Representative Greeb Mool. With it seeming as though the Republic had no choice but to strike against the Fractio's newly discovered droid army before it was too late, the Senate, shocked by the Dissident Droid Army and scared it would attack an undefended Republic, agreed to confer emergency powers to Mal. Mal feigned reluctance to accept this authority, promising to return it to the Senate once the crisis ended. His first act was to allow the use of the replica army, which had been discovered by Kade on Gelvaris, to counter the Dissident threat.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The adoption of the replica army resulted in the First Battle of Pyralis , which served as the opening salvo of the Replica Wars . After replica template Garrick Vark was killed and his Dissident partners escaped the battle, Varek met with Mal at the Vantor tower in the Works with good news that the war the Umbra had been orchestrating had begun, as well as preliminary blueprints for a Pyralian superweapon that could be of use to their future Umbra-led regime. Mal was pleased with the turn of events, and he later, with the leaders of the Senate, oversaw the Concordat army marching towards war, while Mal additionally would be able to control and deceive both sides from the start of the war. Drayden and Ondar secretly wed on Ondara. The sole witnesses to the clandestine ceremony were their two droids, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 , and a local holy man who officiated the rite. However, the secret was unknowingly passed to Mal, which the Umbra Lord would later use during his quest to lure Drayden into becoming his next apprentice.

Converting future servants

title: Theron Mal
text:
Converting future servants

> " I enjoyed our talk, Iskat Vekkis, and I will take your thoughts into consideration. I feel certain you have a bright future ahead of you. " ―Theron Mal, to Iskat Vekkis

At some point, Mal infiltrated the Aetheri Sanctum with a number of agents, including the former Adept Heezo , ordering them to identify Aetheri dissatisfied with the Order and covertly nudge them towards the umbra side. Shortly after the mission to Thule , he met with the Aetheri High Council. On his way to their chamber , he was escorted by one such Aetheri, the Knight Iskat Vekkis . Mal took advantage of the opportunity by getting her to voice her secretly held opinions of the Order to him while subtly encouraging her darker impulses. Mal would be escorted by Vekkis to meet with the Council several more times throughout the Replica Wars.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Meanwhile, a new cropping of senators would emerge as wartime-elected representatives. This new grouping of senators were much more likely than their pre-existing counterparts to support Mal. In fact, Mal handpicked some of the senators who came into the government during the war, yet even those who had not been selected by the Chancellor would display a great reverence for the man.

After the Fractio's Droid Army seized control of the major hyperspace lanes , Mal had Varek and his assassin, Kessa Vray , kidnap the Grak Clans ' Council leader, Grukk's son, Rotto . Once they had reached Teth , Mal contacted both Vray and Varek. He assured them that the Aetheri would be at war with the Graks as well as the Fractio. As Mal, he then received a message from Grukk, asking for help in rescuing his son. Despite Master Koss's reservations about allying the Republic with the Grak, Mal knew they needed the Grak's space lanes to move their troops. Despite General Skarn spreading the Republic forces thin, Koss told Mal that Drayden and Kade could carry out the rescue.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The eruption of several new battles across the Outer Reach, including those relating the Grak endeavor, gave Mal the ability to implement a series of new secruity measures on Ondara, something that came to Senator Ondar's attention and resulted in her requesting a chance to speak with the Chancellor. During the rescue, Mal learned that Grukk believed that the Aetheri were behind his son's kidnapping and told Ondar of this when she arrived to discuss his new security plans. Grukk refused to speak with him, so Ondar decided to speak with Grukk's uncle Ziro at his palace , despite Mal's warning. Kade, Drayden, and his new Adept, Sela Marr , were able to return Rotto to his father and secure a treaty with the Graks. Following the events, Mal spoke with his apprentice about this setback. He assured Varek that the war was turning in their favor.

Gunray's capture

> " Gunray's capture could be a serious threat to us, my friend. " ―Vael Mal, to Vael Varek

title: Theron Mal
text:
Gunray's capture

> " Gunray's capture could be a serious threat to us, my friend. " ―Vael Mal, to Vael Varek

Mal learned that Senator Ondar had moved through enemy territory into the Outer Reach, causing him to contact her aboard her H-type Nubian yacht . Ondar explained that an old family friend, Senator Farr of Rodanor , had asked for her personally, as his people were starving. Mal claimed to understand, although he argued that she should have a replica trooper escort. However, Ondar had trust in diplomacy. After Representative Mool tried to talk to Mal, he caused Astra-9's chair to move, knocking the Mool down and causing the ship to veer off course. Ondar was able to regain control, but Mal discreetly urged her to keep Mool out of the negotiations, which she agreed to.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Yet once Ondar was planet-side, she learned Farr had joined the Dissidents to help his people, and she was captured by Nutis Gunray's battle droids. However, Mool helped disrupt the Dissident's plans and Farr decided to side with the Republic. Thanks to a message sent by Astra-9, the 41st Elite Corps arrived on the planet and captured Gunray. Mal contacted them via hologram, stating that Ondar had brought Rodanor's needs to his attention. The Chancellor had deployed a convoy of supply ships and stated that Gunray's capture was a major Republic victory. However, the secret Umbra Lord saw the danger Nutis Gunray's capture posed, as the viceroy would not last under the Aetheri's questioning. Contacting Vael Varek, Mal was informed by his apprentice that Kessa Vray could infiltrate the Republic warship, allowing her to rescue or kill Gunray. While Mal was apprehensive about using an agent who had previously failed them in the past, Varek argued that she was a skilled assassin. Ultimately, the master allowed his pupil to proceed in this plan; Vray successfully rescued Nutis Gunray, denying the Aetheri and the Republic the opportunity to extract secret information from the Dissident leader, whilst also demonstrating her ability to handle an Iron Cruiser 's contingent of replica troopers, an Aetheri Adept, and an Aetheri Master all at once.

Chancellor at war

> " With the final votes tallied, let it be known that the motion to stop the creation of more replica troops has failed, and the continued manufacturing of replica troopers shall proceed as scheduled. " ―Theron Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
an alert from a nanny droid told the Umbra Lord of an incoming shuttle that was approaching and it did not belong to the bounty hunter. This surprised Mal as he did not foresee this and ordered the droids to evacuate the children and destroy the facility to protect his identity and ended the transmission quickly. the Aetheri foiled Vorek and rescued the younglings . During the Battle of Malastare , the Zyll Beast was inadvertently awakened and Mal wanted the creature killed, but changed his mind when Doctor Sionver Boll and Drayden pointed out the beast's indestructible hide could prove fruitful if analyzed. The Zyll Beast was instead rendered unconscious, and transported to Vantor. It broke out of its restraints and rampaged through the Senate District before being killed with poison gas. Mal ordered Boll to replica the animal.

During the Senate hostage crisis , Cad Vorek demanded Ziro the Grak be released from prison in exchange for the hostages' release. Mal reluctantly complied after Drayden was subdued by Vorek's gang .

The following year, while the Senate was considering deregulating the banks to increase funding for the war. Mal was soon informed by Ondar that the Dissident Senate , led by Mina Bontero , was considering peace negotiations . Varek had the central power distribution grid bombed , and then staged another attack on the Fractio, which killed Bontero and was blamed on the Republic, dashing any hope of peace.

title: Theron Mal
text: Desperate, Ondar attempted to rally support for opposing a new bill but found few willing to do so. Upon further investigation, Ondar found that many of the senators who voted in support have actually been blackmailed to do so. She also discovered that supporting the bill would mean bankrupting certain segments of the Republic such as their social programs, due to the Banking Clan's high interest rates. Pursued by assassins, Bael Solen, Onacondo Farr and Ondar continued attempting to oppose the bill with Ondar stepping up in front of the Senate. In her speech, she pointed out that passing the bill would harm the citizens it was supposedly attempting to protect. Her speech marshals loud respect and support from the Senate audience. Later, Mal expressed his displeasure to Mazan Veldon, noting how the success of one individual's passionate voice can have over his power. Mal resolved to wait until fate and the Senate once more turn to favor him.

title: Theron Mal
text: When the military enhancement bill for more replica troopers was introduced, Mal claimed to be opposed to it. The bill encountered minor but effective coalition , although one of its greatest critics, Onaconda Farr , seemingly died of a heart failure before it could be voted on. Mal attended the funeral , but, in the Chancellor's office, he and others met with inspector Tanivos Exantor Divo , who revealed a poison had actually killed the senator. As the inspector left, the Chancellor claimed that murder in the Senate was unthinkable. Later, Mal and the others reunited in his office, where Divo nearly arrested the false suspect, the Gelvarian Senator Halle Burtoni . However, Ondar realized Farr's aide, Lolo Purs , was the true culprit, and the Rodanori was arrested. Soon afterward, the military enhancement bill was passed; Mal claimed to a disappointed Ondar that he too was disappointed, but that democracy needed to be respected, and stated that, with more troops, the war could possibly end more quickly.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Mal ordered Varek to ally with the resurgent Zygeran Slave Imperium , explaining past Umbra Empires were built on the backs of slaves and theirs would be no exception. They soon plotted for bounty hunters such as Cad Vorek and Rako Hardeen to "kidnap" Mal during the Festival of Light on Ondara. Kade infiltrated the plot and helped the Aetheri to prevent it, lulling them into a false sense of security. Varek showed up the evening after the festival but was defeated and forced to flee.

The next year, Vreth returned to the galaxy after a decade of hiding, with his brother Savage Opress now acting as his apprentice. The Aetheri were concerned but Mal disagreed, convincing Zho that the Dissidents should be their concern and that Vreth's vendetta was a private matter for Kade to resolve. When Vreth seized control of Ferrum , the most powerful planet in the Council of Neutral Systems , Mal realized that Vreth had grown too dangerous and was a threat to his future conquest of the galaxy. Deciding to end the threat personally, Mal had his shuttle flown to Sundari , where he confronted Vreth and Opress.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Trial of Sela Marr

> " I'm sure many of you look at this former Aetheri and think, 'Surely she cannot be this murderer or saboteur that they speak of.' And yet think of all the times we have been fooled by the Dissidents and how they have infiltrated the Republic, and ask yourself, 'Is this yet another Dissident scheme?' Another way to rip the Aetheri, and subsequently all of us, apart. " ―Theron Mal

Chancellor Mal served as the judge of the trial of Sela Marr , who was accused of masterminding a bombing at the Aetheri Sanctum. Flanked by two crimson-robed guards, he listened while Senator Ondar and Admiral Varrix made their arguments as the defense and the prosecutor, respectively. When they had finished, the Chancellor delivered a speech warning the court to beware of Dissident schemes that aimed to undermine the Aetheri Order, and by extension, the Vantor Republic, from within. Before he could announce the verdict, however, Drayden interrupted with Barris Ovva , who confessed to the crime. Mal ordered Ovva taken away, and Marr was acquitted. The ordeal left Marr disillusioned and she refused an offer to rejoin the Aetheri Order.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Manipulating and deceving two sides

> " Each day, we grow closer and closer to victory. " ―Theron Mal During the Battle of Ringo Vindra , the replica trooper CT-5385 "Tupp" suddenly faltered, becoming confused, betraying and killing the Aetheri Master Tiplar , before ultimately succumbing to insanity and dying himself. This incident was instigated by his faulty biochip, inserted into replicas for the purpose of enforcing loyalty to the Supreme Chancellor and which laid the groundwork for their execution of Protocol 66. With his plans threatened, Mal, as Chancellor Mal, had Tupp's body taken to the Grand Republic Medical Facility for autopsy. Shaak Ti and Nalle Seris brought the rebellious replica CT-5555 "Fivva" to Mal, who had uncovered the inhibitor chips implanted in each replica trooper, and believed them to be part of a Dissident conspiracy. The Chancellor informed Fivva of his involvement with the chips and had his guards stage an attack, deceitfully making Fivva look dangerous to the Republic and discrediting him. Following Fivva' death, he lied to the Aetheri that a parasite native to Ringo Vindra was responsible for Tupp and Fivva's behavior, for which all of the replica troopers would be inoculated against. Mal furthered the beneficiary opportunities from this series of events as he transferred the bulk of his Umbra artifact collection to

Varek blackmailed Korvex into raising the Republic's interest rates and sent a fleet to blockade Scipio, to which Mal responded by sending a fleet commanded by Drayden. As Scipio fell under the Republic's control and Korvex committed suicide , the Muuns ceded control of the banks to the Office of the Chancellor .

title: Theron Mal

Business on Uthara

When he learned the otherwise unremarkable planet Uthara had produced a massive kyber crystal , the world became of interest to Mal, as he wanted the large crystal for his battle station project. With the crystal in the hands of a Sulie arms dealing group , Varek agreed to a sale, claiming he wanted the crystal for the Dissident Alliance. Skarn himself arrived to oversee the deal, ultimately killing the Sulie leader, Endente , and taking the crystal to his Dissident fleet. However, after they had arrived on Uthara to investigate the death of Aetheri Master Tu-Anh , Kade and Drayden fought to stop the Dissident operation, pursuing the crystal into space and destroying it aboard Skarn's Dual Hemisphere-Omni Support Vessel . Nevertheless, Zho feared that Mal was planning to create a superweapon, and Mal remained interested in Uthara. Thus, the planet was targeted to be occupied, which would allow a crystal search to begin. Within months, the Dissidents invaded the world.

title: Theron Mal
text: The trio, however, crash-landed onto Krestophis under Republic pursuit, with the Count of Sireno suffering grievous injuries. Having sought shelter in a hidden Fractio fortress, Varek contacted a long-awaiting Vael Mal within a hologram communications chamber in seek of help, yet not before Vossa and Vray slipped in. Varek was thus forced to introduce Daren Kelv, presenting the former Aetheri as his "new assassin" to Mal, who had customarily hidden his facial features behind his dark cowl, whilst Vray remained hidden in the shadows. After expressing disapproval with his apprentice's new employ, Vael Mal listened to Varek' plea for an evacuation ship as a second battle of Krestophis ensued with Drayden leading the ruthless Republic onslaught. Giving only a vague answer, Mal ended the holo-communication as the Krestophis Dissident tower fell to Republic gunship fire. The battle resulted in an inevitable Dissident loss, and with Vray' redemption through appearing to sacrificing herself for her lover, Daren Kelv, Varek' "new assassin" chose to allow Kael Drayden and Orien Kade take him back to the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor for reassessment. Meanwhile, as the Aetheri took Vossa, a ship sent by Vael Mal arrived to retrieve Varek, letting the Dissident leader return
