Believing himself to be leaving, he, after scouting around the frozen wastes of Frostmark with Drayden under the callsign Echo Seven , had a heated conversation with Elira, claiming that she had romantic feelings towards him. After this debate, Karrick learned Joren had gone missing on patrol. Riding out on a tauntaun named Murra in the midst of snowstorm, Dax found Joren had been attacked by a frostmaw.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
After Murra collapsed and died from the cold, Dax used Joren's flux blade to cut the animal open and placed him inside to prevent him from freezing to death. After bringing Joren back to recover from his injuries, Dax and Brevok went out to investigate a signal and encountered an Imperial probe droid . Realizing the Imperium had discovered their location, the Insurgents decided to evacuate. During the ensuing battle , Dax rescued Elira from the collapsed command center, leading her towards her transport. A tunnel collapse cut off their way there, so Dax, Brev, Elira, and Astra-9 escaped on the still-unrepaired Corsair .

#### On the run from the Imperium

> " What are you doing? You're not actually going into an asteroid field? " " They'd be crazy to follow us, wouldn't they? " ―Princess Elira Solen and Dax Karrick

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### On the run from the Imperium

> " What are you doing? You're not actually going into an asteroid field? " " They'd be crazy to follow us, wouldn't they? " ―Princess Elira Solen and Dax Karrick

In space, the Corsair was pursued by several Star Destroyers and SKREE fighters. While Karrick was working on repairs, the ship drifted into an asteroid field . Claiming that the Imperials would be "crazy" to follow them, Karrick flew into the asteroid field, which would cause extensive damage to the pursuing Imperial Fleet. After the immediately pursuing SKREE fighters were destroyed by asteroids, Karrick landed the Corsair in a cave on a large asteroid, where he continued to work on repairs. While repairing the Corsair , Dax and Elira shared a kiss before being interrupted by Astra-9.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Inside the cave, Elira saw something outside the ship, so she, Dax, and Brevok went out to investigate. Discovering that mynocks were the cause, Brevok accidentally fired a shot into the cave, which caused a tremor. Karrick realized something wasn't right; he fired his volt pistol into the ground, causing another tremor. The three returned to the Corsair , flying out of the cave, which they discovered was actually the inside of an exogorth slug named Syra-O . Although Syra-O attempted to keep them inside the internal ecosystem of itself by closing its mouth, the Corsair escaped, with Karrick and the others never knowing Syra-O had loved them as friends despite their brief stay. Fleeing back towards the Imperials, Karrick flew straight towards the bridge of the Iron Cruiser Avenger , then hid on the back of the bridge. The ruse worked; the Imperials were unable to find the ship. Preparing to spread about the galaxy to search for the Corsair , the Imperial fleet dumped its trash, and Karrick detached the Corsair , which floated off with the rest of the trash. Karrick then decided to go to Aether Spire , a tibanna gas mine on Mistral run by

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Karrick was then tortured by the Imperium, but he claimed they didn't even ask him any questions. When placed in a cell, Quill arrived and told the prisoners that Karrick would be handed over to Vark, who would take him to Grukk, and that they were a trap set by Velgor for Dax and Elira's friend Joren Drayden. Angrily, Karrick attacked his "friend", but was restrained.

Velgor planned to take Drayden to his master, Galactic Emperor Theron Mal , by encasing him in carbonite . Unsure if a human could survive the process, he decided to test it on Karrick. Tearfully, Elira confessed her love to Dax, to which he simply replied that he knew. Elira, Brevok, Quill, Vark, and Velgor looked on as Dax was lowered into the carbon-freezing chamber and frozen. He survived the freezing process and fell into hibernation. He was then handed over to Vark and loaded onto Reaver One . Despite a rescue attempt by Elira, Lando, and Brev, Vark escaped Aether Spire, taking the frozen form of Dax Karrick with him.

#### Stolen by Vessa

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Stolen by Vessa

> " They all love him. Hate him. Need him. Owe him or are owed by him. Dax Karrick unites the galaxy. And that, right now, is exactly what I need. Dax always wanted to save me. Now he'll get his chance. " ―Lady Vessa, to Margo Due to the instability of the carbonite freezing process, Dax began to melt aboard Reaver One , forcing Vark to make an emergency landing on Nar Shaddaa. He met with Doc Ragon , a doctor with whom Vark had a history, and the Besalisk tasked Vark with killing Wyrmen Lictor in exchange for his help. As he fought against various pit warriors, Doc managed to halt the melting and keep Dax alive. However, he was then killed by a group of assailants who took Dax and left Nar Shaddaa. After securing Dax, they arrived at the Vermillion , where he was delivered to the reformed Carmine Dawn and its new leader, Vessa, who intended to use Karrick to lure together major galactic players for her own plans . With Dax in her custody, Vessa sent out a message to various factions in the criminal underworld, inviting them to an auction on Jekara . After delivering the message, Vessa then explained to her associate Margo that Dax was directly connected to almost every powerful faction in the galaxy. Thus, he would be useful to both her and Carmine Dawn. Still, Vessa fully intended for Karrick to end up back with the

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Rescue and marriage

#### Rescue from Grukk

Prelude

> " Over and over, he fought and risked his life and sacrificed and personally saved the entire Alliance more than once. He stayed because even if he couldn't admit it, even to himself, he believes in this cause. Dax Karrick's a smuggler because he likes it, but he's a insurgent because he's Dax Karrick. And Dax Karrick complains and jokes and is generally half-useless…but he doesn't leave. That's inspiring. He matters . To the Insurgency…and to me. " ―Elira Solen, on Dax Karrick Through her tracker, Vessa learned that Karrick had been brought to Grukk's Palace and discovered he had been placed on the Grak's wall as a decoration. Traveling to the Corsair Wing , where everyone aboard believed Karrick had died in the fall to Jekara, Vessa revealed Karrick's survival and imprisonment in Grukk's Palace. Solen agreed to wait for Vessa to confirm the time was right to launch a rescue operation, knowing she was needed with the Alliance and could not spend time on a rescue mission at the moment. Vessa promised to reach out, even arguing that Karrick would be safe in Grukk's Palace while the insurgents waged their war with the Imperium, but Carmine Dawn would be destroyed in the Battle at Amaxine Station .

Later, the Free Coalition began preparations for the mission. Elira, Brevok, and Bolt-3 sought the help of Maz Oru, but were forced into a brief skirmish with the Ubese bounty hunter Boushh . After quickly overpowering him, Elira took his clothes, helmet, and thermal detonator as a disguise to sneak into Grukk's palace.

The rescue

title: Dax Karrick
text:
The rescue

> " Victims of the almighty devourer: His Excellency hopes that you will die honorably. But should any of you wish to beg for mercy, the great Grukk the Grak will now listen to your pleas. " " Astra-9, you tell that slimy piece of worm-ridden filth he'll get no such pleasure from us. Right? " ―Astra-9, translating for Grukk the Grak, and Dax Karrick

After almost a full year in captivity, Karrick was released from the carbonite by Elira, disguised as the bounty hunter Boushh. Due to hibernation sickness, Karrick was temporarily blind, but recognized Grukk's laugh when he revealed himself to be watching the rescue. Karrick was then placed in a prison cell with his partner Brevok, while Elira was taken as a personal slave by Grukk. After Elira was captured, Joren Drayden arrived, and faced off against Grukk's prized Rancor, killing it. In rage, Grukk sentenced Drayden, Karrick, and the Vorak to be fed to the devourer in the Great Pit of Karkoon.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
At the pit, Grukk offered the prisoners one last chance to plead for mercy, to which Karrick replied that Grukk would receive no such pleasure from them. Drayden then offered Grukk one last chance to free them, which he denied. Bolt-3 then released Joren's flux blade ; Joren caught it and began a battle. In the ensuing struggle, Dax was still mostly blind, rendering him unable to contribute much. However, after being told by Brevok that Vex Vark had joined the battle, Dax unintentionally swung an axe into Vark's jetpack, sending him flying into Grukk's sail barge and then rolling into the devourer. After a volt pistol shot knocked Lando, disguised as a palace guard, off the skiff they were on, Dax lowered the axe for Lando to grab, but Quill's foot was caught by one of the devourer's tentacles. Claiming his vision had "gotten a lot better," Dax shot the tentacle and pulled Lando back up into the skiff. Joren then rescued Elira, Bolt-3, and Astra-9 from the sail barge and destroyed it, and then the insurgents escaped.

#### The Battle of Mossfell

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Aftermath of the battle

Following the battle, Karrick, Brevok, and Bolt-3 were sent by Solen to General Kryll's camp to obtain food rations for the Mosskins as a means to keep the furry creatures from making a meal out of the captured shock troopers. While at Kryll's camp, Kryll forced Karrick to admit that her ship the Wisp was superior to the Corsair in order to get the rations.

The morning after the Battle of Mossfell, Karrick led the Pathfinders on an assault on an Imperial outpost on the far side of Mossfell. Knowing that the Imperial outpost was preparing for a counterattack, the insurgent commanders dispatched Dax Karrick on a mission to destroy the base. Dax outlined a plan for the Pathfinders and their Mosskin allies to strike the outpost with limited air cover. During the assault, the insurgent pilot Lieutenant Shara Bey served as the transport's pilot. The Pathfinders quickly wiped out the garrison, and Karrick uncovered a lot of data in the outpost's computers, which led him to conclude that the war was not over.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Concordat

#### Honoring a life debt

Gathering intelligence

Before the formal establishment of the Concordat , Karrick, Astra-9, and the Pathfinders participated in a raid on an IVB black site at the Wretch of Tayron . During the assault, the Pathfinders managed to down an AT-ST walker, which caused a breach in the facility's hall. This allowed Karrick and his men to enter the base and secure the computers before the base commander could initiate a purge of the computers. With the aid of Astra-9, the Pathfinders were able to hack into the Imperial data files and discovered that the Imperium had begun to execute Operation: Cinder , a posthumous order issued by the Emperor to devastate several worlds including Ondara as retribution for his demise. The Pathfinders' actions enabled the Free Coalition to deploy forces to halt Operation: Cinder, saving many lives and worlds.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Several months after the Battle of Mossfell, Dax arrived at Maz Oru's castle on Takodana to rendezvous with an Imperial defector named Ralsius Paldora , who had stolen intelligence crucial to the liberation of Thornwood. The Imperium had quickly discovered his treachery and followed him. Recovering the data cubes and fighting their way back to the Corsair , Dax and Ralsius were saved by the arrival of Inferno Squad , buying them time to escape the planet.

False leads

> " C'mon, Brev. Set new coordinates. It's time to get you home. " ―Dax Karrick to Brevok, on the way to liberate Thornwood

Some time later, Dax and Brevok received additional intelligence from the smuggler Imra that the Vorak homeworld of Thornwood would have a decreased Imperial presence. Against the advice of his wife, Elira, the two friends gathered several fellow smugglers and people who owed them favors for a hastily planned campaign to liberate the planet. However, this turned out to be disinformation from the Imperium to lure Dax and his companions into a trap.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Finding new allies

Nevra, her son Temmin Wexlin , his battle droid Mister Bones , the Zyrrak bounty hunter Jas Emari , the former Imperial loyalty officer Sinjir Rath Velus , and the Concordat soldier Jom Barell traveled to the planet Irudiru after learning that Karrick had last been sighted at Warrin Station . There, they found Karrick while scouting the compound of the Siniteen prison designer Golas Aram . At a nearby cantina , Karrick informed his allies that he had discovered that Brevok was being held at Ashmead's Lock and that Aram was responsible for designing the prison. During their initial encounter, Karrick was accosted by Mister Bones, who mistook him for a threat.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Working together, Karrick and Nevra's team managed to breach the compound and capture Aram. Under duress, Aram told the insurgents how to enter Ashmead's Lock. However, he omitted the password that would allow them unhindered passage inside the prison. Traveling to the Thornwood system in the Corsair Wing and Emari's ship Halo , Karrick and Nevra's team gained clearance to land at Ashmead's Lock by claiming to be a repair team. Upon entering the prison, Dax and the insurgents were accosted by the prison's computer security system SOL-GDA , which dispatched droids to integrate them. Temmin discovered that the prison was being powered by the prisoners who were being housed inside stasis cells. Using this information, Dax and Nevra managed to disable the power generator. As a result, Dax and Nevra's team were able to free Brevok and a hundred other prisoners including Nevra's husband and Temmin's father Brentin Lore Wexlin . While Nevra, Temmin, and Mister Bones took the liberated prisoners back to Serenne on the Corsair , Dax stayed behind with Brevok, Jas, Sinjir, and Jom to complete their mission to liberate the Voraks. Unknown to Dax and his allies, the Imperial Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen had inserted inorganic bio-chip implants inside the prisoners as part of a plot to assassinate the Concordat leadership.

Liberating Thornwood

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Liberating Thornwood

Dax and his team learned that Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck had fitted all of the Voraks on Thornwood with inhibitor chips . Tolruck controlled these inhibitor chips with a control module which he kept on his person. For the next month, Dax and his team spent their time searching for Tolruck's island fortress and gathering Vorak exiles and smugglers for a mass uprising. On one mission, Jom Barell was captured by Tolruck's forces and imprisoned at his island fortress . While Sinjir entered the island fortress to free Jom and disabled Tolruck's control module, Dax and his team disabled the deflector shield generator at Camp Sardo . Despite being attacked by Imperial forces, Jas managed to take out the shield generator.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
After Sinjir disabled Tolruck's control module, a mass planetwide Vorak uprising broke out. The Voraks and their insurgent allies quickly overwhelmed the outnumbered Imperial garrison. When the orbiting Imperial Star Destroyers began bombarding Thornwood, Dax, Brevok, and their fellow insurgents managed to evacuate the civilians underground. They then took a ship loaded with webweaver spiders aboard the Iron Cruiser Dominion and fought their way through the ship's corridors. However, they were captured by shock troopers who brought them before Vice Admiral Domm Korgale .

Before the admiral could eliminate Dax and his team, Concordat reinforcements arrived in the Thornwood system in the form of Elira and the Corsair Wing , Rask' Phantom Squadron, and Admiral Vorian's flagship, Home One . Dax and Brevok managed to break free of their captors and seize control of the Dominion . Dax and his team then turned the ship's guns on the Iron Cruiser Vitiator . As a result, the remaining Iron Cruiser Neutralizer surrendered to Admiral Vorian.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Following the battle, Dax and Elira experienced an emotional reunion aboard the Dominion . Returning to Thornwood, Dax, Brevok, and Elira learned about the Liberation Day attacks on Serenne. With the Voraks undertaking mop-up operations against the remaining Imperial holdouts on Thornwood, Dax insisted that Brevok stay behind and reunite with his family . However, he told Brevok that he would return if he ever needed help. Dax then left Thornwood aboard the Corsair with Elira and their unborn child, Beno Karrick .

#### Balancing family and duty #### Balancing family and duty

Over the next several months leading to the Battle of Ashden , Dax Karrick and Princess Elira prepared for the coming of their child. With Elira approaching labor, Karrick hired a protocol droid named T-2LC (or "Elsie") as a nanny. One day, Karrick bought his wife a sack of jogan fruits . Elira was annoyed with Karrick for overdoing it and reminded him that Dr. Harter Kalonia had said to incorporate jogan into her diet and not to replace everything with it. While chatting with his wife about the liberation of Thornwood and galactic politics, Dax and Elira were contacted on hologram by the Concordat operative Nevra Wexlin. Nevra said that she was traveling to the Inner Reach world of Ashden to hunt down Grand Admiral Raena Vexana , the purported instigator behind the Liberation Day attacks on Serenne.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Nevra Wexlin's team subsequently discovered that most of the Imperium had retreated to Ashden. While Nevra, the bounty hunter Jas Emari, and the battle droid Mister Bones infiltrated Ashden, Temmin and Sinjir returned to Serenne with news about the Imperial presence. They visited Elira's domicile and warned Princess Elira and Dax Karrick about the Imperium. Temmin tried to convince Karrick to lend him his famous freighter, the Corsair Wing . However, Karrick thought that the mission was too risky and was unwilling to risk his ship.

Before the argument could escalate, Chancellor Vela Sess entered the domicile and asked Temmin and Sinjir about the Imperial presence on Ashden. Following the meeting, Temmin and Sinjir managed to convince Dax and Elira to lend them the Corsair Wing . However, the two were stopped from leaving Serenne by Senate Guards who had been dispatched by Senator Tolwar Wartol , a rival of Chancellor Sess. Wartol had secretly installed a listening device inside T-2LC. In an attempt to discredit Chancellor Sess, Wartol leaked news about the Imperial presence to HoloNet News . Karrick and Elira learned about the leak while watching the morning news.

#### Unmasking a conspiracy

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Unmasking a conspiracy

Dax and Elira were later confronted by an angry Sinjir, who believed that they had double-crossed him and Temmin. Dax and Elira managed to set the record straight. They then realized that Senator Wartol's leak and the Senate guards stopping Sinjir and Temmin were linked. When Sinjir voiced his suspicion that there was a spy bug in Elira's domicile, Dax did not believe it, but Elira shared Sinjir's suspicion. Sinjir brought his former lover Conder Kyl , a slicer, to Elira's domicile. Conder found that the listening device was inside T-2LC. Following the discovery, Dax told Elsie to hold still and warned that it was going to sting a little.

title: Dax Karrick
text: After removing the listening device and handing it to Chancellor Sess, Dax led a team consisting of Sinjir, Temmin, Conder, and Jom Barell to the Concordat's new capital of Nakadia . Their mission was to investigate the five senators who had opposed Chancellor Sess's resolution to send military forces to Ashden: Ashmin Ek , Rethalow , Dor Wieedo , Grelka Sorka , and Nim Tar . While Sinjir and the others trailed four of the senators at a restaurant called Izzik's in Nakadia's capital Quarrow , Dax went to spy on Senator Dor Wieedo. The Rodanori senator was aboard his ship at the northernmost spaceport outside Quarrow.

title: Dax Karrick
text: After several hours had passed, Karrick witnessed two Niktal and a Klatooinian approach Wieedo's ship. Unknown to Karrick, these aliens were members of the Red Key Raiders , a crime syndicate that was plotting with Black Sun to prolong the war. Karrick managed to warn his comrades. However, the criminals discovered his presence and locked him in a rubbish bin. Meanwhile, Conder was kidnapped by other Red Key gangsters. Sinjir and Temmin found Karrick and returned to the Corsair . Despite their setbacks, Jom managed to kidnap Senator Rethalow, who confessed to his dealings with Red Key and Black Sun.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Before they could spirit Rethalow away into hiding, Dax and his team members decided to rescue Conder, Nim Tar's child , and Sorka's pet jerba . Conder used his transceiver tooth to transmit his coordinates to Sinjir. Dax and his team flew the Corsair Wing through a red warehouse roof, which turned out to be the Red Key's base. After subduing the gangsters, they rescued Conder and Nim Tar's child. Posing as an adviser to the Chancellor, Sinjir transmitted a missive offering the five senators pardons and other political favors if they changed their votes during the re-vote scheduled to be held at the Quarrow Senate house . As a result, Sess's resolution passed, and the Concordat was able to dispatch military forces to Ashden.

#### War's end

> " Yeah. You, me, Joren. Brev. The Corsair . Those two walking talking garbage cans. It feels weird we're not part of it. " " We've got our own adventure. " ―Dax and Elira

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### War's end

> " Yeah. You, me, Joren. Brev. The Corsair . Those two walking talking garbage cans. It feels weird we're not part of it. " " We've got our own adventure. " ―Dax and Elira

Following the events on Nakadia, Dax returned home and reunited with his wife. When Elira praised him for "making things right", Karrick told her that the Battle of Ashden was happening. He predicted that it would be a big battle. In private, Dax confided that it felt strange that he, Elira, Joren, Brevok, Astra-9, and Bolt-3 were not part of the final battle. Elira reassured him that they had their own adventure. Dax responded that it was the end of an era while Elira replied that it was the start of a new one.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
The Battle of Ashden turned out to be a decisive victory for the Concordat. Facing imminent defeat, Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon on Vantor sent peace overtures to Chancellor Sess. Dax and his wife attended the peace talks where Chancellor Sess and Grand Vizier Veldon signed the Imperial Instruments of Surrender and the Galactic Concordance . The signing occurred during the third hour of Elira's labor, but she only told her husband after the ceremony was complete. Karrick rushed her to the birthing chamber in the heart of Hanna City .

Elira gave birth to a son named Beno Karrick. Following a gathering of family and friends, Dax stared into his son's eyes and pondered how he had become a father. While Elira was showering in the next room, Karrick told his son that while the whole galaxy was against them, they would still make it through okay. Though Karrick confided that he might not make a good father, he promised to keep them pointed in the right direction. Karrick also gave Beno his first lesson: sometimes doing the right thing doesn't mean following a straight line. Karrick told his baby son not to tell his mother.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Baylan Skoll's gauntlet

Around 9 AVE , during the search for Grand Admiral Vorren , the former Aetheri Knight and General turned mercenary Baylan Skoll listed Karrick's name in a device on his gauntlet, as well as the names of other key members of the Heroes of Cinderfall .

#### Starting a family

> " I'll be back. We're not done, you and I. We'll see each other again. I'm gonna be a father and no way my kid won't have you in his life. " ―Dax Karrick parting ways with Brevok

Finding himself husband of an important politician, Dax passed the time by becoming a successful racing pilot. On one occasion he returned to Korrath to compete in The Gauntlet , where he raced against Greer Sonnel and offered her a spot on his team for the Five Blades race.

In the years after the end of the Galactic Civil War, Karrick became the owner of a shipping company and developed a reputation for being a vigilant and responsible owner. Outside of his work, Dax often raced for charity and sponsored several piloting matches. Due to his work, Karrick found himself traveling through different systems, working on ships.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Twenty-four years after the Battle of Mossfell, Dax Karrick traveled to the planet Theron to manage a prestigious racing championship called the Five Blades. While staying in temporary quarters, he corresponded with Elira, who told her husband about the fractured state of the Galactic Senate. When Elira told Dax about her desire to resign from the Senate, Dax expressed puzzlement, since his wife had devoted much of her adult life to politics. Sensing Elira's frustration, Karrick invited his wife to take a break and travel around the galaxy with him for three months. Despite their different personalities, Elira agreed that she needed a break from her senatorial career.

title: Dax Karrick
text: However, Elira was forced to suspend her vacation plans after her faction, the Populists , convinced her to stand for the position of First Senator . The rival Centrist faction, which supported a stronger central government, had successfully passed a motion calling for the creation of First Senator in order to end the deadlock plaguing the Republic. Despite their initial opposition, the Populists, who preferred a more decentralized government, had decided to change tactics in order to prevent a Centrist from holding that office. Due to her prestige as a prominent former insurgent leader, Elira had reluctantly agreed to allow an exploratory committee to explore her suitability for First Senator.

title: Dax Karrick
text: While Dax was repairing the rear engines of a starship, he was contacted by his wife. Karrick was mildly disappointed with his wife's change of plans but agreed that a Populist should serve as First Senator. Karrick also informed his wife that he was supervising the lunar relays of the Five Blades. Due to the complicated nature of the repairs, Dax remarked that he wished that Greer Sonnel, a former racer and Junior Blades champion who was serving as Elira's pilot, was still on his team. When Elira apologized for delaying their planned holiday, Dax reassured her that she was doing the right thing by putting duty to the Concordat first. Elira promised to take a break with her husband "someday."

title: Dax Karrick
text: In addition to the First Senatorship, Elira was involved in a sensitive Senate investigation into the Niktal crime lord Rinnrivin Di 's cartel , a new criminal outfit that was choking the economy of the Gaulus sector . Elira was assisted in this investigation by an unlikely ally, the idealistic Centrist senator Ransolm Kastor . Over the course of their investigation, the two discovered that Rinnrivin was linked to a paramilitary faction called the Amaxine warriors . In an attempt to sow discord, Arliz Hadrassian , a former SKREE fighter pilot who had become the Amaxines' leader, bombed the Concordat senatorial complex 's conference building . Elira survived the bombing and transmitted a voice-message telling her husband that she was safe and that he did not need to come to Hosnian Prime. While on Theron, Karrick received news about the Senate bombing and saw footage of the damage. Later, Karrick contacted Elira to send his wife a goodwill message and to keep in touch.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Still determined to continue her investigation into Rinnrivin's cartel and the Amaxines, Elira and her team took leave to travel to Sibensko , where the two groups were hiding. There, Elira discovered that the Amaxines were funding Rinnrivin's cartel and were also marshaling troops, weapons, and starships for an attack on the Concordat. During her mission , Elira was pursued by the Amaxine warriors and fled up a landing platform, where she was corned by two Amaxine starfighters. Dax arrived on a racer and rescued his wife. Together, the couple shot down the enemy fighters. One of the fighters, a Bulwark , collided with the underwater base's ammunition depot, triggering a massive explosion that destroyed the underwater city and the Amaxine army.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Following the Sibensko mission, Dax and his wife returned to Elira's apartment in Hosnian Prime. When Elira expressed despair that many of her former colleagues and comrades were shunning her for simply being Velgor's daughter, Karrick reassured her that this storm would pass and that people would remember her for who she was. Dax counseled his wife to remember those friends who stuck by her and to ignore the rest of the galaxy. When Dax criticized Kastor, Elira sprung to her former friend's defense by pointing out that he was a decent man who hated Velgor. Dax then advised his wife to forget Kastor and to use the political scandal as an opportunity to retire from politics for good.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
However, Elira still had one piece of unfinished business left: the findings of her investigation into Rinnrivin Di's cartel and the Amaxines. Elira wanted to address the Senate, but she needed to gain a quorum from a majority of senators. While Dax thought that no more threats to the Republic existed with the demise of Rinnrivin and the Amaxines, Elira suspected that there were other like-minded groups seeking to overthrow the Republic. Dax counseled his wife to rest for the night, and the couple expressed their love for each other. The following morning, the sports channels reported that Dax Karrick had left the Theron system after the end of the last Blades round. There was also speculation on whether he would return for the final championship race. Later that evening, Dax bought his wife Bilbringi cheesy meat pies for dinner. While eating, the couple received news that Elira had received a quorum to address the Senate due to Kastor's favorable vote. Dax then told his wife that things would improve and that he would stay with her for as long as she needed him. Elira reassured her husband that she would be able to handle the hearing on her own and told him that he could return to the Blades championship. Shortly, Karrick returned to the Five Blades race.

### Cold War

#### Family strife

> " And Karrick… Did you know that's not even his real name? He's a lie . " ―Beno Karrick, to Vorr, about his father

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Losing the Corsair

> " Short-handed? I can help. I can be your co-pilot. " ―Gannis Ducain to Dax Karrick

In 31 AVE Karrick traveled to Maz's castle, where he spoke with Oru about Brevok being unable to do a job with him. Gannis Ducain , who worked for Oru, overheard and suggested he help on the job. The job was to deliver cargo to Krestophis . When Dax and Ducain arrived, Dax left Ducain to guard the Corsair Wing whilst he met with his contact. Ducain, however, stole the Corsair . Ducain became a rich gunrunner . One day the Irving Boys stole the Corsair from him.

After losing the Corsair , Dax and Brevok obtained a Baleen -class heavy freighter named the Eravana that they used for their smuggling operations and even assembled a crew to assist them. Dax spent the majority of his free time trying to track down the Corsair .

#### Smuggler's run

title: Dax Karrick
text:
After losing the Corsair , Dax and Brevok obtained a Baleen -class heavy freighter named the Eravana that they used for their smuggling operations and even assembled a crew to assist them. Dax spent the majority of his free time trying to track down the Corsair .

#### Smuggler's run

Sometime later, Karrick and Brevok went to the Serendipity , a yacht that was owned by Leighton. There, Karrick engaged a trio of bounty hunters— Strater , Hove , and Rigger —sent to capture him on the Serendipity cantina, and told them about their mission to Cyrkon before they realized who he was. Once they were aware of Karrick's identity, Brevok snuck behind them and took hold of Rigger, only to send him flying to the Serendipity ' s door and knock Strater out with a punch, while Karrick disarmed Bobbie. Then, the Korrathi told them to warn their possible employers (Ducain, the Irving Boys, the Guavians, etc.) that they were not afraid of them, before saying goodbye to Leighton and leaving the bar together.

#### Cindervalean data archive heist

title: Dax Karrick
text:
In 34 AVE while transporting a cargo of three Rathtars aboard the Eravana for the King Prana , Dax and Brev found the Corsair floating in space near the desert planet of Ashden, pulling his prized vessel in with a grapple beam. Upon boarding their old vessel, the two went about inspecting their ship and found two stowaways, Ashden scavenger Nyla and former New Imperium shock trooper Jax , who he assumed were the thieves who had stolen the Corsair . When Nyla and Jax explained that they were going to take a droid named Orio-6 to the Coalition as he had a map to the location of Karrick's old friend Joren Drayden, Dax and Brev agreed to help them.

Karrick rediscovered the Smuggler's Guide that was previously owned by Unkar Gruven aboard the ship, thinking it was a bad omen that this thing keeps resurfacing. However, Brevok thought it was a good luck that it keeps coming back and was happy to see the logbook and kept opening different pages. Dax thought if that was true his life would have turned out differently. These reflections were recorded in the logbook.

#### Skirmish aboard the Eravana

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Skirmish aboard the Eravana

> " What are you going to do? " " Same thing I always do, talk my way out of it. " ―Nyla and Dax Karrick

Dax's freighter had been boarded by the Guavian Death Gang and Kanjiklub, whom Karrick was indebted to. Not wanting Nyla and Jax to be involved, Dax placed both of them in the lower corridors of the freighter while he and Brev went to meet with the criminals, with Orio-6 accompanying them. The smuggler tried but failed to convince both gangs that he would fix things eventually, with one of the gang leaders threatening to take away the Corsair Wing as payback. Dax having just retrieved his vessel, responded that they would have to take it over his dead body. One of the criminals then recognized the Orio-6 unit from a New Imperium bounty placed on it along with Nyla and Jax, and demanded that Dax hand over the droid and any stowaways he might have on board. Right before a firefight broke out, Nyla accidentally released the rathtars, providing a diversion for an escape in the Corsair .

#### Journey to Takodana

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Journey to Takodana

> " She's run this watering hole for a thousand years. Maz is a bit of an acquired taste, so let me do the talking. And whatever you do, don't stare. " " At what? " "Any of it. " ―Dax Karrick, Nyla and Jax

Dax explained that Joren tried to rebuild the Aetheri Order, but an apprentice of his turned to the umbra side and became Zarrin Karrick, destroying all that Joren had built, including the other Adepts that Joren had trained. Feeling responsible and blaming himself for the failure, Joren went into exile. Dax explained that Joren tried to rebuild the Aetheri Order, but an apprentice of his turned to the umbra side and became Zarrin Karrick, destroying all that Joren had built, including the other Adepts that Joren had trained. Feeling responsible and blaming himself for the failure, Joren went into exile.

En route to Takodana, Dax reminisced about the Corsair , her corridors, fresh smell of thread grease, stale funk of the couch fabric. The way the aircycler makes the whine before it switches off and Brev's feet clomping all over the hollow deck plates. He thought about dropping the logbook off with Maz, but changed his mind. His thoughts were recorded in the Smuggler's Guide . Later on the same route, the Corsair ' s hyperrelay cut out. Nyla, Jax, and Brevok investigated and found a tracker near the sensor pulse generator . Jax removed the tracker, only to discover that it was rigged with explosives. Nyla and Brev jettisoned the tracker bomb out the airlock, while Jax informed Dax of the situation and the Corsair jumped back into hyperspace.

Scoundrel's redemption

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Scoundrel's redemption

> " And maybe she could carry on after I'm gone. Another roll of a dice. A scoundrel's redemption. " ―Dax Karrick, in the Smuggler's Guide

Karrick handed Nyla an NN-14 volt pistol pistol , knowing she would be able to defend herself with it, and asked Nyla what her name was. With the two formally introduced, Karrick said he was considering bringing on a new crew member. Impressed with Nyla's piloting and repair abilities, he said he would consider offering her a job as a second mate aboard the Corsair . Nyla was flattered by the offer and briefly excited by the prospect, but she turned it down because she had to return to Ashden to wait for her family, claiming that she'd already been away for too long already.

Takodana Castle

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Takodana Castle

Karrick took Nyla and Jax to meet his old friend Oru at her castle. There, he learned that Oru had found and kept the old flux blade that once belonged to Joren, and he asked where Oru got the weapon, but Oru dismissed him, saying it was a story for another time. While there, the New Imperium was alerted to Orio-6's presence and attacked. During the ensuing battle, he killed several shock troopers both with his DL-44 volt pistol and Brevok's bowcaster , Karrick, Jax, and Brevok were initially captured, but escaped when the Coalition, also alerted to Orio-6's presence, counterattacked. Despite the New Imperium being driven off, Dax witnessed his son Zarrin Karrick carrying away Nyla. Among his rescuers on Takodana was Dax's estranged wife, General Elira Solen. She took Dax, Brevok, Jax, and Orio-6 to the Coalition base on D'Qar .

#### Reunited at the Coalition base

> " If Joren couldn't reach him, how could I?" "Joren is an Aetheri, you're his father. " ―Dax and Elira

title: Dax Karrick
text:
> " If Joren couldn't reach him, how could I?" "Joren is an Aetheri, you're his father. " ―Dax and Elira

It is revealed that Dax and Elira are aware that their son is Zarrin Karrick, and that their son's fall to the umbra side caused them to separate, with Dax returning to his smuggling business, and Elira spearheading the activities of the Concordat and the Coalition. As Voidfang Base prepared to wipe out the world of D'Qar, the site of the Coalition's headquarters, the Coalition planned an attack of their own. Jax had given them the Base's blueprints, which revealed that the base drained the energy of the sun in order to charge its superweapon, and that it required a thermal oscillator , which sustained the energy on the planet, that, if destroyed, would destabilize the planet's core and implode the Base. However, they would need to do it before the Base fully charged its weapon. Having experience in taking down superweapons' shield generators, Karrick and Brevok volunteered to disable the shield. Before he left, Elira told Dax to find their son, and convince him to reject the umbra side and return to the light .

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Battle of Voidfang Base and death

> " I'm being torn apart. I want to be free of this pain. And I know what I have to do, but I don't know if I have the strength to do it. Will you help me?" "Yes. Anything. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Dax Karrick

Karrick, Jax, and Brev took the Corsair Wing to Voidfang Base, exiting hyperspace inside the planet's shield just above the surface and landing just at the side of a high cliff. When Jax revealed his stationing had previously been in "sanitation" and that the real reason he had come along was to rescue Nyla from the New Imperium, Karrick and Brevok agreed to help him with a bit of annoyance. While inside the base, they captured Captain Phasma and forced her to lower the shields, after which Karrick claimed that they would not leave the base without Nyla.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Legacy

> " I know what I have to do, but I don't know if I have the strength to do it. " " You do. " " Dad… " " I know. " ―Beno Karrick and a memory of his father, Dax Karrick

Shortly after the battle, Elira asked Nyla to tell her about how Karrick died, as she only had sensed it. Nyla told her that while she didn't hear what Karrick told Beno, he didn't fight nor call out, to which Elira assured her that he always knew when to run and when to make a stand. Sometime afterwards, a funeral was held for Karrick. During the evacuation of the D'Qar base , one of the proton bombs carried by Paige Holt 's bomber , Cobalt Hammer , succeeded in destroying Captain Moden Canady 's Mandator IV -class Siege Dreadnought Fulminatrix . The ordnance crew had a message inscribed on the bomb in Aurebesh , stating "Dax says hi."

title: Dax Karrick
text: It was ultimately through their bond that Nyla gained new insights into Karrick, making her aware of the conflict between the umbra side and the light within him. Unable to persuade Drayden to end his self-imposed exile, she concluded that the son of Dax Karrick was the last hope of the galaxy, and therefore went directly to Karrick in the hope of helping him find redemption in the light. Her arrival on the New Imperium Navy flagship Supremacy provided Karrick with an opportunity to assassinate his dark-side mentor, Supreme Leader Vorr. Although they worked together to kill Vorr's Praetorian Guards , Nyla was dismayed to see that Karrick did not intend to forsake his allegiance to the umbra side. Instead, he invited her to rule the galaxy with him, bringing a new order to the galaxy. When she rejected his offer, Karrick blamed Vorr's death on Nyla and claimed the title of Supreme Leader for himself.

title: Dax Karrick
text: When Drayden later projected to the planet Saltmark from Tidehollow in order to confront Karrick, he mentioned that Dax would always be with him. Before succumbing to his projection, Drayden's last words to Zarrin were, "See you around, kid," remembering Karrick even in the last seconds of his life. After escaping from the New Imperium aboard the Corsair Wing , both Solen and Brevok sat in the cockpit, where Solen remembered a young Karrick sitting in the captain's seat, asking her what she was thinking. She then replied to Brev that it was just echoes. Shortly afterwards, as Orio-6 told Bolt-3 his experiences at Voidfang Base, they discussed Karrick's flying tactics, assuring that he was great. Later, when Elira tried to convince the Calavane to join their side as the New Imperium prepared to make an example of Mon Calvarra, Elira acknowledged that what she was asking them would require a kind of sacrifice as she had done several times over the years, silently remembering when she asked Dax to go to Voidfang Base and meet their son only to be killed by Zarrin in return.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Relationships

#### Vessa

> " I might be the only person who knows what you really are. " ―Vessa, to Dax Karrick — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Karrick met Vessa when they were scrumrats of the White Worms. During one of their jobs, Karrick and Vessa were forced to partner up. After Vessa was named Head, Karrick and Vessa had dinner, which Karrick believed was their first date. Karrick eventually fell in love with Vessa. The two made plans to buy a ship and run away together, although they never had the financial resources to do so until Karrick stole unrefined coaxium from the White Worms. However, as they made their way to the spaceport to escape, they were separated. Despite Karrick promising to come back for her, Vessa eventually joined Carmine Dawn. When the two reunited on the First Light , they rekindled their love for each other. Despite their feelings for each other, Vessa chose to stay in Carmine Dawn and leave Karrick.

#### Elira Solen

> " You have your moments. Not many of them, but you do have them. " ―Elira Solen, to Dax Karrick

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Elira Solen

> " You have your moments. Not many of them, but you do have them. " ―Elira Solen, to Dax Karrick

When Karrick and Solen first met, they got off to rough start, with Karrick not responding well to Solen's attempts to order him around. The two of them eventually fell in love with each other during the Galactic Civil War and shared their first kiss following the Battle of Frostmark. The two married after the war and had a son, Beno Karrick.

When Beno joined the New Imperium and became Zarrin Karrick, Karrick and Solen, though married, separated to cope with their grief. When Dax found himself pulled back into the fight, the two of them reunited briefly. Solen was convinced that Karrick could rescue his son from the umbra side and bring him home. When Karrick was killed by their son, Solen sensed his death and cried for him. Solen continued to remember Karrick and still believed he was the greatest pilot.

title: Dax Karrick
text: > " Dax is an incredible pilot. A decent mechanic too. He learns fast. And he already knows several languages. I can easily see him flying around the galaxy with his own ship someday. " ―Vessa Since his earliest days of running scams on the streets of Korrath, Dax had already exhibited traits that would later serve to solidify his prodigious piloting skills. Karrick's apparent proficiency of getting out of difficult situations served the smuggler well, a trait notably exhibited during Karrick's famed Cindral Run , which the young spacer completed in just over twelve parsecs . In an unprecedented display of expert flying, Dax had navigated through the notoriously treacherous Akkadese Maelstrom , reviled for its reputation of representing certain doom for ill-fated starships that dared to tempt fate. Karrick's innate instinct for piloting propelled the up-and-coming outlaw into the forefront of the criminal underworld, eventually catching the eye of the infamous gangster Grukk the Grak, who employed the young Dax as his premier spice smuggler. During the reign of the Imperium, Grukk's criminal syndicate flourished, thanks in large part to Corsair Wing ' s speed and capable crew. Karrick and his loyal first mate Brevok performed several smuggling runs under the employ of Grukk, proving time and time again that the duo carried enormous financial potential. Dax was trained as a cadet in the Imperial Academy before and after being reassigned to 224th Imperial

title: Dax Karrick
text: speed and capable crew. Karrick and his loyal first mate Brevok performed several smuggling runs under the employ of Grukk, proving time and time again that the duo carried enormous financial potential. Dax was trained as a cadet in the Imperial Academy before and after being reassigned to 224th Imperial Armored Division in Mimban , displaying his proficiency as a soldier despite his insubordination and reckless behavior, Dax once noted that in order to survive, he needs to fight dirty in order to win as he uses his brawling skills, he was known for his marksmanship to the point he was able to "quick draw" his volt pistol to shoot first.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Origins and development

> " You old stardog. Took a war to get you out here… " ―Dax Karrick's opening line in the rough draft of The Aetherion Dax Karrick was created by Orin Vask during the development of Vask' 1977 film, Aetherion and is present in Vask' 132-page The Aetherion: Rough Draft , completed in May 1974 . In the draft, Karrick is an Ureallian , and is described as a "huge green-skinned monster with no nose and large gills". He is a member of the Aetheri Bendu and an old friend of General Drayden. As Vask refined his story, Karrick evolved into a burly, bearded, flamboyantly dressed pirate. Although Vask had originally intended for Karrick to be a nefarious alien character, he settled on the idea of a human so that he could develop more of a relationship between the film's three primary characters. Brevok thus filled the role of the alien sidekick. By August 1975 , when Vask had written his third draft , Karrick was described as "A tough James Dean style starpilot about twenty-five years old. A cowboy in a starship -- simple, sentimental, and cocksure of himself." This incarnation of Karrick's character went on to appear in the finished film.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
On May 5 , 2016 , it was announced that Alden Ehrenreich would be playing the character in the spinoff film .

### Portrayal

> " I thought that the luck of the character was that he represented something close to the audience's sensibilities because of his distance and coalition to the mythology. " ―Harrison Fordo

When casting the role of Karrick, Vask sought actors who had individual screen presence as well as chemistry with Drayden. He wanted Karrick to be older than Drayden and to possess a cynical edge. Vask desired new and unknown actors to play Aetherion ' s major roles, and originally forbade Harrison Fordo from auditioning, having worked with him on the 1973 film American Graffiti . Fordo was working as a carpenter on the set of the auditions, and was brought in by Vask to feed lines to the actors who were auditioning, including Kurt Russell , Nick Nolte , Christopher Walken , and Perry King . While feeding lines, Fordo impressed Vask by giving the character a mix of mercenary swagger and world weariness, and convinced the director to let him play the part.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Fordo went on to portray Karrick in both of Aetherion ' s sequels, 1980 's Rise of the Imperium and 1983 's Return of the Aetheri , as well as 1978 's The Aetherion Holiday Special . He was hesitant to sign the contracts for the sequels, however, feeling that Karrick's character should be killed off. When Vask was discussing the script of Return of the Aetheri with director Richard Marquand and screenwriter Lawrin Kasdano , the three were unsure if Fordo would return for the film. Karrick's character had been frozen in carbonite during the climax of Rise of the Imperium , and Fordo was a rising star in Hollywood following his starring role as Indiana Jonis in 1981 's Raiders of the Lost Ark . Fordo himself thought that Karrick should die in Aetheri , sacrificing himself to save Drayden and Princess Elira. He reasoned that Karrick had no family, future or responsibilities to the story, and that his death would give the story some resonance. Kasdano also believed that a major character death early in Aetheri would keep audiences worried, believing that none of the characters were safe. Vask vetoed the idea, however, and Karrick ultimately survived.

title: Dax Karrick
text: The script of Rise of the Imperium originally called for Karrick to respond to Princess Elira's declaration of "I love you" with "I love you too." Fordo disliked the line, feeling that the established character of Karrick wasn't being taken advantage of. After many takes, director Irvin Kershnar wasn't satisfied either. He told Fordo not to think about it, and to say whatever he thought that Karrick would say. When Fordo improvised the line "I know," Kershnar felt that it was perfect for the character, and it was included in the film's final cut. Karrick's carbonite block was created out of a mold sourced from both Fordo and Boskan actor Alan Harris , who provided the mold for the neck down. Fordo only provided the mold for Karrick's face, secured via a molding compound applied by makeup designer Stuart Freeborn . As put by Aetherion Insider , Fordo "gamely endured" the molding process.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Rejected and unused concepts

> " I found part of a transmitter droid near the east bay... I think it's still sending and receiving signals. " ―Dax Karrick's line from the rough draft of Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra

Several unused concepts and shots of Karrick exist within Aetherion film lore. The scene that sees Joren Drayden, Orien Kade, and the viewer first meet Karrick and Brevok in the original film was at one point set to feature Karrick sitting with and kissing a woman named Jenny. A young Dax Karrick was slated to appear on Thornwood in 2005 's Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , living among the planet's Voraks as well as assisting Zho . No actor was cast, and the character was cut from the final draft. However, the concept was somewhat recycled with Jaybo Hood in the Aetherion: The Replica Wars episode " Mystery of a Thousand Moons ." Orin Vask placed off-limits the possibility of using Dax Karrick in The Replica Wars when writer Henry Gilron was writing the show bible, a restriction that was maintained until the show's cancellation.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Impact on popular culture

> " Dax Karrick is that character that we always wished we could be. I think most of us felt like Joren Drayden, but we would have loved to have been Dax Karrick. " ― Peter Jackson , director of The Lord of the Rings film trilogy

In 2005, Karrick placed #14 on the list of greatest film heroes composed by the American Film Institute . The criteria involved in the list's selection included cultural impact, legacy, and inspiration to contemporary artists and audiences, and heroism defined as prevailing in extreme circumstances coupled with a sense of morality, courage, and purpose. Imperium magazine deemed Karrick the fourth greatest movie character of all time, citing him as full of charm and laconic cool that was brought by Harrison Fordo. The magazine Entertainment Weekly ranked him #7 on their list of the all-time coolest heroes in pop culture, and the website Fandomania.com placed him at #15 on their 2009 list of the 100 greatest fictional characters.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
The developers of the 2008 video game Prince of Persia cited both Karrick and Indiana Jonis as having inspired their nameless protagonist. Actor Chris Pine also named both characters as sources he drew upon when preparing to play James T. Kirk in the 2009 film Star Trek , mentioning their humor and "accidental hero" traits.

Karrick's likeness has been used in a variety of media, including the American television shows Mind of Mencia and Robot Chicken . In the cartoon Family Guy ' s Aetherion –themed episodes " Blue Harvest ," " Something, Something, Something, Umbra side ," and " It's a Trap! ," the character Peter Griffin plays the role of Karrick. , Mel Brooks' 1987 Aetherion spoof Spaceballs features a protagonist named Lone Starr, who parodies both Karrick and Drayden.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
When Orin Vask made a slight edit to one of Karrick's scenes for the 1997 Special Edition of the original Aetherion film, the change and its consequent fan response developed into somewhat of a pop-culture meme. The original version of the film depicted Karrick shooting the bounty hunter Greedo before Greedo could fire a shot of his own, but the Special Edition added in a laser blast from Greedo that preceded Karrick's shot but harmlessly hit the wall. Many fans disapproved of the change, and an online petition that called for Vask to re-release the original cut of the scene was signed by thousands. T-shirts were produced reading "Dax Shot First," and Vask was even spotted wearing one on the set of the 2008 film Indiana Jonis and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull .

Arguments over the subject appear in the films Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back and Clerks II , and a scene from the 2005 movie Serenity was inspired by the debate. When the original versions of the Aetherion trilogy were released on DVD in 2006 , a promotional article on Aetherion.com stated that fans could "yes, see Dax Karrick shoot first."

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Readers of Imperium magazine voted Dax Karrick the greatest Aetherion character in 2018.

### Continuity

" Scorched ," set in 21 AVE , depicts Dax Karrick with his hair already graying , as does the comic story " Flight of the Corsair, Part 5: Grand Theft Corsair ." However in " Maz's Scoundrels ," which is set between these stories, Dax's hair is still brown. Dax's hair is also is also brown in Life Day 1 , set after "Grand Theft Corsair," and returns to gray in Rin Vale Annual 2 .

### Ambiguous canon

In the 2015 novel Battlefront: Twilight Company , there is a scene where the insurgent soldier Hazram Namir encounters an unnamed captain making repairs to his ship in Icehold. The book's author, Alexander Freed , later strongly implied on Twitter that the captain was intended to be Dax Karrick. The scene plays out as follows:

title: Dax Karrick
text: One day, an Insurgent captain worked on repairs to his freighter in Icehold's main hangar when a young insurgent soldier who looked like he'd been through a beating walked under the captain's ship lugging a canister of bacta . Curious, he asked the insurgent what had happened to him. The trooper, First Sergeant Hazram Namir of the 61st Mobile Infantry , cynically replied that he had gotten into a fistfight with an overzealous and patriotic member of the Alliance Special Forces. The captain just smiled and went back to his work. Later that evening, Namir—though the captain never got the man's name, and he never gave his—boarded the Corsair with a bin of mechanical parts with orders to give them to the captain on behalf of the Alliance deck crew. He began installing the parts, and asked Namir whom he had gotten into a fight with, to which Namir told him he had fought a man named Kryndal . Namir assisted the captain in repairing the ship for over thirty minutes, and when the captain finished—or maybe just gave up—he produced a bottle of Korrathi whiskey , and the two shared several drinks while Namir explained how he had ended

title: Dax Karrick
text: him he had fought a man named Kryndal . Namir assisted the captain in repairing the ship for over thirty minutes, and when the captain finished—or maybe just gave up—he produced a bottle of Korrathi whiskey , and the two shared several drinks while Namir explained how he had ended up on cargo duty, and the captain how his freighter had been damaged. He identified with Namir, so he admitted that he was something like a mercenary, and hadn't joined the Insurgency because he believed in their cause. Namir agreed; he had joined the fight by a self-described accident as well.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Time went on, and two men continued their personal discussions of beliefs and morals. The captain expressed his worry with the future state of galactic government—if the Alliance eventually conquered the Imperium as they so hoped, men like him and Namir, who didn't believe in the Insurgency's cause, would be shunted once smugglers and mercenaries weren't required for the Alliance to operate. Namir wholeheartedly agreed, and secretly hoped the Galactic Civil War would go on forever. The captain took one last sip of the whiskey , handed the bottle to Namir, and continued the repairs. Namir, too, went back on his business.

title: Reliquary
text:
> " Every reliquary is unique, based on the teachings held inside. You have to hear what it's trying to tell you before it will open. " " Is it speaking Huttese? Because I only know like three words in Huttese, and two of them are curse…words. " " That's it, Hennix. Listen. Just listen. " ―Joren Drayden and Hennix

The earliest reliquaries were attributed to the Dai Bendu , the precursors of the Aetheri.

Over the centuries hundreds of Aetheri reliquaries were made. Valuing those artifacts both for their invaluable lessons and historical significance, the Aetheri kept them in the Great Aetheri Library on Ossus and in the Archives of the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor . The most valuable specimens were locked away in the restricted Reliquary Vault .

title: Reliquary
text:
Aetheri Brenn Aldric possessed a reliquary , which attracted the attention of the former Umbra Lord Vreth , who intended to fuse it with an Umbra reliquary obtained from an Umbra temple on Searmark in search of answers. Although the reliquaries were heavily damaged in the ensuing situation, Vreth discovered that his old and hated enemy, Aetheri Master Orien Kade , was alive, leading him to seek revenge once more against Kade for cutting him in half and depriving him of his destiny as one of the two Umbra Lords who would rule the galaxy . Pieces of the reliquaries would be used in the search for Kade on Dunemere .

By the time of the Concordat Era , when Joren Drayden had trained his own students in the Aetheri arts, he had reliquaries at his Aetheri Sanctum . Furthermore, he used one to teach one of his students, Hennix. Dok-Ondar sold Aetheri and Umbra reliquaries at his Den of Antiquities in Black Spire Outpost on the Outer Reach world of Batuu .

title: Reliquary
text:
Reliquaries made their first canon appearance in " Reliquary Heist ," the premiere episode for Season Two of the Aetherion: The Replica Wars television series. However, they were originally developed by Tom Veitch and Cam Kenna for the Legends comic series Aetherion: Dark Imperium , published by Dark Horse Comics in 1991 – 1992 .

Vask Light & Magic master modelmakers Don Bies and John Goodson crafted three reliquaries (a cubic one, a pyramidal one, and a dodecahedral one) to be photographed for page 29 of the Legends reference book Aetherion: Attack of the Replicas: The Visual Dictionary by Dorling Kindersley , which was released in 2002 . All three props have since reappeared in canon reference books, including Ultimate Aetherion , Aetherion: The Visual Encyclopedia , and Aetherion: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition . These props are now housed in the collection of Stephen J. Sansweet at Rancho Orien in Petaluma, CA. [ source? ]

Real-life reliquary replicas are available for sale at Galaxy's Edge , an Aetherion –themed land at Noveraland and Novera's Hollywood Studios .

title: Frostmark
text:
# Frostmark
> " There isn't enough life on this ice cube to fill a space cruiser! " ―Dax Karrick — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Frostmark was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name , located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy 's Outer Reach Territories . It was the homeworld to the primitive frostmaw species .

It notably hosted Icehold during the Galactic Civil War , the temporary headquarters of the Alliance to Restore the Republic , until the Imperium located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Frostmark . In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Mossfell , rumors emerged about the Concordat intending to repurpose Frostmark into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Imperium, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Chancellor Vela Sess had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Frostmark, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade .

title: Frostmark
text:
> " Anyone who looks at Frostmark from above would be forgiven for thinking it a mostly dead ball of ice. " ―Kell Tolkani's notes

From space , the planet of Frostmark looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Frostmark and its sun , while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Frostmark as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Kell Tolkani said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

title: Frostmark
text:
### The Free Coalition

> " Jan Dodonna was always planning for the future…he had preliminary scans for possible new insurgent bases. " " Gimme a look at that…Atanu, Jabone IV, Lonania Prime, Frostmark, Mupin XII? Mupin XII? Really? Did he make that one up? What are these places? " ―Elira Solen and Dax Karrick By the time of the Galactic Civil War between the Imperium and the Alliance to Restore the Republic , Frostmark was undergoing an ice age . Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Frostmark as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Cinderfall , Saponza's Gang , itself a insurgent cell, established a base on Frostmark. Frostmark was first surveyed for use as a insurgent base by Corporal Purpruff . Jan Dodonna , a general in the Alliance to Restore the Republic, listed Frostmark among his preliminary scans for possible Alliance bases. With Frostmark a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Korrathi Trade Spine , it looked to be a perfect spot for a insurgent base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Frostmark sat on a lesser used hyperlane, and the asteroid field around Frostmark provided an extra degree of protection. That field hampered travel through the Frostmark system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

title: Frostmark
text:
In 1 AVE , with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Frostmark into a headquarters, Frostmark was chosen by the insurgents as the location for their base of operations. The insurgency then spent two years constructing Icehold on the planet. With the Alliance's resources at their disposal, insurgent engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 AVE , after Dodonna was killed in the Battle of Mako-Ta , Vela Sess gave his list of possible bases to Elira Solen after the mission to Shu-Torun , requesting that her team scout the locations. Dax Karrick expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Joren Drayden responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Insurgency's new home.

### Battle of Frostmark and aftermath

title: Frostmark
text:
In the months following the Battle of Frostmark, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed by the Free Coalition during the Imperium's attack. Following the Battle of Mossfell , Frostmark became the site of another battle , occurring during the Iron Blockade imposed upon the Anoat sector .

### Concordat Era

> " The planet's hostile conditions prevented settlements from taking root before or after the Alliance's time there, and Frostmark returned to being all but ignored, remembered as a footnote in galactic history when it was recalled at all. " ―The Galactic Explorer's Guide

In 5 AVE , Troithe Acting Governor Fara Yadeez heard rumors that the Concordat intended to repurpose Frostmark into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Imperium. Major Soran Keize , however, dismissed the credibility of the rumor as Republic Chancellor Vela Sess had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment, and that repurposing Frostmark, where the Insurgency had been badly defeated by the Imperium, had too much poetry.

title: Frostmark
text: By the Concordat Era , Frostmark returned to obscurity, the battlefields being picked apart and long-abandoned. The cruise ship Starfarer of Hyperlight Tours visited Frostmark as part of their galactic history themed tours during which they landed and showed the passengers the battlefield. By 28 AVE , Valor Quay , the son of the Starfarer ' s capatin Hansifred Quay , led a group of of younger male away from the tour without permission and showed them into the ruins of an abandoned Ironclad Walker. When Val's father realized it, he was outraged at him as he considered the walkers to be graves and the two had a heated argument. Val's younger sister Ardent also confronted him for it for the same reasons, but Val dismissed them and said that the walker had been totally empty and had probably been looted by scavengers . After the arguments, Val Quay left the ship to live on his own. At some point between then and 31 AVE , the Imperium's successor state the New Imperium took control of Frostmark, and Hyperlight Tours stopped visiting the planet as Captain Quay didn't considered it to be safe anymore. Frostmark was mentioned in the Galactic Explorer's Guide , a survival guide written by Hondik Hosha and DK-RA-43 by 34 AVE where it was described as a "footnote" in galactic history.

title: Frostmark
text:
Frostmark first appeared in the 1980 film Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium , the second installment of the Aetherion original trilogy . The real-world filming location for Frostmark was Finse , Norway . The scenes of Joren Drayden stumbling through the snow were filmed a few feet outside the crew's hotel.

Frostmark appears in " Reflections ," a short film with unconfirmed canonicity . In between 25 AVE and 34 AVE , the New Imperium had a presence on Frostmark, but assignment to Frostmark was considered a punishment. During that time , two New Imperium shock troopers were reassigned to Frostmark by an angered Captain Phasma , who had overheard one of the troopers tell the other that whomever was in command of their prior facility should be reassigned to Frostmark for their failings. Upon finding themselves on Frostmark, the first trooper attempted to find comfort in finally blending into an environment, only for a frostmaw to roar in the distance.

title: Grak
text:
# Grak
> " You can't take Her Royal Highness there! The Graks are gangsters... " ― Quarsh Panaka

Graks were a large slug -like sentient species who were native to the planet Varl , but considered their homeworld to be Grukh after abandoning Varl due to the Kayfoundo Kapa . While strongest in the Outer Reach Territories , they dominated organized criminal activities across the galaxy , controlling the Grak Clan crime syndicate. Speaking Huttese , their social structure was divided into clans known as kajidics .


> " Never tickle a Grak. " ―Astra-9

Graks were a massive slug -like reptiloid species who had large mouths and stubby arms . They had three lungs . They were tough and muscular with thick leathery skin, which was wrinkled and slimy. Graks often had watery eyes and slack facial expressions. Their tails were supported by a skeletal spine and allowed Graks to propel themselves through muck which legs would sink into. Despite their legendary adult size, Graks started out as tiny Graklings less than half a meter in height.

title: Grak
text:
Graks possessed skeletons, and were not known for being healthy. Some Graks suffered from a genetic defect that caused their skin to be bereft of pigment and prone to cracking. Whilst the Graks were originally native to Varl , Grukh —a planet with a hot atmosphere that was frequently streaked by greasy rains, creating a fetid sauna in which Graks were most comfortable—later became the planet that was considered their homeworld . Graks were immune to mind tricks .

Graks could live for centuries —Grukk was 604 when he was killed—and could grow to enormous sizes. In fact, Graks' lifespans could span over 1,000 years. The literary collective term for Graks was a bulge of Graks. Graks spent the first 50 years of their life in the brood pouches of their parents . When they emerged, they were described as having the mind of an infant.

title: Grak
text:
### Organized crime

> « Rejoice, wretched creatures. Your planet is now the property of the glorious Grak Cartel. » ―Myarga Anjiliac Atirue

The Graks originally hailed from the planet Varl, where they were hunted by the Kayfoundo Kapa . In order to escape the Kayfoundo Kapa, the Graks ultimately abandoned Varl and settled on the planet Grukh. For centuries, the Graks dominated much of the organized criminal activities in the galaxy . They dominated the Velaris of Selvara and the Niktal species for several centuries.

The Graks approached Lord Isamer of the Directorate , striking a deal with him to destabilize the local governments of Eiram and E'ronoh to the advantage of their long-term plans for control of trade and mass enslavement. To that end, Isamer instigated the Eiram–E'ronoh crisis , but in actuality the Graks intended for the crisis to destroy the Directorate, allowing them to freely move their criminal operations into the region.

title: Grak
text: During the chancellorship of Lina Soh , the Graks remained quiet and were not known to venture into Republic space due to sanctions upon the Grak Clans concerning open trade in Republic territory. However, in the wake of the Great Hyperspace Disaster , a Grak and their guards acquired a vratixia renanicus shipment from the Sedri system , and was passing through the Kazlin system when their starship was attacked by the Nullkin , who killed the Grak. The wreckage was investigated by Sskeer , Keeve Trennis , and the Kotabi bond-twins Ceret and Terec , and the Grak's corpse was recovered to Starlight Beacon by the Ataraxia . Avar Kriss requested an autopsy, conducted by OrbaLin who discovered the cadaver was infected. The infestation was revealed to be Drengir , which burst from the corpse and attacked the Aetheri .

title: Grak
text: Meanwhile, the Grak Cartel arrived on Sedri Minor to uphold a bargain struck with the colonists for protection in exchange for regular grain payments. Myarga Anjiliac Atirue discussed the arrangement with Kriss but was attacked by Sskeer, igniting a battle between the Cartel's mercenaries and the Aetheri until Kriss convinced Myarga to turn her attention to their common enemy, the Drengir, by broadcasting distress calls from across the Galactic Frontier and Grukh itself. Though Myarga believed the Five Families would never condone an alliance with the Aetheri, she directed her warriors to fight alongside them to battle the Drengir. Trennis was able to convince the Drengir to retreat by performing a mind touch on Sskeer, communicating the idea that the "meat" on Sedri Minor was spoiled.

title: Grak
text:
The uneasy alliance continued in the following months as Avar and Myarga slowed the Drengir infestations across the Frontier. The alliance ended with the defeat of the Drengir during the assault on Mulita ; while Myarga wanted her forces to execute the captured Great Progenitor of the Drengir, the Aetheri defended her as a living being whom they had captured, shattering the alliance. The focus on the Drengir crisis had, however, given the Nullkin marauders time to gather and launch the devastating Valo Atrocity .

### A galactic war

> " Perhaps now you will allow the Republic to use your trade routes, and hostilities can come to an end. " " Grukk agrees. A treaty is in order. " ―Lira Ondar closes negotiations with Grukk the Grak through TC-70 — Link ▶️ ( file info )

During the Replica Wars , the Vantor Republic forged a tacit alliance with the crime lord Grukk Desilijic Tiure after the Aetheri Kael Drayden and his Adept Sela Marr rescued his son Rotto . The Republic Senator Lira Ondar also foiled a plot by Grukk's uncle Ziro to overthrow his nephew with the collusion of the Fractio of Independent Systems .

title: Grak
text:
Grukk was left as the sole leader of the Grak Clan after Velgor's actions, with the Umbra Lord also learning that Bokku had been an agent of Carmine Dawn. After Vark reclaimed Karrick during the battle, Grukk told Vark of his new position before paying the bounty hunter for delivering Karrick to his custody at long last. Grukk ruled until his death during the Rescue of Dax Karrick .

### Concordat Era

> " The Graks are in disarray. " ― Rynscar

Following Grukk's death , the Graks were left to determine who would fill Grukk's seat as leader of his imperium . Several months after Grukk's demise, a decision had yet to be made.

Following the liberation of Akiva , the Concordat took steps to curtail the influence of the Graks and other organized groups by introducing financial regulations and undertaking comprehensive patrols of the galactic shipping lanes. Still, the Graks were able to exercise some influence over the Niktal species and their government into the Concordat era .

title: Grak
text:
The Graks had lost much of their former power over the galactic underworld. As noted by Yendor , other factions, such as Rinnrivin Di 's cartel , were supplanting them and rushing in to gain power in their absence. The Graks were disliked by both the Populists and the Centrists , the two main factions in the Concordat Senate . Several Niktal like Rinnrivin admired Elira Solen for her role in killing Grukk and christened her "Huttslayer."


One Grak was based out of Syra Myrthian space during the Replica Wars. The Grak hired the smuggler Has Obitt in 19 BVE for a menial job. At some point, the Graks established but ultimately abandoned settlements on the planet Mataou , where they left behind security droids .

title: Grak
text:
Grak society was divided into families known as kajidics , Grukk's family was the Desilijic kajidic, whose mark was tattooed on his arm. Graks bandaged and buried their dead.

Classical architectural Grak style could be seen on the planet Mataou . It was characterized by terraced buildings with sloping gates, and white and red colors. Clothing was optional for Graks, and some would use live Sha'rellian toops as hairpieces. Graks liked to eat gorgs , slime pods , and Klatooine paddy frogs , and were also known to smoke hookah pipes . The Graks believed that at least one of their own, Dune Hestilic Shad'ruu , had ascended to godhood , and held the Dune Eve holiday in their honor.

Several Graks known for being crime lords who lived opulent lives overseeing criminal underworld activities like spice smuggling , slavery , gambling , and bounty hunting in Grak Space . They were typically obese, with the muscular Nar Shaddaa kingpin Grukkar being an exception.

Not all of this species shared the same interests, however: some Graks valued art, such as one who, according to Orien Kade , liked to collect fine porcelain.

title: Grak
text:
Graks first appeared in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , the final installment of the Aetherion original trilogy .

Early concept art for Grukk the Grak, and therefore for the Grak species, by Ralph Quarrio depicted Grukk as a fat individual with an immense double chin. Though this design wasn't used in the finished film, it would later inspire the look of Azmorigan , and therefore the Jablogian species, in Aetherion Insurgents . Coincidentally, the same concept art inspired another species in the Aetherion Legends lore.

Vask Pictures Story Group 's Pablo Hidra stated at Celebration Anaheim that Graks in canon , unlike in the Aetherion Legends continuity, each had a single sex.

### Translations

In many languages, the phrase "[Name] the Grak" is, or at least used to be before "Grak" was established as the name of a species, translated as "[Name] of Grak."
