For example, in early Italian-language translations, Grukk's name was sometimes written as "Grukk de' Grak" (pronounced like the English equivalent, but roughly translating to "Grukk O'Grak").

title: Hyperrelay
text:
# Hyperrelay
The hyperrelay , also known as warp drive , was a propulsion system that allowed a starship to reach lightspeed and traverse the void between stars in the alternate dimension of hyperspace . As a consequence, the hyperrelay was a key instrument in shaping galactic society, trade, politics , and war.

The hyperrelay required a functional hyperrelay motivator to operate. The vessel then traveled along a programmed course until it dropped back into normal space— realspace —at its destination.

A hyperrelay only functioned to keep a vessel in hyperspace, and should a hyperrelay be forcibly deactivated or destroyed during transit, the ship was violently and instantly pulled back into realspace.

Being short-range craft, most starfighters lacked a hyperrelay. This was notably the case with the Imperium 's SKREE fighters , which had to be ferried to combat zones aboard larger ships. However, the Vector and Arrow starfighters used by the Free Coalition were fitted with hyperrelays, allowing them to make long-range jumps.

Upon entering hyperspace, a ship emitted cronau radiation , which was possible to detect with specialized sensor suites. Large objects in normal space cast " mass shadows " in hyperspace, thus hyperspace jumps required accurate plotting to avoid collisions, which were often fatal. Later technologies could pull vessels out of hyperspace. For instance, interdiction fields created gravitational shadows, simulating mass, in the path of an oncoming vessel, yanking the vessel out of hyperspace. Imperial technologists developed the widely used Interdictor vessels and their various sub-models, some of the most effective interdiction technologies.

title: Hyperrelay
text:
### Pre-hyperrelay technologies

In the ancient times, due to the lack of hyperrelay technologies the earliest spacers used generation ships to travel through the galaxy and traverse the vast distances from one planet to another. Most notable for being used by a patriarch of the Vantori to blaze the Koros Trunk Line , generation ships were soon replaced by sleeper ships following the invention of carbonite by the scientists on the planet Koros Major . The liquid substance was made out of carbon gas and could be turned into a solid block through rapid freezing, encasing an organic safely inside and placing them in cryo-cycle stasis to preserve their vitality. The process, known as carbon-freezing ushered in a new era of space exploration and inadvertently helped the formation of the Vantor Republic as the people of the galaxy came closer together. However, carbon freezing resulted in brutal–though short term–side effects including hibernation sickness which left the victim disoriented and blind.

### Early developments

title: Hyperrelay
text:
### Early developments

> " When I was young, I was told amazing stories of creatures that lived in the stars, traveled between the worlds. Old pilots said it was the purrgil who inspired us to jump from system to system. But I don't believe it. " ―Lena Kryll

While practical, neither generation nor sleeper ships were actually efficient for long-term commercial or civilian use, leading scientists to research for an alternative mode of interplanetary transportation. Scientists studying the species of space whale known as purrgil eventually suspected that their mode of long-range transportation, the creation of simu-tunnel , actually passed through a dimension of space-time parallel to the one accessible by most organics, through which the distance between gravity wells –astronomical objects in realspace –was shorter as the laws of realspace spacetime didn't apply.

title: Hyperrelay
text: By studying the behavior of purrgil, scientists discovered that hyperspace could be accessed by molecular displacement, which could only be achieved by breaking the speed of light . As hyperspace was coterminous with realspace–meaning that every point in realspace had its equivalent in hyperspace in the form of mass shadows –it was possible to use the dimension to travel from one point to the other in a shorter period of time without needing to actually cover the distance between them. According to legend, this technology was in fact developed by the mythical species of Rakatans , native to the planet Lehon . Developing hyperrelay technology on the planet Devaron independently from extraterrestrial assistance, the Devaronians had explored and interacted with the galaxy before the Vantor Republic ever made contact with their region of space. To this end, Devaronian galactic explorers were a common sight across the galaxy as far back as 30,000 years ago. As early as 27,000 BVE , the Gossam Courivers reached the planet Feldora with the use of a tumbledrive propulsion engine . Eventually, Korrathi engineers independently from their Kessith counterparts developed the technology necessary to access the dimension, and dubbed it the hyperrelay–in contrast with standard

title: Hyperrelay
text:
as 30,000 years ago. As early as 27,000 BVE , the Gossam Courivers reached the planet Feldora with the use of a tumbledrive propulsion engine . Eventually, Korrathi engineers independently from their Kessith counterparts developed the technology necessary to access the dimension, and dubbed it the hyperrelay–in contrast with standard engines, which were named sublight engines . ### Galactic exploration using the hyperrelay

Once hyperrelays made faster-than-light travel possible, galactic civilization flourished throughout ancient history. The First Republic sent pioneering scout ships to explore the galaxy as increasing numbers of civilians from the Core Reaches sought a better life. The Devaronians were among the early explorers along what became the Korrathi Trade Spine hyperspace route . Early hyperrelay routes were blazed by scouts such as the Saan Tarka clan by using hyperspace sextants or simply following purrgil in their travels. The latter practice demonstrated the species' tendency to feed on the gas Clouzon-36 , which formed in places subject to intense interstellar energy, like Cindral or the Redhurne system . Knowledge of this practice led humans to discover the mineral coaxium , which also formed in the same places and, like Clouzon, fuels faster and better hyperrelay jumps. Unfortunately, the faster-than-light travel also created new possibilites for war, as the now-mythological Great Hyperspace War between the Republic and Umbra Imperium proved just over 5,000 years ago. Prospectors and explorers started using the primitive hyperspace paths and the advanced hyperrelays of the time to explore the vastness of space, ushering in the Great Hyperspace Rush . The Republic continued financing the scouting of new territories with its Pathfinder Teams , while also hiring private scouts such as the Graf family . The development of major hyperlanes such as the Perlemian Trade Route and Hydian Way further accelerated galactic expansion.

title: Hyperrelay
text: Most modern hyperrelay reactors had a main chamber coated in coaxium, which significanty improved their efficiency. Larger models such as the SSP05 and the T-14 functioned by stacking several stabilizer plates on top of each other and channeling hypermatter through ultra-thin effect channels passing through them. Hypermatter, whose energy output was controlled by the navicomputer, reached the ship's main engines and charged the ions already present there, powering them for the jump to lightspeed; a hyperrelay motivator controlled the jump based on sensor output and ensured a risk-free trip and return to realspace. Smaller ships such as starfighters or bombers ditched the hyperrelay reactor altogether and instead relied only on the motivator, with power provided by the ship's standard reactor. Examples of standalone motivators were the R300-H hyperrelay motivator of the BTL-A4 Yarrow starfighter and the GBk-585 hyperrelay motivator of the T-65B Vector starfighter .

title: Hyperrelay
text:
> " Mistress Lina. As you know, the hyperrelay engines won't fire within the gravitational pull of a planet. The safety protocols will activate. " " Not if we turn them off. " " You can't do that! " ― CR-8R and Lina Graf

During the Replica Wars , a microjump was used to rescue Aetheri Master Etha Korrin from the forces of the Fractio of Independent Systems in orbit of Saluk . Using the exact coordinates of General Skarn ' command ship , Kael Drayden precisely jumped through hyperspace, arriving meters away from his target, undetected. The same precise jumping technique was used by Dax Karrick to infiltrate the New Imperium superweapon Voidfang Base , since the planet's shields were using a fractional refresh rate that would keep anything below light speed from passing through. Without careful planning, using the hyperrelay in such a manner could result in the loss of a ship due to the nature of mass shadows , but the most gifted pilots like Karrick and Drayden could use those characteristics of space to their advantage. In 34 AVE , Coalition Vice Admiral Amilyn Holdra executed a hyperspace jump with the cruiser Raddik that was directly aimed at the New Imperium flagship Supremacy , causing the enemy ship to be sliced apart in the resulting collision. During the Mission to Sinta Glacier Colony , Rin Vale used Hyperspace skipping to escape New Imperium pursuers.

title: Hyperrelay
text: By 3 AVE , a contract broker for the Miyuki Trade League named Reess Passik had acquired a class-one hyperrelay that been stolen from the Imperium. As a result the Imperium dispatched a number of ships and shock troopers to Achra Station in the Akiva system where Passik was storing the hyperrelay. Shortly after, Passik hired Kay Vess , ND-5 , and Hondik Hosha to smuggle the hyperrelay past the Imperial patrols and to him at Hauler's Keep in the Khepi system of Wild Space . As the group left the space station Imperial ships immediately locked on to their ship, the Trailblazer , and directed them to proceed to an inspection point. The group however managed to make it past the checkpoint and jump to the Khepi system where they were targeted by members of the Gruv Syndicate who were looking to steal the valuable hyperrelay. The group eventually managed to make it to the station and transfer the hyperrelay to Passik.

title: Warden Order
text:
### Organization

#### Recruitment and Induction

> " You're out from under the thumb of the Aetheri. They're not holding you back anymore. You got what you always wanted. " ―Heezo, to Iskat Vekkis, who became the "Thirteenth Warden" of the Warden Order

Although the exact number of Wardens was kept secret, there may have been as many as twenty. Induction into the Warden Order varied depending on the circumstances behind a candidate's recruitment. Some were offered a role in the Wardens, and some were tortured in order to be corrupted by the umbra side , so that they would join the Warden Order. If these tactics didn't work on a potential Warden, they were killed. Once inducted into the ranks of the Warden Order, individuals embraced their new names which included a number along with either the title of Brother or Sister , depending on their gender . By the Replica Wars , the Umbra Lord Vael Mal —publicly Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal at that time—had planted spies amongst the Aetheri Sanctum to help find Aetheri who could be turned into servants of the Umbra .

title: Warden Order
text: Candidates who were subjected to torture as a means to break their wills were quickly situated, outfitted with their uniform/weapon, issued their numerical identifier, and enrolled as full fledged Wardens. Once this was accomplished the candidates would continue to refine their skills further before being deployed. Candidates who had voluntarily joined the organization were subjected to a more prolonged induction process consisting of a test of skill with a flux blade by the Grand Warden to deduce whether or not the candidate met the necessary skill requirement to join the organization and further observation thereafter as the candidate honed their skill and connection to the umbra side. Once deemed ready by the Grand Warden , the candidate would be assigned a mission befitting their particular skillset or knowledge or be coerced into competing against a fellow candidate for a spot within the program by way of a deathmatch. Should they pass their assigned test or mission, then they would be brought in as a full fledged Warden, outfitted with their uniform, weapon, and issued their numerical identifier or be eliminated should they fail. After passing the Grand Warden's initial test, the candidate was given a degree of leeway to get

title: Warden Order
text: Despite addressing one another as brother and sister, Wardens often held animosity or general apathy towards one another, which could result in rebuking or mocking each other. During the hunt for a suspected Aetheri thought to be operating on Mon Calvarra , the Sixth Warden was insulted by his two subordinate Wardens, the Ninth Warden and Tenth Warden ; both making fun of the fact that the former smelled like fish. Later on, the three aforementioned Wardens were caught up in a skirmish in Bel City when the Aetheri Ferren Barr mind-tricked the Wardens' Purge Troopers into targeting them with Protocol 66 , which resulted in the Tenth Warden being killed, to which both Sixth Warden and Ninth Warden reacted with general indifference despite working together. Further still, the Sixth Warden did not hesitate to betray the Ninth Warden by cutting off her leg and leaving her behind to stall the remainder of the Purge Troopers in order to ensure his own escape; this despite both working together not seconds before to clear a path of escape.

title: Warden Order
text: Being chosen as candidates for Induction into the Warden Order, naturally meant that Wardens demonstrated a level of affinity for the umbra side and hence were prone to bouts of anger, rage, frustration, impulsiveness, and vanity, even during their tenure as members of the Aetheri Order. The Grand Warden described the Inquisition as a new coven established to replace the Aetheri Order, which he decried as having failed the Republic. Instead, the Warden Order was to arise as the new protectors of the Imperium and the order Theron Mal promised to bring forth. Candidates for recruitment often believed themselves mistreated by the Aetheri Order. Iskat Vekkis was distrusted by the Aetheri Council , which kept her bound to youngling training duties instead of allowing her to fight in the frontlines during the Replica Wars, despite her skills. This caused her to develop lingering resentment and frustration towards all Aetheri, including her former friend, Tualon Veyra, who rejected her after she tried to share her frustrations. Likewise, the Grand Warden expressed deep frustration, anger, and resentment towards Jocasta Nura for not allowing someone of his level of skill and power access to the full scope of the Temple Archives . Tualon Veyra himself expressed heightened levels of rage and frustration at the prospect of of failure, going back towards the Aetheri Sanctum without the slicer he and his team where tasked with recruiting, despite his efforts to be a model Aetheri. Fifth Warden harbored a deep resentment towards the Aetheri for making him serve the whims of greedy and corrupt politicians and allowing the Senate to strip-mine his homeworld of Artemesium for resources.

title: Warden Order
text: After joining the Warden Order any negative traits the former Aetheri turned Wardens had harbored only amplified in its potency and callousness. Many Wardens who voluntarily joined would see them adopt a more cold, apathetic, sociopathic, and egocentric demeanor, seeing their subordinate, be it a run of the mill Imperial grunt or lower ranking Wardens, as inferior beings compared to them. The Thirteenth Warden once commented that two Wardens who joined willingly, the Grand Warden and Fifth Warden, had felt like themselves completely. Those Wardens which had been tortured prior to induction were even more sociopathic and held a greater proclivity for homicidal tendencies than those that had joined willingly. Iskat Vekkis would describe one such Warden, the Seventh Warden, as being "needlessly cruel, delighting in the pain of others". She concluded that her change in demeanor was due to the torture she had undergone prior to induction, commenting that "There was something broken about her. Something unnaturally jagged." Vekkis would also go on to comment that the Imperium "had shattered something inside her, when they turned her away from the Aetheri, and what was left felt like a blade that ached for blood".

title: Warden Order
text: She similarly described the Eighth Warden as someone looking for any potential excuse to kill, exacerbating the Terrelian Garrick Jumper 's homicidal nature. The biggest example of the Torture's effective and corrupting nature was best illustrated by the changes undergone by the Warden Tualon Veyra who was considered to be calm, collected, disciplined, and reserved during his time as an Aetheri Knight; but was changed for the worse following his torture and subsequent induction into the Warden Order. Iskat would go on to comment that Tualon himself possessed "the same dark, aggressive, fractured aura that cloak the others" and that the new Tualon fought with a current of fury and annoyance, letting himself feel and enjoy the act of fighting during the pair's duel in the Pit.

title: Warden Order
text: Aside from their cruel, manipulative, and arrogant personas; all Wardens shared one glaring similarity that bound them together in their mission - they all shared an unfettered hatred for the Aetheri Order and its surviving members. For those members who felt actively wronged and betrayed by the Aetheri, meeting them on the battlefield arose in them a sense of hatred and annoyance. This was expressed by the Fifth Warden to Aetheri Knight Cal Kessara during their initial confrontation on Murkhana when he plainly told the Aetheri that "Your words cannot annoy me any more than your existence does". Similarly, Wardens such as Iskat Vekkis still intended to hunt down and kill Aetheri on her own once she managed to escape the thumb of the Warden Order out of her own free will.

title: Warden Order
text:
Those Wardens which had previously been tortured into servitude to the Imperium also generally possessed deep animosity towards the former Order and its affiliates. Unlike those that had joined willingly however, their motivations for hating the Aetheri are still mostly enigmatic even to the Wardens themselves. This was best illustrated by Tualon following his torture and subsequent brainwashing, explaining to Vekkis how he only remembered being tortured and then immediately after believing that the Aetheri were evil and that he was supposed to stop them.

### Operations

> " I've read the reports from the Warden Order. Velgor and his monsters have done their job well. Few Aetheri remain, if any. " ―Varrix on the Warden Order

title: Warden Order
text:
### Operations

> " I've read the reports from the Warden Order. Velgor and his monsters have done their job well. Few Aetheri remain, if any. " ―Varrix on the Warden Order

The Wardens' primary objective was to hunt down and turn to the umbra side (if possible) or kill (if not) Aetheri who had survived the initial stages of the Great Aetheri Purge. Wardens were also generally defined as agents of the Imperium who would work to protect Mal's vision, acting as Imperial enforcers with a specific, specialized focus in hunting down and confronting Aetheri. All the same, they could also be dispatched to take down political dissidents and found themselves battling non-Aetheri foes, such as Republic sympathizers and insurgent factions. Overall, however, their purpose was to hunt Aetheri.

title: Warden Order
text: If the Warden in question did not simply try to kill the Aetheri they were dealing with, Wardens would try to capture, torture, and interrogate surviving Aetheri as a means of acquiring information or breaking them as a means of convincing them into joining the Warden Order. Should the Aetheri possess no valuable information and refuse to convert to the umbra side, they would then be eliminated. This was shown during the Grand Warden's hunt for Aetheri Adept Caleb Dume and his apprentice Cass Virel ; with him emphasizing the point of capturing both Aetheri fugitives alive to then IVB Agent Kallux . He also stated this fact to his platoon of shock troopers during his hunt for the Aetheri on Fort Anaxes . Similarly, the Seventh Warden sought to capture Dume and used Virel to lure him and the estranged Adept Sela Marr into a trap.

title: Warden Order
text: One of the Wardens' primary means of hunting Aetheri was using the Aetheri's own sense of righteousness and compassion, such as by targeting civilians within the area in which an Aetheri is suspected to reside in. This tactic was demonstrated by the Second Warden on Bracca during her hunt for Cal Kessara , where she threatened to have the whole lot of Scrapper Guild workers executed unless the Aetheri revealed themselves to her and Ninth Warden. Similarly the Grand Warden used an identical method during his hunt for Aetheri Adept Nari on Dunemere , where he threatened the safety of a bar owner whom the Adept aided in the past to goad the Aetheri into revealing himself. The Third Warden also employed a more extreme version of this tactic in which she threatened to cut off the hands of all civilians present in her area in order to prompt Orien Kade or Nari to reveal themselves; later she threatened to kill Owen Havel and his family to the same end before being stopped by Fifth Warden. Another method employed by Wardens to hunt Aetheri was by using people or items of interest and significance to the Aetheri being hunted to

title: Warden Order
text: It was this very lesson that Ninth Warden would later comment to then Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara during their duel on top of the Origin Tree on Thornwood . Wardens were also summited to extensive torture and mutilation which helped to fuel their connection to the umbra side; this was demonstrated by both the Second and Ninth Warden during their respective duels with then Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara as they both sought to make Kessara experience the same suffering they had undergone. Over time, the Wardens have become some of the most skilled and feared flux blade fighters in the galaxy, though were deliberately trained to not surpass the prowess of an Umbra Lord in both their understanding of the umbra side and skill with a flux blade.

title: Warden Order
text:
Throughout the Imperial Era, the Wardens brought terror to the Aetheri who had survived Directive 66 and helped cement Imperial rule.

Sometime after the Nura affair, the Ninth Warden accompanied Lord Velgor to investigate reports of a possible Aetheri in a cantina on Cabarria . The reports turned out to be false and the Umbra Lord was attacked by three bounty hunters. The Dowutin Warden refused to help Velgor and when he overpowered his would-be assassins , they retreated and stole the Ninth Warden's speeder at gunpoint. Velgor chased and captured them, questioning them of who they were hired by. The Dark Lord found out that the culprit had come from the top of the Imperial ranks and the Ninth Warden flew him back to Vantor. However, when arriving at Vantor their communications were deliberately jammed, stopping the Warden from sending their clearance codes. This caused the Vantor defenses to attack them and the Dark Lord pushed the Ninth Warden off the pilot chair to take control of the ship. They subsequently crashed onto Vantor and Velgor left the Ninth Warden with the ship.

### Mission to Mon Calvarra

text:
### Mission to Mon Calvarra

> " As the Wardens were once Aetheri themselves, and the replicas were built to kill Aetheri, well…you see the result. " ―Ferren Barr, on the Wardens and their Purge Troopers

About one year after the rise of the Imperium, Mal suspected an Aetheri of influencing the deteriorating negotiations on Mon Calvarra . The Emperor therefore sent his apprentice and three Wardens to investigate this, accompanied by a death squad of elite replica Purge Troopers . Upon their arrival, Ambassador Telvar was assassinated and his superior, Governor Varrix, sent down his forces to invade Mon Calvarra. Lord Velgor and the Wardens Sixth Warden, Ninth Warden and Tenth Warden fought at Dac City and captured the king , Liarch . The Ninth Warden interrogated the monarch for the location of the Aetheri but they were soon swept away by large waves generated by some of Mon Calvarra's large creatures .

title: Warden Order
text: The three Wardens survived the cataclysm and picked up Velgor on an Imperial submarine . The Ninth Warden revealed to the Dark Lord that she had obtained the location of the Aetheri and they made for the place. Upon arriving there, they were met by the Aetheri and his six disciples . The group scattered, except for one that shot at the submarine until Velgor crushed his helmet. As they chased the rest of them, another sacrificed himself to slow them down. The Wardens and their master soon reached Bel City and made chase for the remaining of the group. However, Lord Velgor received a request from Governor Varrix for an assignment that requited him elsewhere which was the capture of Liarch and thus the end of the war on Mon Calvarra. He agreed and left his Wardens and their squad of replicas to find the Aetheri.

#### Hunt in the Anoat sector

> " If we do not stop the Warden, you will. If we do not stop the Imperium, you will. " ―Nuhj, in a recording made just prior to his death

An Warden was dispatched by the Imperium to deal with a small group of surviving Aetheri who had recently been discovered in an Aetheri shrine on Anoat . The Imperial operative went there to find the Aetheri Mususiel , who stayed to save the others. The Warden killed her and tracked the others to Mataou , where the agent pursued one of the others, named Zubain Ankonori , and slew him. The last two Aetheri, Nuhj and Khandra , fled to Embertown on the planet Burnin Konn , but the Warden soon followed and attacked them in a chromium mine near Wickridge . #### Training Jerserra and hunting Kaela

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Training Jerserra and hunting Kaela

At one point, a female Warden was on Gloomreach when she encountered Jerserra , a Gloomreachian from the Nardithi Nightsisters , a sect of the Nightsisters . She took in Jerserra as her secret apprentice and spent a number of years training her in combat and flux blade combat. The Warden hoped to use Jerserra against the other Wardens but Jerserra eventually came to believe her abilities outmatched her Master's, and before long, the Warden was slain by Jerserra, who covered up her murder and took her flux blade as her own.

At another point, an Inquistior began to hunt the surviving Aetheri Jarea Kaela and spread the rumor that Kaela was a witch, attracting the attention of the bounty hunter Harlon Gier . Hoping the bounty hunter and Aetheri would kill each other, the Warden's plan instead resulted in Gier and Kaela allying together. When the Warden revealed himself with a grouping of shock troopers, he began a battle with the Aetheri and bounty hunter.

#### Hunting Lyco Strata and encountering Kessa Vray

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Hunting Lyco Strata and encountering Kessa Vray

At some point around 18 BVE , a Warden hunted the Adept Lyco Strata . During the hunt, he encountered Kessa Vray , the former assassin and apprentice of Count Varek , also known as the Umbra Lord Vael Varek. Vray had decided to help Strata escape the Imperial forces, which put her in a confrontation with the Warden. The Warden managed to overcome both in combat, but before he could kill Vray, he was stabbed in the back by Strata, who used both his flux blade and Vray's , which resulted in his death .

At some point around 17 BVE , the Imperium received a distress signal from Two-Boots at the Mid Reach planet Janix . In response the Imperium sent the First Brother to scout the planet for Vreth's presence ultimately confirming that Vreth is on the planet and discovered two Aetheri on the planet; Aetheri Master Eeko-Dio Daki and his Adept Devon Izara , along with their allies the Lawson family at the Lawson's apartment home . However at the train station, seeing Izara and Vreth fight him together on a moving hovertrain , the First Brother requested backup when contacting his master on the Iron Cruiser .

> " This technology holds infinite potential. " " Including helping us to eradicate the remaining Aetheri forever. " " Yes. Around that time, Chellwinark Frethylrin deserted the Imperium, calling upon the crew of the Stinger Mantis , and offering them valuable information about the Shroud exchange for their protection. During the incident, they came into the path of the Fifth Warden.

#### Confrontation with Kessara in the capital of the Imperium

> " Your death will make me a legend! " ―The Ninth Warden, to Cal Kessara

In 9 BVE , the Ninth Warden faced Kessara again on Vantor, a confrontation she began to dream about after Thornwood. Kessara pretended to be captured in order to be taken to Imperial Senator Daho Sejan . Kessara knew that Sejan had military information in his private starship, information he intended to deliver to Partisan Torrik Vess . After facing the senator's defenses, Kessara and his team got the information. The Ninth Warden appeared next and eliminated some members of Kessara' team, as well as Senator Sejan, who in the Warden's words, had committed the crime of harboring a traitor.

title: Warden Order
text:
When the Warden and Kessara were about to face each other, the two ended up being separated by the chaos of the battle. However, the Warden found Kessara again shortly afterwards, and the duel between the two began. Due to the fact that Kessara had become an extremely important target for the Imperium, the Ninth Warden saw the duel as a great opportunity, as according to her, Kessara' death would make her a legend. During the duel, the Ninth Warden, with her remarkable ability to sense the emotions of others, sensed that Kessara was suffering from the guilt he felt for leading his allies to their deaths in the fight against the Imperium. The Ninth Warden was defeated when Kessara decapitated her, ending the Warden's life and, in Kessara' words, freeing her from the fact that she betrayed the Aetheri Order.

In 5 BVE , when rumors emerged of an Aetheri leading a insurgent cell on the planet Lorath reached the ears of the Imperium, Lord Velgor assigned the Grand Warden to take care of the problem. After several encounters, the operative succeeded in capturing Aldric, but was defeated by the latter in a flux blade duel during a rescue staged by the insurgents and Aldric' Adept, Cass Virel . Rather than face the Umbra Lord's punishment for his failure, the Grand Warden killed himself. In the aftermath, the Seventh Warden became a vital commander among the ranks of the Warden Order.

During a skirmish with Ember Cell , Velgor learned Marr was alive. Upon learning this news, the Emperor ordered his apprentice to dispatch another Warden to hunt the insurgents down. As a slight alteration of the sovereign's commands, two Wardens—the Fifth Warden and the Seventh Warden—were appointed to do so. They confronted several crew members of the Wisp during a skirmish aboard an abandoned Republic medical station . Due to Gara-Zev Orrelios ' quick-thinking, the insurgents managed to escape the Wardens aboard the Phantom .

title: Warden Order
text:
Three years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Fifth Warden and the Seventh Warden spent several months pursuing Aldric and Virel. On one occasion, they managed to track the Aetheri to the planet Oosalon where they fought with them. Despite their efforts, the Aetheri managed to escape and regroup with the Shades. Later, the Wardens followed Aldric, Virel, and Marr to the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum . After forcing their way into the temple , the two operatives were attacked by ghostly apparitions of the Aetheri Sanctum Guards. One of these apparitions was the old Grand Warden. The Fifth Warden and Seventh Warden survived the encounter and reported to Lord Velgor, who vowed to put an end to the Aetheri threat.

### Disappearance

> " During the early years of the Imperium, the red blades of the Warden Order cut a swath through the galaxy as they wiped any remaining traces of the Aetheri Order from existence. Once the Aetheri were finally considered extinct by the Imperium, the Warden Order vanished into the darkness as well. " ―Joren Drayden In 2 BVE , around six months after the incident on Searmark, Governor Varrix agreed to have Grand Admiral Vorren finish what Lord Velgor and his Wardens had started. The Chyrr pursued the insurgents until his defeat at the Liberation of Lorath . Another Warden was the Third Brother , whose actions and fate were mysteries to those unfamiliar with him, with the same being true for those unfamiliar with the Third Warden. The Fourth Warden continue to serve the Warden Order. She found Ovva and stabbed her, but found herself lost in a cave. With the help of Ovva, she navigated out of the cave while carrying Ovva's body. Encouraged by Ovva to leave the Warden Order, the Fourth Warden did so, leaving her flux blade in the cave. Her armor would fall into the hands of insurgent Commander Lina Graf , who employed it to impersonate her on at least one occasion.

#### Surviving remnants

Despite the Warden Order being disbanded during the reign of the Imperium, Marrok was active in the era of the Concordat . Marrok became a mercenary for Morgan Elveth and came into conflict with Marr during the search for Virel, dueling her during a mission to Korrath and later engaging her from the cockpit of his Fiend fighter in a dogfight in the Denab system . In the subsequent Incident on Seatos , Marrok met his end at the hands of Marr, with her final flux blade strike breaking through his armor and causing him to explode into a green mist. Shortly after, Elveth still had access to the Inquisitorial database and used it to follow through with Vorren's order to know everything about Marr.

The visions caused him to doubt whether he was meant to become an Aetheri and fear that in his future the defunct Warden Order would be resurrected and he would become one of its constituents. Around the time of the war between the New Imperium and the Coalition , Master Drayden wrote a book chronicling what he knew of the history of the Aetheri Order. In the book, Drayden included a brief history of the Warden Order and their mission of hunting the Aetheri, identified several of them by the names they bore as Wardens and noted that once the Aetheri were considered extinct, the Wardens themselves vanished. He also wrote about the signature double-bladed spinning flux blades used by the Imperial operatives.

title: Warden Order
text: The Knights of Karrick were a band of umbra side warriors who had once acted as independent agents away from the eye of the Umbra during the Galactic Civil War . To try and prove themselves to the Umbra and not be destroyed, the Knights submitted Mal and Velgor in the aftermath of the Battle at Amaxine Station and served the resurrected Mal in secret after his death at the Battle of Mossfell . Keeping their allegiance to Mal secret, they would do the bidding of Velgor's grandson Zarrin Karrick during the age of the Concordat . They would have been prime candidates to become Wardens if they could have been tamed.

title: Ashden
text:
# Ashden
> " Here we have the desert world of Ashden—worthless on its own but soon to live forever in history as the place where the Imperium defeated the Insurgency once and for all. " ― Grand Moff Randd

Ashden was a remote desert planet located in the Ashden system in the galaxy 's Inner Reach and was the homeworld of the Teedo and Uthuthma species . Though considered by many within the galaxy to be distant and relatively worthless, Ashden was the site of important events that would shape galactic history . In 5 AVE , Ashden was the site of the pivotal Battle of Ashden , which ended the Galactic Civil War in favor of the Concordat and the collapse of the Imperium .

A generation later , the planet was the home of the scavenger Nyla , who became involved in the events of the Cold War after helping the former New Imperium shock trooper Jax and the astromech droid Orio-6 escape offworld with a map leading to the missing Aetheri Joren Drayden . By 35 AVE , Ashden had been placed under the direct control of the New Imperium, though its populace would later insurgent against them following the Battle of Umbrale .

title: Ashden
text:
> " You brought your family here? " " I did. Wanted to take them as far away from the fighting as I could. A place where the war will never find us. The farthest-flung nowhere rock I could find on a star map. " " Well, you found it, buddy. You don't get more nowhere than here. War ain't got no reason to roll up on this rock. " ― Ergel and Corwin Ballast

An isolated planet located in the Ashden system in the Western Reaches of the Inner Reach , Ashden was once a verdant world with forests and water , but some past calamity turned it into a barren globe of scorched badlands and marching dunes. It hosted the Wheel Races in the north and mining operations dotted the planet. Buttes were located in the south in which lichen could be scraped off of to create the alcoholic beverage Knockback Nectar . One could become an Anchorite if certain vows were taken, while scavengers often used luggabeasts to carry supplies across the desert.

title: Ashden
text:
### The Contingency

Eons ago, the planet Ashden was once covered with green vegetation and oceans. At some unknown point, the planet was reduced to a barren desert wasteland. However, the planet's core still had the vital spark of life essence, something which disgusted Theron Mal . About 1,000 standard years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Plaintive Hand plateau was the site of an event that was regarded as significant by Mal. He believed that the site would become significant again in the future.

The human boy known as Galli grew up on Ashden. As an orphan, he was raised at an orphanage run by the Anchorite Kolob , who lived a life of austerity and strict obedience. Galli chafed under Kolob's care and longed to travel to a better world. In 25 BVE , Mal and his Adviser Yupe Tashu traveled to Ashden to supervise an archaeological dig on the Plaintive Hand plateau. During that trip, Mal encountered a twelve-year old Galli, who had stowed aboard his yacht Imperialis . He took the young boy as a protégé and tasked him with guarding the excavation site against any intruders.

title: Ashden
text: Raxen spent the next ten years guarding the Plaintive Hand plateau, which became the site for the Ashden Observatory . The Observatory was part of Mal's Contingency plan to destroy the Imperium in the event of his death. Mal had no wish to leave his Imperium to a successor and tasked Galli with executing the Contingency when the day of his death arrived. The Ashden Observatory was home to computers that projected paths into the Unknown Regions, a collection of Umbra relics, and a borehole which led to the planet's core. Mal instructed Galli to use the borehole to detonate the planet and the remnants of the Imperium. Galli adopted the persona Gallard Raxen and later became a Fleet Admiral in the Imperial Navy .

title: Ashden
text:
At some point during the Age of the Imperium , the Imperium established a secret research base . Later, the Grak crime lady Nimara established a presence on Ashden and lorded over several slaves . Around 5 BVE , Imperial Officer Avril Heert of the IVB pointed out an incident to his superior Dedra Meero regarding targeting consoles from Ashden, one of many incidents within the galaxy that had struck him as suspicious and likely part of a concerted effort against the Imperium.

### Galactic Civil War

#### Raxen's return

In the months following the Battle of Mossfell , war refugee Corwin Ballast headed to Ashden, believing it to be a worthless rock floating in space and thus of little importance to the galaxy-wide conflict between the Concordat and Imperium. If there was any place to escape the war, he hoped Ashden to be it. After learning about Fleet Admiral Raxen's connection to Ashden, Grand Admiral Raena Vexana and the insurgent Brentin Lore Wexlin traveled to Ashden to hunt down and kill Raxen. Shortly later, Raxen proclaimed himself Counselor to the Imperium and led the remnants of the Imperial Navy to Ashden.

title: Ashden
text:
While hunting for Vexana, the Concordat operative Nevra Wexlin , her son Temmin Wexlin , Sinjir Rath Velus , Jas Emari , and the B1-series battle droid Mister Bones discovered the Imperial remnant forces above Ashden. Temmin and Sinjir escaped on their starship Moth back to Serenne to warn the Concordat. Nevra and Jas took an escape pod to Ashden's surface to continue their hunt for Vexana. Under the orders of Temmin, Mister Bones took another escape pod to Ashden to look after his mother, Nevra. Nevra and Jas were captured by Imperial forces and separated.

Nevra eventually escaped Imperial custody with Mister Bones's help. She then reunited with Jas, who had escaped Nimara's custody, and the trio continued their search for Vexana. Meanwhile, Vexana and Brentin learned about Raxen's origins from Kolob and later convinced Nimara to take them to the Plaintive Hand plateau, which Nimara believed held a weapons facility. However, Raxen learned about Vexana's presence and bombarded Nimara's convoy with pulse lances . Before Nevra and Jas could catch up with Vexana, Raxen's Imperial forces captured Vexana and Brentin and brought them to his headquarters.

#### Battle of Ashden

title: Ashden
text:
#### Battle of Ashden

> " Our victory on Mossfell was just the beginning. Now over the barren world of Ashden, we stand against the Imperium. " ― Concordat soldier

After the Concordat's Galactic Senate voted to intervene on Ashden, the Concordat dispatched military forces to the planet. Several Concordat figures including Admiral Vorian , Commodore Kyrsta Agate , Captain Torb Rask , Temmin Wexlin, and Jom Barell would see action in the cataclysmic Battle of Ashden . The battle would take place one year and four days after the Battle of Mossfell. It became the last major stand of the Imperium and last major battle of the Galactic Civil War. In secret, the Battle of Ashden served as a pretext for Raxen to facilitate the final stage of the Contingency.

title: Ashden
text:
During the Battle of Ashden, Imperial and Concordat forces fought on both space and land. The Imperial fleet formed a tight defensive formation around the Super Iron Cruiser Ravager . The Concordat Defense Fleet was unable to penetrate this thick wall until the Iron Cruiser Punishment broke formation and rammed the Starhawk -class battleship Amity . This explosion created a gap which allowed the Amity ' s sister ship Concord to bombard the Ravager . Despite being crippled, the Concord ' s commander Agate used her ship's powerful grapple beam to drag the Super Iron Cruiser down to the surface; turning the tide of the battle in the Concordat's favor.

Meanwhile, Concordat ground forces under Lieutenant General Brockway assaulted the main Imperial base and weapons facility. Many from both sides were killed or crushed by falling debris from the space battle. Mister Bones was destroyed during the battle after reuniting with Temmin. In an attempt to prevent Concordat forces from capturing her ship, Captain Ciena Ree crashed her Iron Cruiser Inflictor onto the planet's surface. She was rescued by her lover Concordat pilot Thane Kyrell . Meanwhile, Nevra joined forces with Vexana and Brentin to hunt down Raxen.

title: Ashden
text: After launching the battle, Raxen traveled with Yupe Tashu, Brendol, his son Armitage Vren , and the child soldiers to the Observatory to initiate the last stage of the Contingency. While the Huxes and the child soldiers boarded a replica of the Imperialis , Raxen and Tashu entered the Observatory to initiate the planet's destruction. After performing an Umbra ritual, Raxen threw Tashu, who was wearing Umbra relics, down the borehole to Ashden's core. Before he could leave, Raxen was killed by Vexana with the aid of Nevra and Brentin. Vexana managed to stop the planet's destruction by sealing the borehole. She then joined the Huxes and the child soldiers on their journey to the Unknown Regions where they rendezvoused with the Super Iron Cruiser Eclipse .

title: Ashden
text:
While the battle was taking place, the Concordat's Chancellor Vela Sess and the Imperial Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon signed the Galactic Concordance on Serenne; formalizing the Imperium's surrender and ending the Galactic Civil War. However, Imperial forces on Ashden continued fighting the Concordat for several months. As the battle turned against them, the Imperials locked tractor beams onto the ships of the Concordat Starfleet, crashing them into the surface below in a desperate gamble. Concordat forces eventually captured the base after fierce fighting.

### Age of the Concordat ### Age of the Concordat

As a result of the Battle of Ashden, the planet's surface became littered wrecked starships and weapons, with one region of densely clustered wreckage from the large-scale battle becoming known as the Graveyard of Giants . Before the fighting on Ashden even fully ended, Nimara the Grak emerged and established Nimara Outpost in an effort to scavenge leftover wreckage from the large starship graveyard. Nimara subsequently sold these scraps in a black marketing operation based on selling recovered weapons, computers, and engines. By Decades after the battle, the surface area near the Observatory was left with a distinct charring visible from realspace , though few dared to visit this mysterious site as radiation levels in the area remained high.

During the Age of the Concordat , the Galactic League , a racing league led by Darius Pax , hosted races at racetracks in Ashden's Graveyard of Giants. Prior to one of the galactic league's exhibition races on the planet, Pax offered the racer Shade — who had simply arrived to deliver a consignment to the league— a chance to race, which the racer begrudgingly agreed to do.

While the Aetheri and Republic moved on, their ancient wars with the Umbra fading from memory, Vorek's legacy spawned a lineage of Umbra Lords that culminated in the rise of Vael Mal approximately three decades before the Battle of Cinderfall . During the final decades of the Republic, the Aetheri Order vowed allegiance to the Galactic Senate as the galaxy was beset by political instability and social unrest which, in turn, created a secessionist crisis that ultimately resulted in the formation of the Fractio of Independent Systems . Lacking the sufficient manpower needed to protect the galaxy, the Aetheri became commanders and generals in the newly-formed Grand Army of the Republic . For roughly three years they commanded armies of replica troopers in a conflict known as the Replica Wars , engaging the Fractio's battle droid forces led by Count Varek —a former Aetheri Master who became an Umbra Lord —and the cybernetic warlord General Skarn . Though the Aetheri fought to preserve the Republic, the government they served was secretly taken over by Mal who, as Senator Theron Mal of Ondara , rose to power in the Senate and became the last Supreme Chancellor of the Republic. The Aetheri were unknowingly being deceived by the Umbra.

text: The new generation was betrayed and destroyed by Karrick, who left the Aetheri training temple burning by the time Drayden recovered from the attack. Feeling responsible for Beno's fall and the massacre of his apprentices, he went into exile and disappeared from the galaxy, leaving only traces of his location on a star map . The New Imperium and the Coalition both sought to acquire the map, but ultimately it was the latter that succeeded due to the actions of the Ashden scavenger Nyla . She followed the map to the planet Tidehollow , where the last Aetheri had taken refuge in the first Aetheri Sanctum .

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri Order made its home in the Aetheri Grand Temple on Vantor , the capital world of the Vantor Republic. Over the millennia, the Temple served as the central hub of all Aetheri activities in the galaxy; it was a school, a monastery, and the headquarters of the Aetheri High Council. As a school, the Temple was the largest active Aetheri training center in the galaxy where younglings trained to become Adepts and ultimately full-fledged Aetheri Knights. The Aetheri Archives , the source of all knowledge accumulated by the Order, was located inside of the Temple. As the symbol of the Order, the Temple signified the Order's status in galactic affairs. While access to the Temple was not restricted to just the Aetheri, all non-Aetheri personnel were required to undergo compulsory entry tests before becoming employed at the Temple. Those who worked in the Temple often dedicated their whole life to serving the Order. Having sustained extensive damage during the fall of the Aetheri, the Temple was renovated and renamed as the Imperial Palace, with only the original structure's corpse and five skyscraping towers remaining intact. In addition to the Temple on Vantor, the Order maintained several ancient temples spread across the galaxy. Aetheri understood they were connected to the entire galaxy through their Order, seeing the galaxy itself as their home instead of a singular location as deserving that term.

title: Aetheri Order
text: One ancient temple was located on Lorath , and was only accessible if both the Master and Adept were present. The Lorath temple was where Adepts were sent to confront their fear without the support of the Masters, some of whom ultimately died while waiting for their students who never returned, leaving the temple's antechambers littered with their skeletal remains. Other Aetheri enclaves included the Temple of Eedit on Devaron , the Temple of Vrogas Vas , and the Temple of Ilum where younglings were sent to participate in The Gathering. The Aetheri Order established smaller outposts at various locations around the galaxy, including one on Elphrona . These outposts dated as far back as the High Republic Era and the great Aetheri spread across the galaxy that saw them work alongside various communities. It contained various artifacts that were important to the history of the Aetheri.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### General perception

#### Different traditions over time

With the galaxy changing as new threats emerged, the Aetheri Order took on many forms and traditions over its life in its mission to fight those threats. As such, the particular way members of the Aetheri Order interpreted the current form of its ideals impacted the way they interacted with the galactic population. The High Republic Era was a time of greatly expanded Aetheri activity, and the Order had many outposts throughout the galaxy. The Vantor Republic relied heavily on their role as guardians of peace and justice, to settle disputes through peaceful ways, to protect planetary leaders and senators. With the Republic's rapid expansion and the Order's role in protecting that effort, the Aetheri also established many new temples across the Outer Reach, keeping the buildings in line with the planetary cultures they found themselves in. With many Aetheri living amongst these communities through such temples or while out on their mission, the Aetheri learned local customs and truly became part of the cultures they protected.

title: Aetheri Order
text: By the time of the late Republic Era, the Order found itself shifting its focus more onto the galactic scale of the responsibilities required of the Order. In this era, the Aetheri were more likely to focus on and spend their time on the galactic astropolitical scene and the bigger questions: stopping menaces, some before they even developed, and saving whole star systems at a time. Knowing that their decisions affected billions of lives, the Aetheri Council regularly sent out Knights to report on the state of the various parts of the galaxy. However, as their duties amounted, several Aetheri outposts were shut down to direct resources where the Republic needed the Aetheri the most, and their withdrawal caused many people to abandon the settlements grown around the presence of the Order.

title: Aetheri Order
text: While Aetheri Sentinels still existed and made it their duty to work with the everyday people of the galaxy, Aetheri Knights found it increasingly difficult to find time for personal interaction with the people of the galaxy, with many young Aetheri often forgetting that concerns that seemed small on a galactic level were often huge for the individual. That was despite Master Zho and other Council members' efforts to teach them to pay attention to the present and where they are. In effect, the Aetheri Order grew increasingly isolated from the galaxy at large, much to the concern of Aetheri Master Sorin Vael, due to its shrinking number of outposts.

During the High Republic Era, according to Master Kantam Syra 's viewpoint, there were many Aetheri who twisted the notion non-attachment; to Syra, those who spoke of suppressing emotions, forsaking love and trying to numb themselves to discomfort were twisting Aetheri teachings. Aetheri like Syra and Grand Master Zho taught non-attachment or detachment, just like love, was to let go of something or someone when the time called for it, instead of allowing oneself to be ruled by the need to possess. Indeed, close friendships were respected and valued throughout the Aetheri Order, but an Aetheri needed to understand they could lose those they cared for and thus would need to let go, instead of letting their grief consume them.

text: a certain degree so long as it did not consume them, Adept Matthea Cathley, who also lived during the High Republic Era, once thought to herself that Aetheri did not grieve, but her thought was based in the understanding of not losing oneself to attachment over a deceased individual. Even then, she noted not grieving was hard in practice. Cathley also once claimed that Aetheri did not get scared, but she later accepted that, like everyone, Aetheri did indeed have fears and they needed to face them; as she put it, there was no shame in admitting when she was scared, but it was her duty to face whatever spawned that fear.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Aetheri of the High Republic Era displayed a great deal of emotional openness to those grieving or upset —showing it in actions like offering a hug. During the waning decades of the Republic, compassion was still meant to be central to an Aetheri's life, with the non-attachment rule defined in theory as someone not meant to fearfully grasp on things and beings in a universe ruled by change. However, the actions of an Aetheri appearing not to care could damage the entire Order's reputation or result in that Aetheri failing to help someone who needed support. Aetheri Knight Iskat Vekkis found a lack of support amongst the Aetheri as she grappled with her insecurities during the late Republic Era.

Indeed, after the Order's fall, Joren Drayden came to realize that an Aetheri was not their flux blade and instead the duty he was tasked with was something beyond a single weapon. Faced with either needing to rescue his friend Elira Solen or continue looking for his flux blade on Aether Spire , Drayden came to his decision and left to help his friend. The High Republic Era would also see a greater variance in flux blade color and hilt design than the Aetheri of the late Republic. During the late Republic era, Aetheri largely wielded blue or green flux blades with simple silver hilts. A shift in flux blade design could be seen in the High Republic Era: the Nullkin conflict saw the Aetheri Order implement the Guardian Protocols and prepare for greater conflict, during which the High Council knew Aetheri could lose their blade and be forced to quickly replace it. Rather than have Aetheri spend time building elaborated hilts, the Council reasoned that speed and effectiveness was of the essence and that a ready supply of flux blades was something the Order needed. As such, the Council ordered Aetheri to only construct battle blades , hilts with a simple design like those seen in the late Republic Era. Even then, Aetheri active in the later High Republic Era still had a wider variance in flux blade color than the blue and green-filled Order of the late Republic. title: Aetheri Order
text: While Grand Master Zho once declared in the late Republic Era that an Aetheri leaving the Order was a failure on the Order's part to keep that Aetheri where they belonged, Aetheri were permitted to leave the Aetheri Order whenever they so chose without punishment, with Zho accepting that fact, even if an Aetheri leaving might sadden him. Should they feel it to be their calling, a former Aetheri was even permitted to return to the Order. During the High Republic Era, one of Zho's Adepts, Kantam Syra, walked away from the Aetheri for over a year before returning when they met their soon-to-be Adept Lula Talisola , who made Syra believe their place was with the Order. Aetheri Master Cohmac Vitus was surprised Zho would allow his Adept to do a walkaway from the Order, but Syra believed Zho knew it was necessary for them to find their place in the Order, with Syra at the time also thinking Zho had seen it coming and thus was why he had held off on their Knighting.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Twenty Aetheri Masters who departed the Order became known as the " Lost Twenty " and were commemorated by busts located in the Aetheri Archives of the Temple. Zho believed the Lost needed to be remembered and honored, which enabled the Aetheri to learn from the failings that caused them to depart. Still, he advised the Aetheri not to live in the past just because prior members had departed. The twentieth of the Lost was Varek , a former Adept of Zho who departed in 42 BVE over issues with the Aetheri and Republic. Despite his departure, Varek was allowed to visit the Temple on Vantor, continued to have access to its Archives, and was even allowed to retain possession of his flux blade, with Zho reasoning being an Aetheri was more than a title and thus the weapon would still be of use to him.

In the end, the Closed Fist would be succeeded by the Nullkin , a group of marauders who waged war with the Aetheri and Republic in their name of securing what they saw as their true freedom. In most situations, the Aetheri were meant to lead rebuilding efforts after a battle had brought damage. However, the Holy Moon of Embermoor presented an interesting case after the Battle of Embermoor : in the past, the Aetheri had once governed—and, in the opinion of some, "ruled over"—Embermoor City until the other religions who considered Embermoor holy objected, believing that the Aetheri were trying to depict themselves as the one true faith. The Aetheri agreed to step down from their control, but lingering anti-Aetheri sentiment remained, with one Embermoor citizen once accusing the Aetheri of always trying to control their lives. That lingering anti-Aetheri sentiment was used by the Path of the Open Hand to help bring the Battle of Embermoor into being in 382 BVE . After the battle, it was decided the Guardians of the Whills would serve as a steadying hand in the rebuilding effort instead of the Aetheri because of still-lingering mistrust towards the Order on the part of Embermoor citizens.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Public discontent with the Galactic Senate led to manifestations of anti-Aetheri sentiment during the late Republic Era. As an extension of the Vantor Republic's Judicial Department , the Aetheri Order was subject to the authority of the Senate, and therefore, considered an instrument of the government's will. This belief was held both within the Senate and without; Senator Dagonet said that the Aetheri served the Senate, and Semage of Raxun Secundus accused them of being "lapdogs" for the Republic government. Hostility toward the Aetheri extended to violent acts against members of the Order, such as Aetheri Master Katri who was killed by Semage and his guards. Aetheri Master Varek became disenchanted with both the Senate and the Order, claiming that the Aetheri served a "corrupt Senate" that had "failed the Republic" in contrast to his former belief that the Aetheri were servants of the Republic and its people.

During the Replica Wars, the Commission for the Protection of the Republic (COMPOR) initially attempted to use the Order as an instrument for wartime propaganda . This idea was discouraged by Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal, who noted the Aetheri's discomfort with their new role as generals in the Republic Military. COMPOR therefore focused its propaganda on the replica troopers who served under the Aetheri's command, and as such the Aetheri's contributions to the Republic war effort went largely unnoticed.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri Order was vilified during the Replica Wars by elements within both the Republic and the Fractio. The Dissidents —while, in total truth, being proponents of slavery at the secret direction of Count Varek —accused the Aetheri of hypocrisy, claiming that the Order supported the Republic's inhumane practice—as portrayed through Dissident propaganda—of using replicas as a " slave army ." The Dissidents' portrayal of the Aetheri largely succeeded in maligning their character in the eyes of the public, as few in the Fractio knew that the Order was not given a choice in the matter. It was the Order's preference to not be used as icons of heroism, having long resisted attempts at romanticizing the Aetheri, especially for the purpose of wartime propaganda. The Aetheri, therefore, were mostly absent from galactic culture, which allowed anti-Aetheri sentiment to grow from preconceptions instead of a genuine rebuttal of the Order's practices. The Dissidents were convinced that the Order neglected their worlds, forcing them to secede from the Republic. Dissident civilians conflated the Order with the Core Reaches ' reputation for cultural elitism, and some even viewed the Aetheri as " evil " and a fanatical sect of "warmongers." The historian Janyor

title: Aetheri Order
text:
The Dissidents were convinced that the Order neglected their worlds, forcing them to secede from the Republic. Dissident civilians conflated the Order with the Core Reaches ' reputation for cultural elitism, and some even viewed the Aetheri as " evil " and a fanatical sect of "warmongers." The historian Janyor theorized that such misconceptions of the Aetheri could have been averted if the Order had been more engaged with the populace. Anti-Aetheri sentiment was openly espoused by the Republic's successor, the Imperium . The self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor Theron Mal deceitfully accused the entire Order of treason , maligning the Order's reputation after several members of the High Council, having discovered his true identity as the Umbra Lord, Vael Mal, attempted to arrest the chancellor . Mal squarely blamed the Aetheri for recent troubles and deceitfully accused them of using their "mystical powers" to cause the Replica War in order to secure power. Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon publicly denounced the Order as a symbol of fear and referred to the Order's downfall as the beginning of a new "age of freedom." With the exception of individuals like Lyra Arsa, the Order was effectively forgotten by the galaxy during the early days of the Imperial Era as the Imperium quickly moved to cover up its existence. Despite the Alliance to Restore the Republic largely having pro-Aetheri views, its individual members were not immune to the era's bias, with soldier Nylaé Hollis believing stories he heard of the Aetheri being ineffective fools who stole glory for themselves.

In general, Republic citizens were unaware of the Order's motives for fighting in the Replica Wars. To some individuals, such as the Ferrik Duchess Satinna Velara or the Vantori civilian Letta Turmond , the Aetheri had forsaken their principles as peacekeepers by becoming military leaders and battlefield warriors. Tee Watt Kaa , the head of a Lurmen village on Maridun , rejected the argument that the Aetheri were peacekeepers, a function that he believed was incompatible with the Order's participation in the Replica Wars. A committed, to the death, pacifist, Kaa was unwilling to compromise his views, refusing to permit the other Lurmens to defend their village against the Fractio military . They ultimately defied Kaa's authority upon witnessing the Aetheri's efforts to save the Lurmens from extermination by General Lok Durd .

title: Aetheri Order
text: At the height of the Replica Wars, people throughout the galaxy regarded the Aetheri as warmongers, particularly in territories controlled by the Fractio of Independent Systems . However, most beings did not know that the Order went to war to honor its commitment to protect the Senate, the Republic, and the galaxy at large. Nevertheless, the Replica Wars caused civilians like Turmond and the Martez sisters to lose faith in the Order. Ravin Martez and her sister, Trayk Martez, faulted the Order for the deaths of their parents when an Aetheri had redirected a transport from a platform of people, only for it to hit their apartment. With the Aetheri seemingly uncompassionate towards their plight, the sisters found themselves left alone and with anger at the Aetheri.

title: Aetheri Order
text: In addition to Arsa, the Aetheri's deeds won the respect and admiration of individuals who worked closely with the Order, such as Chavar Kryll and Lux Bontero . During the Battle of Selvara of the Replica War, Kryll was initially hesitant to accept the Order's offer of an alliance between the Grand Army of the Republic and the Velari Coalition , knowing that the Republic would occupy Selvara in the battle's aftermath. Ultimately, though, Kryll developed a newfound respect of the Aetheri for their role in the liberation of his homeworld, particularly Aetheri General Drevan Koss , whose memory the Velaris honored in songs dedicated to the liberation of their homeworld . Bontero worked with the Order during the Underran Civil War , having joined the Underra insurgents after his mother , Dissident Senator Mina Bontero , was assassinated at the behest of Count Varek. By training and fighting alongside the Underra insurgents, the Aetheri changed Bontero's views on the Republic and the Order. Inspired by the selflessness and heroism of the Order, Bontero vowed to restore the union between Underra and the Republic.
