During this early period, the Order also established itself on Ossus, Embermoor, Xenxiar , and other worlds. Later, some Aetheri scholars argued that a number of locations could be considered the birthplace of the Order. The scholars argued that Vantor, Embermoor, and Ossus as well as worlds shrouded in myth, such as Tython and Tidehollow could all be considered candidate worlds for the Order's birth and the location of the first Aetheri Sanctum.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri religion, as it was called by Joren Drayden, was based around eight "sacred texts" that "describe tenets, history, and specific guidance to those studying the path of the Aetheri." These texts included the Rammahgon and the Aionomica —separated into two volumes, Aionomicum I and Aionomicum II . These books included a number of aspects of the Aetheri religion that appeared to have little influence on later Aetheri, such as references to "gods" and the World Between Worlds . They also included more mundane information, such as flux blade designs. The theology of the Aetheri religion changed over time; many Aetheri, such as Master Odan-Urr , annotated even the sacred texts. Much was added to the Aetheri canon over time, giving rise to the belief that the Aionomicum II doubled in size during its compilation. The fortunes of the Aetheri waxed and waned over the centuries; multiple times throughout its long history, the Order had been reduced to a mere handful of adherents.

title: Aetheri Order
text: At some point prior to around 20,000 BVE , an Aetheri sect known as the Ordu Aspectu broke off from the Aetheri Order. Led by the enigmatic Rur and his second in command, Amon , they sought to achieve the secrets to immortality. Eventually, a conflict broke out between them and the orthodox Aetheri. The conflict ended with the signing of a peace treaty . The treaty allowed the Ordu Aspectu to continue their research but under Aetheri scrutiny. During his experimentation, Rur attempted to copy his intellect into his citadel's computer core, only to accidentally transfer his very sentience as well. When the Aetheri sought to investigate the computer closer around 20,000 BVE, the computer activated the citadel's security droids, killing all members of the Ordu Aspectu and Aetheri alike; but not before it was deactivated by Rur and Amon before they died themselves, thus ending the Ordu Aspectu.

title: Aetheri Order
text: About five-thousand years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Order eventually came to be headquartered at Vantor, wherein they built a Temple that would pose as their main hub for thousands of generations. Underneath the structure lay buried an ancient Umbra shrine , the inherent power of which was believed by the contemporary Aetheri to have been neutralized and successfully capped. In truth, that power had seeped upward and outward since its entombment, infiltrating the hallways and rooms above, and weakening the Aetheri Order for millennia without their knowledge. It was during this time that the Aetheri Order came into the service of what would be later called the First Republic. Promising to uphold its ideals, the Aetheri fought to maintain peace and freedom. When the First Republic outlawed slavery, the Aetheri set about to free those held, notably under the Zygeran Slave Imperium . The Aetheri declared war on Zygerrians , whose economic success had resulted from enslaving beings from all corners of the galaxy before selling them at auctions. The Aetheri Order managed to put an end to their practices, destroying their imperium and exiling them to their homeworld, Zygera . The Zygerrians developed a fierce hatred for the Aetheri as a result.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Conflicts also arose between the Aetheri and the inhabitants of the world of Ferrum who had rapidly developed into a warlike culture in which strength was valued above all else. Their beliefs of continual warfare went contrary to the Aetheri's mission of protecting the weak, they quickly mobilized to stop the destructive Ferriks from expanding in the galaxy. The constant warfare was a strain and, as the First Republic crumbled, the Ferrik warriors sacked the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor, an event during which Pre Vizsla 's ancestors stole the Darksaber .

Prior to 1032 BVE , the galaxy entered an era known as the Dark Age . During this time the Aetheri-Umbra War occurred. Early on in the war, the Umbra attacked and captured Vantor and with it the Aetheri Sanctum. Towards the end of the war the Aetheri reclaimed the Republic capital and their temple during the liberation of Vantor .

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Even as the First Republic collapsed, the Aetheri emerged victorious from their wars with the Umbra. In their constant thirst for power, the Umbra had weakened themselves through infighting, which allowed the Aetheri to defeat the weakened Umbra. Unbeknownst to the Aetheri at the time, Vael Vorek remained as the sole surviving Dark Lord of the Umbra . As a result of the infighting that weakened the Umbra, Aetheri Knights were able to defeat the Umbra at the Mid Reach planet Ruusan This confrontation nearly destroyed the ancient Umbra Order, and forced the Umbra to go into hiding . After this, Vorek established the Rule of Two , declaring that the Umbra thenceforth would consist of an Umbra Master and an Umbra apprentice . Vorek's Rule of Two was discovered by the Aetheri, but, as recounted by an imprint of later Aetheri Elzar Mann , the Aetheri Order believed they ended Vorek's rule. His death falsely convinced his enemies that the Umbra had truly died out.

### Keepers of the peace

#### Knights of the High Republic

Across the stars

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Keepers of the peace

#### Knights of the High Republic

Across the stars

> " I just didn't realize the Aetheri ever had an official presence so far from the Core. " " It's probably High Republic Era. It was a time of greatly expanded Aetheri activity throughout the galaxy. " ―Joren Drayden and Lor Saan Tarka

The formation of the modern Vantor Republic heralded a new era of democracy, peace, and prosperity under the Galactic Senate and its elected leader, the Supreme Chancellor. Due to the Vantor Republic's demilitarization, the Aetheri Order fully embraced their responsibilities as peacekeepers and rejected their roles as soldiers. Assisted by the Republic Judicials , the Aetheri were responsible for maintaining law and order, namely by mediating conflicts to bring about peaceful solutions between various rival factions and planets, as well as serving as interplanetary law enforcement by pursuing wanted and dangerous criminals, pirates , and smugglers . While they ultimately collapsed, the Vantor Republic and the Aetheri Order were able to preside over a thousand years of peace sustained without major warfare. One of their philosophical sayings was " the simplest gesture of kindness can fill a galaxy with hope. "

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Defeating the Path

> " The Night of Sorrow is over, but the brave warriors who fell will not be forgotten. These Aetheri came to answer our call of need without hesitation or doubt, because at the heart of the Aetheri is a heart that fights for good. These Aetheri fought bravely and selflessly, against the darkness that is ever-present in this galaxy. […] As stars are born and die, so does time move forward. Relentlessly so. And yet we fight. We will never stop fighting for the light and life in this galaxy. " ―Master Creighton Sun speaks after the Battle of Dalna

title: Aetheri Order
text: Adept Sav Malagán fought alongside pirate queen Maz Oru 's crew during the Battle of Embermoor , a conflict instigated by the Path. Several Aetheri teams investigating the Path converged on Dalna, where the Battle of Dalna exploded into being. The conflict had such a high death count it would devolve into massacre arguably caused by Republic and Aetheri's close connection. All the same, much of the death was caused by the Path, which reformed into the war-like Path of the Closed Fist. During the battle, they also released Nameless that proved highly effective against the Aetheri. Nonetheless, many Dalnans held the Aetheri responsible for the massacre they remembered as the "Night of Sorrow." At the time, however, the defeat of the Path was seen as proof of the benefits of Aetheri-Republic partnership; as reasoned by former Supreme Chancellor Kyong Greylark , current Chancellor Orlen Mollo , and Master Zho, the Path's defeat was only possible thanks to the work between both organizations, with their alliance a strength they believed the galaxy could call on for centuries to come.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After the battle, Zho and Aetheri Master Creighton Sun also agreed to cover up all information on the Nameless, including keep details on the creatures out of the Aetheri Archives, until they learned more about the mysterious threat. However, one Aetheri who encountered the effects of the Nameless, Azlin Rell , abandoned the Order and attempted to learn more about the creatures. Driven mad from his fear and falling to the umbra side, Rell still heard the song Shrii ka rai ka rai from his encounter with the Nameless on Dalna and kept the secrets he learned tucked away, yet still lost due to his insanity, in his mind.

Conflict with the Nullkin

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Republic underestimated the Nullkin until the massive attack on Valo , where the raiders cut down Aetheri and civilian alike amid the Valo Republic Fair , which was supposed to be Chancellor Soh's show of unity for the Republic. When the Aetheri launched a counterattack through the Battle of Grizal , Ro unleashed the Great Leveler, which petrified Aetheri Master Loden Greatstorm , leaving the Aetheri to realize their enemy had a weapon they did not yet understand. The Republic and Aetheri Order grew closer during the Nullkin conflict, with Soh and her aides even continually trying to become part of the Aetheri High Council's meetings. As debate on how involved with the Republic they needed to become spread across the Order, many Aetheri expressed worry that the Order's focus was at risk of moving to politics and war. Vitus was one such Aetheri who questioned how much the Order actually owed the Republic, even though he agreed the Nullkin were a serious threat, while his Adept Reath Silas saw both sides to the debate.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
As the conflict and bloodshed carried on across the Galactic Frontier, more and more Aetheri fell in battle against the Nullkin, who the Aetheri came to see were ruthless enemies who lacked any form of honor. Many Aetheri had trouble adapting to the newly war-torn Outer Reach they needed to serve in. With it even coming to seem like acting only as peacekeepers was a recipe for defeat, Vitus came to believed the galaxy had grown to become a different place than the type the Aetheri Order was made for and refused to finch in battle. After Ro unleashed more Nameless during the destruction of Starlight Beacon , the Aetheri Order's reputation took a hit when it ordered a mass recall of its members back to Vantor; while Grand Master Pra-Tre Veter argued the Aetheri needed to retreat until they could learn how to fight the Nameless, some Republic officials took it as the Aetheri running away in fear.

Defeating the Nullkin

Ultimately, the Aetheri resumed their stand against the Nullkin under the Guardian Protocols and managed to defeat the muaraders, but Aetheri Master Keeve Trennis feared that the conflict had forever shifted the Aetheri Order.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After serving as an unwitting pawn for the Umbra, Sifas Dyen was betrayed by his childhood friend, the Aetheri Master Count Varek, who had him assassinated by the Gruv Syndicate at the behest of Mal. Disillusioned with the Aetheri Order, yet also ambitious for power, Varek rejected the light side and became an agent of Mal, adopting the moniker of Vael Varek. Following the Battle of Ondara, he replaced Vael Vreth (who was presumed dead) as the Umbra apprentice of Vael Mal. The Umbra guided the creation of the replica troopers after Sifas Dyen' death, covertly taking control of the army and its Gelvarian developers. Varek maintained secret contact with two officials of the Gelvarian government , Prime Minister Lamir and the Chief Medical Scientist Doctor Nalle Seris , who were supplied with behavioral modification biochips to ensure the replicas' compliance with their Umbra programming. The chips were implanted in the brain of every replica trooper during the early stage of their development; Sifas Dyen, who originally thought of the chip, intended for it to be a safeguard against rogue Aetheri, but Varek and Mal reprogrammed the chip. Varek deceived the Gelvarians into believing Sifas Dyen' intention. However, the biochip's true purpose was to guarantee that the replicas would carry out Directive 66, a secret protocol that was integral to the destruction of the Aetheri Order.

### Invasion of Ondara

### Invasion of Ondara

> " At last we will reveal ourselves to the Aetheri. At last we will have revenge. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

In 32 BVE , Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum requested the Aetheri Order's assistance in negotiating a dispute that resulted in the Commerce Combine 's blockade of the planet Ondara . The High Council dispatched Aetheri Master Sorin Vael and his Adept, Orien Kade, to negotiate with the Commerce Combine. However, Vael Mal, whose public persona was Senator Theron Mal of Ondara, insisted that the Commerce Combine, which was under his sway, initiated an invasion of Ondara and overwhelmed the Royal Ondara Security Forces . Circumventing a trap by the Federation, Vael and Kade were able to escape to Ondara and arrive in Serath in time to rescue the Ondara Queen , Lira Ondar , who was being held captive by Federation forces. Together with the Queen's Handmaidens and her close security detail , the Aetheri fled the planet but their ship was damaged in the escape, causing them to land on the desert planet of Dunemere .

title: Aetheri Order
text: Queen Ondar on her return to Serath. At the same time, Ondar was deceived by Mal into calling for a Vote of No Confidence in Chancellor Valorum by pointing out that Valorum was ineffective and under the control of the Bureaucrats , which would eventually lead to the election of Mal to the chancellorship. Vael and Kade then assisted Ondar and her forces during the ensuing battle against the Commerce Combine, when Vreth killed Vael in combat , only for the Umbra to be defeated by Kade. Given the status of Aetheri Knight afterward, Kade took Drayden as his apprentice, despite Zho's reluctance, and the Aetheri Order was left in the dark as to what the Umbra's actions were for ten years. The Aetheri were left unaware that they were being deceived by Mal, who was using his double identity to eventually complete the Umbra's revenge by destroying the Aetheri and taking over the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Dissident Crisis

> " I will not let this Republic that has stood for a thousand years be split in two. My negotiations will not fail. " " If they do, you must realize that there aren't enough Aetheri to protect the Republic. We're keepers of the peace, not soldiers. " ―Theron Mal and Drevan Koss

Having broken all ties to the Aetheri Order, secretly replacing Vreth as Mal' apprentice, Varek was believed to be a mere "political idealist" by his peers at the Aetheri Order. For eight years, Varek was scarcely heard about until he staged a theatrical return to public life by delivering a rousing speech that condemned the Republic and essentially set the stage for the Dissident Crisis . At the same time, he fomented political turmoil in many worlds, including Selvara, Thornwood , Garnethex , and Underra, or tried to convince their leaders to leave the Republic, as in Eriadu 's case. Soon enough, Varek became the face of the Fractio of Independent Systems, convincing several thousand systems to leave the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri Order was unable to ensure the Republic's safety in the event of a war due to its limited numbers. The Republic lacked a standing army, while the mandate of the Aetheri was to maintain order as peacekeepers instead of soldiers. Concerned by the growing number of star systems seceding from the Republic, the Senate debated the Military Creation Act . During the debate around 22 BVE , a plot to assassinate Senator Ondar forced the Ondara senator to return to her homeworld with Adept Kael Drayden serving as her bodyguard . The task of investigating the plot against Ondar was given to Drayden's master, Aetheri Knight Orien Kade, who tracked the assassin to the planet Gelvaris.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After discovering the Gelvarians' creation of the replica army at the behest of the late Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen, Kade deduced that the army's replica template, the bounty hunter Garrick Vark , was the assassin who tried to kill Ondar. Garrick and his cloned son, Vex Vark , fled from Gelvaris to escape interrogation by the Aetheri. However, Kade followed the Fetts to Pyralis where he discovered the Dissident Droid Army , prompting the Senate to empower Chancellor Mal to unilaterally create the Grand Army of the Republic, although they were unaware that this was exactly what Mal had intended.

### Replica Wars

#### The first battle

> " I have to admit that without the replicas, it would not have been a victory. " " Victory? Victory, you say? Master Orien, not victory. The shroud of the umbra side has fallen. Begun the Replica War has. " ―Orien Kade and Zho

title: Aetheri Order
text:

As the Republic prepared for war, Aetheri Master Drevan Koss led an Aetheri assault team to rescue Kade on Pyralis. The Aetheri confronted the Dissidents in the Pyralian Petranaki Arena , destroying many battle droids but also sustaining a large number of casualties, including Tan Yuster , Sar Labooda , and Coleman Trebor . The remaining Aetheri were evacuated from the arena by the Republic replica army that arrived on Pyralis under the command of Grand Master Zho.

title: Aetheri Order
text: the High Council were nothing more than warmongers. Despite his personal reservations, Koss's experience on Hissrich reminded him of the Aetheri Order's commitment to safeguarding the lives of others. With his newfound resolve, Koss affirmed his belief that the Order had a moral responsibility to defend the citizens of the Republic as well as all beings throughout the galaxy. During the Replica Wars, the Aetheri were victorious on battlefronts across the galaxy, including Krestophis , Selvara, and Umbara . In their capacity as leaders of the Grand Army of the Republic, the Aetheri came to be seen as great warriors. Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden, for example, was considered by some to be the greatest warrior of the Aetheri Order and became known as the " Hero With No Fear " to the HoloNet . Believing the Order was not political, one Dissident fighter, Poan of Riek , believed the war would end quickly because he thought the Aetheri would, soon enough, intervene against the Republic. However, Poan then came face-to-face against an Aetheri during a Mission on Leyoye Prime , in which the Aetheri singlehandedly wiped out most of his unit.

title: Aetheri Order
text: During the Battle of Krestophis , Replica Sergeant Slick was arrested as a spy and traitor for the Fractio of Independent Systems. The sergeant claimed that he acted in the interests of the replicas, whom he viewed as a slave army fighting for the Aetheri and the Republic. However, the replica trooper officers who arrested him— Replica Commander Cord and Replica Captain Vek —questioned Slick's motives, noting how he betrayed the Republic for money and that his actions endangered replica lives. Although Slick succeeded in sabotaging much of the Republic's military equipment, Aetheri Generals Orien Kade and Kael Drayden successfully led their battalions , respectively the 212th Attack Battalion and the 501st Legion , to victory over the Dissidents on the Christophsian homeworld.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Battle of Selvara was a coordinated effort by the Republic to liberate the Velaris' homeworld from Dissident occupation. With the Aetheri in command, the replica troopers mainly relied on using volt pistol rifles and Electro Magnetic Pulse grenades to reduce the level of destruction on Selvara. Whereas the Dissidents used the Velaris as living shields to deter a direct Republic attack, the Aetheri and their replicas were careful to avoid causing civilian casualties. During the final phase of the invasion, General Koss endeavored to take the capital city of Lessu with the support of the Velari Coalition led by Chavar Kryll. Setting aside his dislike for politics, Koss used diplomacy to win the freedom fighter's help, convincing the rivals Kryll and Senator Orn Free Taa to work together in common cause. The combined forces of Aetheri, Republic, and Twi-leks captured the capital along with the Dissident Emir of Selvara Wat Tambra .

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Renegade Aetheri

> " I did it because I've come to realize what many people in the Republic have come to realize, that the Aetheri are the ones responsible for this war, that we've so lost our way that we have become villains in this conflict, that we are the ones that should be put on trial, all of us! And my attack on the Temple was an attack on what the Aetheri have become, an army fighting for the umbra side, fallen from the light that we once held so dear. This Republic is failing! It's only a matter of time. " ―Barris Ovva, admitting to the bombing of the Aetheri Sanctum hangar

title: Aetheri Order
text: Though originally a Republic loyalist world at the onset of the Replica Wars, Umbara defected to the Dissidents in the wake of Senator Mee Deechi 's assassination. The Republic therefore invaded the Umbaran homeworld, precipitating the Battle of Umbara. By then, Krell had foreseen the rise of a New Order in the aftermath of the Replica Wars. Convinced that the Aetheri Order would be defeated, Krell secretly betrayed both the Order and the Republic. He sought to prove his new loyalties to Count Varek by undermining the Republic's efforts to retake Umbara. However, Krell's plans ended when the 501st discovered his betrayal and as such, mutinied agaisnt him. Krell was taken into custody after killing multiple replicas while resisting arrest. Ultimately, the traitorous Aetheri Master was executed by one of his strongest supporters, Dogma , after admitting his betrayal of the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Barris Ovva believed the Aetheri had deviated from their course as peacekeepers and so she betrayed the Aetheri by arranging a bombing at the Aetheri Sanctum, for which deceitfully framed fellow Adept Sela Marr. Marr, in turn, left the Aetheri Order unable to trust the Council after turning its back on her during her trial . Eventually, the High Council came to be aware of Varek's hand in the creation of the replica army, and of the lies and mistrust that surrounded them, both inside the Temple and the Senate. Grand Master Zho even (as it turned out correctly) foresaw that the Aetheri might not win the Replica Wars, just as public support for the Aetheri weakened due to their management of the conflict.

#### The last stand

> " In the name of the Galactic Senate of the Republic, you're under arrest, Chancellor. " " Are you threatening me, Master Aetheri? " " The Senate will decide your fate. " ―Drevan Koss and Theron Mal

title: Aetheri Order
text: The final stages of the war came in 19 BVE . It began with the Battle of Vantor , which Mal orchestrated as part of his overall plot to convert Kael to the Umbra side and make him his apprentice. During the battle, Varek was betrayed by Mal, who as Mal, had him executed by Drayden. With Varek dead, the Aetheri calculated a decisive Republic victory through the destruction of General Skarn , which was achieved by Orien Kade during the Battle of Uthara a few days or weeks later. However, Drayden, whose turmoil clouded his judgment, learned that Mal was Mal. Though he informed Koss of Mal's identity, Mal resisted the Aetheri's efforts to arrest him, killing three Aetheri Masters—Kit Fisto, Agen Kolar , and Saesee Tiin —forcing Koss to duel the Dark Lord alone. Drayden rushed to Mal's office as Koss and the chancellor fought, arriving moments after the Aetheri champion disarmed the Umbra Lord. Before Koss could kill Mal, Drayden, who believed he needed Mal alive to save his secret wife Padme Ondar from potentially dying from childbirth, betrayed him by severing his hand, which led to the Aetheri Master's death. Knowing there was no turning back

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Aetheri survivors that were captured were taken to Emberfall for interrogation and execution, as well as the Spire on Stygeon Prime , wherein the body of Luminara Undula was preserved to lure out any surviving Aetheri. Among the last reservoirs of knowledge of the Order were Antron Bach 's vault in an abandoned colony , created at Uvell's behest, and Grukkar the Grak 's private collection on Nar Shaddaa . Safeguarding reliquaries, flux blades, journals, archives, and other artifacts, they partially preserved the teachings of the fallen Order. The surviving Aetheri Nedriss Narr and Vanzell Mar-Klar attempted to train new younglings in a secret temple.

### Dark times

#### Fallen order

text: > " The Aetheri were good . Like all of us, they failed to secure the peace. They were drawn into the war like everyone else, and their hands were not clean. If I can accept the blame for my part, they certainly earned their share, too. But for thousands of years they could have ruled the galaxy, and instead they chose to serve. They had their own vested interests, their own ways of politicking. But they believed their power came with an obligation to live humbly, to do good without asserting authority. Maybe they failed to live up to those ideals in the end. I haven't seen your evidence. What do I know about the extent of their betrayals? They deserved better than to die at the hands of power-hungry old men who saw them as a threat. We deserved better than to lose another people, another religion, from the universe. All of us are poorer for their loss. […] The Aetheri deserve justice… or at least a decent

All of us are poorer for their loss. […] The Aetheri deserve justice… or at least a decent funeral. " ―Vela Sess, to Soujen Vak-Nhalis For nearly twenty years, the Imperium was able to expand without opposition of a disbanded Aetheri Order. A few of its former members, however survived and stayed true to their code of honor and continued to fight the Imperium's injustice, albeit in different ways. Though former Adept Sela Marr had become disillusioned by the Council's actions and no longer identified as an Aetheri, she came into contact with Bael Solen from Cindervale , with whom she worked to coordinate the efforts of a insurgency under the codename "Fulcrum," fifteen years after the fall of the Republic.

#### Rediscovery of an abandoned world

> " Tanalorr's a fortress. We should use it for the Hidden Path. Gather allies. Train. They'd never see us coming. " ―Cal Kessara

Over the five years following the reliquary's destruction, Kessara had become an extremely important target for the Imperium, having attracted the attention of not only the Warden Order but also the Imperium Vigil Bureau through his crusade against the Imperium . In 9 BVE , on the planet Koboh , Kessara encountered something from the Aetheri's golden ag;. Kessara encountered the Aetheri Dagan Gera , who had been preserved in bacta since the days of the High Republic. Kessara freed the old Aetheri and asked for his help in his fight against the Imperium. However, Gera had fallen out with the Aetheri Order, which he believed had betrayed him because the Aetheri had given up on Tanalorr , a hard-to-reach world Dagan had become obsessed with, after an attack by the Nullkin . Gera, who had fallen to the umbra side, bled the kyber crystal from his flux blade and began a duel with Kessara.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
By 21 AVE , the new Aetheri Order had grown to the point where it already had senior pupils on top of a new class of younglings in training. Around this time, Joren Drayden experienced visions that distracted him from some of his basic duties at the academy, leaving some of his senior students to take over for him on this duties. A Velari woman named Enyo served as an instructor on flux blade combat, running a class of younglings through a series of exercises with training blades . When Drayden went on a mission with Lor Saan Tarka that distanced him from his temple, Beno Karrick, who had also taken the duties of running training exercises on the younger students, stayed to oversee the academy.

#### The temple's destruction

> " I never… I didn't want this. " " And you did not choose it, Beno. The Aetheri did. Drayden. " ―Beno Karrick and Vorr

text:
#### The temple's destruction

Karrick's family would ultimately learn that he was gradually seduced to the ways of the umbra side through the machinations of the New Imperium's ruler, Supreme Leader Vorr . Solen blamed Vorr as the sole cause of her son's descent into darkness, culminating in the destruction of the Aetheri Sanctum , but Drayden felt responsible for his nephew's fate. Sensing the umbra side's influence within Karrick, Drayden probed his nephew's mind and beheld visions of the dark warrior that he was becoming. Drayden instinctively raised his flux blade to kill his nephew while he slept, believing Karrick would destroy all that he loved; however, he stopped himself from killing his sister's son, and was overcome by shame. He then saw that Karrick had awoken. He saw fear in the eyes of his young nephew, and in that moment Drayden felt he had failed as an Aetheri Master.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Drayden regained consciousness in the rubble of his nephew's hut too late to prevent Karrick's destruction of the Aetheri Sanctum and the deaths of the students inside. Karrick had already fled, and Drayden could only witness his temple still burning alongside his astromech droid , Bolt-3 . Drayden felt responsible for the ordeal and decided to exile himself, although those closest to him learned that he was also searching for the first Aetheri Sanctum. Drayden only left traces of his location in a single star map , with the remaining data being present in old Imperial records. Drayden eventually found the first Aetheri Sanctum on the aquatic world of Tidehollow, where he took up refuge and lived in exile as a hermit . Drayden vowed to never attempt another rebirth of the Aetheri Order, and therefore resolved to die as the last Aetheri.

> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Beno Karrick

Traveling to the Aetheri outpost on Elphrona, Karrick contacted Karrick, who told him to find the Knights of Karrick on Varnak. However, Hennix, Tai and Voe caught up with the fugitive Karrick. Though Tai preferred to reason with Karrick, Voe and Hennix fought him, believing that he had a role in destroying the Aetheri Sanctum and killing their brethren. Karrick killed Hennix in self-defense before fleeing to Varnak. However, Karrick was still unsatisfied that Karrick was worthy to become a Knight of Karrick but took him on a trial run.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After a devastating attack against the Concordat's capital by the New Imperium's Voidfang Base , the Coalition sought to destroy the New Imperium superweapon. Once there, Dax Karrick attempted to turn his son back to the light, but he was killed by Karrick instead, who was attempting to fully commit to Vorr and the umbra side. Nyla subsequently defeated Karrick in a flux blade duel and Voidfang Base was destroyed, after which the Coalition finally pieced together the map to Drayden with help from Bolt-3. Solen, relieved to finally find her brother, sought to bring him home. She sent Nyla, along with Brevok and Bolt-3, to Tidehollow, where the young girl found Drayden among the refuge of the first Aetheri Sanctum.

There, Nyla presented the Aetheri Master with his father's flux blade —which he had lost on Aether Spire decades prior— as a symbol of the only hope the galaxy had left in defeating Zarrin Karrick, Vorr, the New Imperium and Knights of Karrick by bringing about the Return of the Aetheri Order.

### Last of the Aetheri

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Return and Demise of the Umbra Order

> " I am all the Umbra! " " And I… I'm all the Aetheri. " ―Vael Mal and Nyla

In the year following the Battle of Saltmark , Nyla repaired the Drayden flux blade continued her Aetheri training under Joren Drayden's twin sister, Elira Solen, who had once briefly trained under her brother as an Aetheri herself. Meanwhile, Zarrin Karrick and the New Imperium cracked down on any worlds that spread the tale of his defeat at the hands of Joren Drayden. During that time, a cult of loyalists to the extinct Umbra, the Umbra Eternal , revealed themselves to the galaxy from the Unknown Regions by broadcasting the voice of the late Theron Mal, the public identity of Vael Mal, who was thought to be dead since the Battle of Mossfell . After obtaining an Umbra wayfinder from Emberfall , Karrick traveled to Umbrale and found that Mal still lived. The Emperor promised Karrick the Umbra Eternal's fleet of Xyston -class Star Destroyers , the Final Order , if he killed Nyla, the last Aetheri and the granddaughter of Mal.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
For the word "Aetheri," Vask took inspiration from the Japanese term " Jidaigeki ," which refers to a drama set during the Edo period of Japanese history, when samurai were still in activity. The word "Aetheri" is a singular plural. The Aetheri Order originated in the rough draft of Aetherion as the Galactic Emperor's bodyguard . They became affiliated with the Republica Galactica in the second draft. Later, when composing background information for licensees in 1977 , Orin Vask described the Aetheri Order as being "several hundred thousand" strong before the Purge.

### Prequel trilogy and The Replica Wars ### Prequel trilogy and The Replica Wars

Ahead of release, Orin Vask claimed that Veiled Threat depicted "the heyday of the Aetheri," during which time there were thousands of Aetheri and they acted as the "guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy, sort of like the old marshals out West." Vask felt he needed "to establish Aetheri as what they were, which is sort of peacekeepers who moved through the galaxy to settle disputes." He described the Aetheri as "warrior-monks who keep peace in the universe without resorting to violence." In the overall story of Aetherion , however, Veiled Threat kicks off the prequel trilogy , which depicts the downfall of the Aetheri Order. Within Aetherion Legends and canon, the prequel era overall represents a time in which the Aetheri were losing their way, with Episode II supporting that by featuring Zho reflect on the increasing arrogance of even elder Aetheri.

title: Aetheri Order
text: there's a bunch of in my movies. You have to think it through. Are they going to stick with their moral rules and all be killed, which makes it irrelevant, or do they help save the Republic? They have good intentions, but they have been manipulated which was their downfall." The Aetherion: The Replica Wars animated series produced under Vask continued to study the themes of the Aetheri Order and the road to its downfall. The Replica Wars Supervising director Dave Filono once noted that, in his mind at least, one of the story elements of the prequels was showing how the Aetheri "almost forgot to care" and "[lacked] compassion" for Kael Drayden's situation, which leads to his fall to the umbra side and the destruction of their Order. Filono also pointed to Zho's quote about Aetheri arrogance in Attack of the Replicas , saying Zho “criticizes the Aetheri in Episode II and says that they’ve become arrogant” and that “because they’ve become arrogant and very sure of themselves” they lack love and compassion. Vask, however, has said that Zho was simply reminding Orien Kade that "arrogance exists in the older Aetheri too, which is a way of warning Orien that he may be suffering the same hubris [as Kael]."

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Vask also once stated that some people "didn't seem to understand the fact that Kael is simply greedy" as the Aetheri are "trained more than anything else to understand the transitional nature of life, that things are constantly changing and you can’t hold on to anything. You can love things but you can't be attached to them," which allows one to be "compassionate and loving and caring, but not be possessive and grabbing and holding on to things and trying to keep things the way they are." Kael's issues are stemming not from some kind of failure of the Aetheri, but from the fact that he started his training late in life, since if he would've been raised by the Aetheri from a very early age, "he’d have been trained to love people but not to become attached to them."

### Sequel trilogy

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### The High Republic

> " I think when people think about The High Republic down the road, they'll think about the Aetheri. We've seen so many stories in Aetherion set during an era when they were in decline, or essentially gone, or bravely trying to rebuild themselves from almost nothing. The High Republic , at its heart, is an attempt to show an Order, and a Republic, at their strongest point. We've been hearing about what the Aetheri meant to the galaxy for a thousand generations—we wanted to show it, and I think we succeeded. " ―Charles Soulea

Writer Cavan Scott explained a theme of the Aetherion: The High Republic is seeing the Aetheri live out amongst local communities, instead of being, comparatively, "locked away in their temples. Charles Soulea also explained, "The thing to know about The High Republic's Aetheri is that the rules that exist in the prequel trilogy still exists. They still take the same vows, they still have the same feelings about it, but their understanding of the strength of the Order and flexibility within the Order and the interpretation of those rules ... they're more diffuse, I would say." According to actor Charlie Barnett , the High Republic Era-set series Aetherion: The Adeptis explores the theme of the Aetheri Order having an ego due to it being their golden age, at which the Order was at its height. According to Barnett, this ego began to take control of the Aetheri during the time of The Adeptis , paving the way for the Order's downfall.

title: Gelvaris
text:
# Gelvaris
> " With all due respect, General, if someone comes to our home, they better be carrying a big volt pistol. " ―Replica Captain Vek, to Orien Kade

Gelvaris (pronounced / kə'minoʊ /) was an aquatic planet located in a remote star system in Wild Space of the galaxy . Gelvaris was sometimes classed as extragalactic due to its secluded location. It was inhabited by the Gelvarians —a race of tall, elegant beings with long necks who were regarded as a mysterious species that tended to keep to themselves. They were also known for their replication technology, which was used to create a replica army for the Vantor Republic .

title: Gelvaris
text: Largely isolated from the wider galaxy, Gelvaris's existence was erased from the Aetheri records by Count Varek . Aetheri Knight Orien Kade , who was investigating the attempt to assassinate Lira Ondar , traced the bounty hunter Garrick Vark to the planet, where he discovered the replication program. With the outbreak of the Replica Wars , Gelvaris became a prime target for the Fractio of Independent Systems and a vital asset for the Republic, resulting in at least two attempts to invade the watery world. During the early days of the Imperium , with the replication program halted, Gelvaris's civilization was almost completely wiped out via orbital bombardment of all cities and structures, including the capital of Tipoca City , leaving only a small diaspora of Gelvarians in Imperial custody or scattered amongst the stars as all that remained.

title: Gelvaris
text:
> " Gelvaris. I'm not familiar with it. Is it in the Republic? " " No, no. It's beyond the Outer Reach. I'd say about, uh, 12 parsecs… outside the Rishi Maze. " ―Orien Kade and Dexter Jettster

Located seventy thousand light-years from the Core Reaches , of Wild Space , Gelvaris was located twelve parsecs away from the Rishi Maze dwarf satellite galaxy , and was sometimes classed as extragalactic .

Gelvaris was a remote and inhospitable planet which was covered in oceans that held an abundance of life. Its savage storms and powerful lightning bursts could be seen vaguely through its relatively thick atmosphere . The native Gelvarians lived on stilt-cities scattered across Gelvaris's watery surface. The majority of these cities were devoted to replication projects, as the highly intelligent Gelvarians specialized in replication for clients needing workers or private security forces, along with other one-off requests. Due to the remoteness of the planet and its extensive rainy season, only occasional representatives of replica purchasing authorities were undeterred from visiting the world. During some parts of the year was covered with heavy electrical storms, where Gelvarians rode on aiwhas underwater and resurfaced once they were near their destination.

title: Gelvaris
text:
### Early civilization

> " These, uh, Gelvarians keep to themselves. They're replicators. Damn good ones too. " ―Dexter Jettster

At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Gelvarians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Gelvarians to build their structures on stilts.

The Gelvarians were generally isolationists, staying out of contact with the wider galaxy . This behavior could be traced back to the great flood that changed their homeworld, as they decided it was less risky to adapt their genetic code and planet than to ask for aid from the Vantor Republic .

### The Republic

#### Creating the replica army

title: Gelvaris
text:
#### The dawn of the Replica Wars

In 22 BVE , Gelvaris was governed by Prime Minister Lamir . Working on a request from Viceroy Nutis Gunray , Vark attempted to assassinate Ondara senator Lira Ondar on the Republic's capital planet, Vantor , during the Dissident Crisis . However, Vark's fellow bounty hunter tasked for the assassination attempt, Zam Wesell , failed to kill Ondar and was cornered by the Aetheri Knight Orien Kade . Vark killed Wesell before she could reveal any information. Kade went on to investigate the assassination attempt, searching for clues from the Gelvaris saberdart used to kill Wesell. After receiving no answers from the Aetheri Archives, Kade sought counsel with Dexter Jettster , a Besalisk chef and information broker who owned and operated Dex's Diner in CoCo Town on Vantor.

title: Gelvaris
text:
Jettster informed his Aetheri friend that the dart originated from Gelvaris, a planet located twelve parsecs outside of the Rishi Maze , a satellite galaxy in orbit of the main galaxy. Jettster explained that Gelvaris was home to highly competent replicators who mostly kept to themselves. Gelvaris had been removed from the records of the Aetheri Archives, so Kade and Master Zho had to locate the planet by other means. After finding a way to reach Gelvaris, Kade traveled to the planet, where he discovered the production of the replica army supposedly commissioned by the Aetheri Order.

### Replica Wars

> " There's only one target of interest in this sector: Gelvaris. It's the closest thing we replicas have to a home. Today we fight for more than the Republic. Today we fight for all our brothers back home. " ―Replica Captain Vek

title: Gelvaris
text:
### Replica Wars

> " There's only one target of interest in this sector: Gelvaris. It's the closest thing we replicas have to a home. Today we fight for more than the Republic. Today we fight for all our brothers back home. " ―Replica Captain Vek

Following the outbreak of the Replica Wars , Gelvaris was one of the main operational areas of the Vantor Republic. It served as the main training grounds for replica cadets as well as the location for the replica army's creation. As such, it was a major military asset for the Republic and a prime target for a Dissident attack and thus warranted the protection of a massive Republic naval blockade of ten Vorash -class Star Destroyers , one Acclamator -class assault ship , and two Arquitens -class light cruisers ; the size of this blockade discouraged all but the most risky of full-frontal assaults by the Dissidents to stand a chance of taking Gelvaris.

title: Gelvaris
text: At some point, a galactic explorer—who may have been the Ithorian artist Gammit Chond —elected to make the long journey needed to visit Gelvaris, wanting to visit Tipoca City and meet the replicators who had come to play a vital role in galactic history . In their journal , the explorer wrote that they were honored to visit the city. From the beginnings of the war, the Dissidents plotted their assault on the replica homeworld. In 22 BVE , the cyborg General Skarn sent a strike team of commando droids to take out Rishi Station , a Republic outpost that could warn Gelvaris of an impending attack. The base was taken over by the droids, but as Skarn's fleet arrived in the system before attacking Gelvaris, replica trooper Hevy sacrificed himself to alert Republic forces of the enemy fleet, causing the Dissidents to retreat and call off their attack.

title: Gelvaris
text: Another battle of Gelvaris involved Aetheri General Kit Fisto , who fought against Dissident droids deployed in the battle. An important mission to Gelvaris was arranged for occurred between 22 BVE and 21 BVE , with Aetheri Master Bavoc Ansho , Aetheri Knight Tualon Veyra, and Aetheri Knight Charlin Plaka being selected for the mission. Before leaving Veyra asked his friend and fellow Knight Iskat Vekkis if she would be joining them, but the angered Vekkis informed him she was still stationed in the Aetheri Sanctum, which she believed was a punishment for her actions during the mission to Thule . Late in the war, the Umbra's plan to destroy the Aetheri using the replica troopers was almost revealed. During the Battle of Ringo Vindra , the replica trooper Tupp , designated CT-5385, executed the Aetheri Master Tiplar during the confrontation due to a defect in his inhibitor chip . Wanting answers, it was decided that the replica would be sent to Gelvaris.

title: Gelvaris
text:
The Gelvarian leadership did everything possible to prevent the truth about the chips from being revealed, that they would guarantee the replicas' obedience when the order to destroy the Aetheri was given. Although Tupp died during a procedure carried out without permission to remove the chip by his replica friend Fivva and the medical android AZI-3 , the threat to the Umbra plan did not end while Fivva continued to investigate. Fivva found that all replicas had chips and decided to remove his, and he and the two chips were sent to Vantor for analysis. Fivva was eventually killed on Vantor and the truth about the chips was kept secret.

### Imperial Era

#### New relations

> " The Imperium is not like the Republic. We have empowered them to our own detriment. I fear they will destroy us rather than allow this operation to continue. " ―Lamir, to Nalle Seris

title: Gelvaris
text:
The Imperium slowly dismantled the replication program as the troops in the Imperial Army were gradually replaced by non-replica recruits. As the Imperium began to cancel contracts, the Gelvarians grew wary of them and made arrangements to flee from the Imperium, only to be foiled. The Imperium had the Prime Minister arrested, with Chief Scientist Nalle Seris forced to cooperate with the Imperium and disclose her scientific knowledge.

#### Decommissioning of the replication facilities

> " It's...all...gone. " ―Omaya #### Decommissioning of the replication facilities

> " It's...all...gone. " ―Omaya

Hunter, who was captured by the Imperium while extracting a replica Gregor on the planet Daro , was brought back to Gelvaris by Crossline. The rest of the Bad Batch returned to the planet to extract Hunter. Noticing the absence of troops and the facilities stripped down, the Bad Batch encountered Crossline and his squad with Hunter in the training chamber. Crossline offered the Bad Batch to join the Imperium, declaring that they were superior to the "regs" and that they would aid the Imperium in establishing order as its elite squad. Chaos ensued, as Crossline fired on his squad-mates to make his point and Omaya activated the battle droids. Vice Admiral Edmon Rampart , who oversaw the evacuation of all remaining replica troopers and essential personnel from Gelvaris, abandoned Crossline and received the order from Varrix to destroy Tipoca City. As the Bad Batch attempted to return to their shuttle, they were caught in the bombardment and fled back inside the falling city.

title: Gelvaris
text: Like Tipoca City, all other Gelvarian facilities the Imperium knew of were targeted and destroyed, causing their civilization to sink beneath the waves. Alerted to their success by a replica trooper , Rampart ordered his trio of Star Destroyers to reunite with his overall fleet, leaving the remains of Tipoca City to sink into the ocean, completing the Imperial withdrawal from Gelvaris. Meanwhile, through the actions of Omaya and AZI-3, Crossline was saved from drowning and reunited with his former squad, regrouping in their former barracks, which had ironically become one of the few rooms that was temporally safe to reside in. After the squad debates about Crossline's recent actions, the group decided to make their way to Nalle Seris's secret laboratory, evading a kamoradon sea dragon along the way.

title: Gelvaris
text:
#### Cover-up and revelation

Following the Attack on Gelvaris , Imperial officials including Vice-Admiral Rampart claimed that the planet had been devastated by a cataclysmic storm, that had destroyed the replication facilities and almost annihilated the Gelvarian population. Rampart claimed that he had been unable to intervene since he was in an off-world training exercise. Despite Rampart's efforts to suppress the truth behind Gelvaris's devastation, the Replica trooper Cade , who served aboard Rampart flagship VZ-114 , attempted to convince Rampart to tell the Imperial Senate the truth. Rampart sent the Replica assassin Replica X to assassinate him. Cade's friend Slip managed to contact Senator Riyo Chuchi , who was sympathetic to the plight of Replica troopers, before being assassinated by Replica X. The assassin was subdued by fugitive Replica Commander Vek but committed suicide.

title: Gelvaris
text:
Chuchi sought the help of the Bad Batch replicas in exposing Rampart's role in the attack on Gelvaris. The Bad Batch managed to infiltrate Rampart's flagship and uncover footage of Rampart's fleet bombarding Tipoca City. In addition, Chuchi and Omaya learnt from former Gelvarian Senator Halle Burtoni that Rampart had diverted Senate funds earmarked for the replication facilities. Using these pieces of information, Chuchi was able to temporarily derail the Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill and expose Rampart's role in the destruction of Gelvaris. In response, Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon and Theron Mal ordered Rampart's arrest and claimed he was acting against Imperial orders. However, Mal was still able to use the devastation of Gelvaris to convince the Imperial Senate to pass the Bill by claiming that Rampart's replicas had followed his orders without question.

### Galactic Society of Creature Enthusiasts

During or after 34 AVE , a city was present on Gelvaris. SF-R3 and CAM , two members of the Galactic Society of Creature Enthusiasts , visited the planet to witness a Kamoradon hatching.

title: Gelvaris
text:
> " Fighting a war tests a soldier's skills, defending his home tests a soldier's heart. " ―Opening quote for " ARC Troopers "

### Creation and development

Gelvaris was created for the 2002 film Aetherion : Episode II Attack of the Replicas , the second installment of the Aetherion prequel trilogy . Originally, Orin Vask promised to explain the mystery behind the erasure of Gelvaris from the Aetheri Archives in 2005 's Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra . However, after refocusing the story on Kael Drayden, Vask opted to sacrifice extraneous plot points related to Attack of the Replicas , including Gelvaris's mystery. It would not be until twenty years later that the mystery behind Gelvaris's deletion from the Archives would be revealed in the Aetherion: Tales of the Aetheri episode " The Umbra Lord ."

### Inconsistencies The location of Gelvaris has not been consistent throughout the Aetherion canon . Some sources, such as Aetherion: Galactic Atlas placed Gelvaris in Wild Space . Others, such as Aetherion: Complete Locations stated that Gelvaris was not even part of the galaxy , while Ultimate Aetherion, New Edition places Gelvaris in the Outer Reach Territories , but states that it lay beyond the Outer Reach.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Early years

> " I know where you come from. Before you called yourself Zarrin Karrick. " ―Lor Saan Tarka

Beno Karrick was prone to crying as an infant , particularly in the first months of his life, and had difficulty falling asleep . He would settle to sleep when he was held by his father or upon sensing the presence of his parents or their friend, Dax's Vorak First Mate Brevok . During the Fenril crisis and other early conflicts in the Concordat era , young Karrick was a consistent concern on his parents' minds and often found himself adjacent to their involvement. On Nagi , Dax Karrick received a call from Solen, who was with Beno at their apartment . Dax requested help from the Concordat, and Solen worriedly held her son. She later attempted to depart for Nagi with Beno in a hover pram , but was convinced by Vela Sess to stay, lifting Beno out of the pram.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
At that time, the Karrick family utilized the class-3 culinary septoid droid BX-778 to help them with the household chores. While supervising Beno at T-2LC's direction, a virus within BX-778 activated and caused the droid to consider cutting Beno's throat in order to stop the toddler's temper tantrum. The droid's programming was restored as a result of Dax destroying the Phylanx Redux Transmitter , erasing the command to kill organics that BX-778 had been infected with. The child was not consciously aware that his life had been endangered and he may not have remembered it later; however, the incident may have been retained subconsciously as a near-death experience.

Karrick grew close to his parents' friends in his childhood; in particular, he showed great affection toward Dorian Quill , whom he referred to as "Unca Wanwo" —and later "Uncle Lando" when he was older —and who told him stories of Dax's days as a smuggler. Brevok, whom Karrick referred to as "Uncle Brev," mentored him as he learned how to fly a speeder and fire a volt pistol , and he sometimes provided childcare when the boy's parents were occupied with their respective careers.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
In 9 AVE , Beno's name was included on a list of heroes on the gauntlet of Baylan Skoll , a former Aetheri Knight and an ally to the efforts to find the missing Grand Admiral Vorren of the Imperium .

In his youth, Karrick's parents had active lives in their respective professions. Restless with settling in one place for long, Dax began mentoring young pilots; he hoped to someday help Beno learn how to repair the hyperrelay of the Corsair Wing and acquire a starship of his own. He also hoped that Beno would someday choose the same simple path of adventurer rather than the path of an Aetheri like his uncle and grandfather. Beno enjoyed playing with the gold dice that belonged to his father and would often follow him around. The boy aspired to become a pilot like his father and inherited piloting skills from both his father and his maternal grandfather. Meanwhile, Solen was a respected senator of the Concordat, and as she worked to repair the galaxy and prepare for the future conflict she sensed, she became occupied with routine senatorial duties.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Though he befriended the other Adepts while training with them under Drayden's watch, Karrick also suspected that they viewed him as a symbol of preferential treatment, benefitting from his Drayden bloodline instead of earning his place in the restored Aetheri Order. This belief led Karrick to feel like an outcast rather than part of a new generation of Aetheri. At some point during his training, Karrick would face a group of IG-RM assassin droids alongside his uncle.

#### Exploration and discovery

> " I'm glad you came along, Beno. " " Yes, Master Drayden. So am I. " ―Joren Drayden and Beno Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Exploration and discovery

> " I'm glad you came along, Beno. " " Yes, Master Drayden. So am I. " ―Joren Drayden and Beno Karrick

Around 19 AVE , Karrick accompanied his uncle to uncover knowledge of the Aetheri Order. Lor Saan Tarka , a traveler noted for his expertise on the Aetheri Order, informed Drayden about the discovery of an ancient Aetheri outpost on the planet Elphrona . Embarking on a mission to investigate Saan Tarka's findings, Drayden brought his apprentice with him, knowing that, like himself, Karrick was interested in discovering Aetheri artifacts. Along the way, Karrick was contacted by Vorr without Drayden's knowledge. Vorr, having sensed anxiety in Karrick, inquired after the boy's state of mind. They conversed telepathically while Drayden and Saan Tarka talked about the outpost, noting that it may have dated as far back as the High Republic Era , when the Aetheri greatly expanded their activity throughout the galaxy.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Their private conversation was interrupted by Drayden and Saan Tarka; as they drew closer to Elphrona, Drayden talked about how they not only had a chance to gain new insights into the ancient Aetheri, but also how the mission could give Karrick an opportunity to indulge his fascination with ancient weapons, knowing that his pupil was particularly interested in them. Karrick smiled when his Master expressed how pleased he was to have his apprentice by his side, and told Drayden that he felt the same.

The outpost that they discovered was well preserved and the entrance intact. Both master and apprentice were impressed by it, though Drayden warned that they should exercise caution while exploring the outpost, recounting a similar situation that nearly ended with his death in years past. The outpost was a repository of reliquaries and other artifacts that Drayden likened to a treasure trove. Karrick had been inspecting a flux blade rifle up close when he and his Master grew cold upon sensing the power of the umbra side.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick was one of Drayden's senior pupils by the time he became a teenager; as such, he was entrusted with some of his Master's responsibilities, such as the supervision of training sessions in which the younger students practiced with training flux blades . In 21 AVE , Lor Saan Tarka visited the temple on Ossus to speak with Drayden. Karrick went to Drayden's hut to inform him of Saan Tarka's arrival, inadvertently interrupting Drayden's meditation. Embarrassed at his intrusion, Karrick accidentally referred to Drayden as uncle instead of Master. Having been lectured by Drayden on the need to exercise discipline and control, Karrick composed himself and addressed Drayden by his formal title as he informed him about their visitor. After Drayden welcomed his old friend to the temple, Saan Tarka addressed Karrick directly to inquire on the progress of his training. Karrick's efforts at formality amused his Master, who assured Saan Tarka that Karrick was a better student than he could have hoped for.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Flux, and the fact that he stood poised to be among the first in his generation to complete his instruction in the Aetheri arts. Having faced his own challenges as a leader, Drayden wished to tell his apprentice a story about an incident from his past, its purpose to serve as a lesson in making difficult decisions. Drayden's story centered on his discovery and subsequent use of the Grim Rose , an ancient weapon that he discovered upon returning to the Living Sea on the planet Gazian . Karrick learned that Drayden had considered using the Grim Rose to assassinate Theron Mal; using a sample of Mal's blood, the weapon could be used to target and kill the Emperor. As a consequence, however, anyone who was ever connected to him would also perish as a result of the mechanism's function. Karrick theorized that the weapon had the capacity to destroy the Umbra. Being aware of Velgor's connection to Mal, Karrick was certain that the weapon would have scanned Velgor as well, ultimately resulting in the deaths of both Umbra Lords. Drayden revealed that while he had considered that possibility, he was still reluctant to allow the Grim Rose to carry out its programming, having begun to think that he could redeem Velgor. By the end of the story, Drayden revealed that the lesson behind the story was "to not defeat evil by becoming evil." Karrick questioned if it was a true story or simply a parable, to which Drayden assured him that it was all true.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick emerged from the ruins believing he had killed Drayden, and he raged in anger and confusion over why his uncle had attacked him. The night sky was clear as Karrick shouted questions and pointed his ignited flux blade at the Aetheri Sanctum . As his eyes changed to constricted pupils and irises clouded with red, Karrick briefly surrendered to the umbra side and summoned a storm that could destroy the temple . He then noticed the red storm clouds he had summoned appear above the temple, which rained lightning upon the temple and set the buildings ablaze . The fire that Karrick started when he lashed out destroyed most of the students along with the temple, which collapsed and burned to the ground. The lightning strike caused an explosion that knocked back Karrick and scattered debris and the bodies of dead students. When Karrick attempted to run inside the burning temple, he was thrown back by another explosion. He surveyed the death and destruction around him and, horrified, said that he never wanted this. However, a voice inside of Karrick's head told him that the fault lay not with himself, but rather with Drayden and the Aetheri. He assumed that a reliquary containing a message from the former Aetheri Grand Master , Zho , was destroyed in the blaze.

#### A dark path

> " The Knights of Karrick could be your first step on that path. They always seek powerful people to join their ranks. But be warned… the price of admission is steep. " ―Vorr, to Beno Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Having rejected his future as an Aetheri, Karrick expressed interest in learning what he could from the Knights of Karrick. Vorr not only supported Karrick's new path, but also encouraged the fallen Aetheri to take the opportunity of forging his own identity absent of Drayden's influence. Karrick had long felt the pressure of living up to the legends he was named after, and therefore wished to be rid of his given name as well as his father's surname. Even before he departed to search for the Knights of Karrick, Karrick began entertaining the idea of using a name he coined as a child. Vorr approved, believing that the new name represented Karrick's true nature and would become known to the entire galaxy one day. Returning to the place where he last saw the Knights, Karrick made contact with Karrick by using the latter's helmet as a direct line of communication, and was told to seek them out on Varnak in the Mid Reach . By then, the other Aetheri students had caught up to Karrick, intending to prevent him from going any further down the path of the umbra side.

#### Confrontation on Elphrona

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Trials of Knighthood

> " But Vorr vouched for you, and you're strong in the shadow, and that's not nothing. Let's spend some time, see if you like us, see if we like you. Maybe you'll find that good death after all. " ―Karrick, to Beno Karrick

With the Aetheri subdued, Karrick completed his journey to Varnak, where he found Karrick and the other Knights lounging in a cantina . Knowing that Vorr had sent Karrick to them, Karrick informed the young Aetheri that he would have to offer them a sacrifice before he could join their ranks. As with Vorr, Karrick was doubtful that Drayden died by Karrick's hand, although Karrick confirmed that at this point he was responsible for the destruction of the temple and deaths of other Aetheri. Karrick, however, needed to know if the Aetheri that Karrick killed held any significance to him, so he asked Karrick to recount the details of his confrontation with Tai, Hennix, and Voe. As Karrick began telling his story, his thoughts drifted to years past when he was younger—a child surrounded by other young students whom Drayden had taken under his wing.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Having learned enough about the other students of Drayden, Karrick directed Karrick to return to the more recent past regarding his confrontation with the trio that pursued him in the wake of the temple's destruction. Karrick took responsibility for Hennix's death, telling Karrick that he killed his fellow Aetheri. Karrick, however, remained skeptical as were the other Knights. Karrick protested, believing he met their qualifications, and although Karrick agreed that Hennix was technically a death caused by Karrick, he knew that the young fallen Aetheri was conflicted about it. Nevertheless, Karrick allowed Karrick to accompany the Knights, at least for the time being, given that he was strong with the umbra side as well as the fact that Vorr had already vouched for him. Karrick also suspected that, in the course of Karrick's journey with the Knights, the former Aetheri would eventually make a sacrifice that was worthy of the Knights of Karrick.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
As far as Karrick was concerned, Karrick's appearance as an Aetheri made him unsuitable to be seen in the company of the Knights. As such, Karrick was made to set aside his tattered Aetheri robes for a set of black clothes. Once dressed in his new attire, Karrick was told by Karrick that they would now depart from Vanrak and find something to burn.

By then, Tai and Voe had managed to create an opening in the destroyed entrance of the Aetheri outpost. Tai, having seen glimpses in Karrick's mind, knew that his former peer was seeking to join the Knights, believing his truth path was with the umbra side warriors. His faith in Karrick began to erode upon discovering the dead body of Hennix, whose flux blade was claimed by Voe as a replacement for her weapon, which was destroyed during her battle with Karrick.

#### The fall of Beno Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick then returned to the Night Buzzard and retreated to a workbench within to modify his flux blade. Deeply frustrated with his family's expectations of himself, Karrick used the kyber crystal from his blade to bleed his hatred for the legacy of his family into it, renouncing his origins to the distant Vael Mal and Vorr's approval. His eyes briefly turning yellow and red, the crystal cracked in its master's grip with a surge of fiery energy.

Afterward, he had to modify his weapon to contain the power of the broken crystal, which produced a red blade with an unstable and fiery appearance, a design after the weapon of an ancient Umbra Lord, Vael Atrio. After bleeding his kyber crystal and modifying his weapon, the newly-turned umbra side warrior brandished his crossguard flux blade and took on the name Zarrin Karrick.

#### The rise of Zarrin Karrick

> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Beno Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Beno Karrick

Zarrin Karrick sacrificed everything in his pursuit of power through the umbra side, choosing to isolate himself from the people he loved as Beno Karrick. In addition to becoming a champion of the New Imperium , the Imperium's successor that Vorr ruled as Supreme Leader , Karrick gained the title master of the Knights of Karrick, having inherited his predecessor's command with Vorr's blessing. Through his new master's training, Karrick became nothing more than a distant memory in the life of Karrick. He was the Supreme Leader's most gifted apprentice as well as the embodiment of a new generation of umbra side warriors that emerged to fill the void left by the fall of the Umbra, which became extinct with the deaths of Mal and Velgor as the last Umbra Master and Umbra apprentice under the Rule of Two . During his training, Vorr warned Karrick that, as his umbra side powers grew, an equal of the light side—whom Vorr believed would be Drayden but later reasoned was Nyla—would arise to challenge him.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: By decree of the Supreme Leader, Karrick's true name could never be spoken. Karrick sought to put his past behind him, become immune to the temptations of the light, and claim his birthright by ruling the weaker beings of the galaxy. He typically wore a combat helmet , patterned after the battle gear of the Knights of Karrick, in order to conceal his identity and give him a more intimidating presence. This helmet also contained a vocal modifier, which lowered the pitch of Karrick's voice considerably. Karrick's actions at Drayden's temple earned him the nickname "Aetheri Killer," a name whispered amongst the New Imperium ranks who knew Karrick had prevented the Return of the Aetheri Order. No longer an Aetheri but neither an Umbra, Karrick strove to harness the pain of his emotional conflict in order to fuel his extraordinary powers and destroy the last traces of the Aetheri tradition.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Following the incident on board their shuttle, Vorr and Karrick proceeded towards the Cave of Evil on Mirefall. Karrick commented that he could still sense his uncle from his time on Mirefall training with Zho . Vorr nodded and told Karrick that one of the most formidable Aetheri began his training here. Karrick then asked Vorr why he spoke of Drayden with respect. Vorr said that Drayden had earned his respect and fear. Karrick told Vorr that Drayden was weak. Vorr replied that Drayden was not weak, merely misguided. If Vorr had had Drayden by his side, the galaxy would have belonged to him a lot earlier. They then went to the cave, from which Karrick could sense a coldness radiating, along with death and other things. Vorr explained that was where all the fears Karrick had been too weak to bury resided. He could go in or run away. But Karrick's mind was already made up. He ventured in.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Once inside, Karrick had a vision of his uncle Joren, saying that he didn't want to fight Karrick. Karrick told him that he did not care and activated his flux blade. Vorr sensed the decision Karrick had made and told him that it was good and that Drayden would have murdered him in his sleep because he feared Karrick and how formidable he'd become. As the two dueled, Vorr advised Karrick to use his hatred, rise above what was holding him back, and strike against the light within him. Karrick did so and impaled the vision of Joren. Thinking he was finished, Karrick told Vorr that he was done. But Vorr told him that the vision had just started.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick then caught sight of his parents, begging him to quit his actions. He tried to kill the light within him by saying that Beno wasn't his name, but Elira insisted it was and that he was loved. Outside the cave, Vorr could sense the conflict within Karrick, but then he sensed Karrick ignite his flux blade. He told Karrick to kill the connection and snuff it out. But, in the cave, Karrick hadn't killed his parents; instead, he used his flux blade to slice a tree. This action proved that though he hated his uncle, he loved his mother and father, and it foreshadowed what he would do to Vorr, who couldn't sense that he had not killed the vision of his parents. Karrick then destroyed the Cave of Evil, surprising Vorr, who told Karrick that the cave had stood for thousands of years and that he had planned to bring other apprentices there. Karrick answered by telling Vorr that the past was the past and that Vorr would no longer need any more apprentices.

### Enforcer of the New Imperium

#### Mission to Karaxis

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Colonization of the Unknown Regions

> " They also said that someone called Zarrin Karrick was leading the New Imperium army. Does that name mean anything to you? " " You could say that. General Solen will want to hear about this immediately. " ―Kazuda Xiono and Ello Asty

As one of the commanders of the New Imperium's military, Karrick was heavily involved in its campaign to colonize the Unknown Regions, where the former Imperials had been rebuilding their strength since the Battle of Ashden. Aided by mysterious alien navigators known as the Attendants , the New Imperium had been able to navigate beyond the frontier of the known galaxy, allowing them to survive and rebuild their power. Several threats lurked in the Unknown Regions, hermetic kingdoms who were confronted by the growing new power. On Supreme Leader Vorr's instruction, the new military undertook a major offensive against several of these kingdoms to seize their worlds and resources to fuel their rise.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
At some point, Karrick led an army to the world of Tehar , where they subjugated the local population by massacring a village. However, the siblings Kel and Eila survived the destruction of their village and fled Tehar after stowing away on a cargo ship. Since the children bore the knowledge of its aggressive actions against the people on Tehar, the New Imperium placed a large bounty of twenty thousand credits on their heads, telling informants that Kel and Eila were members of a high-ranking New Imperium family from outside its military hierarchy.

Kel and Eila eventually made their way to Castilon and sought refuge on a supertanker fuel depot known as the Colossus . After meeting the Coalition spy Kazuda Xiono , Eila told him about Karrick's involvement in the raid on her village. Though she knew little about the warrior dressed in black, apart from his name and affiliation with the army that invaded Tehar, Karrick's flux blade reminded Eila of the legends about the Aetheri who carried the same weapons. Xiono, who was also unaware of Karrick's identity, passed this information to the Coalition while reporting to Ello Asty .

### The search for Drayden

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### GUHL-J03870

> " General Vren… I know where we must go… and I know this is the key. We are so close. " ―Zarrin Karrick

Later, Karrick, Vren and two New Imperium admirals gathered in a conference room aboard the Finalizer over the planet GUHL-J03870 . They were discussing travel to a planet in the Western Reaches . While in the conference, the creature that the shock trooper, FN-2187 , was chasing turned off the lights, interrupting the conference. Karrick, his temper under control, felt something nearby: something from the planet that should not be on board. He activated his flux blade to illuminate the room and looked around, but whatever it was had now gone.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
After the conference, Karrick transmitted orders to Phasma via private frequency. But he had to make sure she got them, so he walked over to the captain's quarters and called her from outside. Only Phasma's helmet appeared through the opened doors. Pleased by her punctuality, Karrick relayed what he sensed to Phasma, for he planned to have a discreet search throughout the Finalizer . He ordered her to take a squad of trainees to investigate the planet for any Coalition activity. Anything Phasma may find, she must deliver to Karrick. Then the dark warrior left.

#### Marooned with Vren

> " How did we…? Did you…did you save me? " " Not intentionally. I saved myself. You were just nearby. Communications are out. " " Which means I have no choice but to talk to you instead of literally anyone else. " ―Armitage Vren and Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Vren, who had been hiding in the trees and watching as the event occurred, cautiously approached Bylsma from his hiding place. Recognizing the old man's uniform, Vren came to the conclusion that Bylsma was a Cindervalean palace guard . Bylsma confirmed as much and revealed that he had fled into exile after the destruction of Cindervale. He stranded himself on a distant planet and severed his connections to the larger galaxy, fearing that his new home would suffer Cindervale's fate if he attempted to use his ship's communications, but as a result, Bylsma had no knowledge of the events that unfolded after the disaster. Vren used Bylsma's ignorance of recent galactic history in order to gain his trust. In addition, he used Karrick's heritage to his advantage, informing Bylsma that the man whom the norwoods attacked was, in fact, a fellow son of Cindervale. More to the point, he was the son of Elira Solen, the princess of Cindervale. Bylsma, who had known both the princess and her adoptive father, saw the physical resemblance between Karrick and his mother and wondered if Karrick was anything like the princess he once served. Vren assured him that Karrick was indeed like his

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: the son of Elira Solen, the princess of Cindervale. Bylsma, who had known both the princess and her adoptive father, saw the physical resemblance between Karrick and his mother and wondered if Karrick was anything like the princess he once served. Vren assured him that Karrick was indeed like his mother, even if he would have denied it. Bylsma built a stretcher and carried Karrick to his home, where Vren convinced the retired soldier to give him access to the ship's communications so that they could be rescued. After regaining consciousness, Karrick played along with Vren's deception until a shuttle arrived to retrieve them. The shuttle ramp lowered revealing Captain Phasma and a squad of shock troopers, leading to the norwoods' immediate death by volt pistol fire. Karrick boarded the shuttle in silence alongside Vren, who told the captain to spare the old man's life but to disable his communications array, leaving Bylsma truly stranded and alone. They reported directly to Vorr via hologram after their return to Voidfang Base; although Karrick offered to punish the culprit responsible for sabotaging the shuttle, Vren insisted on handling the matter personally, given that the conspiracy was directed at him. Vorr approved the general's request, causing Karrick to question the Supreme Leader's faith in Vren. Karrick, who could sense Vren's ambition to kill and replace Vorr, and therefore, deemed him untrustworthy, was certain that his master knew it as well.
