Vorr dismissed Karrick's concerns, however, and explained why Vren—a vicious and unforgiving man, consumed by ambition and driven by spite, molded

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Leading by example like his grandfather before him, Karrick fought alongside his shock troopers as they engaged the Benathy and personally killed numerous enemy combatants until their deity arrived. Despite Ruthford's skepticism, Karrick was undaunted and ordered his men to keep fighting. After their initial efforts to kill the beast failed, he improvised a plan to kill the creature to the dismay of Ruthford, who could no longer restrain himself from expressing his disapproval of Karrick's desire to match Velgor's achievements. In his view, there was no competition between Karrick and Velgor because the latter was long since dead. Despite the captain's lack of faith in him, Karrick commanded a shuttle to bring him to the jaws of the Zyll Beast, diving head-first into its mouth. Convinced that Karrick was dead, Ruthford was in the middle of recommending the option of retreat to a nearby admiral when the Zyll Beast suddenly collapsed and died. Karrick had killed the creature from within, where it was vulnerable, and managed to cut his way out, emerging from its corpse covered in the blood of the Benathy's deity. Declaring that their god was now dead, the dark warrior commanded the Benathy to submit to the New Imperium, and they did by kneeling in submission to him. In the end, he not only gained the allegiance of the Benathy, but also Captain Ruthford's respect.

#### Mission to Pillio

> " Tell me where Lor Saan Tarka took the map. " " …Bayora. He took it to Bayora. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Del Meeko

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Mission to Pillio

> " Tell me where Lor Saan Tarka took the map. " " …Bayora. He took it to Bayora. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Del Meeko

The hunt for Drayden caused Karrick to undertake a journey the planet Pillio . Although Saan Tarka was not found on the world, the New Imperium's allies captured and detained Del Meeko , a veteran of the Galactic Civil War who served the Imperium and Concordat, in turn, as a member of Inferno Squad . Upon his arrival, the dark warrior was greeted by Protectorate Gleb of Jinata Security . Dismissive of the formalities, he instructed the Aquari officer to lead him to Meeko. He found the former soldier wounded and alone on the bridge of the Raider II -class corvette Corvus .

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Having gained the information he sought, Karrick turned the prisoner over to New Imperium officer Giedan Hask , one of Meeko's former teammates in the Inferno Squad prior the Imperium's fall, who executed Meeko shortly thereafter.

#### Raid on Ashden

> " The map to Drayden. We know you found it. And now you're going to give it to the New Imperium. " " The New Imperium rose from the umbra side. You did not. " " I'll show you the umbra side. " " You may try. But you cannot deny the truth that is your family. " " You're so right. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Lor Saan Tarka

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Eventually, the New Imperium learned that Saan Tarka was on Ashden . Karrick, who knew Saan Tarka from childhood as the explorer was once an old ally of Solen and Drayden, brought the Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser Finalizer in his search for the map. The New Imperium's military attacked the village of Tuanul , where Saan Tarka lived. Once the New Imperium shock troopers, under the command of Phasma, rounded up the denizens of the village, Karrick arrived on the battlefield and confronted Saan Tarka, lamenting how old the former explorer had become, to which Saan Tarka replied that Karrick's fall to the umbra side was far worse. Karrick demanded that Saan Tarka give the map to the New Imperium, but Saan Tarka refused to submit to the will of the umbra side and reminded the one-time Aetheri that Karrick could not deny the truth of his heritage, at which point Karrick struck him down with his flux blade while sarcastically agreeing with him.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Shortly after leaving Vale under the guard of several shock troopers, Karrick arrived on the Finalizer ' s bridge upon hearing that the Coalition pilot escaped aboard a SKREE fighter . Vren confirmed this with the additional information of Vale having had help from someone within the New Imperium's ranks. Karrick realized that it could only have been FN-2187, after remembering how the conflicted soldier had hesitated in Tuanul, and he said as much to Vren. The SKREE fighter was eventually shot down after a brief skirmish, and it crash-landed on Ashden. The New Imperium recognized that Vale and the deserter designated FN-2187 were looking for the droid, so Vren ordered a squadron to be sent to Ashden to recover it first. Vren soon spoke to the Supreme Leader, who ordered them to capture the droid if they could, but destroy it if they must. Karrick questioned the capability of Vren's soldiers and training methods, wondering aloud whether the Supreme Leader would be better off using an army of replicas as the Vantor Republic and the early Imperium had once done. Vren told him that they were more than capable, and warned Karrick not to let his personal mission to find Drayden interfere with the Supreme Leader's orders.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Return of the past

#### The pull to the light

> " The droid we seek is aboard the Corsair Wing . In the hands of your father… Dax Karrick. " " He means nothing to me. " " Even you, master of the Knights of Karrick… have never faced such a test. " " By the grace of your training, I will not be seduced. " " We shall see. We shall see. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Vorr

With the droid gone, the Finalizer made its way to Voidfang Base. Once there, Karrick and Vren spoke to Supreme Leader Vorr, who communicated to his subordinates via an enlarged hologram . Vorr remained concerned that Drayden's return would be a threat to the New Imperium, so Vren proposed that they finally use the weapon as intended and destroy the Concordat one and for all. Without the Republic, Vren knew that the Coalition would be vulnerable and could be stopped before they found Drayden. The Supreme Leader gave the general his permission and Vren left to oversee preparations, while Karrick remained behind.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick brought Nyla to Voidfang Base via his command shuttle and restrained her in an interrogation chair. When she awoke, she asked where her friends were, and Karrick told her he had no idea and pointed out that would be a relief to her. He sensed she still wanted to kill him, and she said it was because she was being hunted by a creature in a mask. He removed his mask to show his young face and asked about the droid, but the girl only gave him Orio-6's technical specifications. Karrick told her that he knew about the map and that the New Imperium had recovered the rest of it from the archives of the Imperium.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
> " I'm being torn apart. I want to be free of this pain. I know what I have to do… but I don't know if I have the strength to do it. Will you help me? " " Yes. Anything. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Dax Karrick

Karrick commanded the New Imperium troops to be on alert for Nyla as she began making her way through the base, as he knew that the longer she was able to tap into her powers while escaping, the more dangerous she would become. A trooper reported sensor readings in Hangar 718 , which meant Nyla could be there. But investigations turned up nothing. Nonetheless, Karrick wanted every hangar on lockdown to prevent Nyla from commandeering a ship. Right in the middle of that order, he was interrupted by a familiar presence: Dax Karrick. His father was on Voidfang Base.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick ordered for a search of the Corsair Wing , for the ship had shortly been sighted at the edge of a cliff. By the time he arrived on the scene, everything checked clear and not a single hidden trap could be found. He boarded the Corsair and sat on the pilot's seat, looking for anything that may lead him to Karrick's whereabouts. Just then, he spotted Coalition Vectors flying past and assaulting the thermal oscillator , hoping to destroy it and set off a chain reaction that would cause the planet to implode before the weapon could destroy D'Qar. Karrick rushed to the oscillator, commanding his troops to find the intruders. He knew Karrick had to be nearby, as well as the fact that he did not come alone.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: As Karrick advanced on the walkway, he stopped upon hearing the voice of his father, calling out to him from behind, using his birth name. He turned about face and said he had been waiting for this eventuality. Karrick told him to remove the mask so he could see the face of his son once more. Karrick removed the mask but told Karrick that he had destroyed Beno, who Karrick thought was weak and foolish, much like his father before him. Karrick refused to acknowledge Karrick's pessimistic stance on the matter, retorting that his son was very much alive and Vorr was simply using Karrick for his power, and that once Vorr had exhausted Karrick's usefulness, he would be disposed of.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick, while neither denying nor confirming what Karrick said about Vorr to be true, stated that it was too late for him. Karrick pleaded with Karrick to come home to his true family, claiming that he and Solen desperately missed the presence of their son. Karrick, conflicted by the pull towards the light, broke down in tears and told his father that he was being torn apart by the constant struggle between the dark and the light inside him and wanted to be free of the pain that he was feeling. He knew what he had to do to put a permanent end to his inner turmoil, although Karrick was uncertain whether or not he could perform the necessary act to do so. Asking for his father's assistance in ceasing the struggle, Karrick agreed, not knowing that it was the light that Karrick felt conflicted by.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick, who was being watched from afar by Brevok, Nyla, and Jax, took out his flux blade and Karrick grabbed hold of it. As the Voidfang finished draining the star it orbited to power the weapon, and the light on the planet died out, Karrick ignited his flux blade and impaled his father through the torso. A mortally wounded Dax Karrick touched his son's face one last time before falling to his death in the bowels of the oscillator. Despite Karrick's role in his death, Dax died refusing to believe that his son was lost to the umbra side forever.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Unbeknownst to Karrick, he had carried out an Umbra trial of ascendancy , a trial that required the sacrifice of a loved one to unlock newfound depths of dark power. The act of patricide had an unsettling effect on Karrick, as did Karrick's gesture of compassion which tormented Karrick far more than killing his own father. Rather than make him stronger in the umbra side, as he had thought, it had weakened his spirit. He became unbalanced, and was more miserable and weak than before. The shock had been so profound, he did not register Brevok's roar of anguish nor Nyla's scream of horror.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Jax ignited the Drayden flux blade that had been given to him for safekeeping by Maz Oru—a flux blade that once belonged to Joren Drayden, and to Kael before him. Karrick demanded that Jax give him the flux blade, claiming it belonged to him, but instead the former shock trooper engaged him in a flux blade duel. It was a short but brutal contest, in which Karrick kept striking his bowcaster injury in order to fuel his anger and power. In the end, Jax, who nonetheless landed one blow on Karrick's right shoulder, was no match for Karrick's power. Karrick overwhelmed and disarmed his opponent, ending the fight with a punch and a flux blade blow across Jax's back that left the one-time shock trooper comatose.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
anger rage, and fury. She turned the tide of the fight and pushed her own offensive against the dark warrior, who she was finally able to disarm. Karrick realized that he dueled an opponent with more anger than he, or with an emotion that he didn't even recognize anymore. In doing so, she slashed her blade across his face, knocking him down and disfiguring him in the process. Phasma briefly bore witness to Karrick and Nyla's duel but did not provide aid to the umbra side warrior, as she was busy searching for the officer she had framed for the fall of Voidfang Base, Sol Rivas . With Nyla having rejected an amorphous, dark voice in her mind that demanded she kill Karrick, the young woman and Karrick were separated for long enough that, before they could engage any further, the surface of the planet began to break apart—the Coalition was victorious, and the destruction of the oscillator triggered the Voidfang's implosion. Karrick and Nyla were separated by a deep chasm, so Nyla left the dark warrior behind, recovered Jax, and fled the planet with Brevok aboard the Corsair Wing .

As the planet continued to collapse, Vorr ordered General Vren to find Karrick and bring the young knight before the Supreme Leader so the young warrior's training could be completed. Vren and several troopers tracked Karrick's signal and took him aboard a shuttle, leaving before the planet exploded. Immediately following Voidfang Base's destruction, Karrick received treatment for the long scars on his body, though it was too late to erase them completely.

### Let the past die

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Let the past die

#### A child in a mask

> " Yes. There it is. You have too much of your father's heart in you, young Karrick. " " I killed Dax Karrick. When the moment came I didn't hesitate. " " And look at you. The deed split your spirit to the bone. " ―Vorr and Zarrin Karrick

Following the Coalition's evacuation of the base on D'Qar, Karrick was summoned to Supreme Leader Vorr's throne room on the Supremacy . The blows inflicted on him, by Nyla and Brevok, though stitched up some by microsutures , were still as fresh as ever, causing him some discomfort, though he tried to hide this. Kneeling before his master, he listened as Vorr loudly recalled the raw, untamed power that Karrick possessed, abilities which had originally brought him to the umbra sider's attention. Knowing the potential of the powerful Drayden bloodline, the Supreme Leader revealed his belief that Karrick could fulfill his grandfather's dark legacy.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Chasing the Coalition

> " Follow my lead. " ―Zarrin Karrick, to his wingmen

As Vren had anticipated through new tracking technology, the New Imperium armada emerged from hyperspace to find the Coalition fleet unprepared and defenseless in the Oetchi system . The Battle of Oetchi commenced as the warship Supremacy led the charge, its powerful pulse lances showering the fleet with unyielding blasts. To complement the barrage, the Supremacy scrambled its short-distance fighters, with Karrick spearheading the assault in his personal SKREE silencer . Covered by three wingmen , until the third pilot was quickly destroyed, the dark apprentice intercepted the Coalition's MC85 Star Cruiser Raddik , capital ship of the fleet. Before the insurgent pilots could launch a counterattack, he destroyed the Raddik hangar, leaving them unable to resist the fighter wing.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Upon discovering Drayden's location, Vorr planned to wipe him out from above as soon as the more immediate enemy had been dealt with. Nyla summoned Drayden's flux blade to her hand, only for Vorr to redirect the hilt onto her head; Karrick, eyes shut, merely tilted his head to the right to avoid being struck by the flying object. The Supreme Leader revealed through his oculus the Coalition being picked off one by one as they tried to flee aboard transports for safety. All that Karrick's mother had fought for would be destroyed by the Supremacy ' s guns. In response, an enraged Nyla pulled Karrick's flux blade into her hands and charged at Vorr, who effortlessly overpowered her. Karrick watched the flux blade fall out of Nyla's grip and shut off, sliding on the floor back to its owner's feet.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Convictions and rejections

> " It's time to let old things die. Vorr, Drayden. The Umbra, the Aetheri, the Insurgents… Let it all die. Nyla, I want you to join me. We can rule together and bring a new order to the galaxy. " ―Zarrin Karrick Nyla, who stared at Karrick through eyes filled with joy, beseeched him to help her save the Coalition fleet. To her disbelief and horror, Karrick proposed that he and Nyla join together and "let old things die," including the Coalition, and bring a new order to the galaxy. Neither fear nor anger influenced his decision; he had chosen to continue down the dark path with a deep resolve. Nyla begged Karrick to not give into the umbra side, but the latter stood behind his convictions. To his frustration, he could see that Nyla was still clinging to that futile hope of hers. He urged her to "let go," to admit the truth about her parents—a truth she had always known but hidden away for years. Nyla struggled to control her emotions as she admitted that she knew this, that her parents were simply "nobody," but the revelation that she came from nothing threatened to overwhelm her. At that moment, Karrick called Nyla "nothing," and said she was not that to him. Karrick, who saw Nyla as an ally in destroying the past he hated, wanted the former scavenger to join him. Motioning her to take his hand, he pleaded with

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### The reign of Zarrin Karrick

#### The New Supreme Leader

> " Get all our forces down to that Coalition base. Let's finish this. " " Finish this? Who do you think you're talking to? You presume to command my army? Our Supreme Leader is dead! We have no ruler— " " The Supreme Leader is dead. " " Long live the Supreme Leader. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Armitage Vren

Karrick regained consciousness shortly after Vren reached the throne room. Having killed the Supreme Leader and his guards, Karrick falsely accused Nyla of murder, claiming that she was the one responsible for Vorr's death. Vren, who had contemplated shooting the fallen knight before he awoke, informed Karrick that the girl escaped from the Supremacy using Vorr's private shuttle. Realizing that Nyla had awoken before him, Karrick pondered why she had spared his life, knowing he was at her mercy while in an unconscious state. It then occurred to Karrick that Nyla did, in fact, care about him. Regardless, he dismissed it as a sign of sentimental weakness that would eventually lead to Nyla's destruction.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Battle of Saltmark

> " General Vren, advance. No quarter, no prisoners. " ―Zarrin Karrick, to Armitage Vren

As far as the new Supreme Leader was concerned, the Battle of Saltmark would prove to be the final battle in the war between the New Imperium and the Coalition. He would give no quarter to his enemies, nor take a single prisoner. Looming overhead in his command shuttle, Karrick oversaw the deployment of AT-ATs , AT-M6s , and AT-STs to the salt-covered surface of Saltmark, gathered from what remained of the Supremacy . It would be a relatively straightforward operation, with Karrick's forces marching on an abandoned insurgent base which the Coalition had appropriated for its defense.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: The time had come for Karrick to face Drayden personally. He slowly advanced until he was but a few meters from the old Aetheri. He tauntingly asked if Drayden had come to be his salvation. Drayden answered half-heartedly in the negative. Then flux blades were drawn. Drayden made no effort to harm his nephew and only moved to avoid Karrick's attacks. He apologized for failing in his duty as Beno Karrick's mentor, but Karrick took it with sarcasm and declared that the war had ended with the death of the Coalition. In addition, he stated that Drayden would die as well, marking the end of the Aetheri Order itself. He was wrong on all counts, according to Drayden: the war had just begun, the Insurgency was reborn, and he would not die as the last of the Aetheri.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: At that moment, Karrick realized what had his uncle had done: by distracting him, the old Aetheri had bought time for the remaining members of the Coalition to escape. Vren had been right all along. Angered by the deception, Karrick, Vren, and their forces scoured the now-empty base, but finding only a projection of his father's golden hanging dice, all Karrick could do was kneel in defeat as they vanished from his hand. As the Coalition evacuated, Karrick saw Nyla once more as she boarded the Corsair Wing ; no words were said as she closed the door on him, although Karrick sensed that Nyla felt neither hatred nor compassion for him. Both knew that this struggle between them was far from concluded. Karrick had become the Supreme Leader, all but destroyed his mother's Coalition and struck down his uncle on the battlefield of Saltmark, but it did not feel like a victory to Karrick.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: After his display of power, Karrick reminisced alone about recent events and his encounters and memories with his father, mother, Vorr, and Nyla. Though trying to affirm to himself that the past did not matter and that it was done, he could not let go of the images of those who were once close to him. Sending for Vren, Karrick met with the General, telling him that he was a trusted advisor and that he needed advisement on military matters, which Vorr did not often discuss with Karrick. Though Vren confirmed that Vorr had his plans, he implored Karrick to take his own military direction as he now commanded the New Imperium's military. When Vren suggested that Karrick fulfill the dreams of their forebears and rebuild the Imperium, Karrick told Vren that his own forebears shaped the known galaxy while Vren's bloodline produced lesser "lieutenants and lickspittles."

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
The two then conferred on resources, with Vren elaborating that they needed more ships as Voidfang Base's destruction left them without a shipyard and the Coalition's unusual tactics at the Battle of Oetchi destroyed the Supremacy and much of their fleet. With the destruction of the Concordat at Hosnian Prime and the dismantling of the Coalition, however, Vren believed the New Imperium would face little coalition other than local militias for their ambitions of conquest. Karrick cut Vren's deliberations short, as he had not ordered him to perform any military action, instead ordering that a throne be built for himself. Though Karrick suggested that the throne could be anything he liked, such as one made of aurodium , Karrick told Vren to choose and to do nothing else until Karrick had a worthy throne, cautioning Vren to get it right the first time.

The fires of Emberfall

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Wandering the suns-scorched desert, Karrick encountered a Canyon Krayt dragon , slaying it without a weapon and fashioning its hide into clothing. Attacking two other desert wanderers, Karrick used their communications equipment to order the Finalizer to Dunemere. Finding a dewback , Karrick relocated Graska's fortress, ordering General Armitage Vren to hit his given location with a full spread of weapons in twenty minutes. Karrick rushed the fortress, once again dispatching guards, reclaiming his flux blade and escaping shortly before Vren carried out the attack.

Later, Karrick met with Vainé via hologram aboard the Finalizer , the latter having feared the worst after hearing of the New Imperium attack. Vainé asked if Karrick's understanding of Velgor and his power had grown on Dunemere; Karrick confirmed that it had, with there being power and purity in his being alone. Pleased, Vainé told Karrick that there was still more to be shown about Velgor's life and legacy, and after confirming that their adventures would continue, told Karrick that he would await him at the island of Varykino on the planet Ondara .

The waters of Ondara

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
The waters of Ondara

> " The people of this world need to evolve . They need a catalyst , to move beyond what they have been. I am giving it to them. " ―Zarrin Karrick Karrick met Vainé on Ondara at the ruined Varykino Villa , struggling to comprehend its importance as he did with Port Vail on Dunemere. Vainé regaled Karrick with tales of Ondara's former glory, detailing its history as a powerful cultural hub with a democratic monarchy . Vainé shared his knowledge of powerful individuals that once inhabited Ondara, such as Marlowe and Vellis Saan Tarka , but especially Emperor Theron Mal, explaining that Ondara fell into chaos and disrepair after the Galactic Civil War as galaxy felt that Ondara's citizens had profited from their association with Mal. Growing impatient, Karrick did not see the importance of the dead Emperor's past. Vainé explained that Ondara was where Velgor fell in love with and wedded Karrick's grandmother, Lira Ondar, Queen of Ondara and Galactic Senator . Though Karrick rejected the idea of falling in love for the sake of power, Vainé further explained that it was the loss of Lira that granted Velgor his dark power; his lack of limits for attachments allowed the Umbra Lord strength and focus. Though Karrick claimed to have no limits, Vainé asked if Karrick already had everything he needed and desired, causing Karrick to once again reflect

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: observed Karrick's charade quietly for some time, Vainé asked why Karrick was doing what he was doing. Karrick claimed to want to have the people of Ondara to evolve, but Vainé saw through Karrick, recognizing a Velgor-like streak of self hatred in Karrick, interpreting the bizarre charade as a way of attacking himself. Angered by this accusation, Karrick lifted Vainé's droid chassis off of the ground, partially dismantling it. Questioning Vainé's ultimate usefulness, Vainé told Karrick of a vault at Velgor's castle on Emberfall full of power, but that it could only be opened when Karrick was ready. Though Karrick threatened Vainé, demanding that he take him to the vault immediately, Vainé refused, preferring to die than pass Velgor's legacy to someone unworthy. Vainé implored Karrick to find somewhere true to put his hate other than himself: a worthy enemy. Processing Vainé's proposal, Karrick ordered Vren to withdraw the Dreadnought from Ondara, seconds before it would be ready to destroy the city.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Believing they had fought off the New Imperium, the coalition fighters of Ondara returned underground to celebrate and thank the disguised Karrick for leading them. After killing all of the Ondara citizens in his company, Karrick ordered Vainé to find him a worthy enemy, of which Vainé already had one in mind.

Conquering Korrath

> " ...it's the Supreme Leader . " " What? What is he doing? " " General, it's... it's beautiful. " ―A New Imperium communications officer and General Vren

Following Karrick and Vren's previous discussion, the New Imperium brought its forces to bear on Korrath. Despite Vren's control over the battle so far, Karrick took it upon himself to personally fly into the fray in his personal SKREE silencer. Exhibiting phenomenal flying skills and executing exceptionally tight maneuvers, Karrick cleared a path to the heavily defended command center. Though this defied Vren's plan for the battle, which called for a siege anchored by ground troops, Vren did not interfere with his Supreme Leader's strategy. Though his wingmates failed to provide Karrick with adequate cover, Karrick successfully arrived at the command center and secured a victory for the New Imperium.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Shortly after the victory at Korrath, Karrick sat before a procession of New Imperium shock troopers on his newly completed throne. As his followers chanted for their Supreme Leader, Karrick regarded Vren, who stood beside him, telling his General that he knew the display made Vren feel small, and that it was not his role to feel large. Karrick left his throne, ordering Vren to Karrick's chambers for an after-action report and commending Vren for the throne. Vren reported that the invasion was a complete success, and that Korrath's shipyard were ready to begin shoring up losses from Voidfang Base, Saltmark and Ondara. Karrick dismissed Vren, but the General remained, hoping to discuss another matter. Vren expressed his understanding that Karrick used proactive and successful strategies that deviated from Vren's own, but made known his wish to be more informed of such surprise actions so as to be a more effective general. Shutting down Vren's concerns coldly, Karrick simply dismissed Vren again. Picking up his commlink, Karrick answered a call from Vainé, who told Karrick that he had found an Aetheri, a worthy enemy for Karrick, as promised.

The Aetheri on Lahtee

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: After Karrick's encounter with Grandea on Lahtee and the New Imperium's full subjugation of Korrath's shipyards, the Finalizer would be approached by the Night Buzzard , a ship that belonged to Karrick's former allies, the Knights of Karrick. Karrick allowed the ship to board the Finalizer and was greeted by its sole occupant, a woman named Tava Karrick , proclaiming herself to be a Knight of Karrick and submitting herself to Karrick's service. Karrick ignited his flux blade, quickly attempting to strike her down. Tava ignited her own flux blade, engaging Karrick in a fierce duel. Incurious about Tava, Karrick deflected Tava's attempts at conversation but denied nearby shock troopers the chance to take her down, wanting to deal with Tava himself. Asserting that the Knights of Karrick no longer meant anything to him, Karrick rebuffed Tava's goading and disarmed her, holding her neck between both flux blades. Tava pled to Karrick that she was the only one with which he could discuss the "Shadow", and Karrick spared her life, taunting that Tava best remember how easy his victory was. Asking Karrick for something to eat, the two warriors moved to a private dining chamber aboard the Finalizer .

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Reappearing in the dark bog, Karrick was approached by an enormous dark figure. The figure told Karrick that he must be reminded of his pain after trying to return to the light and forget his pain and attacked Karrick with a red-bladed flux blade. Karrick emerged from his vision and stumbled out of the meditation chamber, his body having manifested grievous real injuries. Vainé cradled Karrick, asking what he had done to himself and believing that his grandfather would be proud.

Vainé placed Karrick in Velgor's bacta tank as Karrick faded in and out of consciousness. Reciting Karrick's recent journeys to him, Vainé began to reveal his ultimate plan for Karrick: Karrick's "death" in the service of transforming him into a new Velgor. For this to happen, Vainé told Karrick that he must "die", just as Kael Drayden had, to complete his journey and realize his full greatness. Vainé injected Karrick with a drug, causing Karrick to lose consciousness, and moved Karrick to a platform raised above a chamber of falling lava.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: used his flux blade to smash through the mask and fall further, confronting Velgor's specter once more as it attacked Karrick with his flux blade. Karrick asked Velgor's specter why he was doing this; Velgor's specter replied that he had sought to find and understand Velgor at every opportunity, and advised him to pay attention. As the two dueled, Karrick tried to assert himself as Velgor's equal, which the specter rebuffed, then asked why their family must fight each other generation after generation, to which the specter replied that there was no destiny, instead only power and how it was chosen to be used. Velgor's specter explained that Velgor's greatest power was the truth and that he was strongest when he made his own choices and saw himself as he truly was. To this, the specter removed its helmet to reveal the face of Karrick's former identity, Beno Karrick.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick's specter, now dressed in white Aetheri robes , professed that there was still something for Karrick to learn, which Karrick disbelieved, but Karrick's specter offered himself as the past that Karrick was trying so desperately to kill. Karrick attacked the specter with his flux blade, which the specter deflected with the previous, blue-bladed version Karrick wielded as an Aetheri apprentice. Karrick's specter reminded Karrick of how thoroughly he had destroyed each connection he had with his family, and explained his recent adventures as attempting to connect with his grandfather. The specter believed that the only choice Karrick had made for himself was letting Tava Karrick go, something that was not an attempt to imitate Velgor or anyone else. Karrick's specter revealed the depth of his insecurity, his fear of moving forward due to how thoroughly he had ruined himself. The specter offered that if perhaps Karrick wasn't who he was, then Nyla might've taken his hand. Karrick's specter blocked another blade strike with a bare hand, asserting that Karrick couldn't kill the past or escape the truth.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick's specter said that it would not stop the painful confrontation, as Beno Karrick was an Aetheri. Karrick rejected the specter as another dead phantom, wishing to fight something real instead of ghosts. Karrick's specter advised Karrick to move forward and only make his own choices, but offered Karrick that he would find a real enemy as he wished. Taunting Karrick to be careful what he wished for, he sent Karrick falling out of the vault with a snap of fingers. As the specter faded, Karrick plummeted to the smoldering surface of Emberfall.

#### Campaign of terror

> " We have learned from the mistakes of the Imperium—They were too lenient . The Coalition is looking to replenish their lost ships and weapons… It is imperative they find none. Make sure the word is spread from here—to the farthest corner of the galaxy. " ―Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick ensured that his one-time rival would have little independent authority without supervision, even giving assignments to the Knights of Karrick before entrusting Vren with anything of importance. At some point during the war, Karrick sought an update on the Order's stock of refueling stations, leading to a short notice meeting aboard the Titan that Vren was made to attend. Prior to the meeting, when Shock trooper Commander Pyre complained about the short notice, Vren explained it was due to Karrick's wishes. Karrick also kept Vren close by to countermand the general's orders when necessary; on one occasion, Vren dismissed a reported sighting of the Coalition operative Jax, believing it was a waste of the New Imperium's resources to follow up on every rumor regarding the Coalition. This led Karrick to openly chastise Vren on the bridge of the Finalizer , ensuring the general understood that they would use every available asset to find and destroy the Coalition.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Holding more power than he ever had in his life up to that point, the Supreme Leader made good on his vow to punish any world that showed anything less than absolute loyalty. Making his way to the neutral planet of Fondor , Karrick placed it under military occupation after learning that the Coalition had passed through its system. Although an official of Fondor swore that his government held no allegiance to the insurgents, having refused to assist them in any capacity, the mere contact with the enemies of the New Imperium provided Karrick with his justification for seizing control of the Fondor Shipyards . Convinced the Old Imperium had been too lenient, Karrick adopted a zero-tolerance policy in regard to the Coalition, and as such, he personally decapitated the official. Ultimately, Fondor was made an example to the rest of the galaxy, warning them to stay away from the Coalition on pain of death. Such measures were intended by Karrick to prevent the Coalition from replacing their lost resources.

#### Supervising the advance

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Rebuilding his command in the wake of the Supremacy ' s destruction, Karrick brought Allegiant General Enric Pryde to the forefront of his operations after discovering the reserve forces under his command. He also transferred his command to Pryde's Iron Cruiser Steadfast , bringing Vren with him after the Finalizer sustained significant damage from the run-in with Coalition forces over Batuu. Karrick entrusted important jobs that could have otherwise gone to Vren to the Allegiant General: in effect, the years that Vren spent jockeying for power against Karrick ultimately worked against the general, as his authority was superseded not only by Karrick, but Pryde as well. As Supreme Leader, nevertheless, Karrick formed a regime that was different from the one overseen by his predecessor. He sought to foster cooperation among the top New Imperium military leaders, and as such Karrick formed the Supreme Council , a cabinet consisting of members of High Command, including Pryde, Vren, Admiral Frantis Griss , and generals Amret Engell , Bellava Parnadee , and Domaric Quinn .

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: They were all proud men and women who were unaccustomed to Karrick's leadership, having risen through the ranks in a time when most high-ranking officers knew little of the New Imperium's goals and capabilities. Despite Karrick's motivation for creating the Council, their meetings aboard the Steadfast became marred by sniping and turf wars. Meanwhile, however, the New Imperium's military might cowed many worlds into submission, although some remained defiant despite the threat of annihilation. Karrick, who came to see himself as ruler of the galaxy, toured the worlds that the New Imperium conquered in the name of their new Supreme Leader. One of the worlds that he visited was under military occupation; the officer who greeted him expressed how honored they were by his presence while another prepared his speech to the local population, which included metaphors and allusions of cultural relevance to the world that they occupied.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: As he stood on a balcony overlooking the crowd, he crushed the datapad containing his speech, which was followed by the shock troopers saluting. The civilians responded by kneeling before him with downcast eyes as the New Imperium soldiers shouted "all hail the Supreme Leader!" Karrick visited another world that the New Imperium subjugated on his behalf. However, he was ambushed by a group of insurgents hiding within the crowd. Karrick ordered his shock troopers to stand their ground and fought beside them. During the battle, he targeted the woman who led the insurgents, determined to make her an example to others who defied his authority. Interested in why she would attack him despite the consequences, he allowed her to declare that her people would rather die fighting for freedom than submit to Karrick's fascist rule. Karrick's response was that he would make her people suffer for her actions, but the woman asserted that their sacrifice would not be in vain if it inspired further coalition against the New Imperium. Karrick dismissed her as a fool, and said that she would regret her choice. As a result, her world was set aflame as Karrick returned to the Iron Cruiser in

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Investigation on Vendaxa

> " If they are indeed hiding on Vendaxa, then we will pin them down, smother them with numbers, and the Resistan— " ―Armitage Vren

During the hunt for the Coalition, General Vren announced to a squad of shock troopers that the New Imperium had received word of the insurgents operating in secret on the planet Vendaxa . Supreme Leader Karrick interrupted the general and dismissed the shock troopers, intending to investigate the planet alone. However, Vren insisted on accompanying the Supreme Leader. They began their investigation upon arriving on Vendaxa, only to start bickering over their loyalties and sacrifices for the New Imperium. During their argument, an acklay approached the pair, causing Vren to run for his life while Karrick stood his ground. Karrick was unafraid and fought against the creature, but Vren took the opportunity to shoot at the Acklay with his SE-44C volt pistol pistol , causing it to run away. Karrick and Vren ultimately returned to the New Imperium after confirming that there were no Coalition operatives on Vendaxa.

#### Wisp of Drayden

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Wisp of Drayden

> " Where are you? I can feel you! I know you're watching me! Show yourself, you coward! No more tricks, Drayden...just the reckoning I deserve! You're a fool. " ―Zarrin Karrick, to Joren Drayden

Still sensing the presence of his Aetheri Master Joren Drayden, Zarrin Karrick attempted to have Drayden show himself by visiting locations of their past, starting with Saltmark, the site of their final encounter. As the Steadfast neared the planet, Enric Pryde informed the Supreme Leader that they arrived at Saltmark, only for Karrick to wrathfully order the preparation of his shuttle. Upon arriving on Saltmark, Karrick began to violently swing his flux blade near the location of his fateful duel with his former Aetheri Master. The Supreme Leader and the Knights of Karrick later traveled to the former Aetheri outpost on Elphrona, where he and his master had their first encounter with the Knights.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick commanded the Knights to remain vigilant for sightings of Drayden's ghost , to which the Knight Vicrul replied that no such apparition was felt. Karrick mocked him by saying that they were defeated in that outpost before claiming that he had one final place to look. Zarrin Karrick arrived on Ossus, where the Aetheri Sanctum of his past lay in ruin. Karrick desperately shouted for his Aetheri Master to show himself, but received no answer. After making peace with his fruitless travels, Karrick boarded his ship, ordering General Armitage Vren to bombard the location from orbit, as there was nothing left.

### Dark legacies

#### The phantom Emperor

> " He's gone mad. Flames of insurgency burn across the galaxy and Karrick chases a ghost . " " No. Someone was behind that transmission. And Leader Karrick will answer to no one. " ―Armitage Vren and Enric Pryde

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Within a year of Zarrin Karrick's ascension to supreme power, a mysterious transmission broadcasting the voice of Vael Mal—the long-dead Galactic Emperor and Dark Lord of the Umbra—reached the far corners of the galaxy. Although Karrick doubted that Mal had returned, he was certain that others believed the message, so he was determined to uncover the truth first to prevent any threats to his rule. As a result, he diverted his attention and the New Imperium's resources away from the Coalition to focus entirely on investigating the message. The broadcast bolstered the rumors that the Emperor lived but was in hiding, leading many within the New Imperium to believe that they should follow Mal instead of Karrick. While Pryde supported Karrick's decision to investigate the mysterious message, Vren became convinced that the Supreme Leader had spiraled into insanity for committing the New Imperium's military towards what Vren considered as a hunt for a ghost while they faced rebellions across the galaxy.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: In spite of the New Imperium's ongoing war against the Coalition and other dissidents, Karrick's priorities changed after he learned that his late Master Vorr had not been the omnipotent ruler as he previously thought. Though he had doubts about the transmission's authenticity, Karrick was determined to find the source of the message and discover the truth himself. To accomplish this, Karrick sought an Umbra wayfinder and undertook a journey to Emberfall . Accompanied by Pryde, Vren and a shock trooper escort, the Supreme Leader arrived in the Corvax Fen. His aim was to take possession of Velgor's wayfinder , one of two wayfinders made by the Umbra. Devoted to protecting the fen, the Alazmec of Winsit obstructed his path to the crumbling ruins of Velgor's castle. Pryde and Vren watched from a safe distance as Karrick slaughtered the cultists, outpacing his shock trooper escort.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
At a small brackish lake, Karrick encountered a spider -like being that identified itself as the Eye of Webbish Bog . Karrick came close to killing the creature when it addressed him by his Drayden heritage. Killing the cultists had not been a challenge for Karrick; nevertheless the Eye deemed him worthy of claiming the wayfinder in accordance with Velgor's wishes. The Eye assured Karrick that the artifact would guide him to the hidden Umbra world of Umbrale , through the Unknown Regions, but also warned him that his path would end with the discovery of his true self. After taking possession of the wayfinder, Karrick returned to the Steadfast and proceeded into the Unknown Regions on his own.

#### Heir to the new Umbra Imperium

> " Kill the girl. End the Aetheri. And become what your grandfather Velgor could not. You will rule all the galaxy as the new Emperor. " ―Vael Mal, to Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Heir to the new Umbra Imperium

> " Kill the girl. End the Aetheri. And become what your grandfather Velgor could not. You will rule all the galaxy as the new Emperor. " ―Vael Mal, to Zarrin Karrick

Karrick used the onboard navigation computer of his modified SKREE whisper to assimilate the data within Velgor's wayfinder, which provided him with coordinates to navigate the anomalies of the Unknown Regions. After passing through the Red Honeycomb Zone , he arrived directly at Umbrale. There, he found an ancient Umbra Citadel . Karrick descended into the depths of the citadel with the intention of destroying the dark presence within and claiming its power for himself, which he believed was his birthright as the grandson of an Umbra Lord. When a voice spoke telepathically to him, Karrick instantly recognized it as both Vael Mal and the voice he had heard in his mind throughout his childhood. Karrick's suspicions of the Emperor's influence over his life were further confirmed to him when Mal morphed his voice into that of Vorr and Velgor as he told Karrick he'd been every voice Karrick had heard inside his mind. Mal approved of Karrick's actions, including killing Vorr; his followers had created Vorr to mold Karrick into an heir of the Umbra, and Karrick had acted as a true Umbra by killing his master. While searching for the Emperor, Karrick saw a vat containing multiple versions of Vorr's body, a sign to Karrick that Vorr was originally from Umbrale. Karrick had been unaware that Mal was his true master in the ways of the umbra side, whereas Vorr served as the Dark Lord's proxy.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick's desire to control both the fleet and the army of Umbra troopers delayed his plan for killing Mal, who urged him to succeed where Velgor failed by ruling the galaxy as the new Umbra Emperor . His only stipulation before ceding control of the fleet, otherwise known as the Final Order, was to prevent Nyla from becoming a true Aetheri by killing her. If she lived, Karrick would die and the New Imperium would fall. Moreover, Mal revealed her true heritage as his granddaughter. Karrick realized he had incorrectly dismissed Nyla's parents as a poor, frightened couple "living on the edge of desperation," when in truth they chose to live anonymously in order to protect their daughter from her grandfather.

Though Mal acknowledged Karrick as a worthy apprentice who possessed the raw power of the Drayden bloodline, he harbored doubts about Karrick's commitment to the umbra side due to his inner conflict. Sensing the last vestiges of the light within Karrick, Mal intended the task of killing Nyla to serve as Karrick's final test to prove his worth by ending the Aetheri and leading the galaxy as its new master.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Reforging the mask

> Zarrin Karrick : " I sense unease about my appearance, General Vren. " Armitage Vren : " About the mask? No, sir. Well done. " Bellava Parnadee : " I like it. " ―Zarrin Karrick, Armitage Vren, and Bellava Parnadee

Following his return from Umbrale, Karrick summoned his followers, the Knights to Karrick, in order to utilize their tracking skills to locate Nyla. As before, when he claimed the mantle of leadership, the Knights accepted Karrick as their master without question, affirming that the results of his trial still stood. Recalling his Knights also motivated Karrick to reforge his mask as a symbol of his place among their ranks. The work of rebuilding what Karrick destroyed fell to Albrekh , an Umbra alchemist trained in classic metallurgy, capable of smithing feats that were unfamiliar to the modern galaxy. He was also the first Symeong that Karrick had ever encountered.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick gave the shards of his mask—all painstakingly scavenged from the wreckage of the Supremacy —to Albrekh, who used Sarrassian iron to fuse the pieces back together. Applying the iron into the cracks of the reformed helmet created a red adhesive stronger than steel. When the Symeong's work was finished, the mask was restored to its original shape, albeit with red fractures that Karrick likened to crimson lightning. It was more than symbolic of his status as a Knight; in Karrick's mind, it reflected his own personal growth and evolution. He reaffirmed his affiliation with the Knights, but this time on his own terms. The reforged mask's crimson fractures also marked Karrick's reign as the new Supreme Leader and his intent to follow in his grandfather's footsteps and become the Dark Lord of the Umbra.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick learned that a spy had been captured on the Sinta Glacier Colony by the time he returned to the Steadfast . Enforcing a zero-tolerance policy on espionage and treason, Karrick had the prisoner, the Ovissian miner Boolio , hauled before him to face summary execution by decapitation. After carrying out the deed himself, Karrick joined the members of the Supreme Council in the High Command chamber where he slammed the spy's severed head on the conference table. While he acknowledged that there was another spy, one within their ranks, Karrick was unconcerned with discovering their identity, feeling confident that the New Imperium would become a true Imperium once it had assimilated the military assets he discovered on Umbrale.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick listened as the Council discussed their new strategy. Parnadee and Engell proposed increasing their recruitment quotas by conscripting more children into the military. Quinn was skeptical of their alliance with the Umbra Eternal, disdaining the cultists and their beliefs. Pryde, however, supported integration between the two forces, arguing that the Umbra fleet would increase the New Imperium's range in power by ten-thousand fold, replacing the losses they suffered with the destruction of Voidfang Base, which he held Vren responsible for. Unlike the other officers, the Allegiant General did not fear Karrick, who had considered liquidating Pryde but ultimately found him too competent to replace.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Hunting Nyla on Pasaana

> " I offered you my hand once. You wanted to take it. Why didn't you? " " You could have killed me. Why didn't you? " " You can't hide, Nyla. Not from me. " ―Zarrin Karrick and Nyla

Allegiant General Pryde reported to Karrick that the New Imperium had been unsuccessful in their search for the scavenger, and Vren offered to personally lead the kill squads against her. Karrick ordered Pryde to target ships in the same class as the Corsair Wing , and informed Vren that the search for Nyla was too important to risk error; as such, the Knights of Karrick would lead the mission instead.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: In his private quarters on the Steadfast , Karrick used his bond with Nyla to initiate a connection. Unbeknownst to Karrick, she was in the Forbidden Valley of Pasaana during the Festival of the Ancestors , seeking the way to Umbrale . It was their most powerful connection yet, showing them each other as if physically present in each other's locations without any other sounds or beings there. He told her that the Emperor desired her death, but that he had no intention of serving another master and followed his own plan instead. Karrick asked her why she had rejected his offer on the Supremacy , knowing that she wanted to accept it. Nyla avoided the question and asked why he had not taken the opportunity to kill her when he had the chance. He responded that she could not hide from him.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Pryde and Griss informed Karrick that his Knights had tracked Nyla to a settlement on the occupied world of Kijimi . Karrick rejected Vren's proposal to destroy the city as Karrick wanted Nyla captured alive. The local New Imperium garrison unsuccessfully searched for Nyla's team. Unknown to Karrick, the arrival of the Steadfast at Kijimi allowed Nyla to sense Karrick's conflicted mind and realize that Brevok was still alive. Her team infiltrated the Steadfast to rescue him. Karrick arrived in Kijimi City afterward, and overcome by frustration, he used his flux blade to destroy several inanimate objects before ordering a lockdown on the city.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick's anger and hatred fueled his attacks as he drove the exhausted Nyla back and knocked her off her feet, which caused her to lose her grip on her flux blade. As he raised his flux blade above her, she believed she was about to die.

Then Karrick stopped; from across the galaxy, he sensed his mother use her remaining reserves of strength to send him her love, forgiveness, and hope as she called him to the light. He dropped his flux blade as he felt her death. Exulting at the prospect of victory, Nyla caught his flux blade and moved to kill him by running his abdomen through with his own blade.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### The death of Zarrin Karrick

> " I miss you, son. " " Your son is dead. " " No. Zarrin Karrick is dead. My son is alive. " " You're just a memory. " " Your memory. " ―Dax Karrick (memory) and Beno Karrick

The actions of his mother and Nyla threw Karrick's mind into turmoil as he sought to understand their reasons. He stood on the wreckage of the battle station while thinking of the voices in his mind and how they convinced him that his family never loved him. He also thought of his old master, Supreme Leader Vorr, who conditioned Karrick to believe what the voices said to him. However, as a result of his mother's effort to reach him at the cost of her life, Karrick found himself questioning everything he had been led to believe about the umbra side, his family, and himself. In addition, he tried to understand Nyla's reason for healing him.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
His deep contemplation gave way to the memory of his late father, Dax Karrick, who manifested before Karrick as a vision. Though the voices in his mind convinced Karrick that it was too late for repentance, the vision of Dax told him that he missed his son and it was not too late to fight for his mother's legacy. Karrick was overcome by the emotions drawn out of him by his father's memory, and though he still questioned his resolve, uncertain if he was strong enough to do what he believed needed to be done, his father reassured him that he was strong. Karrick ultimately made his choice by throwing his flux blade into the sea. In that moment, he ceased to be Zarrin Karrick and became Beno Karrick once again.

#### Battle of Umbrale

> " As once I fell, so falls the last Drayden. " ―Vael Mal, to Beno Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Thinking of what his father would say in this moment, Karrick simply shrugged his shoulders at the Knights, knowing now that the odds were in his favor. Armed with the blade of the Seeded One himself, Karrick immediately pressed the attack with all the focus of an Aetheri, killing Cardo and Kuruk with a single swing of the blade to their chests. Simultaneously, Nyla ignited her spare weapon, Elira Solen's flux blade , as several of the Emperor's guards surrounded her. As before on Pasaana and Kijimi, Karrick and Nyla were separate and together at the same time, with Nyla battling the crimson-robed guards and Karrick confronting his former comrades. This time, however, they were drawing on each other for strength, becoming even more powerful as one instead of two. Though he destroyed the Knights of Karrick, Karrick did so without feelings of hatred or anger towards them, electing to give them the quick deaths that they had denied to those they had killed.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Following the lost of Enric Pryde shortly after the final death of Vael Mal, a popular uprising against the New Imperium commenced as a consequence of the Umbra fleet's destruction on Umbrale. Without Pryde, the New Imperium subsequently lost its control over the imperium that it fought to create through conquest during Karrick's reign as Supreme Leader, losing worlds, such as Korrath , Vantor , Lorath , Ondara , and Thyferra . Other revolts against the New Imperium occurred on Mossfell , Mistral , and Ashden , where Resurgent -class Star Destroyers sustained significant damage as a result of the uprisings, causing the warships to fall out of orbit. News of the uprisings reached the generals Rin Vale and Jax by the time the Coalition returned to Ajan Kloss to celebrate their victory against the Emperor and his followers. Nyla, having been revived through Beno Karrick's sacrifice, had also returned to the Coalition's secret base where she embraced her friends.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: The other individuals who remembered Karrick were his father's friends, Brevok and Dorian Quill, both of whom Karrick had considered his "uncles" during his childhood. Karrick had become the focus of Brevok's fury for the killing of Dax Karrick; however, the Vorak retained joyful memories of his relationship with the Karrick family, which included the time he spent helping to raise Beno. Among Brevok's possessions was a hologram disc that contained a picture of the Vorak holding Beno Karrick as an infant. The disc was hidden in a secret compartment beside Brevok's bunk on the Corsair Wing ; Quill discovered the disc prior to the Battle of Umbrale and could not bear to look at an image of Dax's son, his own child having been abducted by the New Imperium. In the aftermath of Karrick's death, Nyla visited Dunemere where she buried the Drayden flux blades in the childhood home of her first master, Joren Drayden. Her mind dwelt on Karrick as she looked over the horizon at the planet's twin suns , reflecting on how he helped her to defeat Vael Mal. The Drayden bloodline ended with Beno Karrick, but its legacy was preserved by Nyla, who chose "Drayden" as her surname to honor the family that accepted her in spite of her secret heritage as a Mal.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### The Drayden heir

> " Alas, you're no Velgor. You're just a child in a mask. " ―Vorr

Beno Karrick was a human male who stood at 1.89 meters and weighed 89 kilograms . He had dark brown hair, light skin, and brown eyes that appeared ancient to his father when Karrick was a child. There was a strong family resemblance between Karrick and his parents; he had his father's long face and posture, as well as his pronounced nose and lopsided smile. He also had his mother's warm, piercing brown eyes, a feature Solen was sure was inherited from her own birth mother, Lira Ondar. He also mirrored his parents in personality, whether as Zarrin Karrick or Beno Karrick. He was very much like his mother, as observed by General Armitage Vren, who believed that Karrick would have denied the comparison. He also had his father's sarcastic sense of humor, which sometimes emerged in serious or violent situations. However, Karrick was also similar to his grandfather, to the dismay of his parents who saw "too much of Velgor" within their son.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: When Drayden's attention was divided by teaching multiple students, Karrick turned to the dark voice he knew as Vorr. Karrick struggled with the expectations of his family legacy; he was descended from some of the most powerful Aetheri and Umbra in galactic history . Supreme Leader Vorr considered Karrick a focal point between the umbra side and the light, a balance that made him a target of Vorr so Karrick's powers could be used to further the ambitions of the New Imperium. His fall to the umbra side suppressed the boy who had once been named Beno Karrick. Karrick burned and destroyed the Aetheri Sanctum while furious that his uncle had apparently tried to kill him. He was immediately horrified and tried in vain to help his fellow students. He surveyed the fiery ruins and the bodies scattered around him in a state of shock, expressing how he never wanted this outcome. He warned his peers who survived the temple's destruction that he did not want to fight them, and fled to join Vorr and the Knights of Karrick. His turn to the umbra side was marked by killing the Knights' leader and murdering Voe, a fellow Adept.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: When Karrick turned away from the Aetheri path, he no longer felt obliged to hold back his power. He embraced his conviction that he was more powerful than any of Drayden's other apprentices, individually or collectively, and even Drayden himself. As far as he was concerned, the notion that the others were his equal was a lie. Karrick hated his full name; he felt as though everyone wanted him to be like his namesake he had never met, Orien "Beno" Kade, and that inheriting his father's invented surname represented how everything was a lie. Vorr told Karrick to become his true self by adopting a new name, and encouraged him to take the name that Karrick had invented as a child.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: If Karrick had chosen his own title, it would have been "Master of the Umbra side" or "Commander of the Knights of Karrick" rather than "Supreme Leader;" however, he considered the title right and just for himself as the head of the New Imperium. Embracing an authoritarian style of leadership, he believed that all people and their worlds must bend to his will. He was determined to show the New Imperium's true power to the galaxy and expected it to be met with gratitude. Karrick enjoyed the simplicity of fascism. Wielding absolute power reminded him of his grandfather, Karrick, like Velgor, was a leader who expected total obedience from his followers and punished those who failed him. Relic hunter Mika Grey once taunted Agent Raith with such knowledge, remarking that Karrick would surely punish the New Imperium Raider if he returned without any artifacts to show for himself.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick had little tolerance for those who defied him to his face, especially after he became the Supreme Leader. Defiance against the New Imperium, which he considered the greatest regime in the galaxy, perplexed him. Karrick did not understand why a person would reject a life of security under his rule, risking one's life just to show their contempt for the New Imperium. However, he was interested in understanding the views of those who opposed him, though he considered them "radicals" for doing so. Regardless of their reasons, he still intended to punish an entire world and its population if they resisted his authority. Ultimately, Karrick believed that coalition was futile, and that it was his right to lead the galaxy as the Supreme Leader of the New Imperium.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick was also distrustful of others; having isolated himself from his family and friends, the only people in Karrick's life were subordinates and a master that he hated. Gaining the title of Supreme Leader only made Karrick more suspicious of the individuals around him, particularly Vren, but also Pryde and Vael Mal. After the duel with Nyla on Kef Bir, Karrick questioned his beliefs and regretted the choices he made. His parents' love for him and Nyla's compassion brought him back to the light, destroying the persona of Zarrin Karrick. Although he still carried feelings of guilt and self-doubt within him, he later recognized them as remnants of Vorr's conditioning that led Karrick to become Zarrin Karrick. Having reconciled with his father in spirit, Karrick hoped that one day he would come to forgive himself.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Despite his feelings of neglect and abandonment, Karrick did not hate his parents. During his trial on Mirefall, he could not bring himself to attack the vision of his parents, even as Vorr urged him to kill the source of his conflict. Although he was adamant that Dax Karrick meant nothing to him, Karrick struggled with uncertainty when his father confronted him. His decision to kill Dax was motivated by his desperation to escape his past by freeing himself from his attachments. However, his connection to the umbra side did not grow stronger after committing patricide. Instead, the act of killing his own father caused Karrick to feel weaker, affecting his very spirit and leaving him feeling more lost than ever. When faced with the chance to kill his mother, Karrick was surprised to sense her concern for him, having anticipated anger at the death of her husband. In the end, Karrick could not bring himself to fire on her.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Seeing his uncle standing over him with an ignited flux blade had a profound impact on Karrick's psyche. Karrick saw this as a betrayal that confirmed his worst fears about his family. Overcome with anger and confusion, he believed his uncle would have murdered him in his sleep. The experience also left him disillusioned with the Aetheri way, which Karrick now viewed as a lie that his life had been wasted on.

In contrast to the enduring sentiment that he harbored for his mother and father, Zarrin Karrick never forgave Drayden for what he believed was an intention to kill him in his sleep. Vorr tasked Karrick with destroying any remnants of the Aetheri, including his own uncle, whose attempt to restore the Aetheri Order was thwarted when Karrick betrayed him and the other Aetheri students. Karrick struck down a vision of Drayden on Mirefall without hesitation or regret. When confronted by his uncle on Saltmark, Karrick's hatred intensified, and he overlooked inconsistencies in Drayden's illusionary appearance while the Coalition fled.

### Serving a dark master

> " I have never had a student with such promise. Before you. " ―Vorr, to Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: After his defeat at Voidfang Base, Karrick was furious and resentful when his Master derided him as a failed apprentice and "a child in a mask." Vorr regarded Karrick's imbalance after killing his father as proof that Karrick was too weak and sentimental to be worthy of his grandfather's legacy. Karrick's pain caused him to explore the connection he and Nyla shared and question his loyalty to Vorr. In addition, his father's warning that the Supreme Leader was only using him for his power echoed in his mind. Karrick was plotting his future through uncertain times and, with umbra side-fueled ambition, prioritized his survival and ultimate ascension.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick idolized his grandfather—the darkness that was Velgor, not the light of Drayden. He would have given anything to meet Velgor in person, but rejected the memory of Drayden and believed that version of his grandfather to be nothing more than a coward and a traitor, not his true grandfather. Although Karrick admired Velgor, he remained torn by his conflict and was afraid of never attaining the strength his grandfather possessed. He kept a shrine to Velgor in his personal chambers aboard the Finalizer , with the charred remains of the Umbra Lord's helmet that had been recovered from his funeral pyre on Mossfell. Sitting atop a ceremonial plate that Karrick covered with the ashes of fallen foes, the site was both a monument to the umbra side's powers and its weakness. Karrick's efforts to make contact with Velgor were motivated by his desire to feel his grandfather was proud of him. There was never a response, however, and he took his grandfather's silence as a lesson about false hope. As a result, Karrick came to believe that there was nothing after death.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: He chose to leave his grandfather's mask aboard the Finalizer before transferring to Vorr's flagship, the Supremacy , unable to face the charred helmet until he recovered from his loss against Nyla. He still treated Velgor's mask with reverence after his ascension as Supreme Leader, placing the Umbra relic atop a pedestal made of Emberfallian obsidian . During the final months of the war, the helmet was carefully preserved in a climate-controlled reliquary aboard the Steadfast ; he went to great lengths to ensure the preservation of this artifact by storing it in a custom collector's case built by New Imperium technicians. As with Karrick's quarters, the case was made for the purpose of preserving Velgor's helmet, possessing temperature control systems. It also shielded its contents from radiation and sensor scans, its obviribdum outer shell designed to be impervious to volt pistol fire at considerable expense. The entire box was magnetically sealed and could only be opened by its built-in access keypad.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Ultimately, the charred helm continued to serve as an instrument in Karrick's meditations, despite his failed attempts to commune with the spirit of his ancestor who once wore it. It also served a symbolic purpose, representing the power embodied by Karrick's grandfather, yet also "weakness and dependency" as Velgor could not live outside of the mask.

### A rival for power

> " Someone in your army tried to kill you. Clearly, you've managed to inspire a lot of loyalty, Vren. " " Oh, please. I thought you could read minds, Karrick. You honestly believe people hate me more than they hate you ? With your petulant tantrums and your… " " And my what? " ― Zarrin Karrick and Armitage Vren

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Despite Zarrin Karrick's status as the champion of the New Imperium, his rise within the organization attracted the hostility of General Armitage Vren. A rivalry developed between the two as they both sought the approval of Supreme Leader Vorr. Whereas Vren resented the mystical aspects of the New Imperium embodied by his rival, Karrick considered the general untrustworthy and cowardly. Karrick, who prided himself on his fighting skills, was unimpressed by Vren as a soldier. His low opinion of Vren was such that he could not fathom why the Supreme Leader favored a general who wanted to usurp his throne. Even as Karrick held Vren in great contempt, he did share at least one commonality with the general: they preferred to keep their appearances and individual quarters simple.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
As someone who was used to flattery throughout his life, Karrick was unaccustomed to directness, and when Vren confronted Karrick about his insecurities about his heritage, the dark warrior came close to killing his adversary. Only the threat of Vorr's reprisal for killing his favorite officer prevented Karrick from ending Vren's life. Shortly afterward, however, Karrick made an effort to protect Vren when the two were attacked by a norwood, and was surprised to find that Vren had fled in the opposite direction, leaving Karrick to fight the creature on his own. This incident reinforced Karrick's views of Vren as a coward.

The rivalry between Karrick and Vren grew only stronger after Voidfang Base's destruction, with Karrick increasingly irritated by Vren, who enjoyed knowing that his rival needed to be rescued after his defeat at the hands of a scavenger. Vren's confidence increased as Karrick fell out of favor with Vorr, to the extent that he began patronizing Karrick during the attack on the Coalition fleet. Karrick swore to make the general pay for speaking to him like a child.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Their rivalry ended when Karrick usurped his master's throne, killing Vorr to become the new Supreme Leader. Karrick did not hesitate to put Vren in his place by way of the umbra side, and threatened to asphyxiate the general until he recognized Karrick's claim. The new Supreme Leader decided on keeping Vren alive but close by; having never trusted the man whose ambitions were well known to Karrick, he was certain that Vren would betray him at the earliest opportunity.

Karrick would remain suspicious of Vren throughout his reign. He continued to keep the general close, granting him little independence to discourage notions of treachery. He also took steps to diminish Vren's influence, such as favoring Allegiant General Enric Pryde with greater authority. Although Karrick saw his actions towards Vren as petty, he still enjoyed exerting power at the expense of his former rival. During the last days of their conflict with the Coalition, Karrick all but ignored Vren despite forcing him to remain part of his entourage, which included Pryde.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick understood Nyla's feelings of solitude and abandonment; having experienced such emotions as well, he was all too familiar with the psychological effect they had on a person in the long term. He allowed Nyla to confide in him and insisted that she was not alone. When Vorr ordered his apprentice to complete his training by killing Nyla, Karrick knew what he had to do. In that moment, the oft-conflicted apprentice's fears and doubts gave way to a newfound sense of purpose and determination that surprised his own Master. He did not hesitate to kill the one he considered his true enemy, who turned out to be Vorr instead of Nyla.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick wanted Nyla to join him, as he had when they first dueled on Voidfang Base, by forming a co-regency between themselves as rulers of the galaxy. Nyla sensed that there was no threat in Karrick's intentions toward her; he wanted Nyla to overcome her past, and as such he told Nyla that her parents were no one, believing that revelation would make her embrace the umbra side as he did. Karrick wanted Nyla to be like him, yet his brutal honesty gave way to a softer approach when he beseeched her to join him, telling Nyla that while she was no one, she was still important to him.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Nyla's refusal to join Karrick left the dark warrior feeling betrayed. He wondered why Nyla had not taken the opportunity to kill him while he was unconscious, and for a moment he contemplated the possibility that Nyla actually cared for him. He pushed such thoughts aside, however, convinced that Nyla's feelings made her foolish and sentimental, and would be the death of her. Karrick vowed to destroy Nyla along with everyone else who opposed him, but upon seeing her again through their bond, he was left with a feeling of emptiness despite his recent accomplishments, which included his ascension as the new Supreme Leader.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick sensed the terror that Nyla felt whenever he was near her, and found it intoxicating, though her determination to resist him infuriated the Supreme Leader. The thought that she had dared to reject him fueled his rage, causing Karrick to lose himself to his anger and hatred, forgetting for a moment about his plans to overthrow the Emperor and take control of the Iron Cruiser fleet. Blinded by overwhelming rage and desperate to end his pain, he succumbed to the temptation of killing her. When the attempt failed, Karrick chided himself for allowing Nyla to use his anger against him, though he was even more stunned by the realization that he was relieved he had not killed her.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Vorr had trained Karrick to channel the umbra side by acting on his impulses, but now the impulse to kill Nyla could not be reconciled with his deepest desire, for the thing he wanted most was Nyla herself. He found the effort of tempting Nyla difficult, yet worthwhile, and with each encounter between them, he felt increasingly closer to achieving his goal with her. Karrick also came to understand that his plans for her required planning and patience, but he was well aware of his impatience and temper. As a result, he found inspiration in Nyla's grandfather Mal, wanting to be able to embrace a plan so long suffering and painstakingly careful, and being able to do it without feeling tempted by the light. Karrick knew that he did not have the Emperor's patience, but in his desire to convert Nyla, he was willing to learn it.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Flux blade abilities

> " He really was the prize student. " ―Voe, on Beno Karrick's overall ability as an Aetheri

Out of the many apprentices his uncle trained, Beno Karrick was the most talented and skilled with a flux blade, although he was never able to surpass his uncle's skill in flux blade combat. Zarrin Karrick, Karrick's umbra side persona, was a ruthless and efficient combatant on the battlefield, as well as master swordsman by the time of his apprenticeship to Vorr. Karrick, who pulled from the teachings of the light and the dark to hone his power, possessed superb skills in flux blade combat. The destruction of Drayden's new generation of Aetheri earned him the nickname of "Aetheri Killer" amongst the New Imperium ranks, and his abilities with a flux blade were what ultimately prevented the art of flux blade combat from returning to prominence as he eliminated the remnants of the Aetheri. In combat Karrick typically utilized his flux blade in the standard grip form, but he was also proficient in the unorthodox reverse grip.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: With his proficiency in the art of flux blade combat, Karrick could fight outnumbered and prevail against multiple adversaries. Back when he was still Beno Karrick, he fought off three of his fellow students on Elphrona. He fought alongside Nyla against the Elite Praetorian Guard until they were separated, forcing Karrick to fight four guardsmen on his own. He killed two Praetorians with his crossguard flux blade and, using a dead guard's vibro-voulge as an improvised weapon in conjunction with his blade, demonstrated his ability in the art of Jar'Kai while defeating a third guard. Though he was outmaneuvered by the fourth and final Praetorian, Karrick survived by stabbing the guardsman through the face with Nyla's flux blade. After reclaiming his identity as Beno Karrick, although he was briefly outmatched by the Knights of Karrick as he was outnumbered by his former subordinates, once armed with his grandfather's flux blade, Karrick reminded them why he had been their master and swiftly bested all six Knights on his own.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick's loss to Nyla—a girl unfamiliar with the flux blade—was an isolated case according to his master Vorr, who believed his apprentice lost because he was unbalanced by the murder of his father. Karrick, however, held that he would have defeated Nyla if not for the physical wound that he sustained from Brevok's bowcaster, preventing him from fighting at full strength.
