#### Scum and villainy

Schemes in the shadows

> " I sense something, Master. And I don't like it. " " It's the umbra side, Sela. This is the right place. " ―Sela Marr and Kael Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info )

During the Replica Wars, the Emberfallians aligned themselves with the Fractio of Independent Systems . However, they were not fanatically committed to the cause, having only joined to secure themselves Dissident contracts, and life continued much as it had before. With members of the Aetheri Order , the galaxy 's guardians of peace and justice, focused on defeating the Dissidents, law enforcement found itself in a declining state, especially in the infrequently patrolled Outer Reach. Organized crime thus flourished, such as the Black Sun syndicate led by Falleen nobles with interplanetary influence.

title: Emberfall
text: The Falleen operated clandestinely, establishing elusive holdings on Emberfall and headquartering themselves in a well-defended fortress , where they regularly met and found the surrounding lava useful for the disposal of evidence. The native Emberfallians cared little for Black Sun, since most of their operations took place elsewhere in the galaxy. Hidden away from prying eyes, the Artificer Union also produced battle droids behind their Emberfallian mining operations, situated within the same mountain as their Klegger Corp Mining Facility, at the time of the Replica Wars. By the time of the war, Vael Mal was familiar with the existence of the Umbra temple at the Gahenn Plains.

title: Emberfall
text:
fuel logs, Aetheri Adept Sela Marr reasoned the world could be where Vorek deposited the kidnapped children so she and her mentor , Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden , traveled to Emberfall to rescue the children. As the Aetheri arrived at the facility, Vael Mal ordered the nanny droids to destroy the installation so as to ensure the loss of any evidence of the plot. The nanny droids attempted to relocate the children, but Drayden and Marr managed to rescue them as the facility sank into the lava lake below it. In 19 BVE , renegade Umbra Lord Vreth , his apprentice Savage Opress , and Pre Vizsla , the leader of the Ferrik terrorist organization Grave Watch , traveled to the Black Sun fortress with the intention of recruiting them to their newly founded criminal imperium, the Shadow Collective . As four Kom'rk -class fighter/transports landed outside the fortress, the Captain of the Guard , Ziton Moj , greeted them upon their arrival. With both Vreth and Moj backed by large amounts of soldiers, the renegade Umbra requested a meeting with the Black Sun's leaders, which Moj agreed to. The syndicate was headed by the Falleen Xomit Grunseit , who hailed from Emberfall. After negotiations with the leaders went sour, Savage beheaded all of them with his flux blade . Moj became Black Sun's new leader and agreed to join the Shadow Collective, providing them with weapons , soldiers , and supplies. Shadow Collective forces then began to load all of the supplies the Black Sun had at their disposal onto ships.

The lost children

title: Emberfall
text:
The lost children

> " Ah, yes, scenic Emberfall, because everyone looks good in red lighting. Become a bounty hunter, see the galaxy! " ―Daren Kelv, to Kessa Vray

When Daren Kelv was sent undercover as a bounty hunter to work alongside Varek's former apprentice, Kessa Vray , the pair was hired by the Gruv Syndicate to retrieve Marg Krim 's wife, Tezzka Krim , and their children, Vram and Laalee , who were kidnapped by Black Sun and brought to their base on Emberfall in order to bribe the Pykes into joining Vreth's Shadow Collective. The two traveled to Emberfall in Vray' ship, the Banshee , and entered Zitontown , where they sought to gather information at the lone bar in the town, named The Last Resort . Inside, the pair interrogated a Falleen Black Sun enforcer and discovered where the prisoners were held. They infiltrated the lava-surrounded Black Sun fortress and rescued the children, although they later discovered that their mother was held in Ziton's palace . After the pair freed Tezzka, Moj had mobilized his forces for departure from Emberfall to attack the Pykes on the planet Oba Diah .

#### Mirror of the soul

title: Emberfall
text: Fascinated by the power he tapped into in the Umbra cave on Emberfall, and associating the world with his rebirth and personal connection to the umbra side, Velgor requested that the world be given to him by his master in 14 BVE, believing that the planet held the key to seeing the deceased Lira Ondar once again. Gifted with the late Ondar's royal starship , the mask of the ancient Umbra heretic artisan Vael Mornick , and a team of top Imperial architects , Velgor departed Vantor for his new home. The Umbra Lord entered the planet's violent atmosphere unshielded, causing severe damage to his vessel and casting a streak of fire across the smokey sky. His entry was witnessed by the Emberfallian Father Kkkt , who warned his clanmate Zzzs that the fireball was an omen of events to come.

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Portal to the past

> " I have been in contact with the other clanholds. We are not the only one affected—the entire planet screams at what the dark one is building on the Gahenn Plains. " ―Father Kkkt

The construction of Velgor's fortress was not a simple task. Over the course of eight attempts with at least five separate designs, Mornick struggled to find the perfect structure that could correctly channel the umbra side. The energy Velgor exerted while attempting to open a rift in the locus caused electromagnetic storms to rage across the planet, throwing the world's creatures into a frenzy and casting the Emberfallian people into disarray—the natives found that their "lifefires" barely burned. As an Imperial -class Iron Cruiser loomed overhead, the new Imperial garrison managed to defend the site against small uprisings by the Emberfallians and lava fleas. Father Kkkt, realizing the danger Velgor posed to his world, rallied the clanholds across Emberfall prepared to mount an attack on the Imperial intruders.

title: Emberfall
text: In 4 BVE , the Aetheri Brenn Aldric of the insurgent cell named the Shades was detained aboard the Imperial Iron Cruiser Sovereign , the flagship of Wilhard Varrix , Grand Moff and Governor of the Outer Reach. The vessel entered Emberfall's orbit after the Imperium's capture of the Aetheri on the Outer Reach planet Lorath , where the Shades were based. Escorted by a fleet of three other Star Destroyers and support vessels, the Sovereign bore witness to the Grand Warden 's interrogation of Aldric for information about the insurgency and the informant named " Fulcrum " —who was secretly the former Aetheri Sela Marr. Lena Kryll led her Shades crew on a rescue mission over Emberfall. Using a stolen Imperial Gozanti-class cruiser and SKREE fighter to infiltrate the Sovereign , the Shades freed their captive Aetheri from the Grand Warden. The latter's flux blade was bisected during flux blade combat against Aldric and his Adept, Cass Virel , and fell into the Sovereign ' s reactor , dooming the Iron Cruiser. The Warden himself chose to fall to his death rather than suffer for his failures.

title: Emberfall
text:
Later in the war, a crew of insurgents led by Commander Lina Graf was attacked by Imperial forces, and their ship, the Auric , was heavily damaged. They were forced to crash-land on Emberfall, a planet that Graf hoped would lead to her crew's salvation. Surrounded by lava, the insurgents abandoned their ship and began toward the only structure in sight; Velgor's fortress.

They did not make it far before being attacked by Emberfall's exploding beetles. After defeating the beetles and arguing over the best course of action, Graf and her crew were cornered by a squad of Imperial Lava Troopers. Escaping the troopers, the group entered the fortress but soon became separated in its dark halls. Alerted to their presence by his aide Vainé, Velgor confronted the insurgents, capturing Lieutenant Thom Hudd and destroying the bodyguard droid XM-G3 , although Graf and her remaining crew managed to escape Emberfall. The insurgents' successful escape from Velgor's castle was remembered by the native Emberfallians by the aftermath of the Imperium's collapse.

title: Emberfall
text: For the next several weeks , Vainé kept Hudd locked within the fortress and tortured him, all the while tormenting him with horrific tales from across the galaxy, including the story of Velgor's brutal murder of Sssl years prior. The abuse and starvation that Hudd suffered while chained to the Umbra servant's torture web was so severe that he lost enough body mass to slip from his shackles and escape his cell. Hudd managed to send a distress signal to the Alliance but was ultimately recaptured and sentenced to death. His execution was stalled by Graf, however, who had returned to Emberfall disguised as a Warden . Although Vainé saw through her ruse, Graf and Hudd were able to escape and flee the planet with the rest of their crew. Velgor, angered at his servant's ineptitude, rigged Vainé up to the torture web.

title: Emberfall
text:
### Crucible of fate and hate (3–4 AVE)

#### Into the fire

> " The last time you were broken …I found you…and I rebuilt you. This time… you must rebuild yourself. " ―Mal, to his battered apprentice

In 3 AVE , Velgor attempted to turn his son, Joren Drayden, to the umbra side during a duel over the planet Mistral . After Drayden fled , Velgor temporarily abandoned his duties to the Emperor, embarking on a personal quest that led to the discovery of a insurgent cell led by Sable , the former decoy of Lira Ondar. Velgor allowed the insurgents to live, a decision which convinced Mal that his apprentice was in need of a reminder of his place. The Emperor mutilated Velgor on Vantor, ripping his cybernetic limbs from his body and strangling him as he had done to men like Vossik in the past.

title: Emberfall
text: Having reached the Artificer Union installation ruins, the very building where he had slaughtered the Dissident Council decades prior, Velgor repurposed surrounding Dissident droid parts as his own limbs and confronted Orrin, overpowering the assassin and demanding him to reveal Vael Mal' plans. As Velgor did so, the oracle Eye of Webbish Bog called out to the Umbra Lord, who, despite being deprived of his chest box and flux blade by Orrin, fought his way through hordes of lava nymphs, lava fleas, and even a roggwart to reach the Eye's lava cavern. As Velgor did so, he was tested by the Eye and reminded of his inner conflicts between his chosen Umbra and Aetheri destinies as well as between his personal desire of power and his need for his son. During Velgor's journey to the Eye's lair, Senior Administrative Aide Sly Moore and a group of death troopers spoke to Orrin, reminding the assassin to abide by the Emperor's directives.

title: Emberfall
text: At the end of Velgor's trek to the Eye, the latter gave the cyborg a wayfinder and allowed him to leave the cavern to rejoin Orrin. Once outside, Velgor made his way to the green Aetheri starfighter that he took to Emberfall at the end of the Replica Wars, repairing the ship until Orrin reappeared with the Droid Crush Pirates of Bestoon . Having been promised Velgor's cybernetic parts by Orrin, the army of droid pursued the Emperor's enforcer until they found that his parts were no more special than their own. In the midst of a quarrel with Orrin about their deal, the droids were interrupted by Velgor, who took down the machines for use in retrofitting his green starfighter and an escape pod , which he locked Orrin in after forcing the assassin to activate his wayfinder. In his determination to find the Emperor's secrets, Velgor bound the pod to his starfighter and set off to the wayfinder's coordinates, reaching the vicinity of the Unknown Regions world Umbrale via hyperspace.

title: Emberfall
text:
With Orrin in tow, Velgor confronted Mal on Umbrale, an ancient Umbra world which housed hundreds of Mal' secret experiments and weapons. The Emperor reminded his wayward apprentice that he left him weak and broken on Emberfall's burning shores, and asked Velgor what he learned from the experience. However, Velgor remained rebellious, stating his intention to make his "master" fear him. Despite Velgor's efforts, he was overwhelmed by Mal' power. Terribly pained, Velgor, despite having experienced a vision of his son telling him it was his destiny to destroy Mal, accepted his master's dominance over him before leaving Umbrale with him and Orrin.

#### Carmine Dawn intrusion

Later, between 3 AVE and 4 AVE, Lady Vessa 's criminal syndicate, Carmine Dawn , hired the Knights of Karrick , a group of umbra side warriors, to raid Fortress Velgor and acquire the Screaming Key artifact —Vael Mal had placed the key there, but did not know that it unlocked Mornick's fabled Fermata Vault , which held power that threatened even the Umbra. In her quest to destroy the Umbra, Vessa had obtained the full layout, access codes, and security details of the fortress and convinced the Knights' leader , Karrick , to go ahead with the raid despite initial reluctance from other Knights. The Knight Massif had complained that "the job was too hot" not just because Emberfall's surface was a hellscape, and fellow Knights Bazzra and Marinda also had their own concerns. Nevertheless, Vessa promised the Knights glory and the freedom to claim any objects to keep for themselves aside from the key.

title: Emberfall
text: While training with his droid army, Velgor received a hologram transmission from Grand Vizier Veldon, who relayed the Emperor's order to reclaim his flagship, the Sovereign —it had been infiltrated by the Vrak. Velgor and his droids thus departed for the Sovereign aboard an Imperial transport . After successfully reclaiming the flagship, the Umbra Lord took his droids and his personal SKREE fighter and returned to Emberfall, where another droid repaired its fellow veterans while Velgor confronted the Eye of Webbish Bog, demanding power and control—while battling the Vrak, Veldon had ordered the Sovereign ' s destruction with Velgor onboard. The Eye reminded Velgor that power lied with his master, Vael Mal, citing the Tragedy of Vael Plagueis the Wise in which Mal murdered his own master. While Velgor prepared to depart for Vantor's Imperial Palace with his droids and a Vectis -class shuttle , one of his droids, ZEV-6-7 , succumbed to the Vrak and activated an octuptarra tri-droid in the secret Artificer Union droid factory.

title: Emberfall
text: Velgor's attack failed, as the Emperor turned Velgor's own troops, including his hand-picked squad of death troopers, against him. Velgor eliminated the squad and had their bodies sent to a medical lab on Emberfall. There the Umbra Lord mused that although the death troopers organic minds made them superior to droids, it also supplied them with a will that could be turned against him. Following the end of the droid crisis, Velgor sought to appropriate the Vrak's ability to control automatons and cyborgs for his own ends. The Dark Lord captured the members of M.A.R. Corps —a Free Coalition squad of cybernetically-enhanced commandos—and brought them to Emberfall for experimentation. Under the supervision of ZEV-6-7, the insurgents were equipped with droid brains that allowed Velgor to interface with and command them. The process was extremely invasive, however, causing severe mental anguish in the commandos that was shared by Velgor. During these experiments, Administrator Sly Moore met with Velgor in his fortress with the intent of persuading him to join her Schism Imperial , a splinter group of disaffected Imperial officers and bureaucrats who planned to overthrow the Emperor.

title: Emberfall
text:
Velgor and the Schism's crusade against the Emperor finally came to a head in a skirmish on Caranthanax B , where Velgor fully submitted to the will of the Emperor. The aftermath of the battle saw the Schism revealed as a ruse concocted by Mal, as well the recovery of energy capsules from the site by the former slaves Kitster Banai and Wald . Orrin of Bestoon later recovered the capsules on Dunemere and presented them to Velgor in his castle throne room on Emberfall.

### Ashes of Imperium (4–35 AVE)

#### Lingering darkness

> " It is not over. Not yet. Not while you can bring him back…your master will return to the fires of Emberfall and, this time, will be made whole… Velgor triumphant. Velgor supreme. Velgor… reborn ! " ―A voice speaks to Vainé

text:
Nevertheless, Giggek led Tuttel into Velgor's castle by way of lava flea, venturing in to find a pit trapping Vainé, the servant of Velgor and the self-styled "one true Adeptis of the Beyond " who was detained by Velgor there some time ago. Rescuing The Adeptis in hopes of not bringing death upon anyone in the process of destroying Velgor's castle, Giggek was at once betrayed by Vainé, who dropped the boy down the pit in hopes of bringing death to those who sought to tarnish his master's legacy. However, after instructing his Emberfallian companion to flee, which Tuttel did with their lava flea, Giggek ignited his explosives through a remote detonator , and although the blast did not bring down Velgor's castle, Vainé was buried in black sand. However, the Umbra servant survived. A voice familiar to Vainé told him not to fear, and assured its servant that he could return Velgor to the fires of Emberfall and be made whole.

#### Wrath of Velgor's ghost

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Wrath of Velgor's ghost

> " And I'm sorry. You of all people must be— " " Scared out of my wits? Wishing I'd never even heard the word Emberfall? It's the dreams, Lina. They're getting to us all. " " You're right, Hudd. That's all they are… dreams. And dreams aren't real… Dreams can't hurt you. " ―Lina Graf and Thom Hudd, on Emberfall once more At some point, Vainé witnessed holonews reports on the Battle of Mossfell and the death of Velgor, but he refused to believe that his master had met his end. The Adeptis continued to maintain the Dark Lord's castle, anticipating his return at any time. Following the Imperium's defeat at the Battle of Ashden in 5 AVE , Vainé told the voice he believed to be his master that everyone in the galaxy believed that he was dead, which the supposed ghost of Velgor replied to by saying that the Umbra can never truly be killed since it was the will of the umbra side. Vainé then orchestrated a ritual in which Velgor's ghost reached out across the galaxy to imprint nightmares upon others' minds. One such nightmare reached Milo Graf , brother of Lina Graf, in which Milo had a nightmare about undead droids and himself being taken to Emberfall by CR-8R , controlled by Vainé.

title: Emberfall
text: After he discussed Velgor's castle with his sister and CR-8R, Milo Graf and the droid went missing for days —CR-8R had been afflicted by a signal that scrambled his processors and had incapacitated the organic before bringing him to Vainé on Emberfall. Suffering from a dream of her brother being trapped on Emberfall, Lina requested Concordat Chancellor Vela Sess and Senator Elira Solen on the capital world Serenne to spare a ship to investigate the lava world, which had remained under Imperial control. Although Sess denied Graf's request, Solen suggested that she contact the smuggler Jaxxon T. Tumperakki for passage to Emberfall. Before arriving at Velgor's castle, they enlisted Graf's old crew, Thom Hudd and Skritt ; Hudd had also been experiencing nightmares related to Vainé and the fortress.

title: Emberfall
text: Emberfall grew in obscurity in the decades that followed, and Velgor's castle eventually fell into ruins. Thanks to the destruction of the Bright Star, Emberfall's ecosystem began to be healed. In 9 AVE , the competitive sporting show Hunters of the Outer Reach featured many environments for its cast to contend in, including Velgor's Castle —a battlefield that was modeled after Fortress Velgor and Emberfall's scorching surface—at the Grand Arena on the planet Vespaara . To complete the immersion of the battlefield, a wide screen projection was used at the side to display Emberfall's rocky terrain and flowing lava rivers. One Hunter, the former shock trooper Sentinel , utilized a pro-Imperial persona on the show and exaggerated his exploits as a soldier, though in truth he had grown to hate the Imperium. He claimed to have been deployed to a very hot lava planet and fought against a Fireworm on that world, although he could not recall if it had been Emberfall or Senna . In another instance, Sentinel claimed he once went to Emberfall as part of a pilgrimage , but was called away before he could complete his journey to the remains of Fortress Velgor. Another Hunter, the
