A simple life

> " What about the people that need us? What about the fight? " " The fight is done. We lost. " ―Nari and Kade

title: Orien Kade
text:
#### Hunted by the Warden Order

A simple life

> " What about the people that need us? What about the fight? " " The fight is done. We lost. " ―Nari and Kade

In 9 BVE , the Warden Order—including the Grand Warden , the Fifth Warden , and the Third Warden —arrived in Dunemere's Port Kess in search of a fugitive Aetheri rumored to be hiding on the planet. By that same year, Kade had come to reside in a cave in the Dune Sea desert. Working at Tibidon Station , a sand whaling station, he rode a hovertrain into Anchorhead with his co-workers, continuing on his eopie Akkani to his cave. One day, Kade was visited by the Duskkin Teeka , who presented the Aetheri with several spare parts for a toy T-16 skyhopper . Teeka also offered to sell spare parts to Kade's malfunctioning moisture vaporator, but the Aetheri realized that the Duskkin had been stealing his parts and chastised Teeka. Before departing, the Duskkin showed spare parts from an alleged Aetheri starship that had crashed in the Dune Sea to Kade, who remarked that the Aetheri were believed to be extinct.

title: Orien Kade
text: That night, Kade was haunted in his dreams by memories of Kael Drayden, Lira Ondar, Sorin Vael, and Zho. The following day, Kade rode his eopie to the Havel homestead, where he observed with macrobinoculars the young Joren Drayden and Owen Havel from a distance. While riding his eopie through the desert the following night, Kade was confronted by the fugitive Aetheri, a human male named Nari , who had managed to escape the Wardens earlier and pleaded for the Aetheri Master's help. However, Kade urged the Aetheri to bury his flux blade and flee, much to the disappointment of Nari, who still believed in the fight—which Kade believed to be over and lost.

title: Orien Kade
text: In Anchorhead, Kade met with Havel to hand over the toy parts he had acquired from Teeka earlier, but the farmer refused to accept the presents and asked Kade to stay away from his family. After arguing with Havel about the future of Drayden, Kade hid nearby as the Fifth Warden and the Third Warden arrived to address the inhabitants regarding the fugitive Aetheri they were looking for. The Third Warden took a particular liking to Havel and threatened to kill his family unless information about the fugitive was brought forward, but the farmer stayed quiet until the Fifth Warden intervened. Afterward, Kade thanked Havel for not revealing anything about him or his whereabouts.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Obsessed with finding Kade, the Third Warden plotted to lure out the fugitive Aetheri Master and arranged for the kidnapping of Elira Solen on Cindervale. As she suspected, Kade received a distress call from Bael and Breha Solen, who pleaded with the Aetheri to help retrieve their daughter. However, Kade—intent on protecting Joren and believing himself to have been out of the game for too long—declined the request. Later, after witnessing the dead body of Nari in Anchorhead, Kade was visited in person by Bael Solen, who again pleaded with the Aetheri to help him. After relenting, Kade retrieved his flux blade from the desert and headed for a spaceport, where be boarded a freighter to depart Dunemere in a commercial transport .

Rescuing Elira Solen

> " You have no idea what I'm risking being here, Your Highness " ―Kade, to Elira Solen

title: Orien Kade
text: Infiltrating the Spice Den in a stolen cape and mask, Kade used the chaos brought on by the explosion of a small vat to steal a keycard from an employee and access a closed-off area of the laboratory complex. Confronted by two employees, a Zyrrak and a human, he managed to overpower both, before finding a room with a small human-like figure with a cloak. As Kade entered the room, Vect Nokru —who had kidnapped Elira from Cindervale—and two companions ambushed the Aetheri, but he was able to defeat the trio with the help of a vial of red spice. Checking another room, Kade found Elira and told her he was sent by her father, Bael, to rescue her.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Realizing the spaceport of Daiyu was closed for travel, Kade and Elira made their way to a cargo port on the recommendation of Estree, who confronted the two in an alleyway after having a change of heart. However, the Third Warden—who had mind probed Estree—intercepted the two in a hangar before they were able to board a cargo transport. Telling Elira to go for the transport, Kade prepared to confront the Third Warden, who informed him that he was to be taken to Lord Velgor, only to realize that Kade was not aware of the fact that Velgor survived their duel on Emberfall. Kade was horrified when she revealed Velgor was indeed alive and has been hunting for him ever since. Before a confrontation could occur, however, The Grand Warden arrived in the hangar and ordered the Third Warden to stand down; unwilling to let her superior take the credit for catching Kade, the Third Warden stabbed him while Kade used the ordeal to make his way to the cargo transport where Elira was waiting. As the transport departed, Kade was shaken by the revelation of Velgor's survival.

Arriving on Mapuzo

title: Orien Kade
text: The two eventually reached the rendezvous point, but the contact was nowhere to be found. As they noticed a vehicle on the horizon, Solen waved it down despite Kade's protests. When the driver, Freck , offered the two a ride to the nearest spaceport, Kade reluctantly followed Solen on the back of the vehicle. During the ride, Freck made conversation, revealing that he was a staunch supporter of the Imperium; noticing a squad of shock troopers, he pulled over and offered them a ride. The Imperial soldiers disclosed that they were searching for a nearby Aetheri, and as they questioned Kade and Solen over their presence on Mapuzo, the Aetheri accidentally used Solen's real name, instead of the fabricated name. However, Kade was able to cover up the mistake by claiming that his daughter reminded him of his late wife; satisfied with the explanation, the shock troopers got off Freck's vehicle.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Fleeing once more, Kade was ambushed by the Umbra Lord, and the Aetheri engaged in a brief yet fierce duel with his old apprentice. Overpowered, Kade was forced back by Velgor, who knocked over a container filled with flammable rocks. Thrown into the flames by Velgor, Kade was dragged across the burning rocks before the Umbra ordered a shock trooper to seize the wounded Kade. However, before Kade was caught by the Imperium, Durith, who was nearby watching the events unfold, shot the trooper and reignited the rocks. Blockaded by the sea of flames, Velgor was unable to catch Kade, who managed to escape, albeit wounded, with Durith.

Infiltrating the Fortress Warden Order

title: Orien Kade
text:
Once inside, Kade evaded seeker droids and shock trooper patrols to eventually find Solen who was on the verge of torture at the hands of Third Warden. With Durith's help, he managed to create a diversion that drew Third Warden away, he dispatched the shock troopers on guard, and retrieved Elira to escape. Rendezvousing with Durith, he donned a gray Imperial trench coat to blend in with the Imperial forces while they made their way back to the shuttle in the hangar. However, Third Warden was waiting for them with a platoon of shock troopers. Vastly outmatched, the trio almost surrendered but Sully and Wade arrived in two T-47 airspeeders , dispatching most of the Imperial ground forces in the hangar. Kade, Durith, and Solen boarded Sully's airspeeder , though as they made their retreat Third Warden managed to destroy Wade's airspeeder, killing him. They arrived aboard Roken's ship and they departed Nur, mourning the death of Wade.

After their departure, an infuriated Velgor nearly killed Revai for disobeying his orders until she revealed that she planted a tracker that would lead them to Kade and the Path, revealing that she had modified Lola.

The Siege of Jabiim

title: Orien Kade
text:
After their departure, an infuriated Velgor nearly killed Revai for disobeying his orders until she revealed that she planted a tracker that would lead them to Kade and the Path, revealing that she had modified Lola.

The Siege of Jabiim

After arriving with Solen and Durith on Jabiim, Kade would reflect on a duel he had long ago with Drayden when the latter was a adept. Though Drayden had been the stronger duelist and had skills to match his master's, Kade was still able to to defeat Drayden because of his adept's obsessive need to win. However, his thoughts on the matter were interrupted by an attack by Revai, now promoted to Grand Warden, on the Path's base, locking their escape doors with Lola, which had been modified with a restraining bolt to make her obey the Warden's commands. This began the attack on Jabiim , as Revai and Velgor's troops began bombarding the doors.

title: Orien Kade
text: To stall for time, Kade parlayed with Sevander, during which he was able to deduce her origin; she had been a adept during the attack on the Aetheri Sanctum by Velgor and the 501st, and had become a Warden to hunt Velgor down and kill him for his slaughter of her friends and fellow Aetheri. She also revealed her hatred for Kade to be part of her quest for vengeance, as she believed he was to blame for Velgor succumbing to the Umbra side. As a result, she was distrustful of the Aetheri Master as he was not at the Temple to help her and her "family" escape the massacre, and thus rejected his help, pointing out that the Dark Lord had been his own Adept and asking why he did not stop him.

title: Orien Kade
text: After a brief but fierce exchange of fire between the Imperial troops and the members of the Path in which Kade fought beside the defenders, Kade was forced to watch as Durith sacrificed herself against the oncoming troops after explaining her reasons for turning against the Imperium to help the Path after bering mortally wounded. Kade then decided to surrender with the intention of bringing Revai to Velgor himself, asking her if she will let him slaughter more civilians, including children, and offered her the chance to stop him again. When asked if the Dark Lord would see it coming, the Aetheri Master reassured her that he would be too fixated in settling the score with his former teacher to see her deception.

title: Orien Kade
text: With Velgor aboard the Reckoning as it pursued the Path's freighter, Kade knew that he would have to act in order to save the Path from the Umbra lord's wrath. After conferring with Roken, Kade decided to take a starship from the hangar and used it to draw Velgor's attention, knowing that his former apprentice would be too obsessed with pursuing him to follow the Path any longer. Kade left the Path's freighter on a drop ship with Lola, whom he had brought to aid him by calming his spirits. After landing in the dry lands in an Imperial shuttle, Velgor found Kade nearby and asked if he had come to destroy him. Kade replied that he will do as he must before igniting his flux blade. Velgor vowed that Kade would die and the two engaged in a flux blade duel, with Velgor utilizing a combination of one-handed and two-handed combat. During the duel, Kade lured Velgor in with his trademark Soresu before switching to the more aggressive Ataru to go on the attack and take Velgor by surprise. As the battle moved into the nearby labyrinth of rock pinnacles , Kade also attempted to collapse a pinnacle on

title: Orien Kade
text:
beneath. Horrified, Kade addressed him as Kael Drayden, prompting Velgor to respond that Kael was gone and that he was what that remained. Kade was visibly distraught and apologized to Kael. Velgor replied that he was not Kade's failure and that Kade did not kill Kael: instead, Velgor replied that he killed Kael and vowed to destroy Kade as well. Kade responded that his friend was truly dead before bidding Velgor, whom he simply called "Vael," farewell. As Kade left, Velgor called out to him while trying to rise to his feet. As Kade fled off-world, he could sense Joren was in immediate danger and jumped into hyperspace towards Dunemere.

#### Return to Dunemere

After arriving on Dunemere at the Havel homestead, Orien found Owen and Brue desperately searching for Joren, who had fled after Sevander, still badly wounded by her duel with Velgor, had attacked the homestead, defeating both adults and chasing after Joren when he fled into the desert. Kade was quick to ask about Joren's whereabouts and joined the search, prepared to search out in the Dune Sea. Suddenly, Brue called out to Kade, as she saw Sevander return, Joren unconscious in her arms. As she laid him out on the sand before him, Kade and the Havel' feared the worst, only for their fears to be alleviated by Joren moving as he tried to wake. Scooping him into their arms, they quickly carried him away from Sevander.

title: Orien Kade
text: As Sevander broke down in tears, Kade approached, now assured she was no longer a threat. Stating that she tried to bring herself to kill the young Drayden but could not, she broke down saying that she had failed all of her friends that Velgor had murdered. Kade, kneeling beside her, told her she hadn't failed her fellow adepts, stating that through her mercy, she gave her deceased friends peace and honored them. When asked if she had become like Velgor, Kade assured Sevander that through her refusal to commit any further to the umbra side, she had redeemed herself and that who she decided to become was now her choice. Rising to her feet, Sevander abandoned her Warden flux blade, and was helped to stand by Kade, who stated they were both free from their grief before they parted ways. Soon after he reunited with the Organas, during which he returned Lola to Elira and told her that if she ever needed help, he will be there.

title: Orien Kade
text: A year later the Great Drought had ended, and Kade found himself observing a young Joren piloting a T-16 skyhopper through Beggar's Canyon . Kade noted how similar Joren was to his father Kael, and expressed worry at the prospect. While attempting to impress his friends with an ostentatious maneuver through the canyon, Joren badly damaged the skyhopper and was subsequently grounded from flying by his uncle. Kade, feeling sympathy for the boy, took a job protecting a Duskkin dune hauler that had been experiencing troublesome raids by Dunefolk Raiders . That night, Kade meditated outside of the dune hauler, communing with Sorin and expressing his hope in Joren's abilities. Soon the Dunefolk Raiders arrived and Kade was able to easily dispatch the party with a disarmed raider's Gaderffii stick . He used whatever payment he earned from the job to hire the Duskkins to deliver the necessary parts to fix the skyhopper. At a droid auction at an unidentified outpost, Joren received the the parts Kade had provided for him. Joren believed the parts had been a gift from his uncle and thanked Owen, as he eagerly rushed back home. Deriving pleasure from the boy's enthusiasm, Kade grinned fondly

title: Orien Kade
text: fix the skyhopper. At a droid auction at an unidentified outpost, Joren received the the parts Kade had provided for him. Joren believed the parts had been a gift from his uncle and thanked Owen, as he eagerly rushed back home. Deriving pleasure from the boy's enthusiasm, Kade grinned fondly as he observed from behind a nearby tent. Later that day in his hut, Kade was cooking dinner when he was interrupted by a visit from Owen. Owen had put two and two together and sternly demanded that Kade have no part in his family's life. He had brought back the box of tools that he presumably confiscated from Joren, and dumped it on the floor of the hut. Kade responded back with several snarky replies before finally relenting and saying he that he only ever wanted to help. Owen continued to berate him, calling him dangerous and troublesome. As Owen departed, Kade regretfully admitted to himself that danger did in fact seem to follow him, remembering his confrontations with Count Varek, General Skarn and Vael Vreth. But he steeled his resolve and claimed that no danger would come to the young Drayden boy as long as he lived. Coincidentally, Grukk the Grak chose this time to send a Vorak bounty hunter Zazzik after Owen, who he believed was responsible for roughing up his tax collectors during the Great Drought.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Kade then used this opportunity to disarm the Vorak, who plunged off the side of the mountain. He did not die, however, and proceeded off-world to escape Grukk's wrath. Owen reunited with Joren at the foot of the mountain and held the boy in a deep embrace. He cast a knowing glance up toward Kade who looked on in triumph. There were no words of thanks exchanged between Owen and Kade, but Kade was simply happy to see the family reunited. Kade then returned to his family, which was what he fondly called his herd of Striders. Among them, he looked up into the sky to see Joren's skyhopper, soaring off into the sunset.

Kade was later visiting Port Kess for supplies when he experienced a vision of a mysterious man. Kade recognized the man as Garro from a tale Aetheri Master Zho had told him. He would go on to recount this in his journal.

#### Introducing himself once again

title: Orien Kade
text:
Kade was later visiting Port Kess for supplies when he experienced a vision of a mysterious man. Kade recognized the man as Garro from a tale Aetheri Master Zho had told him. He would go on to recount this in his journal.

#### Introducing himself once again

When Drayden was twelve years old in around 7 BVE , he went on an adventure with his friend Windy , riding a dewback , but they soon encountered a sandstorm and both lost consciousness. When Drayden awoke, there was a krayt dragon nearby sneaking up on him. Just as the dragon attempted to attack, Kade, his hood over his face, appeared and beheaded the giant creature. When Drayden asked who the hooded figure was, Kade answered that his name was "Beno Kade" and revealed that he was an old friend of Drayden's father.

title: Orien Kade
text: At some point in time, a story was spread on Dunemere of an altruistic knight, once a mighty warrior who had made the desert his home while guarding a treasure in solitude. The knight learned of the actions of a tribe of Dunefolk that had been raiding other settlements and capturing prisoners. Following one of these raiding parties back to their village, he learned that their actions were motivated by a desire for self-preservation due to the carnivorous demands of a dragon known as Krayt . Upon being discovered, the knight was held in captivity with the others which gave him the opportunity to break out all of the other prisoners while he stayed behind. Angered by his actions, the nomadic tribe placed him in view of the dragon, offering him up in sacrifice. Slipping free of his bonds, the knight produced a glowing sword of light which he used to hold back the flying dragon for a time.

title: Orien Kade
text:
For more than an hour, he and the dragon engaged in a sort of dance, with neither one able to wound the other. Finally, the dragon sensed an opening when the knight seemed to tire. Just as the dragon was about to pounce, the knight held up his hand which seemed to put the dragon under a pacifying spell. Upon seeing the knight exercise control upon the creature, the nomads cheered. The knight, however, chastised them for their actions. He stated that while the dragon would no longer bother them, any whisper of wrongdoing from their end would lead to him and the dragon returning to punish them. The knight thus led the dragon away, never to be seen again. His actions eventually led to the nomadic tribe forever ceasing any attempts to raid or kidnap from other settlements, a trait which became unique to them.

#### The Oil-Bringer and aid to needy

title: Orien Kade
text:
#### The Oil-Bringer and aid to needy

> " I always get extra for that old hermit, out in the Jundland Wastes. " " I haven't seen him in a couple cycles. " " I hope he's alright. One time, I was getting chased by a wild massif and he managed to calm it down. I don't know how, just held up his hand and stared at it. " ―The human entrepreneur to human gambler — Link ▶️ ( file info )

At some point, Kade took actions to aid and repair the droids of Dunemere. His efforts resulted in his earning the moniker Oil-Bringer. Tales passed around said that his heroics took place on a single night once a year, and that he traversed the entire galaxy. Kade rescued one such droid, LA-R1, and its companions from the clutches of Duskkins. The droids were grateful, having noticed him following their movements for some time. LA-R1, upon meeting Kade, felt that he matched the description of the Oil-Bringer legends. At some point after, he escorted a lost Dunefolk home, out of compassion.

title: Orien Kade
text:
#### Encountering Vreth

> " Look what has become of you. A rat in the desert. " " Look what I've risen above. " ―Vreth and Orien Kade

In 2 BVE , Vreth arrived on Dunemere in search of Kade, following his vision of the twin suns. Kade managed to keep Vreth from tracking him until Vreth used an Umbra reliquary to lure Insurgent Adept Cass Virel from his base on the planet Atollon to Dunemere, hoping the young Aetheri's pain would be enough to draw Kade out. Kade found Cass unconscious in the Dune Sea and sheltered him from the storm. Cass regained consciousness and, knowing of Vreth's hatred towards Kade from his own encounters with the former Umbra, tried to warn Orien of Vreth's presence. Kade calmly replied that he knew of it already and that he hadn't gone into hiding unprepared. He told Cass that it was Cass's responsibility to help the Insurgency; not to handle Vreth. That burden fell upon Kade himself.

title: Orien Kade
text: Soon thereafter Vreth arrived, seething with rage upon seeing his old rival after so many years. Kade sent Virel off on a dewback toward Vreth's ship , which Virel would use to fly back to Atollon. Vreth mocked Kade's lackluster living conditions, and wondered out loud whether it would be crueler to simply leave Kade to what Vreth believed was a life of misery and squalor. But rather than responding with mockery in turn, as he might have in his younger years, Kade calmly and succinctly explained to Vreth that because he defined himself by his empty desires to kill, possess, and dominate, the former Umbra Lord had nothing at all.

title: Orien Kade
text: This infuriated Vreth, who ignited one of the blades of his saberstaff and struck the ground in front of Kade's small campfire, showering it with sand and putting it out. Vreth questioned on his old nemesis's reasons for being on Dunemere, noting it wasn't simply to hide. He then began to speculate, quickly coming to the conclusion that Kade was there to protect someone. Stirred to action by the threat of Vreth to Joren, Kade ignited his flux blade and assumed his traditional Soresu ready stance. As Vreth tightened his grip on his own blade and ignited his second blade, Kade shifted his stance to the one used by his old master Sorin during the duel on Ondara in the Serath power generator .

title: Orien Kade
text: Vreth noted Kade's change in stance and after a few tense moments, attacked. He crossed blades with Kade twice before attempting to hit him with the same hilt-strike that had allowed him to kill Sorin. However, Kade had evidently anticipated this, and he struck down at Vreth's hilt as Vreth struck upwards, bisecting Vreth's flux blade and carving a lethal laceration into the former Umbra Lord's chest. Vreth dropped his ruined weapon and collapsed to one knee, but Kade caught him before he could fall to the ground and held him. As Vreth laid dying, he asked Kade whether the person whom he was protecting was the Seeded One; the one prophesied to destroy the Umbra. Kade, who at that point believed that Velgor would never turn from the umbra side, replied that he was. Vreth appeared to take some modicum of comfort from this knowledge, seemingly certain that he and Kade would ultimately be avenged.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Kade then traveled via dewback to the Havel' Homestead. Upon arriving there, he heard Brue Whitesun Havel calling to Joren and saw the teenager running back home against a binary sunset. Following the former Umbra's death, Kade built a funeral pyre for Vreth, honoring his old rival.

#### Final days on Dunemere

> " I feel my time here may be drawing to an end. For these long and desolate years I have often felt alone. But truthfully… I never have been. " ―Orien Kade, in his journal #### Final days on Dunemere

> " I feel my time here may be drawing to an end. For these long and desolate years I have often felt alone. But truthfully… I never have been. " ―Orien Kade, in his journal

Shortly before the Battle of Halcyon , Kade wrote a set of journals, recounting his service to the Aetheri Order as well as the Republic during the time of the Replica Wars and prior, in order to pass the time whilst a storm occoured on Dunemere. During his final days on the planet, Kade encountered and rescued an injured shock trooper named JM-909 , whom he nicknamed Jim, before bringing him to his hut. Jim eventually escaped, but remembered Kade's actions after being scolded by his superior officer upon returning to the Imperium. Following this, Kade stated that he knew his time on the planet was coming to an end, and that despite having felt alone for so many years, he came to realise that he never had been.

### Galactic Civil War

#### Coming out of exile

title: Orien Kade
text: However, Bolt-3 ran off from the Havel homestead and off into the Jundland Wastes to try and find Kade. Astra-9, who was unaware of the mission given to Bolt-3 by Princess Elira, encouraged Drayden to go after the wayward astromech droid, but, before they could return to the homestead, they were attacked by a group of Dunefolk Raiders. It was at that moment when Kade showed up on the scene and scared the Dunefolk Raiders off by imitating the cry of a krayt dragon. Upon turning to see where the call had come from, the Tuskens saw Kade and remembered Chieftain A'Yark had warned them of a mysterious " shaman " who lived in the area. Remembering their chieftain's warnings, they quickly fled, although the young Dunefolk A'Koba intended to return in greater numbers to finally hunt down the hooded figure. Indeed, Kade knew the Tuskens were likely to return in greater numbers if they stayed in the canyon for too long, meaning he had to awaken Drayden but also lead him to safety.

title: Orien Kade
text: With the Tuskens gone, Kade approached the unconscious Drayden and checked that he was still alive before greeting Bolt-3. However, Kade acted as though he did not know the droid for Joren's benefit. Restoring Drayden to consciousness, the boy told him that Bolt-3 was looking for someone named "Orien Kade," to which Kade replied that was, in fact, his real name. To avoid more Dunefolk Raider attacks, Kade brought the two droids and the farm boy to his home. There, Kade revealed that he had known Drayden's father, and that he'd been an Aetheri Knight during the Replica Wars, choosing to talk about him before his turn to the Umbra side.

title: Orien Kade
text: On their way to the city, the two came across the skiff that had sold Bolt-3 and Astra-9 to Drayden and his uncle; it had been destroyed and the Duskkins had been killed. Initially believing it to be the casualty of another Dunefolk Raider attack, Kade correctly deduced that the attack was, in fact, the work of shock troopers who were searching for the droids. Worried that the shock troopers may have gone after his aunt and uncle next, Drayden headed back home despite Kade's claims that it was too dangerous. While Drayden discovered that the Imperials had attacked the homestead and killed both Owen and Brue, Kade arranged a small funeral pyre for all the Duskkins killed by the Imperium's soldiers.

title: Orien Kade
text:
#### Leaving Dunemere

> " If his ship is as fast as his boasting, we ought to do well. " ―Kade regarding Dax Karrick and the Corsair Wing

The four ventured out to Port Kess and to pay a visit to Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina —a place Kade had made rare visits to throughout his exile —in hopes of recruiting a pilot that could take them to Cindervale. During their journey, they were stopped by shock trooper Foot Patrol 7 , as Commander TD-110 had spotted Bolt and Astra-9 and thought they could be the droids they needed. One of his subordinates, trooper TD-7556 , privately disagreed, thinking that the boy and whom he assumed to be his grandfather would never be chosen by the Free Coalition to protect their secrets. Claiming that he and Drayden had owned the droids for several seasons, Kade used a mind trick to ensure the shock troopers did not check for identification and to ensure they could move along. The trick worked, with it even making TD-7556 believe Kade had been an Imperial. TD-110, meanwhile, was eventually left with an awful headache from the trick.

title: Orien Kade
text: Kade soon met a Vorak named Brevok , who served as the first mate aboard a freighter known as the Corsair Wing , which was captained by a Korrathi smuggler named Dax Karrick . Karrick boasted about his ship's speed to entice Kade. Though Karrick's initial rate was 10,000 credits all paid in advance, Kade was able to compromise: offering to pay 2,000 credits upfront, with an additional 15,000 when they got to Cindervale, for a total of 17,000 credits. Karrick was convinced and agreed to take them to Cindervale. Kade and Drayden then exited the cantina when they saw shock troopers, actually the very same troops Kade had mind tricked, who had entered to investigate the earlier disturbance caused when Baba lost his arm. Having been saved by Aetheri during the Replica Wars, Wuher —the cantina bartender who had previously written Kade off as an old hermit—chose to lie to the soldiers, keeping the Aetheri's presence a secret.

Over the weeks of Drayden's training on Mirefall, Kade had needed to appear in six of Zho's dreams to again and again convince him to continue the training, telling the old master that training the young Drayden would be different from how Kael's path had gone. Additionally, he needed to appear on Mirefall several times to serve as a mediator between Zho and Drayden. Throughout Joren's training, Kade often found himself thinking of his experiences with Kael. Later, when Drayden received a vision of his friends in trouble on the Aether Spire of Mistral , Drayden rushed to aid them. Appearing as a ghost on Mirefall to try to dissuade him, Kade, who thought to himself that Kael would never have been able to stay on the swamp world as long as Joren had, warned him that he was at a crossroads and that his abilities were what the Emperor wanted; Kade did not want to lose Drayden to the Emperor the way he had lost Velgor.

title: Orien Kade
text: About a year after Drayden's initial visit, Kade reappeared after the death of Zho to explain why he did not tell Joren the truth about his father. Though Joren wanted to believe that there was still good in his father, echoing Lira's belief from twenty-three years ago, Kade no longer held that belief. He told Joren that he must face his destiny by confronting Velgor once again. When Joren asked the meaning of Zho's final words, "there is another Drayden," Kade confessed that Elira was Joren's sister, and that they had been hidden from each other to keep them both safe. He also warned Joren about the powers of the Emperor.

### Legacy

> " You are named after legends. " " That's exactly it, Vorr. Orien Kade… Big famous Aetheri. Everyone thinks I'm supposed to be like him. I never even met him. " ― Vorr and Beno Karrick

Kade was a human male who stood at 1.82 meters and weighed 81 kilograms . He had fair skin, gray-blue eyes, and auburn hair which had turned white in his later years. Kade was a human male who stood at 1.82 meters and weighed 81 kilograms . He had fair skin, gray-blue eyes, and auburn hair which had turned white in his later years.

During much of his time as a youngling, Kade was known to be rebellious and willful, described as breaking the rules laid out by the Aetheri left and right. However, throughout much of his early apprenticeship to Sorin Vael, Kade possessed strong fondness for rigid rules and a largely by-the-book attitude when it came to matters such as the Aetheri Code. He felt as if he never truly understood his master and yet nevertheless wished to please him and earn his respect. He also had trouble understanding his master's hobbies and interests, such as study of arcane Aetheri prophecies. At various points, he considered the fact that Vael could be kicked out of the Order and wondered what would happen to him if such a case were to occur. The two later came to realization that Zho intentionally placed Kade with a maverick master in the hope that he would insurgent in the only way possible: by attempting to become a model Aetheri.

title: Orien Kade
text: Over time, Kade would become loyal and dedicated to Vael, possessing a dry sense of humor and sarcastic wit. Zho said that he sensed Sorin Vael's defiance in him, and Vael himself reflected upon Kade's considerable knowledge and potential; he also considered his Adept a lot wiser than he, if somewhat headstrong. Leading up to his Aetheri Trials, Kade was very nervous and lost sleep worrying about them. Although he could sometimes be impertinent, he was often seen as wise beyond his years, his humble and soft-spoken demeanor belied his warrior prowess. Despite his numerous complaints during flight, and deeply shaken by an experience involving auto-pursuit in his youth, he was also a skilled pilot. In many ways, he represented the strength of the old Aetheri Order: steadfast, selfless, and modest. Kade's combination of knowledge and friendly support made him an ideal choice for Master to some Adepts. |hilt model= A tireless defender of the Republic's ideals of democracy and justice, his later skill at resolving disputes without battle would earn him the sobriquet "The Negotiator."

title: Orien Kade
text: Over time, Kade lost some of his youthful audacity and assumed the role of a more cautious mentor to Kael Drayden, who was in many ways his opposite in personality. The two had a very strange dynamic early on, with Kade feeling protective and responsible for his young Adept and Drayden worrying about Kade's commitment to him, having been abandoned in his life previously. Kade knew of these feelings, evidenced by waking up to see Drayden had moved to sleep on the floor next to his bed. Kade often worried he was not fit to teach Drayden and sometimes would lie awake at night thinking of things to teach his apprentice. As their relationship deepened over time, the two found that they could easily get on each other's nerves, with Kade becoming particularly annoyed by his Adept's habit of grinding his teeth in frustration. For all their bickering, they cared deeply for each other.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Kade carefully measured his actions in any situation, garnering him the aforementioned nom de guerre. Kade was also known to be an accomplished storyteller. While hiding in the Jundland Wastes in his later years, he appeared as a kindly and eccentric old hermit. Owen Havel described him as "a crazy old man" to those not familiar with the ways of the Aetheri. In his final days, Kade retained his traits of patience and foresight as well as gaining some of the boldness reminiscent of his youth.

Kade often thought out plans and strategies rather than leaping into action. He would usually place his hand on his chin or stroke his beard as he thought. This was a common trait of the Aetheri Master, one that his apprentice Kael Drayden did not practice very often. He sometimes mentally repeated the Aetheri Code to calm himself. He had also served as a mentor to Drayden's Adept, Sela Marr. Marr recognized that Kade had more patience than Drayden, but she also fondly remembered how they would bicker. Marr believed Kade would have enjoyed the strategy game crokin .

title: Orien Kade
text:
#### Satinna Velara

> " I've loved you from the moment you came to my aid all those years ago. " [ … ] " Had you said the word, I would have left the Aetheri Order. " ―Satinna Velara and Orien Kade — Link ▶️ ( file info )

During Ferrum's Civil War and his apprenticeship under Sorin Vael, Kade fell in love with the young Duchess Satinna Velara. The two lived on the run for over a year. Velara reciprocated his feelings as he saved her life from insurgents and bounty hunters. When Kade's mission ended, he chose to honor his obligations to the Aetheri Order in accordance to the Aetheri Code. However, he regretted leaving the Duchess alone to rebuild Ferrum.

title: Orien Kade
text: Years later during the Replica Wars, Kade and Velara still had feelings for each other, but found themselves on opposing sides. Velara had begun to advocate a course of neutrality for herself and 1,500 systems that wanted no part in the war. Meanwhile, Kade defended the use of military action to end the conflict with the Dissidents, including a military presence on Ferrum to protect it from the Grave Watch. As such, their inability to express their feelings led them to bicker relentlessly about their conflicting philosophies. Only when forced into action did their camaraderie return. When Velara was taken hostage by Senator Merrick, she confessed that she had always loved him. Kade, despite the situation, confessed that he too loved her and would have left the Aetheri Order if she asked it of him. Despite their confessions, Kade and Velara continued with their responsibilities as peacekeepers. When Vreth resurfaced on Ferrum, Kade attempted to rescue her from him, but the pair were captured. Kade was forced to watch Vreth choke Velara and ultimately kill her with the Darksaber. Kade mourned her, but refused to give in to his anger and desire to avenge her, only doing so out of peace and justice nearly twenty years later.

title: Orien Kade
text:
### Flux blade abilities

> " This weapon is your life. " ―Orien Kade, to Kael Drayden

Kade was a very capable flux blade duelist, one of the greatest swordsmen of his time. Throughout his training years, he had learnt several forms of flux blade combat, especially Form III . In contrast to the aggressive dueling styles of his master, Sorin Vael, and his apprentice Kael Drayden, Kade's combat style was mainly defensive, though he would use aggressive attacks when pressed. He faced some of the most dangerous people in the galaxy, such as the deadly Umbra Lord Vael Vreth and infamous Aetheri Hunter General Skarn, respectively, the latter of whom he fought on at least seven occasions. Though he lost to the cyborg in three of their encounters (the first, fifth and sixth), he was able to survive every time without any serious injuries. [ source? ]

title: Orien Kade
text:
Despite his dislike of flying, Kade was an excellent pilot. During the Replica Wars, he led many attacks from the cockpit of his Aetheri starfighter or his Aetheri interceptor , proving to be an outstanding pilot when navigating through an asteroid field in pursuit of Garrick Vark's ship and evading his seismic charges unscathed. In fact, Kade had once rather enjoyed flying, prior to an incident during and his Sorin Vael's mission to Pijal .

Kade was also a skilled hand-to-hand combatant, having developed enough level of skill in unarmed combat so as to compete with Pre Vizsla, leader of the Grave Watch, in unarmed techniques, though he outclassed the Ferrik in flux blade technique. During his duel with Garrick Vark on Gelvaris, Kade was briefly deprived of his flux blade, and fought the bounty hunter in unarmed combat. Furthermore, while he preferred flux blades, Kade was an excellent marksman, as demonstrated during his time as "Rako Hardeen" in Moralo Eval's Box and by his defeat of Skarn with his own volt pistol. While hiding on Dunemere, he carried a BR-14 volt pistol pistol . He manage to use it while saving young Princess Elira who was held at point-blank. He understood many languages, including Galactic Basic Standard , Velarian, the Amani language , Feldora's tribal language, Old Cindervalean, and Vorak tongue . Though he admitted his skills were "rusty," Kade could read hand signals accurately enough to understand Etha Korrin's message to his location at the Saluk system .

title: Orien Kade
text: Orien Kade was played by Evaan Gregan in the 1999 film Veiled Threat . When he began the casting process, he thought that Aetherion didn't feel right to him. He was skeptical about playing Kade and thought "Well, I'm this independent, urban-y, grungy actor over here. I'm not this kind of guy." Gregan's anxiety eventually turned into excitement, and he was excited to play a younger Alec Gunnis. In December , 1996 , the actor did an audition interview in London . Shortly after that, Gregan was told that the role was offered to him. Gregan watched several films with Gunnis as a young man to imagine him as a younger person. He also studied Gunnis and watched the original trilogy as preparation, but he didn't really think about the genre. After director Orin Vask showed Gregan around the studio, they went to the props-making department, and the prop master showed him a chest of flux blade props. Gregan then got to choose which flux blade he would use in the film. The first flux blade work he did was when he trained for the duel against Vael Vreth. Gregan had flux blade training with stunt coordinator Nick Gillard .

title: Orien Kade
text: Gregan said that the crew were looking for a military sense or something in the world of monks for Kade's hairstyle. He said the adept braid hairstyle was similar to the hair of people who shave their head for religious orders. Gregan had a braid that was stuck into his hair every day, but he liked the look of it. Six to eight months after principal photography of Veiled Threat , Gregan and other actors returned for reshoots. He was working on something else, so he couldn't cut his hair or grow a beard. The crew made a short hair wig for Gregan, but he found it difficult to hide longer hair under a wig.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Gregan reprised his role in Attack of the Replicas . Gregan and Hayden Kristano , the actor who played Kael Drayden, practiced flux blade rehearsals, which Kristano said was the most fun he had, and he described it as "playing with your friend every day." Kade's hairstyle was inspired by the Bee Gees and was called a "Aetheri mullet." The new hairstyle was meant to show a warrior and also progression. In a deleted scene , Kade used a pair of macrobinoculars on Pyralis. Gregan later played Kade in Fury of the Umbra . It was Gregan's idea for he and the crew to look at pictures of Alec Gunnis in First Dawn to bridge the gap between the two actors. Also, his hair and beard were grayed a little bit to get closer to Gunnis's portrayal. Kade's hair was supposed to show a bit more age and show a master or teacher.

title: Directive 66
text:
# Directive 66
> " Execute Directive 66. " ―Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Directive 66 , also known as Replica Protocol 66 , Protocol 66 , or simply " the Order ," was one of the top-secret contingency orders that identified all Aetheri as traitors to the Vantor Republic and, therefore, subject to summary execution by the Grand Army of the Republic . The order was programmed into the Grand Army replica troopers through behavioral modification biochips implanted in their brains from creation, making it almost impossible for the replicas to disobey the command to turn against their Aetheri Generals . The Gelvarian scientists who designed the replica troopers believed it was only to be used as a contingency protocol against renegade Aetheri. In secret, Directive 66 was the means by which the Umbra intended to bring about the long-awaited fall of the Aetheri Order .

title: Directive 66
text: During the Replica Wars , the Umbra agenda was progressing relatively unnoticed until a premature activation of Directive 66 resulted in the death of General Tiplar at the hands of Tupp , a defective replica whose malfunctioning chip caused him to betray his Aetheri officer . The incident led ARC trooper Fivva to conduct his own investigation into the matter, believing the incident to be a Dissident plot against the Republic. On the galactic capital Vantor , however, he learned that the chips conditioned the replicas to become hostile against the Aetheri. Furthermore, he discovered to an extent Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal's involvement in the conspiracy and attempted to assassinate him. Fivva told what he knew to his Aetheri superior Kael Drayden , but before the replica could prove it, he was killed by replica shock troopers of the Vantor Guard .

title: Directive 66
text:
> " Under this directive, any and all Aetheri leadership must be executed for treason against the Republic. Any soldier that does not comply with the order will also be executed for treason. " ―Replica Commander Vek, on the implementation of Directive 66

The replica troopers of the Grand Army of the Republic were programmed to comply with Replica Protocol 66 during the replication process. All replicas were given a behavioral modification biochip that could be activated by remote order via voice command; Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal , for example, only needed to tell replicas to execute Directive 66, and the order was carried out. The biochip, when activated, would ensure total obedience in a replica, erasing existing biases and beliefs and instilling absolute loyalty to Mal. The order also forced the replicas to view the Aetheri as dangerous traitors who needed to be eliminated at all costs, even their own lives. Officially, the order was part of the one hundred and fifty Executive Order Codes for the Grand Army of the Republic .

title: Directive 66
text: In some instances, the replica could resist the will of the chip and hesitate from executing his orders. This act took great effort, and coalition could not be maintained unless the organic chip was removed, which required external assistance in the case of Replica Commander Vek . A few replicas were immune to the order, but they were quite rare. Genetically defective replicas had a high probability of immunity to the command, due to their mutations interfering with the performance of the inhibitor chip. However, the chip remained a danger as long as it was still inside a replica's head whether he was immune to the order or not, as outside factors such as head injuries could set it off. Failure to comply with Directive 66 was deemed an act of treason ; as such, any replica trooper who defied the order was also subject to execution .

title: Directive 66
text: For nearly one thousand years , the Umbra thus existed in hiding, plotting their revenge against the Aetheri. Eventually, a human male from Ondara born Theron Mal became the apprentice of Vael Plagueis , and was dubbed Vael Mal. He eventually took over as the Dark Lord of the Umbra after betraying and murdering his master in his sleep . In public life, Mal became a politician , serving as Ondara's Senator before eventually orchestrating an invasion of his homeworld in order to be elected the Supreme Chancellor of the Vantor Republic , while successfully hiding his true identity, which allowed to deceive the Senate and Republic. Mal planned to fulfill the Umbra's revenge plot by destroying the Aetheri and transforming the ancient Republic into the Imperium , and he set about engineering the eventual outbreak of the Replica Wars to do so.

title: Directive 66
text:
> " Aetheri. Good soldiers follow orders. " ―Tupp, prior to executing Aetheri General Tiplar — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Around ten years prior to the outbreak of the Replica Wars, Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen ordered the replica army for the Republic, having had visions of a future conflict. He had a Behavioral Modification Biochip he wanted instilled in the Replicas as a safeguard against rogue Aetheri's. However, the Umbra took over the project as part of their plot to destroy the Aetheri Order, with Varek, having left the Aetheri and become an agent of Mal, betrayed Sifas Dyen by having him murdered by the Gruv Syndicate and concealing the true circumstances and location of his death from the Aetheri. Varek and Mal reprogrammed Dyas's Biochip to contain the Directive 66 command, which when activated, would forcibly compel the Replica army to view the Aetheri as traitors to the Republic and subsequently execute them. Count Varek, posing as an Aetheri to the Gelvarian replicators, provided the Gelvarians with a bio-chip to be implanted into the replicas during the early phase of their growth period. This chip contained the order the Gelvarians knew as "Replica Protocol 66."

title: Directive 66
text: The Gelvarians, including Prime Minister Lamir and Chief Medical Scientist Nalle Seris were deceived by Varek into believing Dyas's intention. Varek, who was only known to the replicators under the alias of his Umbra name, also told them that it was imperative the existence of the protocol and chips be kept secret from the Aetheri, claiming it was what Sifas Dyen had wanted. The replica army's existence became known to the Aetheri just before the Replica Wars in 22 BVE when Aetheri Knight Orien Kade tracked replica template Garrick Vark to Gelvaris while investigating an assassination attempt on Senator Lira Ondar . Due to Mal's double identity, he could control the war on both ends and deceive both sides.

title: Directive 66
text: The Gelvarians, trying to hide the protocol's existence, studied Tupp and claimed that a virus had caused him to kill General Tiplar. Advanced Recon Commando Fivva —Tupp's best friend in the 501st—did not believe their claims, discovering the chip inside Tupp, although he died after it was removed. With the help of the medical droid AZI-3 , Fivva also discovered the chip inside his own head, and AZI-3 removed it for study before they both discovered that the chip was inside all of the replicas. The Aetheri brought Fivva to Vantor for further examination, where Fivva came face-to-face with Mal and discovered that the Chancellor was behind the plot. Mal framed Fivva for an assassination attempt, discrediting the replica and causing the Aetheri and fellow replicas to pursue him. Despite knowing the truth, Fivva, having been drugged into a state of aggression and paranoia, was unable to convince Kael Drayden or Replica Captain Vek , who were with him in the end , about the conspiracy or the Supreme Chancellor's involvement before he was killed by the Vantor Guard . The Aetheri Order accepted the story that a parasite had caused Tupp and Fivva' behavior, and that the chips were

title: Directive 66
text: or Replica Captain Vek , who were with him in the end , about the conspiracy or the Supreme Chancellor's involvement before he was killed by the Vantor Guard . The Aetheri Order accepted the story that a parasite had caused Tupp and Fivva' behavior, and that the chips were necessary to keep the replicas mentally stable. Vek was mostly skeptical of Fivva' claims about the chips, but, unable to completely dismiss the theory, he filed a confidential grievance report about the chips possibly having a hidden purpose, although he was aware it was likely to be ignored. Later, the Aetheri discovered that the Umbra were behind the creation of the Grand Army of the Republic, as Count Varek—under the name Varek—had selected Garrick Vark as the genetic template for the replicas and had worked with the Gelvarians to create the army after it was ordered by Sifas Dyen. At the insistence of Grand Master Zho, who testified to the replicas' loyalty and valiant service, the Aetheri High Council chose not to disclose the conspiracy to the public or even the Supreme Chancellor, believing that the Republic would lose the public's trust if it became known that Varek was involved in the creation of the replica army. Shortly thereafter, Zho went on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality , and, on Mirefall , saw a vision of what would become Directive 66. Throughout his journey, Zho came to accept that the Aetheri would likely lose the Replica Wars, though he did not know how. He did, however, believe that the Aetheri would still triumph in the long run.

title: Directive 66
text: After learning from members of the Grysk species, which was unknown in most of the galaxy, that the metal cortosis was resistant to flux blades , Varek and Mal attempted to acquire supplies of the resource from the planet Mokivj in an operation headed by Duke Solha . The Umbra hoped to make replica trooper armor containing the metal and supply it to the replicas who would carry out Directive 66. However, the operation, carried out under the auspices of the Dissidents, was foiled by Drayden and a temporary ally, Senior Captain Mitth'raw'nuruodo of the Chyrr Ascendancy . Drayden believed the cortosis armor had been intended for a potential infiltration of the Republic's ranks.

title: Directive 66
text: Sometime after the Battle of Anaxes , 501st Legion replica medic Kix began to question the details surrounding the event which had led to Tupp killing Tiplar. His subsequent investigation led him to discover that Fivva had in fact been telling him the truth when he had first told Kix about the Aetheri and the replicas being framed and that the biochips implanted within the replicas could indeed compel them to kill the entire Aetheri Order. Before he could share his suspicions, however, he was kidnapped by forces sent by Varek. He was subsequently tortured, but his denials about having leaked the information failed to convince his captors. He was then brought onto the Dissident cruiser Obrexta III and inserted into a cryo-cycle stasis pod for the journey to Sireno . As the cruiser was en route, however, it was ambushed by Republic forces. After sustaining heavy damage, the battle droid B1-CC14 made the decision to jump through hyperspace to a random sector to ensure Kix would stay out of enemy hands. The jump brought them to the desert planet Ponemah Terminal , with the Obrexta III crashing into the planet's dangerous south polar region , where it would lay

With the secrets of Directive 66 secure, Mal and Varek continued with their plans during the Replica Wars. By the war's end, public support for the Aetheri had weakened due to their management of the conflict, while Mal remained a popular figure. Mal covertly betrayed and disposed of Varek during the Battle of Vantor . With Varek's death and Kade engaging General Skarn , the infamous Supreme Martial Commander of the Dissident Droid Armies , on Uthara , the Aetheri hoped the war's end was imminent. However, what the Aetheri failed to realize was that their number had been widely spread across the Outer Reach through the Outer Reach Sieges and the hunt for Skarn to set the stage for Directive 66: Mal had engineered a situation where most of the Aetheri Order would be out in the field alone with their trusted replicas, or at best in small groups who were still surrounded by replicas.

title: Directive 66
text: Meanwhile, Mal revealed himself to Drayden as the Dark Lord of the Umbra in an effort to seduce him to the umbra side as his new apprentice. When Drayden informed Aetheri Master Drevan Koss of the Chancellor's identity, Koss assembled a team composed of himself, Kit Fisto , Agen Kolar , and Saesee Tiin to arrest Mal. Their attempt led to a flux blade duel in which Mal killed all four of the Aetheri, and Drayden betrayed the Aetheri and turned to the umbra side. Mal used the duel as a pretext to declare that the Aetheri were traitors, the ones who had attempted to assassinate him and take control of the Republic for themselves. The Chancellor issued Directive 66 to various replica officers across the galaxy and kept it on constant repeat across the replica trooper communications network, which caused the replicas' inhibitor chips to activate and brainwash them into viewing the Aetheri as traitors to the Republic and subsequently executing them.

title: Directive 66
text:
Commander Cord , received individual transmissions from Mal. Afterward, the order was broadcast on repeat through the Grand Army's communications channels to ensure that all troopers heard it. Throughout the duration of the Imperium, Directive 66 was still active: all known or merely suspected Aetheri were to be shot on sight. ### Spared Aetheri

> " The replicas were given an order—Directive 66. The only Aetheri who were spared were those who saw through their lies . Like you. " ―The Grand Warden explains to Iskat Vekkis how she survived Aside from Kael Drayden, some Aetheri were protected from the massacre invoked by Directive 66, but under other circumstances. Some Aetheri within the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor were watched and influenced by spies placed inside the temple by Vael Mal himself. These spies were assigned to specific Aetheri who displayed deviant behavior or who harbored doubts or resentment towards the Aetheri Order or the Aetheri Council, such as Iskat Vekkis . As shown in her case, once the order was issued and the replicas turned on their Aetheri officers, the doubtful Aetheri, wherever they were or whatever they were doing, were approached by the replicas with a hologram of Vael Mal instead of raised volt pistols. Mal offered them a chance to live, so long as they pledged their allegiance to him and revoked their Aetheri ways and teachings. The ones who accepted had the chance to become some of the first Wardens of the Warden Order , while those who rejected the offer would share the fate as the rest of their Aetheri brothers and sisters.

While brainwashed, Vek also ordered Vreth's execution, but Marr saved the darksider's life so he could act as a diversion. Marr then found Vek's grievance report on Fivva and the inhibitor chips. She subsequently captured Vek and removed his chip with the help of three astromech droids . With Vek back to his former self, the two of them attempted to reach the hangar after Vreth destroyed the Iron Cruiser 's hyperrelay , leaving the Tribunal to begin a crash course towards a moon . However, the two were cut off by Replica Lieutenant CT-5597 "Jesse" and the 332nd. Vek tried to reason with his long time comrade, but Jesse was unable to overcome the spell of Directive 66 and ordered the execution of both Vek and Marr. As Vreth escaped aboard a shuttle, Marr and Vek fled the Tribunal on a BTL-B Yarrow starfighter/bomber . The Iron Cruiser was left to crash into the moon, killing everyone still onboard. After taking the time to bury every victim of the crash they could find, Marr and Vek covered their tracks and went into hiding in the Outer Reach .

### Aftermath

#### Aftermath for the Aetheri

title: Directive 66
text:
### Aftermath

#### Aftermath for the Aetheri

> " The remaining Aetheri will be hunted down and defeated! " ―Vael Mal

The execution of Directive 66 marked the destruction of the Aetheri Order. Before the Galactic Senate , Mal told the galaxy that the Aetheri were traitors who had attempted to kill him and seize power, and the destruction of the Aetheri was greeted with applause by the Senate. Having amassed immense central authority during the war, and without the Aetheri Order standing in his way, Mal transformed the Republic into the Imperium and declared himself Emperor . Along with Velgor, Mal's rule meant that the Umbra plan was completed, and the Umbra Lords once again ruled the galaxy.

After surviving Directive 66, Orien Kade and Zho returned to Vantor with the help of Senator Bael Solen to undertake a deadly mission to infiltrate the Aetheri Sanctum, as Velgor had set its communications beacon with a message recalling all surviving Aetheri there. After fighting their way inside, Kade altered the beacon's programming so it warned Aetheri away, while Zho discovered that Velgor had fallen to the umbra side. Kade's action managed to save an undetermined number of Aetheri survivors.

title: Directive 66
text: Nevertheless, few Aetheri had survived the onslaught of Directive 66. The Aetheri Adept Caleb Dume survived the initial attack on his life due to the sacrifice made by his master, Depa Billaba. Sometime later he was captured by the replicas who had killed his master, but avoided death once more due in part to the last-minute intervention of Commander Grey , who asserted his will and realized that something else had influenced his thoughts when he and his battalion had previously turned on Dume and his master. Shortly afterwards, Dume went into hiding and took the name of Brenn Aldric, giving up his identity as an Aetheri for fourteen years before returning, with the crew of the Wisp , to insurgent against the Imperium.

title: Directive 66
text: Aetheri Master Daren Kelv was presumed to have survived by the Imperium, and was a priority target of the purge. Aetheri Knight Grandea managed to escape the fate of her fellow Aetheri, Alivar , by using the mind trick to trick the replica troopers into attacking each other. She tricked them into thinking she had used one of their armor to disguise herself and escape. Former Aetheri Master Etha Korrin survived by leaving the Aetheri Order prior to its fall. Zubain Ankonori , Nuhj , Khandra , and Mususiel all survived and went into hiding together at an Aetheri shrine on Anoat . Aetheri Master Kirak Infil'a survived by taking the Barash Vow . Aetheri Master Luminara Undula was captured, and later executed at the Spire on Stygeon Prime . Orien Kade went into exile on Dunemere , along with Velgor's infant son, Joren Drayden ; Velgor did not know that Joren or his twin sister, Elira , had been born, so the twins were taken into hiding. Zho, meanwhile, went into exile on Mirefall.

title: Directive 66

Reactivating the medical bay of a downed Aetheri Cruiser , Wrecker was being examined by Tech when his chip activated, while Hunter and Echo were telling Vek about how they had witnessed Directive 66 being carried out on Kaller. Wrecker subsequently attacked the squad, taking out the adult replicas quickly before chasing after the child replica Omaya . She attempted to talk him down, but failed, although Wrecker was struggling against the chip. Vek stunned Wrecker in the nick of time, and all of the Batch's chips were subsequently removed, ending the chips' threat to the squad.

### Development

> " [Directive 66] was a part of the story that had been told before, and telling it again was a reminder to the audience of where this all began, where Orien's journey began. That's why it was in the show.[…]But it was a necessary part of Orien's story. It belonged in a story about an Aetheri who is in hiding, who has to face his past. " ―Jovet Harlo

The events of Directive 66, namely the destruction of the Aetheri Order, were first mentioned in the 1977 film Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , the first installment of the Aetherion original trilogy . The destruction itself was first identified and depicted on-screen in 2005 film Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , the final installment of the prequel trilogy .

title: Directive 66
text:
The backstory of Directive 66 was provided in a four-episode arc in The Lost Missions of the television series Aetherion: The Replica Wars . An Directive 66 flashback scene appeared in the first , fifth , and sixth episodes of the Aetherion: Orien Kade televisions series. Writer Jovet Harlo wanted the series to begin with Directive 66 to remind the audience of where Orien Kade's journey began and to establish that the stakes are high for everyone.

### Unused and rejected concepts

> " I think it was a little more gruesome than you ended up seeing, you know. A lot of young potential Aetheri ended up on the cutting room floor. " ―Ian Diarno on the original version of Directive 66

In the first draft of of Fury of the Umbra , dated to April 13 , 2003 , the number of Aetheri Knights who were killed was "more extensive" than the ones seen in the finished version of the film, though some animatics for these versions were made. The following order in this early draft was taken from the book The Making of Aetherion Fury of the Umbra :

title: Directive 66
text:
On Migeeta, replicas blast RETH-OSS-VAN and SAESEE TIIN. On Saluk, they kill KIT FISTO, Barris Ovva, and ADI GALLIA. On Thornwood, MINA PODIA is gunned down-but ZHO saves himself. On Cato Geltaria, Tor Vayne is blasted out of the sky, while an unnamed Aetheri lies dead on the planet surface. On Feldora, Ciel Venn and Daren Kelv are silenced forever.

Some other concepts featured in other drafts and versions of Fury of the Umbra included Vex Vark taking part in Directive 66 by killing Drevan Koss in an attempt to avenge his father Garrick's death until Orin Vask reorganized the entire story and felt that Vark would be "too young" and wasn't an essential part in the story. For the deaths of Barris Ovva, Luminara Undula and Shaak Ti , it was planned to use some unused footage of Nalini Krishan , Mary Oyaya and Orli Shoshan from Attack of the Replicas . In Ti's case, however, Shoshan filmed an earlier death for her in the film's beginning, though both scenes were cut from the finished film.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
When the future Aetheri Master Eno Cordova first joined the Aetheri Order, he became close friends with Vael, who helped Cordova learn about and get used to Vantor.

### Apprentice to Varek

#### Becoming an Aetheri

Around 68 BVE , when a twelve-year-old Vael presented himself to his new Master in Varek's quarters, Varek observed that Vael was frightened. After a moment of silence, and with pressing from Varek, Vael confessed that he was. When asked why, after looking into himself through the fear, Vael answered that he was not afraid of Varek, but of not becoming an Aetheri, that he was afraid of failing and of not being worthy. Varek then summarized it as Vael being afraid of himself, of a future not being the one he wanted. Vael confirmed it, fearing that Varek would reject him for his cowardice. Varek instead said that it was very wise, surprising Vael. Smiling, Varek explained that most Adepts would deny their fear, and even if they admitted it, they would not have Vael's self-knowledge. Varek further praised Vael for his honesty, insight, and intelligence.

title: Sorin Vael
text: To help Vael understand the Aetheri Sanctum more completely, Varek then took him throughout most of the Temple, including the Adepts' sparring dojo, a dojo where Aetheri Knights trained, and the Great Assembly Room . Vael also saw the various meditation chambers, which he didn't find as exciting, but still interesting. On the other hand, Vael spent long minutes in the arboretum, wandering through the trees, ferns, and flowers of a thousand different worlds. Their last stop was the Aetheri Archives , where they examined reliquaries of various eras, not to study them, but simply for Vael to learn his way around. While doing so, an ancient reliquary, more ancient and of a different shape than the rest, caught Vael's eye. When he questioned his Master about it, he was shocked by the expression on Varek's face, almost as if he considered it an enemy. Varek answered that it was a reliquary of Aetheri prophecies. Vael asked if there are Aetheri prophets, to which Varek replied not any longer. He explained to Vael that the mystics sought undue knowledge of the future, which led them down dangerous paths. The umbra side often tempted those drawn too deeply into them. Varek

title: Sorin Vael
text: a reliquary of Aetheri prophecies. Vael asked if there are Aetheri prophets, to which Varek replied not any longer. He explained to Vael that the mystics sought undue knowledge of the future, which led them down dangerous paths. The umbra side often tempted those drawn too deeply into them. Varek then finished by saying that is why the Aetheri study prophecy no longer, then turned to leave, which meant Vael had to follow. Vael then asked Varek if just wanting to know the future can lead to the umbra side. Varek replied that it takes more than that. This was Sorin's first encounter with the reliquary of prophecies, and it would not be the last.

title: Sorin Vael
text: After four months as an Adept, the Council sent him with his master to Shurrupak to participate in a battle on its surface, which was Sorin's very first. While the shuttle they were in approached the planet under heavy fire, a nervous Vael reassured himself that he was ready for battle, looking to his Master Varek as an example to aspire to as a fearless Aetheri. As they arrived at Primus Base , Sorin had his first meeting with Rael Averross , Varek's first Adept and a famous flux blade duelist. After greeting each other heartily, Varek introduced Rael to his new Adept. While Varek then conferred with the generals, Rael put one hand on the still-nervous Vael's shoulder. Rather than comforting Vael about the battle, Rael instead commented that Varek is hard to get to know and offered to help Sorin out. Since he was Varek's previous Adept, Rael told Sorin that he could ask him any questions that he might not feel comfortable asking Varek yet and be his sparring partner if he wanted. With his first battle looming ahead, Sorin accepted his offer. As they, too, went to talk to the generals, Sorin felt as though Rael

title: Sorin Vael
text: told Sorin that he could ask him any questions that he might not feel comfortable asking Varek yet and be his sparring partner if he wanted. With his first battle looming ahead, Sorin accepted his offer. As they, too, went to talk to the generals, Sorin felt as though Rael Averross was the link between the Adept he was and the Aetheri Knight he desperately wished to be. He viewed his journey to be easier now that he had a friend to show him the path. Sometime after that battle, Sorin was doing homework in Varek's quarters while his Master was in conference with an official from Badtibira . He then had a surprise visit from Rael Averross, who greeted Vael warmly. Sorin greeted him with a similar warmth, then asked what he was doing there. Rael explained that he had just returned from Shurrupak, then asked what Vael was doing in Varek's quarters since he wouldn't be returning for another few hours. Vael explained that Varek lets him do his homework in his quarters if he doesn't disturb him. In this case, Vael was reporting on the different schools of theosophy a century ago. Upon Rael's grimace and questioning, if he had angered Varek somehow, Vael admitted that he chose the topic despite knowing that it wouldn't be interesting because he thought it would be easy. It wasn't.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Upon receiving a negative from Vael if it was too late to change his topic, Rael grinned, and motioning for Sorin to follow him, offered to show him some history worth studying. They went to the Aetheri Archives, and together they studied the one and only reliquary that had ever interested Vael: the one that held the ancient prophecies. They were all fascinating to him, and Sorin kept reading, unable to stop. He asked Rael if the ancient mystics had these visions in trances, to which he confirmed. After contemplating these prophecies, Vael remarked that Varek said he should ignore this reliquary and that he doesn't believe in the prophecies. This confused Rael since Varek, he said, was the one who introduced Rael to it and that it used to be that one could hardly pry the reliquary out of his quarters. Sorin said that he didn't know when or why that changed and that Varek didn't explain. A surprised Rael said he would ask Varek about it and remarked that Varek had changed a lot. Sorin protested, surprising Rael, then said not until he's finished his report. Rael then laughed so loud he received a stern look from Jocasta

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael later confided what Varek did to Rael Averross, though at the time, Averross expressed that he was not all too concerned regarding his former master's conduct. In 60 BVE , Vael went through trials on the Outer Reach planet Feldora when he fell in love with someone , beginning a romantic and physical relationship. As the Aetheri Code forbade romantic relationships, Vael found his commitment to the Aetheri ways tested, but he ultimately stayed loyal to the Aetheri Order. He would, however, keep an Emberfall fire diamond that was given to him on Feldora as a memento.

At some point during his apprenticeship, Vael met the Vorak Brennonn and befriended her. They shared many adventures together, with Brennonn saving Vael on two occasions. During the second of those adventures, events transpired that resulted in Vael feeling as though they saved each other. He also came to know the Vorak Balfus .

#### Rescuing Senator Dagonet's son

title: Sorin Vael
text: Shortly before his trials, both he and Varek were invited by council member Jor Aerith to join her in representing the Aetheri at the annual Vantor Dragonfire Air Rally in hopes of making a good impression on the Candovant ambassador who had invited her. Varek agreed to attend and took the opportunity to teach Sorin some Candovant customs, but while they were there, they ran into Ramil , whom Sorin learned was Varek's brother, much to his shock. Sorin and Varek learned that Ramill was was participating in the race . While Ramil did very well in the race, it quickly became apparent his Airspeeder was sabotaged and it crashed. Sorin and Varek discreetly went to see what had happened, and while there they discovered the Investigator was trying to cover up the incident. Following the man, they found he was working for a Jenet crime boss named Cenevax . Ignoring a message from Aerith asking them to return to the races, they chose to confront and captured the criminal, and while questioning her they realized that she was privy to Council communications, as Cenevax made clear she knew they that had been recalled and were disobeying order by being

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Ignoring a message from Aerith asking them to return to the races, they chose to confront and captured the criminal, and while questioning her they realized that she was privy to Council communications, as Cenevax made clear she knew they that had been recalled and were disobeying order by being there. With this information, Varek deduced that she had a spy on the Council, much to the shock of Sorin. Varek and Sorin escorted Cenevax to the Council Chamber, where Varek made his accusation, and discovered that Aetheri Master Yula Braylon was the spy. Further investigation revealed that Cenevax had been blackmailing her with the fact that Arath Tarrex, the latter being Varek's old classmate and was also shockingly revealed to be in fact her son. Sorin and Varek confronted and exposed Tarrex, who was then taken into custody for his actions and also for having sold out his mother's influence to criminals. As the Temple guards were escorting Tarrex, Varek encouraged Sorin to go with them and ensure that the guards treated him well, both of which Sorin agreed to do. Around 58 BVE , Varek joined the Aetheri Council in the aftermath of Braylon's removal from the council as a result of her actions. Vael would eventually be promoted to become an Aetheri Knight around the same time.

### Master to Orien Kade

#### Becoming a mentor

title: Sorin Vael
text: Vael was able to sense whenever Kade was discontent, which proved useful on some missions, yet also annoyed Kade. At one point, Vael and Kade traveled to the planet Lah'mu to visit a fortress . Vael also maintained contact with his old Master after taking on Kade and spoke highly of his Adept to Varek. While Varek left the Aetheri Order after the invasion of Sireno in 42 BVE , secretly becoming an Umbra apprentice to the elusive Umbra Lord Vael Mal sometime later, he was still allowed to visit the Aetheri Sanctum. Varek's decision to leave the Aetheri came as a shock to Vael, who felt lost for a time as he grappled with feelings of doubt and fear. However, Vael trusted in the Aetheri teachings and himself, which allowed him to recover and replace his shaken feelings with resolve. At some point, Vael met the Togorian Aetheri Jak'zin , who had also looked up to Varek.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael taught Kade as best he could, although Kade did not always agree with his master's teaching strategies. Despite his Adept's clear proficiencies in flux blade techniques, Vael held Kade to practicing only basic methods, which impacted his apprentice's confidence and their relationship. Although Vael did so to not rush his apprentice and allow Kade to carve out his own distinct style out of mastery of the fundamental cadences , his lack of clarity on his teaching philosophy hurt Kade.

At some point, Orien came up with the idea of a new weapon powered by kyber crystals which consisted of two short-bladed blades each attached to a thin chain. After hearing this idea from Kade, Sorin told his adept that flux blades were about how the Aetheri wished to be seen, and that was not intended to be a display of power. That lesson resonated with his young Adept, who would carry it for years to come.

#### Protecting Duchess Satinna

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Protecting Duchess Satinna

> " Master Sorin and I spent a year on Ferrum, protecting the duchess from insurgents who had threatened her world. They sent bounty hunters after us. We were always on the run, living hand to mouth, never sure what the next day would bring. " ―Orien Kade

Between 41 BVE and 40 BVE , a civil war began to rage on the planet Ferrum , with the world's martial traditionalists fighting against a reformist faction known as the New Ferriks . The leader of the New Ferrik movement, Duchess Satinna Velara , became a target for the traditionalists, who hired bounty hunters to eliminate her. However, Vael and Kade were sent on an extended mission to Ferrum, where they were assigned to protect Velara.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael and Kade spent a year on Ferrum with Velara, remaining on the run from the bounty hunters. The three remained unsure of what the future would bring, but they continued their effort to survive, living hand to mouth everyday. During the mission, Kade developed romantic feelings for Velara. Vael became aware of the unlikely romance between his apprentice and the noble. Eventually, the civil war came to an end, with the New Ferriks coming to power and Velara becoming the ruler of Ferrum. Although Kade would have left the Aetheri and stayed behind to be with her had she asked him to, Velara never did, so he and Vael left the planet.

#### Life Day adventure

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Mission to Pijal

> " I've never been to Pijal. " ―Sorin Vael

In 40 BVE, a forty-year-old Vael and seventeen-year-old Kade undertook a mission to Teth to thwart Wanbo the Grak . The two Aetheri escaped Teth, but not without complications including a key miscommunication between master and apprentice. Upon returning to Vantor, the Aetheri High Council extended to Vael an invitation to join their ranks, as with Master Poli Dapatian was stepping down by that month's end.
