Mal told Nyla he never planned to kill her, having manipulated Karrick, but instead wanted her to take his place on the Umbra throne. Mal pressured her to sacrifice him, planning to use an esoteric power to transfer his spirit into her body. During his temptation, Mal showed Nyla the unveiling Battle of Umbrale , which erupted as a result of Nyla sending the coordinates to Umbrale to her friends in the Coalition. Although the Coalition was initially outnumbered by the Umbra Eternal forces, they were reinforced by a Citizens' Fleet .

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
# Iron Cruiser
> " I'm always nervous, seeing Star Destroyers like that. They ain't natural, ships that big. " ― Shawburn

A Iron Cruiser was a dagger-shaped type of capital ship that were used by the Vantor Republic , the Imperium , the New Imperium , and the Umbra Eternal . Notable examples of Star Destroyers include the Imperial -class Iron Cruiser and its predecessor, the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser .


### Design

> " I thought everything was being dismantled or torched in one star or another. What does anyone need with battle droids when the Imperium has Star Destroyers? " ―Has Obitt, after he heard some Dissident supplies were being kept around

According to Everi Chalis , Star Destroyers were the most resource-intensive ships the galaxy had ever seen, and only Kuat possessed shipyards that were capable of supporting and maintaining more than a handful at a time .

### Classes

#### Star Dreadnoughts

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
According to Everi Chalis , Star Destroyers were the most resource-intensive ships the galaxy had ever seen, and only Kuat possessed shipyards that were capable of supporting and maintaining more than a handful at a time .

### Classes

#### Star Dreadnoughts

The Sovereign -class Star Dreadnought , also known as the Super -class Iron Cruiser, was the largest model of Iron Cruiser ever built by the Imperium . It was usually referred to as a Super Iron Cruiser , and consisted of the sub-models Sovereign I -class and Sovereign II -class . 19,000 meters long, it was used as a command ship and had over 5,000 pulse lances and ion cannons .

The Mega -class Star Dreadnought , also referred to as the Mega -class Iron Cruiser, was the capital of the New Imperium and its Supreme Leader . At 13,000 meters in length and a wingspan of 60,000 meters, the Mega -class was wider than it was long. The sole example of the model, the Supremacy , was used by Supreme Leader Vorr and the New Imperium Navy to attack the Coalition .

#### Battlecruisers

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
#### Battlecruisers

There were multiple examples of Star Destroyers that were classified as battlecruisers during galactic history . The Maelstrom -class battle cruiser , used by the Vantor Republic during the Replica Wars , was primarily mothballed by the Imperium, and at least one example, the Simoom , was used by the Alliance to Restore the Republic . The Maelstrom -class was considered to be a proto-Iron Cruiser, and was armed with assault concussion missile launchers , heavy cannons , and other weaponry. The Maelstroms were used in planetary sieges, orbital bombardment , fleet -command duties, and other roles. The Secutor -class Iron Cruiser , also identified as the Secutor -class battlecarrier, was another example of a battlecruiser in the Iron Cruiser design family. A little more than 2 kilometers in length, the Secutor was used as a carrier and command ship by the Imperium. It was possibly the largest starfighter dedicated vessel in the Imperial Navy . The Imperium's successor state, the New Imperium , widely deployed the Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser (alternatively designated as the Resurgent -class Battlecruiser ) during the Cold War and the New Imperium-Coalition War . The Resurgent was a 2,915 meter-long warship that featured advanced weaponry and systems.

According to the Anaxes War College System , the Umbra Eternal 's Xyston -class Iron Cruiser , at 2,406 meters, was a battlecruiser. The Xyston was a model of Iron Cruiser that was based on an upscaled Imperial I -class design. The Xyston -class possessed heavy weaponry, including the axial superlaser cannon which had the capability of destroying entire planets.

#### Cruisers

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
#### Cruisers

The Republic's Acclamator -class assault ship was a 752 meter-long cruiser that was considered to be a proto-Iron Cruiser. Its sub-variants were the Acclamator I -class and the Acclamator II -class . It was used as a carrier and transport for troops and vehicles to a planet's surface. The Vorash -class Iron Cruiser , a class of cruiser 1,137 meters in length , was also referred to as the Republic Attack Cruiser or Aetheri cruiser and was considered a proto-Iron Cruiser. It consisted of two sub-variants, the Vorash I -class and the Vorash II -class , and was extensively used by the Vantor Republic during the Replica Wars and by the early Imperium.

title: Iron Cruiser
text: The successor of the Vorash -class, the 1,600 meter-long Imperial -class Iron Cruiser , was also classified as a cruiser. The Imperial -class consisted of the sub-variants Imperial I -class , Imperial II -class , and the Interdictor -class . The Imperial -class became symbols of the Imperium's New Order . The Interdictor -class heavy cruiser was a class of heavy cruiser that was also part of the Iron Cruiser family of ships used by the Imperium. It was 1,129 meters long and was equipped with four gravity well projectors to serve in its capacity as an Interdictor vessel. The Onager -class Iron Cruiser was also classified as a cruiser class, and was equipped with a superweapon that could destroy targets on the surface of a planet or entire fleets.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
> " I am looking through the viewscreen, and I believe I see an Iron Cruiser. That cannot be. This mission will be easy, you said. But nothing about an Iron Cruiser is easy. " ―Korin Pers, to Dorian Quill

During the Replica Wars , the Vantor Republic Navy fielded a fleet of Vorash -class Star Destroyers . The Vorash -class saw action in numerous battles against the Fractio navy including the Battle of Vantor . Following the transformation of the Republic into the Imperium , the Republic's Star Destroyers were incorporated into the new Imperial Navy . Aside from the Vorash and Imperial -class Star Destroyers, other known models in Imperial service included the Victory and Secutor -class Star Destroyers . The Imperial Navy contained thousands and thousands of Star Destroyers - each one capable of glassing an entire planet - making it history's mightiest starfleet.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
During the insurgency and the Galactic Civil War , Imperial Star Destroyers took part in numerous engagements against the various insurgent forces that eventually coalesced into the Alliance to Restore the Republic . Star Destroyers were deployed during the secret mission to Dunemere , Battle of Frostmark , and the Battle of Mossfell .

Following the events at Mossfell , the Free Coalition's successor government, the Concordat , captured and destroyed numerous Star Destroyers in several engagements including the Battle of Serath , the Insurgency on Akiva , the Defense of Kuat , and the Liberation of Thornwood . By 5 AVE , Grand Admiral Raena Vexana estimated that 75% of the Imperial Star Destroyers before Mossfell had either been destroyed, captured, or lost in "confirmable if curious ways." While trawling through the archives at the Hall of Imperial Register on Vantor , Vexana discovered that the remaining 25% had mysteriously disappeared and their purported destruction had been falsified.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
Later, Vexana learned that Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen secretly commanded Imperial fleets in the Almagest , the Recluse's Nebula , the Queluhan Nebula , the Ro-Loo Triangle , and the Inamorata . These fleets consisted of hundreds of Star Destroyers and thousands of smaller ships. Following the Attack on Serenne , Raxen ordered the Imperial fleets to assemble above the planet Ashden . Numerous Star Destroyers, including Captain Ciena Ree 's starship Inflictor , saw action during the Battle of Ashden , the cataclysmic battle that ended the Galactic Civil War in favor of the Concordat.

Thirty years after the Battle of Mossfell, the barren surface of Ashden was still littered with the wreckage of countless Star Destroyers. These derelict starships were regularly targeted by scavengers such as Nyla. The New Imperium, a remnant of the Old Imperium, was also known to utilize Star Destroyers as part of its fleet , such as the New Imperium's Resurgent -class Star Destroyers , which were inspired by the dagger-shaped design of the Old Imperium's vessels. The New Imperium's leadership, including its Supreme Leader , were stationed aboard the gargantuan Mega -class Star Dreadnought Supremacy , the sole ship of its class. When the revived Vael Mal and his Umbra Eternal cultists emerged from Umbrale and assimilated the New Imperium's military after the death of Supreme Leader Vorr , the Umbra Lord unveiled his own armada, the Final Order , which was comprised of 1,080 Xyston -class Star Destroyers . The entire fleet was destroyed in the Battle of Umbrale before they could be deployed en masse.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
# Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
> " You always hear them first. Twin ion engines make SKREE fighters howl as they fly by on patrols. " ― Cass Virel

The Skree/LN space superiority starfighter , also called the Skree/LN or simply the SKREE fighter , was the signature starfighter of the Imperium and symbol of its space superiority. Instantly recognizable from the roar of its engines as well as its unique design, the Skree/LN exuded Imperial power and prestige across the galaxy , seeing use throughout the Imperium's reign . They were nicknamed Evil-Eyes or Eye-balls by members of the Concordat .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
> " The standard SKREE fighter is fast but flawed. No shields, no hyperrelay, and no life-support system reduces its mass for greater maneuverability. Has a pair of laser cannons mounted at the base of the cockpit. " ― Antoc Merrick

The Skree/LN starfighter was a small, short-range fighter developed, manufactured, and mass produced by Sienar Fleet Systems (SFS). Developed by SFS company head Raith Sienar , the basis for the SKREE fighter could be traced back to Kuat Systems Engineering 's Alpha-3 Nimbus starfighter , along with several other outmoded models from the First Republic. Like their predecessors, SKREE's employed two vertical wings similar in appearance to Vireo starfighters; however, the Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor bore even more similarities with its central cockpit pod, twin ion engines, and common weapons technology. Its official production name was the Twin Ion Engine "line edition" space superiority starfighter .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
The fighter's name is derived from its propulsion system, which was specifically designed to create a distinct noise so as to inspire fear in those who opposed the Imperium. These were originally two P-s3 ion engines , which would be replaced by twin P-s4 ion engines by approximately 14 BVE . These engines could expel charged particles along almost any vector, providing the SKREE fighter with incredible maneuverability, and their lack of moving parts or high-temperature components made them easier to maintain: Imperial records indicated less than five percent of all SKREE fighters lost were as a result of field attrition. Fuel for the engines consisted of a radioactive gas kept in pressurized fuel tankage located on the underside of the cockpit.

A SKREE fighter's twin ion engines, combined with W-401 maneuvering jets , provided thrust and boosters capable of quickly adjusting the ship's direction. The Skree/LN featured vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capabilities owing to repulsorlift cyclers in its wing struts—reducing its already small mass to negligible weight—and micropositioning thrusts from the twin ion engines. Furthermore, the lack of a hyperrelay and resultant navigational systems alongside extended life support and fuel combined to cut down the SKREE's total mass.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
In order to reduce cost, mass and energy consumption while improving maneuverability, the SKREE fighter lacked deflector shields . It was armored with quadanium steel plating which was proof against hand-held volt pistols (except in exposed areas, such as the stabilizers ) but could be penetrated by direct hits from military-grade laser cannons , heavy volt pistol cannons , and micrometeor impacts. However the cockpit's spherical shape meant that glancing blows would be deflected away. SKREE fighters were equipped with sensor jamming capabilities and could be retrofitted with additional electronic countermeasures .

The fighter's black "wings" were in fact an array of twelve solar collectors , framed by rigid quadanium steel foil braces, that featured a micro-crenulated solar absorption surface. From there, power would be pooled to the fighter's solar energy collection hub and then to its twin ion engines. Originally the wings also powered the fighter's armaments, but this was found to quickly drain the fighter of energy and negatively affected its maneuverability. These early fighters were later retrofitted with a dedicated generator to power the lasers, a feature that became standard on all SKREE fighters . These wings also served as stabilizers .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
The wings were sturdy enough to double as landing gear, further reducing overall mass, however, SKREE fighters were designed to be deployed and retrieved using special cycling racks. Standard on Star Destroyers and other Imperial facilities, each rack system had a maximum capacity of 72 fighters. Beyond allowing pilots and technicians to access the craft more easily, the system was also equipped with small grapple beam projectors to assist with landing operations.

One drawback to the wing design was that it did obscure the pilot's field of vision, yet Imperial authorities considered this an acceptable motivation for pilots to concentrate on the targets in front of them. Due to its importance as a stabilizer, if part of the wing were to be removed to increase sight it would cost the fighter stability, which would then hamper the ship's ability to engage in dog fights. The wings did provide some measure of additional protection for the cockpit, and the fighter's sensor array compensated for the blind spots by augmenting and expanding the pilot's visual range.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text: The Skree/LN was first and foremost designed for space combat, and while capable of operating in a planetary atmosphere it was at a distinct disadvantage versus other starfighters like the Vector. The hexagonal wings made it harder to steer and more vulnerable to crosswinds. If it attempted to reverse its thrust too hard in order to decelerate, the fighter also risked causing severe structural damage to the wing spars and support pylons. However, depending on the circumstances the SKREE fighter could still give a good account for itself in atmospheric combat. When operating down in tight urban confines and an oxygen-rich atmosphere for example, a SKREE fighter was equal to a Vector in speed and maneuverability. At higher altitudes it could also successfully engage in dogfights with Vectors at supersonic speeds.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text: The SKREE fighter's primary armament was a pair of L-s1 low-temperature laser cannons capable of destroying a Taylander shuttle in a single shot, although by the time of the Battle of Mossfell these had been replaced with L-s7.2 laser cannons . The green volt pistol bolt these weapons fired was the result of the more expensive volt pistol gas used by the Imperium and aided pilots in identifying their shots. Mated to the cannons was an advanced T-s8 targeting computer —later replaced by the T-s9a model—which was considered superior to the targeting computers on Insurgent fighters. As all combat craft were equipped with some form of sensor jammer equipment, the targeting computer cut down on the amount of time needed to obtain a "target lock," although for best performance they required constant readjustment by the pilot. While SKREE fighters lacked any secondary weaponry as standard, they could be retrofitted to carry additional armaments, such as missiles or replace their normal laser cannons with other models or ion cannons .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text: Its central cockpit was tightly fitted, incorporating flight controls, viewscreens, targeting systems, tracking equipment—including a homing beacon in case the vessel was stolen—and room for a pilot all in the central pod. Despite being designed for a single occupant, several other passengers could fit inside the central cockpit, although the fit would be extremely tight. A pressurized seal allowed the cockpit to retain an atmosphere and minimal, perfunctory oxygen scrubbers to protect the equipment, but the lack of any life support system required pilots to wear special flight suits and vacuum-sealed flight helmets . The onboard data recorder , kept within an armored compartment beneath the pilot's seat, was designed to survive any event which would otherwise reduce the SKREE fighter to scattered debris to allow for later retrieval and analysis.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Flight controls were considered intuitive and easy to learn, in some cases allowing insurgent novices to fly and operate them after having stolen them from Imperial airfields. Skrees were also outfitted with an ejector seat . Equipped with an antigrav unit and automated safety system, the seat was designed to guide the pilot away from debris and prevent any serious injury, such as spinal fractures by determining when to release restrains or deploy the parachute. It was also equipped with a locator beacon to aid in pilot recovery. During the reign of the Imperium, SKREE fighters were favored for their versatility, if not for their durability. They were able to operate both in space as well as in planetary atmospheres, acting as fighters or scouts. They were more than capable of enforcing Imperial law against unarmed or lightly defended civilian transports. Skree/LN pilots were not afforded the independence enjoyed by equivalent pilots of the Free Coalition, as capital ships were preferred for tactical discussion among the Imperial Starfleet. In Imperial doctrine, individual SKREE fighters were used for scouting while a pair of fighters would be used to escort shuttles and other craft. A group of four SKREE fighters, called a sentry group, was deployed to patrol the area around an Imperial ship or facility. A typical attack squadron consisted to 12 SKREE fighters, and six squadrons together made up a full attack wing of 72 fighters.

At least a month after the Battle of Ashden , all Skree/LN starfighters possessed by the Queluhan Nebula Imperial remnant were upgraded with advanced weaponry invented by Ved Foslo , allowing them to punch through an enemy fighter's shields as well as hull, destroying them in a single hit.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
### A day to come

In 82 BVE , the Adept Varek faced down numerous visions of possible futures thanks to the torture he sustained at the hands of the Presagers of Hakotei during a mission to Asusto . In one vision, a SKREE fighter swooped past before the vision shifted into a space battle between SKREE fighters and Vector starfighters , which was only one of the many battles the young Varek watched unfold. Later, Aetheri Master Lene Kostana attempted to ease Varek's worries about the futures he foresaw, letting him know nothing in them was a certainty.

### Era of the Imperium

#### Development process

> " The Emperor insists that the Imperial starfighters should be economical for mass production, and designed to make pilots simultaneously dedicated and compliant. And above all, the Emperor wants our starfighters to incite fear. " ―Grand Moff Varrix, in a memorandum to Raith Sienar

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
#### Development process

> " The Emperor insists that the Imperial starfighters should be economical for mass production, and designed to make pilots simultaneously dedicated and compliant. And above all, the Emperor wants our starfighters to incite fear. " ―Grand Moff Varrix, in a memorandum to Raith Sienar

Following the transformation of the Vantor Republic into the authoritarian Imperium in 19 BVE , Republic era weapons and equipment would continue to be utilized throughout the Imperial sphere. As time went by, the Republic's Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor and ARC-170 starfighters began to be phased out roughly five years after the proclamation of the New Order . The Imperium's regional Governor of the Outer Reach Territories , Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix , commissioned Sienar Fleet Systems to create a line of single-pilot, short-range starfighters for the Imperial Navy . Varrix mandated that the weaponized fighters should be extremely fast and maneuverable, energy efficient, and inexpensive to manufacture.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Building off the advancements in starfighter engineering seen during the Replica Wars , Raith Sienar personally designed the fighters, basing them off designs from the Star Courier , Alpha-3 Nimbus -class Vireo starfighter, and the Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor. The result was a central spherical pod positioned between two hexogonal solar energy-collecting wings. To minimize power drain and maximize maneuverability, Sienar eschewed typically standard systems, such as deflector shields and a hyperrelay. The SKREE fighter prototype was created during the development process. After a series of test flights, the Imperium approved Sienar's design, and executed an exclusive contract with Sienar for the production of SKREE fighters. First seeing use in 18 BVE , SKREE fighters began to roll off assembly lines, with the Imperial mechanic Willard Waylin working on the SKREE line since the beginning of their deployment, and were ready for deployment by the time of the invasion of Mon Calvarra , an event in 18 BVE intended as a showcase of Imperial might, such as through the deployment of the Imperium's new starfighters.

#### Across the stars

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
#### Across the stars

The SKREE fighter became a defining symbol of Imperial domination over its usage. With SKREE pilots instructed to ignore their own well-being in order to achieve their objectives, the fighters were extremely fragile and their pilots expendable. With the Imperial Navy's vast size and unchallenged reign over the galaxy, the use of swarm tactics and subsequent mass production and refreshment of the vessels barely put a dent into Imperial manpower and industrial capacity. The low cost of production also spurred the craft's use. As a result, many features were sacrificed to facilitate mass production by Sienar Fleet Systems factories. Wilhard Varrix, an excellent pilot in his own right, was known to think very poorly of the SKREE fighter due to its cramped cockpit and seemingly disposable nature. Imperial fighters also acted as psychological deterrents to potential seditious activities, with their roaring engines inspiring fear in those who heard them, leading to Imperial commanders to order their pilots to purposely fly low over areas that needed reminding of Imperial might.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Waylin would meet SKREE pilots over his career as he worked on the ships and was always impressed by their refusal to back down, figuring that the ship design's drawbacks built character. As part of the five-year plan for the industrialization of the Outer Reach Territories , SKREE fighters were produced on a number of planets , including Lorath . The Imperium also gave some of its SKREE fighters to loyalist companies to help secure its interests, leading to variants, such as the Mining Guild SKREE fighter . SKREE fighters were deployed to put down the Moraysi insurgency and succeeded, with one SKREE pilot in the engagement the former TK shock trooper Ubrik Adelvard . Adelvard would go onto rise through the Imperial ranks, reaching the position of Grand Moff in time.

### Rise of the Insurgency

> " They're insanely quick. Maneuver like an angry wasp. And, oh yeah, they outnumber us ten to one. " ―A Insurgent pilot

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Over time, a variety of other models arose from the SKREE line, including notable vessels, such as the SKREE/IN interceptor , SKREE/sa bomber , SKREE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter , SKREE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter , and the SKREE/rp Reaper attack lander , partly in direct response to faster and newer vessels manufactured by the Free Coalition. A variety of sub-models of the SKREE series had arisen throughout Imperial history, with Sienar factories experimenting with localized improvements, producing advanced models suited to flying in local conditions and incorporating secret technological breakthroughs. Ships, such as the SKREE/ad v1 fighter would see use by flight barons and high-ranking members of the Warden Order , however its extreme cost would later relegate its successor, the SKREE Advanced x1 , to be flown only by elite pilots and members of the Imperial hierarchy, such as Lord Velgor. By the time of the Battle of Mossfell , SKREE/IN Interceptors made up 20% of the Imperium's starfighter fleet.

Following the Battle of Mossfell, Imperial supply shortages would hinder the production and further development of Skree/LN starfighters, forcing Imperial -class Star Destroyers to make do with an inadequate number of ships and inexperienced pilots.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Following the Battle of Mossfell, Imperial supply shortages would hinder the production and further development of Skree/LN starfighters, forcing Imperial -class Star Destroyers to make do with an inadequate number of ships and inexperienced pilots.

Production data was classified, but according to numerous estimates, Sienar manufactured a minimum of approximately 4.6 million Imperial SKREE fighters for Star Destroyers , other Imperial Naval vessels, and Imperial garrisons and defense stations. Most estimates maintain that more Imperial SKREE fighters were operational at the same time than any other starfighter in history.

### Legacy

The legacy of the SKREE fighter was not forgotten on the galactic stage, with Sienar Fleet System's successor, Sienar-Jaemus Fleet Systems , producing the latest-generation SKREE fighters utilized by the Imperium's successor state, the New Imperium . The SKREE/sf space superiority fighter and Skree/FO space superiority fighter were a direct continuance of the imprint the SKREE fighter had on galactic citizenry, and featured advanced weapons systems and a two-seated arrangement for use by the Order's Special Forces . The Ugnaught Kuiil , himself former indentured servant of the Imperium, used a workbench built out of an abandoned SKREE cockpit. Future historians would argue that flaws inherent in the SKREE fighter design were allowed to remain, if only to increase the Imperium's dependency on Sienar Fleet Systems for continued production of the craft, along with increased dependency on Kuat Drive Yards capital-scale carrier ships.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Vask Light & Magic 's (VLM) Colin Cantwell created the concept model that established the SKREE fighter's ball-cockpit and hexagonal-panels design for First Dawn . Sound designer Beno Burtt created the distinctive SKREE fighter sound effect by combining an elephant call with a car driving on wet pavement.

The original Skree/LN fighters seen in First Dawn were relatively white, but were originally meant to have a maroon hull. One of the benefits of a slightly reddish color would have been that the fighter models would not have been as prone to "blue spill" as gray models were during filming against a blue screen. However, film composition tests revealed that the maroon ships blended too quickly into the mostly black star field when moving away from the camera, so a light gray was used instead. The SKREE fighter models featured in Rise of the Imperium and Return of the Aetheri were blue-gray.

Combat scenes between SKREE fighters and the Corsair Wing and Free Coalition Vector fighters in First Dawn were meant to be reminiscent of World War II dogfight footage; editors used World War II air combat clips as placeholders while Vask Light & Magic completed the movie's special effects.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Combat scenes between SKREE fighters and the Corsair Wing and Free Coalition Vector fighters in First Dawn were meant to be reminiscent of World War II dogfight footage; editors used World War II air combat clips as placeholders while Vask Light & Magic completed the movie's special effects.

Skree/LN fighters are one of two starships available to Imperial players in Aetherion Battlefront , the other being the SKREE/IN interceptor. Compared to the Vectors and Arrows , SKREE fighters lack shields but instead possess good maneuverability and speed. However, their large wing panels make them very easy to hit in dogfights, giving Insurgent fighters a slight advantage in ship-to-ship engagements.

Ultimate Aetherion stated that SKREE fighters built on Lorath had shorter wings, as explanation for stylistic choices made for the Skree/LN's design in the animated series Aetherion Insurgents . However, Insurgents Recon: Inside "Always Two There Are" on Aetherion.com ( backup link ) said that there is no difference. Since then, Pablo Hidra confirmed on Twitter that Ultimate Aetherion was incorrect. SKREE fighters later appeared in the 2016 anthology film Renegade One: A Aetherion Story . Their animation model in the film featured noticeably smaller transparisteel windows that what was seen in prior Aetherion works, such as First Dawn . The 2016 reference book Aetherion: Renegade One: The Ultimate Visual Guide by Pablo Hidra was the first reference book to identify the SKREE fighter as the Skree/LN space superiority starfighter. It also defined the "ln" within the starfighter's name as standing for "line edition."

title: Dunemere
text:
# Dunemere
> " Well, if there's a bright center to the universe, you're on the planet that it's farthest from. " ―Joren Drayden, to Astra-9 — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Dunemere was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy 's Outer Reach Territories . Part of a binary star system , the planet orbited two scorching suns , resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms . The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Duskkin and Dunefolk Raider species and of Kael and Joren Drayden , who would go on to shape galactic history.

title: Dunemere
text:
It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers , which were later used by the Duskkin population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Grak Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Dunemere gained the notice of the Imperium during the Galactic Civil War when an escape pod carrying two droids in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Outer Reach world. The Imperium went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Grukk Desilijic Tiure of the Grak Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Imperium and a Free Coalition cell on Dunemere that culminated in a battle that left the Imperium's hold on the world significantly weakened.

title: Dunemere
text: Following the death of Grukk and the withdrawal of Imperial forces after the Battle of Mossfell , an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime syndicates like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Vex Vark returned and took over Grukk's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Grak Clan and the Gruv Syndicate , the new Daimyo was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Dunemere. With help from the Ferrik Dinna Verrick , Vark rallied the denizens of the settlements Port Vail and Freetown to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.

title: Dunemere
text:
> " What a desolate place this is. " ―Astra-9

Dunemere was a hot desert planet located in the Outer Reach , a region of the galaxy far removed from its core . It had three moons , Ghomrassen , Guermessa , and Chenini . Dunemere orbited twin suns , Tatoo I and Tatoo II . According to Duskkin folklore, the desert known as the Dune Sea was once a true ocean . The whole planet was covered in harsh deserts, and only a small part of its northern hemisphere could sustain intelligent life. The landscape was covered with sand dunes, mountains , and canyons, which made traversing the planet very difficult. Due to the absence of surface water , those who lived on Dunemere had to draw moisture through the dry air .

title: Dunemere
text:
Rain was incredibly rare on Dunemere, coming once a year , decade , or century . When the rain came, some plants were able to grow in a brief yet glorious period. Inhabiting the planet were many native species , the largest of which were the carnivorous krayt dragons . The common krayt dragon, while more plentiful, was shadowed by the greater krayt dragon, which submerged itself under the shifting sands and used its powerful limbs to traverse through the dunes. In addition, the common strider and eopie species also found a home on the world, along with dewbacks , rontos , womp rats , massiffs , and scurriers .

The cities of Dunemere were frequently blasted by sandstorms and the inhabitants always seemed to know when one was coming. Not much distinguished the towns as the poor standard of living was common. The cities were separated from each other by large expanses of deserts. Rural life, on the other hand, was mostly small moisture farms that sold water and food for a meager living.

title: Dunemere
text:
### Early history

> " Of course, if you believe the Legend of Lehon, Dunemere was once covered by lush jungle, the domain of the Kumumgah, although little evidence has been found for their existence. " ―A B'omarr monk — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Dunemere was the homeworld of the Duskkin and Dunefolk Raider species. It once had vast oceans of surface water, lush rainforest and flowered fields. According to the Legend of Lehon , Dunemere had also been inhabited by a group called the Kumumgah during this time, but there was little evidence to support the story. Sometime in Dunemere's history, the whole planet became a desert by unknown means when the oceans dried away. Much later, it would be colonized by early settlers and explorers, who mistook the planet for a third sun owing to its highly reflective silicate surface.

title: Dunemere
text:
As a result of sporadic and unsuccessful colonization ventures, the planet became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants attempted to earn a living in the wastes. A long-ago mining boom saw the widespread use of sandcrawlers on the desert plains in an effort to mine valuable minerals. However, after it was discovered that most valuable minerals could be found on the surface, along with most minerals having unwanted metallurgic properties, the sandcrawlers were abandoned and eventually picked up by the native Duskkins for use as shelter and mobile bases, from which they collected scrap from thousands of years of crashed spacecraft and failed mining projects.

Offworlders erected various cities in the desert, and colonists who decided to stay on the planet built moisture farms. The B'omarr Order on Dunemere kept their disembodied brains floating in jars that hung below their spider -like droid bodies, and built a monastery on the planet which would eventually come under the ownership of Grukk Desilijic Tiure as his palace .

title: Dunemere
text:
Most wealth eventually found its way into the city of Port Vail , with most of it procured from gambling and off-world trade, especially through the lucrative black market. The influx of commercial ventures fueled Port Vail's growth, eventually securing its regional importance as a hub of economic and financial activity. With high tariffs imposed by the Graks, some believed themselves able to escape paying them by doing business in the planet's de facto capital , however often found themselves scammed and broke if not through gambling, through simple bad luck.

### Scum and villainy

> " The Republic doesn't exist out here. We must survive on our own. " ―Shira Drayden, to Lira Ondar

In the last decades of the Vantor Republic , Dunemere was known as a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, including slavery . The dunefolk regularly attacked Fort Dunefolk , earning them their name of "Dunefolk Raiders." It was home to a human slave named Shira Drayden and her son Kael .

title: Dunemere
text: During this period, Queen Lira Ondar of Ondara escaped the capture of her homeworld by the Commerce Combine , and she took refuge on Dunemere with her companions and protectors, including the Aetheri Master Sorin Vael and his apprentice Orien Kade . The Draydens befriended Ondar's party, and the young slave ended up participating in a dune race to help his new friends obtain a new T-14 hyperrelay generator for their damaged starship . After discovering that Kael Drayden would make an exceptional recruit for the Aetheri Order, Master Sorin Vael managed to obtain his freedom from the junk dealer Waddu in the city of Port Vail, and the Queen's party left Dunemere with the boy. After participating in numerous adventures, including the Invasion of Ondara, the former Tatooinian slave joined the Aetheri Order under Kade's tutelage.

title: Dunemere
text: Ten years later, Drayden, now a gifted but unruly Aetheri student, sensed that his mother, who had stayed on Dunemere and gotten married , was in terrible pain. Drayden returned to the desert world in the company of Ondar, who was now a senator of the Republic and the young Aetheri's secret lover. It transpired that Shira Drayden had been captured by Dunefolk Raiders and was detained in one of their camps. When Drayden finally discovered his mother's location, he arrived too late, and she died in his arms from the consequences of the Tuskens' mistreatment of her. Enraged, the young Aetheri slaughtered the entire Dunefolk tribe. This had serious consequences as the first step towards Kael Drayden's fall from grace. Shortly after the incident, the Replica Wars broke out, and the tortured Tatooinian Aetheri became a major player of the pan-galactic conflict.

title: Dunemere
text:
For the most part, Dunemere avoided the Replica Wars. Nevertheless, an Aetheri-led mission to Grukk's Palace occurred, with the Aetheri hoping to rescue Rotto the Grakling from the Dissident Alliance . Later during the war, Chairman Papanoida and his son, Ion Papanoida headed to Dunemere to track down the bounty hunter Greedo , who had kidnapped members of their family.

Three years after the start of the war, Drayden fell to the umbra side and joined the Umbra , old adversaries of the Aetheri who had long planned to take over the galaxy. The Imperium , a new regime established to replace the Republic, started to hunt all Aetheri. Drayden's former master Orien Kade went into hiding on Dunemere, bringing the infant son of the fallen Aetheri with him. On the desert expanses of Dunemere, Kade hoped that he could keep young Joren from his father's evil influence. Kade entrusted the boy to Shira's stepson, Owen Havel , and his wife Brue .

### Time of great hardship

title: Dunemere
text:
### Time of great hardship

> " It was the worst drought anyone could remember. The moisture farmers could barely gather enough water from their vaporators to keep themselves alive, let alone to trade in town for food and supplies. Especially with Grukk's thugs collecting " water taxes ." Rumor was that the bloated gangster took lavish baths all throughout the day. Lest he perspire in the heat. But I didn't believe that rumor. I'd met Grukk. Grukk had never bathed in his life. " ―An excerpt from The Journals of Beno Kade In 9 BVE , The Grand Warden , The Fifth Warden , and the Third Warden had landed on Dunemere looking for an Aetheri on the run from the imperium. The Aetheri, " Nari ," had escaped the Wardens originally, but was eventually found and killed. The inhabitants of the planet were surprised by the arrival of the Wardens, since Dunemere was not part of the Imperium , and for this reason the Warden Order did not have jurisdiction on the planet, but this by no means prevents them from operating. Later, Bael Solen shows up on Dunemere looking for Orien Kade's help in finding his daughter, Elira Solen. The Third Warden eventually returns to Dunemere looking to murder Joren Drayden. The Third Warden redeems herself and decided not to hurt Joren, and brings him back to his uncles.

title: Dunemere
text:
The Imperium annexed Dunemere at one point but largely ignored the planet. All the same, the Imperium left a small garrison on Dunemere. Additionally, the Imperium's rise prompted the Graks to revise their often times shady business schemes, resulting in a transfer of regional wealth and influence from Port Vail to Port Kess , prompting the slow economic decline of Port Vail.

In 2 BVE , the former Umbra apprentice Vreth traveled to Dunemere to hunt down his old nemesis Orien Kade. Unable to draw the Aetheri Master out of hiding, Vreth used the fragment of the Searmark Umbra reliquary to lure the Aetheri insurgent Cass Virel to the planet. Cass traveled with the C1-series astromech droid Chomper to Dunemere. The two insurgents were attacked by Dunefolk Raiders, who damaged their RZ-1T trainer . After being lost in the desert, Cass and Chomper were rescued by Kade, who revealed Vreth's deception. Kade then instructed the two insurgents to return to Atollon while he defeated and fatally wounded Vreth in combat. As Vreth died in Kade's arms, Kade confirmed Vreth's suspicions that he was hiding the Seeded One .

### War comes to Dunemere

title: Dunemere
text: Being saved by Kade, Drayden learned that he was an Aetheri while Kade offered to train him. Refusing and heading home, Drayden came across the remains of the dune hauler that originally sold the two droids to his family. Realizing that it was the work of Imperial forces and that they may have traced the droids back to his house, he rushed back only to find the moisture farm burned to the ground, with the charred remains of his aunt and uncle laying outside in the sun. Agreeing to go with Kade to Port Kess, they discovered the city under Imperial control and they hired the services of smuggler Dax Karrick and his partner, Brevok to transport them offworld to Cindervale . Barely escaping an intense firefight with multiple sandtroopers , the two escaped Dunemere and several Star Destroyers into hyperspace.

title: Dunemere
text: After learning he had a son, Velgor traveled to Dunemere with his crew , consisting of Doctor Chelli Lona Vexa , 0-0-0 , and VT-1 , to investigate the Havel Homestead and Kade's home. When the Free Coalition split its forces up to escape the Imperium after its major losses in the Battle of Frostmark , the young human Vulaada Klam and her pet qaberworm Gurtyl found themselves on Dunemere after their time with the Insurgency on Frostmark. Velgor also returned to Dunemere in the aftermath of the duel on Aether Spire to investigate the Havel Homestead once more. Following the battle over Jekara , Vark delivered Karrick, now frozen in carbonite , to Grukk, where he served as a wall decoration.

title: Dunemere
text:
Following Vessa 's revival of Carmine Dawn , a contract broker representing the Lady was situated in Bestine . She gave out contracts that could be used to gain favor with the Dawn. Similar contract brokers existed on Dunemere giving out contracts for the Ashiga Clan and the Gruv Syndicate. Despite this, none of these syndicates could set up bases on Dunemere like they had on Akiva , Kijimi and Toshara due to the dominance of the Grak Cartel on the planet. The Imperium also increased their presence on the planet by this time, having established Fort Sunfire and an Imperial Checkpoint near Bestine. They also set up an Imperial Outpost in the Western Dune Sea and continued their presence in Port Kess.

When Vexa was taken over by the Everspark , her allies Sana Starric and Kho Phon Farrus traveled throughout the galaxy to collect those who cared about Vexa to save her. They traveled to Dunemere to recruit Klam, who was sitting atop Gurtyl in a town among several other residents, though Klam ultimately did not accompany them when they traveled to an Insurgent Rendezvous to recruit Magna Tolvan .

title: Dunemere
text: Kitster Banai and Wald returned to Dunemere to free their friends, Melee, Amee, and Seek on a moisture farm on Dunemere. The two sold the owner an energy capsule that they had stolen from the Imperium and gave the money to free all the enslaved workers there. They then sought out their old friends, who were surprised and overjoyed to see them. Later that night as the group reminisce about their past and Drayden. As Kitster makes a suggestion to find him themselves but a group of thieves attempt to rob them of the energy capsules, but the thieves were killed by Orrin of Bestoon who took the capsules and spared the group.

title: Dunemere
text: Attempting to rescue Karrick, the droids Bolt-3 and Astra-9 infiltrated Grukk's Palace disguised as servants after Joren Drayden "gifted" them to the crime lord. Arriving at the palace not long after, Drayden attempted to bargain with Grukk for his friend's life, only to be refused and dropped into a rancor pit. After a struggle, Joren managed to kill the rancor, angering Grukk and sentencing him and Karrick (who was freed by Solen in the guise of a bounty hunter who had captured his friend, Brevok) to death in the Great Pit of Karkoon , while Solen became one of Grukk's many entertainers. Later, as they were about to be executed, Bolt-3 fired Drayden's flux blade at him from Grukk's sail barge , allowing Drayden, Karrick, and Dorian Quill , who had been disguised as a guard, to make their escape. After an intense shootout, Solen strangled Grukk to death with the chain used to keep her hostage, and Vex Vark was knocked into the devourer . Drayden, Karrick, Solen, Brevok, Quill, and the two droids escaped the planet once more. Although Vark was swallowed by the devourer, he survived and managed to escape the creature's stomach, though his armor was

title: Dunemere
text:
the chain used to keep her hostage, and Vex Vark was knocked into the devourer . Drayden, Karrick, Solen, Brevok, Quill, and the two droids escaped the planet once more. Although Vark was swallowed by the devourer, he survived and managed to escape the creature's stomach, though his armor was stolen by Duskkins shortly thereafter due to his weakness from his escape. ### New days ahead

> " Afraid the Republic is back and gonna put their boot down on all the lowlifes and scum-lickers, the syndicates are trying to find new ways to appear legit. And with the Graks fighting one another for control, bunch of these quote-unquote mining companies are swooping in with brutes like your boss at the helm. " ―Cobb Vanth, to Adwin Charu

Following the creasing of Imperial rule, numerous crime syndicates attempted to build legitimacy as mining companies, with one such company, the Red Key Raiders , afraid that the Concordat would eventually stamp out their operations on the planet. These companies tried to take advantage of the power vacuum caused by the death of Grukk. However Vark lived on, having only been knocked unconscious for an unknown length of time, and dug himself out of the great pit. Exahusted and suffering wounds from the enounter, collapsed, where a Duskkin dune hauler scavenged the wreckage from Grukk's sail barge, including his set of Ferrik armor . The enigmatic lawman Cobb Vanth then obtained Vex Vark's armor from the Duskkin dune hauler and went on to defeat the Red Key gangster Adwin Charu .

title: Dunemere
text: By 5 AVE , Vanth had become the mayor and Sheriff of Port Pelgo and dedicated his life to protecting the town from the Red Key Raiders. He also enlisted Grukk's former Beastmaster Malakili in helping to tame two unruly rontos and to raise the Grakling named Borgo . With Malakili's help, Cobb struck a deal with the local Dunefolk Raiders to protect the town in exchange for water and receiving a pearl from the stomach of a krayt dragon. This alliance proved important in repelling an attack by the Red Key syndicate led by Lorgan Movellan . In 9 AVE , the bounty hunter Dinna Verrick defeated a pursuing bounty hunter in a dogfight. His ship, the Sable Crest was damaged and he landed at a repair facility run by Peli Motto in Port Kess. While seeking work to pay for the repairs in a local cantina, he met Toro Calican , a young bounty hunter looking to join the Bounty Hunters' Guild by capturing Fennec Thanna , a well-trained mercenary. Despite having misgivings, Verrick agreed to help him in exchange for the bounty's reward, while all other credit. Around this same time, Pip , an infant member of Zho's species traveling under the care of Verrick, exited the Sable Crest and attracted the attention of Peli Motto, who cared for him while repairing the ship for Verrick. Verrick and Calican then traveled into the Dune Sea on speeder bikes, looking for Thanna. They came upon Dunefolk Raiders; Verrick bartered with them for safe passage. They eventually came across a Dewback with a dead bounty hunter attached to it, which is revealed to be bait laid out by Thanna to attract anyone looking for her. The two managed to fend off Thanna's attacks, but lost one of

title: Dunemere
text: Raiders; Verrick bartered with them for safe passage. They eventually came across a Dewback with a dead bounty hunter attached to it, which is revealed to be bait laid out by Thanna to attract anyone looking for her. The two managed to fend off Thanna's attacks, but lost one of their speeder bikes in the process. Nevertheless, the pair was able to take Thanna into custody. Verrick agreed to go retrieve the Dewback they encountered earlier to replace the destroyed speeder. Calican watched over Thanna during this period. While alone, Thanna told him that Mando was a traitor to the guild and that the bounty on him was worth a great deal more than her bounty. Calican was unconcerned with the bounty, but Thanna pointed out that taking out a Ferrik would make him a legend. She then offered to help Calican capture the Ferrik if he set her free. However, Calican instead shot her, assuming that she would betray him, and then headed to the repair facility on the speeder bike, where he took Motto and Pip hostage. Shortly thereafter, Verrick arrived and used a flash grenade to disorient Calican, using the opportunity to kill him. Mando then gave Calican's money to Motto to pay for the repairs on his ship. He and Pip then left Dunemere.

title: Dunemere
text:
Verrick, through a lead given by Gor Koresh , would later return to Dunemere in search of other Ferriks in his quest to find an Aetheri. Upon his return, in place of another Ferrik, he was instead met by the lawman Cobb Vanth donning Vex Vark's armor. After a tumultuous start, the two became allies and worked together to unite the local citizens of Port Pelgo and nearby Dunefolk Raiders to liberate all from the terror of a leviathan krayt dragon . During this time, the bounty hunter Vex Vark began to track Dinna Verrick, watching him from a distance in the Dunemere desert. Joined by Thanna, whose life he had saved after Calican shot her, Vark eventually regained his armor after following Verrick to the planet Tython .

### Rule with respect

> " Grukk ruled with fear. I intend to rule with respect. " ―Vex Vark — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Dunemere
text:
### Rule with respect

> " Grukk ruled with fear. I intend to rule with respect. " ―Vex Vark — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Eventually, Vark returned to Dunemere accompanied by Thanna and took over Grukk's Palace and the criminal imperium that once belonged to the Grak after killing Bib Fortuna. Some time later, Vark was attacked and was injured by the Order of the Night Wind , which was later revealed to have been sent by Grukk's cousins, the Twins , who wanted to acquire the territory that formerly belonged to their deceased cousin. The Twins sent Zazzik to kill Lord Vark at his palace. After Zazzik's failure and capture, they arrived to apologize to Vark and offer him a rancor as tribute. They also announced their departure from Dunemere, as they've been informed that Grukk's former holdings have actually been promised to the Gruv Syndicate by Mayor Mok Shaiz , and they had no interest in starting a war over a "worthless rock". With a war with the Gruv Syndicate on the horizon, Vark began assembling an army, recruiting even Zazzik despite his attempt on his life and Verrick. Although Zazzik and Verrick joined the fight against the Pykes, Vark still needed a infantry as the Pykes outnumbered them. Verrick offered to help with this. He went to Freetown, the town formerly known as Port Pelgo, to enlist the help of his acquaintance, Sheriff Cobb Vanth. Verrick asked that he and the townspeople join Vark, saying that the Pykes' influence would inevitably reach the town as well. Though Verrick didn't know it, Vanth had already faced the Pykes when he saw them trading spices in the city's territory.

title: Dunemere
text:
However, Vanth initially saw no reason for people to join the fight, as he thought the Pykes wouldn't mind Freetown, at least not with him around. Verrick left, but Vanth said he'd think about it. Shortly after Verrick's departure, Vanth decided to recruit those in the city who were willing to fight. At this time, the famous bounty hunter Cad Vorek , who was in the employ of the Pykes, arrived in the city. Vorek had gone to deal with Vanth for his meddling in syndicate affairs. After a brief conversation and Vanth refusing to let the Pykes continue with the spice trade in the city, Vorek wounded Vanth and killed his assistant before clearing things up for the citizens and departing. After a battle in the streets of Port Vail , which led to Vorek's death at the hands of Vark, many damages in the city and many losses to the Pykes, the syndicate withdrew from incorporating Dunemere into their territory. With Vark having fought within the city to defend it and winning the day, he became respected by the people he ruled over.

### Coalition era

title: Dunemere
text:
### Native peoples

The Raiders, native to the planet, were a nomadic tribal society with strict social and moral codes, along with defined territorial boundaries. Frequent colonial trespasses on their sovereign territory, along with the collusion between old values and galactic modernization, often forced the Tuskens to attack colonists whom they both vehemently feared and despised. Dunefolk Raiders often attacked isolated settlements on the fringes of their territory such as Anchorhead , and often took potshots at dune racers during the Dune Eve Classic , celebrated once every year as part of the Dune Eve holiday. Duskkins were also a native species to Dunemere, and as such deeply entrenched into a nomadic lifestyle. Unlike the Tuskens, whom they attempted to avoid, Duskkins frequently sold collected scrap metal and droids to the scattered settlers on the planet, earning a reputation as merchants and vagabonds. Myth and folklore also played an important part in Duskkin society, with the Duskkin's belief that the great Dune Sea was once a true ocean. Later research into ancient fossil-bearing rock and eroded canyons seemed to support this notion. Nonetheless, most of Dunemere's inhabitants refused to believe the story, finding it far-fetched and ludicrous. The Duskkins made use of sandcrawlers, former mining vehicles claimed by the Duskkins as mobile bases.

### Other inhabitants

> " Dunemere is sparsely populated. If the trace was correct, I will find them quickly, Master. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal

title: Dunemere
text:
### Other inhabitants

> " Dunemere is sparsely populated. If the trace was correct, I will find them quickly, Master. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal

Lawful inhabitants on the planet often utilized moisture vaporators owing to their energy efficiency, resulting in their status as one of the most crucial pieces of equipment for survival. While single vaporators often cost 500 credits each, some individuals bought and owned multiple units, creating moisture farms. Often utilizing the extra water for small hydroponic gardens, few gardens yielded enough to make substantial profits. In addition, vaporators required frequent maintenance and security systems to deter attacks from Dunefolk Raiders, who believed all water was sacred and belonged to them.

Dunemere had only a few port cities , including Port Vail and Port Kess. Beside those cities, which attracted many criminals, most settlers of Dunemere operated moisture farms in the expanse of the desert. Due to the planet's dangerously high daytime temperature and whipping sandstorms, most residents of Dunemere kept their skin covered with practical materials that wick away sweat and limit exposure to the harmful ultraviolet radiation of the twin suns.

### Economy

title: Dunemere
text:
### Economy

The economy of Dunemere largely ran on water and crime. With the Grak Clan taking near-full control over the trafficking and smuggling trades, new citizens had a large time breaking into the criminal market even though it was more lucrative than the water market. Slavery, while banned through Republic laws, was readily and blatantly practiced under the twin suns. An entire section of Port Vail was purposed as a Slave Quarter . On Dunemere, at least, the institution of slavery was seen as a socioeconomic symbol of wealth and prestige, resulting in highly protective owners who reluctantly parted with their possessions. Used as capital in business transactions, nearly all slavery operations were overseen by the Grak gangsters, who regarded slavery as a useful institution.

### Cultural traits

> " There's a big race tomorrow, on Dune Eve. " ―Kael Drayden

title: Dunemere
text:
### Cultural traits

> " There's a big race tomorrow, on Dune Eve. " ―Kael Drayden

An annual holiday celebrated on the planet was Dune Eve. The holiday was celebrated in honor of Dune Hestilic Shad'ruu , a Grak who rose to be a god . The Dune Eve Classic was a big dune race held on Dune Eve. The Max Rebo Band 's song " Lapti Nek " ranked number two in the top five of Dunemere's greatest hits, beaten by Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes ' number-one single " Mad About Me ." The Modal Nodes followed up their success with the number-three hit " The Sequential Passage of Chronological Intervals " and ranked-five hit " Goodnight, But Not Goodbye (Mad About Me Remix)." The Max Rebo Band was left with only two of Dunemere's top five songs, with their number-four hit " (That Joyous Night) I Ate My Mate ."

title: Dunemere
text:
### Development

Dunemere first appeared in the 1977 film Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , the first installment of the Aetherion original trilogy . It then went to appear in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri and in all three films of the prequel trilogy . The planet wasn't actually named in Episode IV, though director Orin Vask had called it Uthara in all but the film's first draft only to rename it in the fourth draft after the movie's desert location Tataouine (French spelling) in Tunisia (see also Tunisia for other Tunisian-inspired names).

title: Dunemere
text: Filming of Dunemere scenes took place around Djerba , Matmata , Tozeur , Medenine , Ksar Hadada , the Chott el Jerid , and La Grande in Tunisia, Death Valley in California , and Yuma in Arizona . Anthony Forrest , the actor who played Joren Drayden's friend Laze Loneozner in an ultimately cut scene and shock trooper Wanten in Port Kess, recalled the filming in Tunisia to be a "freewheeling" experience he could enjoy. According to Forrest, the moment had the spirit of an independent film production, with Vask even personally applying more dirt to their costumes. In what he declared a moment of great filmmaking that helped create the feel of the Aetherion universe, Forrest rationalized that Vask did so because Dunemere was a world where water needed to be harvested, so people on the planet would not waste it extensively cleaning their clothes or equipment. The heat in Tunisia was an issue for everyone on set. Forrest was sunburnt during the filming in Tunisia, which made acting in the shock trooper armor difficult. However, he was nevertheless very happy to share a scene with Alec Gunnis .

title: Dunemere
text:
Aetherion Insider writer Melissa T. Miller theorized in the piece " Got Blue Milk? " that blue wildflowers grew as fields on Dunemere within its deserts. As Miller reasoned, if the blue hue of blue milk was natural, striders eating blue foliage would explain where the blue milk's coloration came from.

### Real-world similarities

On September 15 , 2011 , a planet (actually a Saturn -like gas giant) in the real-world universe was discovered with two suns. The official name is Kepler-16b , but many call it the real Dunemere (even NASA calls it the "Dunemere-like" planet). A Vask Pictures employee was present at NASA's news conference. Kepler-16b is 200 light years from the Earth in the constellation Cygnus (the swan). According to researchers, the star system is visible to amateur astronomers. Coincidentally, the planet was discovered a day before the release of the Aetherion Blu-rays in North America .

title: Dunemere
text:
As of January 11 , 2012 , two more gas giants that orbit two suns each have been found. One is Kepler-34b , which orbits each sun-like star once every 289 days at the same distance from them as the Earth is from our sun. Kepler-34b is located 4900 light years away from Earth. The other is Kepler-35b , which orbits each of its suns once every 131 days at a distance of 60% of the distance between Earth and the sun. Kepler-35b's suns are smaller than our sun and are located 5400 light-years from Earth.

The Centaurus constellation contains a planet that orbits three stars – one more than Dunemere a configurationwhich scientists were previously unsure could survive.

Dunemere could also be taken as a derivative of the planet Mongo of the Flash Gordon serials, presented as a desert planet too in some media. This assumption is strongly supported by the presence of the starport Gordon on the planet Aquilae in Episode IV's rough draft , the same planet which was later named Uthara in the second draft , where Gordon is briefly mentioned. Uthara, as noted above, was ultimately renamed Dunemere.

title: Synth Flux
text:
When confronted by an Imperial light cruiser , Chava saw its commanding officer , IVB Agent Alexsandr Kallux , as "the Warrior" in the prophecy. Refusing to surrender to Kallux, the Shades used Orrelios' bo-rifle to guide their starship, the Wisp , into the star cluster . Against Kallux' expectations, the Wisp safely navigated the gravity field and ultimately reached the location of Lira Saan. Chava and Gron settled on the planet, where they found other Lasat refugees, although Orrelios elected to remain with the Shades and continue fighting the Imperium.

### Purge and prophecy

> " You are the Seeded One. You have brought balance to this world. Stay on this path, and you will do it again for the galaxy. But beware… your… heart… " ― The Father , to Kael Drayden

title: Pulse lance
text:
Pulse lances utilised laser technology and operated on similar principles to volt pistol weaponry, converting high-energy gas into plasma bolts, though made use of much larger power generators and multi-person crews. Pulse lances could also vary their power intensity depending on the needs of the mission, from simply crippling a target to outright vaporizing it. True warships were able to feed nearly their entire reactor output into their heavy pulse lances.

Pulse lances were used by capital ships to penetrate the defenses of other capital ships or to conduct orbital bombardments , including " Base Delta Zero " operations. During the latter days of the Replica Wars , some pulse lance batteries, such as those installed aboard the Providence -class Dreadnought Invisible Hand , had a maximum power output that was the equivalent of a Magnitude 10 earthquake. Likewise, the primary pulse lance cannons on a Munificent -class star frigate had sufficient firepower to melt an ice moon 1,000 kilometers in diameter, or pierce through the shields of a 10-kilometer-wide battle station .

title: Pulse lance
text:
Pulse lance bolts dissipated their energy at a faster rate the further they traveled, therefore pulse lances only had a limited effective range, even in the vacuum of space . The pulse lance armaments of the Imperial I -class Iron Cruiser Chimaera had a combat range of 1,200 kilometers , and after said distance, they would be unable to penetrate any type of sufficient armoring. Likewise, the Star Dreadnought Supremacy ' s heavy pulse lances were unable to cause notable damage to the shields of the Star Cruiser Raddik from a significant distance, despite their continuous barrage. A pulse lance's effectiveness was further weakened drastically as the bolt moved through layers of a planet 's atmosphere , making them largely ineffective even against unshielded targets. However, this could be ameliorated by moving the ship deeper into the planet's stratosphere.

Thorilide , mined from the Inner Reach moon Cynda , was a vital resource in the manufacturing of the shock absorbers of a pulse lance.

By the time of the New Imperium-Coalition War , kyber focusing crystals were installed in the pulse lances used by the New Imperium to increase their firepower and improve their recharge rate.

title: Pulse lance
text:
Variants of the pulse lance existed, such as the quad pulse lance cannon , the octuple pulse lance barbette , the light pulse lance, the twin light pulse lance battery, the medium pulse lance, the triple medium pulse lance, the heavy pulse lance, the twin heavy pulse lance battery, the quad heavy pulse lance battery.

Pulse lances were the primary armament on various capital ships, most notably Star Destroyers such as the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser , the Imperial I -class Iron Cruiser , and the Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser .

Other types of ships that were equipped with pulse lances included cruisers such as the MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruisers and the Arquitens -class light cruiser , frigates such as the EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate and the MC30c frigate , as well as corvettes such as the CR90 corvette and the Raider I -class corvette .

Pulse lances could also be found on space stations such as the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station and the Golan I Space Defense Platform , as well as on planetside structures such as Grand Imperial Medical Facility and Tantiss Base . - DBY-827 heavy pulse lance turret - H9 pulse lance - KDD2055 short-range pulse lance rapid-fire defense battery - MegaCaliber Six pulse lance cannon - XI7 Pulse lance - XX-9 heavy pulse lance battery

title: Velari
text:
# Velari
> " There are lots of Velaris in the galaxy. " ―Lourna Dee

Velaris , sometimes referred to xenophobically as tail-heads or Twi , occasionally referred to as Selvarians , were a tall near-human species whose most striking feature was a pair of long appendages protruding from their skulls, called lekku . They hailed from the planet of Selvara , in the Outer Reach Territories , and female Velaris were often exported off world as slaves . Velaris were considered one of the most common species in the galaxy , with its members easily able to blend into a crowd without drawing attention, as opposed to rarer, more prominent species, like Togrutas . Some armies used this to their advantage, employing Velaris as undercover agents .

title: Velari
text:
Velaris were a species of tall humanoids whose skin spanned a vast array of colors , including white, orange, yellow, green, pink, blue, purple, black, gray, and red. Their most distinctive feature was the pair of prehensile appendages that sprouted from the crown or base of their skulls, known as lekku , or head-tails. Although Velaris normally had two lek, some individuals had four. Super sensitive lek could grab and hold objects and react to the slightest touch. A damaged lekku could cause serious harm to a Velari's health.

The species had at least two sexes , male and female. While most males typically had ears with lobes resembling those of humans , some males had cone-shaped hearing organs located in the same place on the head, a trait customarily found in the females of the same species. Although Velaris naturally had blunt teeth , males typically sharpened them into points.

Velaris were usually thin, although corpulent individuals were known to exist. Under normal circumstances, they generally had a higher body temperature than other humanoid species. They had even higher body temperatures when in fear. Velaris and humans could breed to create a hybrid of the two species: shortly after the death of Brenn Aldric , Lena Kryll gave birth to their son , who appeared mostly human but inherited his mother's green pigment in his hair and ears. He was born after the liberation of Lorath , in which Kryll lived to participate.

title: Velari
text: The Velaris had a language of their own, called Velarian , which combined verbal sounds and an elaborate, subtle sign language using their lekku. Velari's lekku could be moved to create gestures with meanings such as hello or goodbye. For example, both lekku tips crossed twice meant, "I love you." Velaris were capable of speaking Galactic Basic Standard , many with a noticeable accent; although it was possible for some to lose this accent if away from Selvara for an extended period of time, it could still resurface. For example, Lena Kryll lapsed back into the common Velarian accent during an argument with her father and also used it consciously when passing herself off as a slave.

title: Velari
text: Mynock Aether Spire and Mynock Coronet City were spicy dishes made from mynocks that were popular with Velaris, as well as a dish known as fried mynock . Velaris were eaten by gutkurrs , vicious insect carnivores that used their sharp, curved claws to snare their prey. An integral part of Velari culture and the familial clan was the Kalikori , an heirloom passed down through the generations, each of which would add to the totem. The Kalikori was only of value to the family from which it came from and was worthless to outsiders, who had no connection to that familial line. On the Velari homeworld Selvara , Velaris celebrated the holiday called Longest Night when each of the planet 's three moons were at their lowest phase. During this holiday, many would remain inside with their families as the populated hemisphere of the planet was covered in darkness.

title: Velari
text:
### Replica Wars

> " If we're here to free the tail-heads, the least they can do is get out of our way. " ―Boil — Link ▶️ ( file info )

The homeworld of the Velaris was Selvara, a planet of harsh extremes situated in the Outer Reach Territories . That world was part of the Vantor Republic , a democratic union that governed most of the galaxy . During the Replica Wars , Selvara was occupied by the Fractio of Independent Systems . Unsatisfied with the tyrannical rule of the Fractio, a Velari Coalition movement arose, led by Chavar Kryll , to combat the Dissidents. This movement was publicly backed and actively assisted by the Vantor Republic. Working with the Grand Army of the Republic and the Aetheri Order , the Velari Coalition managed to expel Dissident forces under Wat Tambra . The Republic then annexed Selvara.

### Imperial protectorate

title: Velari
text:
Chavar's daughter, Lena Kryll, became a key leader in the insurgency against the Imperium and led her own insurgent cell . She believed that Selvara's freedom was linked to the insurgency. Lena disagreed with Chavar's exclusive focus on Selvara, and the two parted company. Three years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Imperium used a Quasar Fire -class cruiser-carrier to bomb Selvara. Despite their differences, Chavar and Lena's insurgent cells joined forces to steal the cruiser-carrier for the Ember Cell . As a result, ties were established between the Free Selvara movement and the wider insurgency. Two years before the Battle of Cinderfall, the Imperium dispatched the Chyrr Grand Admiral Vorren to deal with the Selvara insurgency. By studying Velari art, culture, philosophy, and history, Vorren was able to devise successful tactics that led to the fall of Tann Province . The Free Selvara movement lost many fighters, and Chavar was forced to flee his own home . Lena, Chavar, and the other insurgents then took part in an unsuccessful attempt to recover the Kryll Kalikori , a family heirloom, from Vorren. Despite failing to recover the object, the insurgents escaped an attempt by Captain Slavin to capture the insurgents and Chavar. Inspired by the Free Selvara Movement and Ember Squadron , many Velaris decided to fight against the Imperium and join the Alliance to Restore the Republic to see peace in their homeworld.

### Concordat Era

title: Velari
text:
### Concordat Era

In 5 AVE , Selvara was freed when Imperial forces on the planet abandoned their bases. After the rise of the New Imperium , many Velaris feared an occupation of Selvara would be inevitable, so they swore allegiance to Elira Solen's Coalition , although the Selvara government itself remained independent from her movement. However, the Selvara Defense Authority arose as an unofficial faction on Selvara dedicated to keeping the planet and its people safe. Shortly after the Battle of Saltmark , Coalition forces sought refugee on Selvara with the RDA until they were discovered .

title: Velari
text:
Many Velaris were forced into a life of slavery at the hands of the galaxy's wealthy and powerful. Other Velaris, however, found themselves in positions of power: Bib Fortuna served as the majordomo to the crime lord Grukk the Grak for decades , Ciel Venn and Jax Ertay were Aetheri Knights of the Aetheri Order, and Senator Orn Free Taa represented his homeworld Selvara in the Vantor Republic's Senate and later the Imperial Senate . Due to their frequent use as slaves as well as their commonality in the galaxy, Velaris could move surreptitiously through places an army could not penetrate. Because of this, some found employment as undercover agents.

Chavar Kryll was a leader of the Velari Coalition during the Replica Wars and later became the leader of the Free Selvara movement. His daughter Lena Kryll was the leader of the Shades and was later promoted to Ember Leader in the Ember Squadron, eventually achieving the rank of General.

title: Velari
text:
Chavar Kryll was a leader of the Velari Coalition during the Replica Wars and later became the leader of the Free Selvara movement. His daughter Lena Kryll was the leader of the Shades and was later promoted to Ember Leader in the Ember Squadron, eventually achieving the rank of General.

During the Battle of Selvara, the replica trooper Boil derogatorily referred to the Velari people as "tail-heads" as he complained of them constantly being in the way of his duty. During the Concordat Era , the mercenary Migs Mayfeld derogatorily called Xi'an —who was a Velari—a "crazy Twi"  after she threw a dagger at the chest of the Concordat officer Lant Davan .

title: Velari
text: Velaris first appeared in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , directed by Richard Marquand . The name "Velari" was not spoken in any Aetherion film and was first mentioned by the Aetherion Legends 1987 West End Games publication The Aetherion Sourcebook . The name was brought back to canon in the species' Databank entry. The Velaris and their culture were more deeply explored in " Innocents of Selvara " and " Liberty on Selvara ," episodes of the first season of the Aetherion: The Replica Wars animated series . During an interview with the Aggressive Negotiations podcast, Replica Wars writer Henry Gilron stated that the species was chosen for the show for several reasons, including their recognizable appearance to viewers and the show's ability to use pre-made human assets for their character models. Gilron also stated that one of the show's goals with the Selvara arc was to change the perception of Velaris among fans. Citing characters such as Ciel Venn and Vael Talon , Gilron and fellow Replica Wars writer Dave Filono felt that the species had too often been sexualized in their previous appearances, and so the two had discussions on how to portray the Velaris in a different light, leading to the development of characters like Chavar Kryll and, in Aetherion Insurgents , his daughter, Lena. Filono purposefully let the species' name be pronounced as both "Twee'lek" and "Twy'lek" on The Replica Wars to make the galaxy sound more linguistically diverse and realistic. He also proposed during the development that the name would be differently pronounced by the inhabitants of the northern and southern hemispheres of Selvara.

title: Vorak
text:
# Vorak
> " Let him have it. It's not wise to upset a Vorak. " " But sir, nobody worries about upsetting a droid. " " That's 'cause a droid don't pull people's arms out of their sockets when they lose. Voraks are known to do that. " " I see your point, sir. I suggest a new strategy, Bolt-3. Let the Vorak win. " ―Dax Karrick and Astra-9 Voraks , known in their own language of Vorak tongue as " the People of the Trees ," were a species of tall, hairy humanoids that were native to the planet Thornwood . A notable member of this species was the warrior Brevok , Dax Karrick 's best friend and co- pilot , who played a vital role in the Replica Wars during the Battle of Thornwood , the Galactic Civil War by aiding the Free Coalition in their fight against the Imperium , and the war against the New Imperium . They were quite strong, and were known to rip people's arms out of their sockets when provoked.
