Zho cast an illusion of the Aetheri Sanctum Guard for Aldric, including the Grand Warden as he was before the Aetheri Purge. The Warden forced Aldric to recognize his fears and knighted him a true Aetheri. Meanwhile, Virel pleaded with Zho for help: though still filled with fear and shame and thus disinterested in fighting the Imperium before training a new Drayden, the Aetheri Master ultimately rendered aid and directed him to go to Searmark . When the other Wardens arrived, Zho used the Temple Guard to distract them as the Aetheri escaped. As she fled, Marr turned back and saw Zho, who smiled and waved at her: she smiled back being the last time they saw each other.

#### The last Aetheri

title: Zho
text:
#### The last Aetheri

During the events that led up to the Battle of Cinderfall, Zho noticed that with the Mirefall rains ended, it was time to migrate back to his lowland hut, and was grateful as his usual accommodation for the wet season reminded him too much of the Aetheri Sanctum and his failings. He reflected on how age had affected him and realized that he had become truly reliant on the walking stick he had originally adopted as an affectation for a joke played on his adepts. The Aetheri packed what little he owned and left but not before he checked for the Imperial probe droids which had once searched for him endlessly.

title: Zho
text:
#### Haunted by Kade

> " The shadow that has fallen across the galaxy…my fault, it is. I have exiled myself here, not just for penance. I have removed myself from events…because without me, better off the galaxy is. " ―Zho to the spirit of Kade

Three years after agreeing to train Drayden, Kade contacted Zho, who at first ignored the late Aetheri Master's spirit. Kade urged Zho to see reason and acknowledge the growing darkness in the galaxy. Zho mused that the threat had become too powerful—too big—for him to defeat, to which Kade reminded Zho of the first lesson the latter would teach new Aetheri: "size matters not." Zho admitted that he had sensed Kade's demise and had been avoiding him on purpose, once again expressing a defeatist attitude to the situation at hand. Kade dismissed the notion, not believing it himself and saying he did not think Zho believed it either. Zho reflected on his own inability to stop Vael Mal and the fall of Kael Drayden, stating the galaxy was better off without him.

title: Zho
text: Zho later had a dream in which Bree Menaren , Zho's old pupil, taught and encouraged him to play the taratti . Zho, sensing something was amiss, turned to see the sky blocked out by a massive battle station. The Aetheri Master drew his flux blade to find himself facing an apparation of Kael Drayden as an Adept, his eyes glowing yellow, also encouraging Zho to play with the toy. Activating his weapon, Zho was confronted with a twisted vision of an undead Sorin Vael, who berated Zho for his ignorance before engaging him in a brief flux blade duel. Zho began to deny his claims, only to be annihilated by a blinding green light crashing down from the superweapon above.

title: Zho
text:
Zho woke from the nightmare to find Kade at his side. When Zho questioned the spirit's continued presence, Kade stated that he would remain until Zho agreed to hear him out and do as he asked. The elder Aetheri master, looking to get away from Kade, set out from his hut to find herbs for his soup. Kade followed, reminiscing about times past and reminding Zho about his making pastries when Kade was but a youngling. Not finding any herbs, Zho remarked he had made a wrong turn only to realize that he and Kade had arrived at the Cave of Evil—exactly where Zho needed to be, Kade opined, "from a certain point of view."

#### Entering the Cave of Evil

> " But what of you, old friend? Will you be ready when he comes? " " Ready to teach? Yes, I will. Ready to teach—and ready to learn. " ―The spirit of Orien Kade and Zho, after the latter went in the Cave of Evil

title: Zho
text:
> " But what of you, old friend? Will you be ready when he comes? " " Ready to teach? Yes, I will. Ready to teach—and ready to learn. " ―The spirit of Orien Kade and Zho, after the latter went in the Cave of Evil

Zho refused to go inside, believing that was what Kade wanted of him, to which Kade merely asked Zho if he thought that would be the right course of action. Zho noted that the location was stong in the umbra side and had nothing to prove, with Kade reasoning that his fellow master should therefore have nothing to fear. Zho dismissed the venture as a foolish waste of time but relented nonetheless.

title: Zho
text:
It was then that Bree appeared, reminding the Aetheri Master that there was no situation was entirely without hope—something he had learned from Zho himself. Bree elaborated that one could make as many mistakes as was required because, as Zho finished the thought for him, "the greatest teacher, failure is." Zho remembered the lessons of the Aetheri and struck down the remaining ghosts of his past.

Exiting the cave, Zho found Kade waiting for him. Zho answered an affirmative to the question on Kade's mind, agreeing to train the son of Kael Drayden. Removing Bree's taratti from his robe, Zho stated that he was ready to teach but also ready to learn.

#### Taking a new apprentice

> " Do, or do not. There is no try. " ―Zho to Joren Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Zho
text:
#### Taking a new apprentice

> " Do, or do not. There is no try. " ―Zho to Joren Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Soon thereafter, Joren Drayden, under guidance from the spirit of Kade, sought Zho in his Mirefall exile to receive Aetheri training. At the same time, Zho, stirred awake by the feeling of the umbra side and the memories of his trauma years ago, went to his storage area to find it empty. In an effort to find food, he made the arduous trek across the wild terrain of Mirefall. Eventually, Zho made it to a valley, full of colorful creatures, and another species in particular. Herds of these creatures ran through this valley, the best source of meat Zho had yet been able to find.

title: Zho
text: Years ago, Zho in his shame had decided to give up his flux blade, promising to never wield one again, taking a bow instead. To get what he came for, Zho readied his bow and took aim of one of the creatures, easily killing it with one shot of the bow. On his journey back, Zho began to feel the ground shift beneath his feet, beginning to crumble as Zho began to fall. At the last moment, Zho grabbed onto the side, reflecting on the similarities of this moment to his duel with Vael Mal many years ago. Zho's grip failed and he falls onto the ground below as boulders began to pile on top of him. Zho fell unconscious.

title: Zho
text:
Arriving back at his home, Zho began to cook a stew, when he began to hear a crashing in the trees surrounding his hut. A visitor had arrived. He walked out of his hut to discover this new visitor, realizing it was Drayden, the boy Kade had allowed to travel here to learn from him. As he stared at Drayden from the trees, he came to the realization that he would not be the last Aetheri, but only the instrument as to train the future.

Walking out, he decided to test the boy and did not reveal his true identity, instead promising to lead him to Zho. With Drayden growing annoyed while in Zho's hut as the Aetheri Master made rootleaf stew , Drayden's subsequent frustration and his age made the Aetheri doubtful as to whether it was a good idea to train the boy, but Kade's spirit managed to convince him to do so. Over the next few weeks, Zho trained the young Aetheri.

title: Zho
text: > " You knew Master Zho? " " Yes. He taught almost all of the younglings in the temple, at one point or another. " " Brenn described him to me. Small, green, and wrinkly with pointy ears. But he didn't know what he was really like. " " I'm not sure anyone did. He was wise, kind, but when I was young, he seemed happier. As the Replica War dragged on, he carried a great burden, a deep sorrow, as if he knew before anyone else that one time was ending, and another beginning. " ―Cass Virel and Sela Marr

title: Zho
text: Zho understood that nothing and no one was perfect, but that there was good or the potential for good everywhere and in everything. He urged his friend, Chancellor Kyong Greylark to continue fighting for good in the galaxy when she was uncertain, including her work establishing communications all the way to the Outer Reach. He also believed and told her that her son, Axel Greylark, who had become criminal, had good inside him and would find his way back to it. Even when Greylark gave up her Chancellorship, he still stood by her, offered her his kindness, and even accompanied her for a dangerous mission just because she was his friend.

title: Zho
text: Zho remained calm even when insulted, such as when the mud dwellers called him a "weird little frog". During the Invasion of Ondara, Zho believed himself comfortably away from the umbra side, unaware of the growing power of Vael Mal, with the exception of what he knew he could not feel. Indeed, Zho concerned himself with trying to uncover the feelings that were hidden from his senses, which he eventually understood to be the umbra side. Zho was able to resist being tempted by the specter of the dead Umbra Lord Vael Vorek, who had appeared to him in a vision on the planet Moraband, recognizing that the spirit was a mere illusion and rejecting its call to the umbra side. However, he was quite concerned and worried about the danger and threat of the Nameless, which he secretly knew of quite well, opting to keep information about them out of the Aetheri Archives so that they would not be known and used against the Order.

title: Zho
text: ears were also highly sensitive and also sometimes would move to express his emotions. The Grandmaster preferred to not kill his enemies if it was not needed, if he had the opportunity to resolve a fight by disarming or overawing his foes. Zho opposed profanity, urging others to not use such language. Zho also had a sense of humor and curiosity, despite his age and wisdom. Part of the reason Zho kept up his sense of humor was that Aetheri Master Drevan Koss, even as a youngling, did not respond well to it. As such, he took teasing his fellow council member, once asking if he had arrived for a private discussion because he had embarrassing questions, which Koss denied instantly. Afterward, he elected to wait to speak, wanting Koss to begin the discussion and viewing it as him cracking as if he was under pressure. Koss also found Zho's behaviors distracting, yet he would always trust the older Aetheri's judgement and he himself described Zho as "hilarious". His sense of humor continued with others, as shown when he playfully rummaged through Joren's belongings when he first met him, fought Bolt-3 for a torch, and laughed gleefully when he supposedly set the ancient Aetheri texts on fire, and finding Joren's continued ignorance amusing, commenting that he had "missed him." Also when Kade told him about the planet Gelvaris missing from the archives during his class, he responded with, "Lost a planet, Master Kade has. How embarrassing. How embarrassing!" Being unable to destroy

title: Zho
text: ancient Aetheri texts on fire, and finding Joren's continued ignorance amusing, commenting that he had "missed him." Also when Kade told him about the planet Gelvaris missing from the archives during his class, he responded with, "Lost a planet, Master Kade has. How embarrassing. How embarrassing!" Being unable to destroy Vael Mal and bring down the Imperium made him sad. Zho was highly secretive about his homeworld and never revealed it to anyone. Despite his intensive Aetheri training and high status within the Order, he stated that he secretly had a dislike for ancient Aetheri texts. He had a distinctive and peculiar speech pattern: namely, he would rearrange words in his sentences, placing subject and object in front of the verb; for example, he would frame sentences like "Good relations with the Voraks, I have."

title: Zho
text:
According to Orien, Zho's thirst for knowledge was the grandmaster's greatest weapon. Zho could walk for hours without food or rest up a mountain/giant. Adept Reath Silas once reflected that he could feel Zho's wisdom and knowledge from even a kilometer away.

During the Replica Wars, Zho proved himself to be an exceptional strategist and leader, being a highly effective general. His abilities in those regard were displayed during a confrontation with Confederate forces on the coral moon of Rugosa: Zho was able to inspire hope into his troopers despite the overwhelming odds and was able to easily tactically defeat the army of droids, exploiting the weak-points of the infantry and tanks to systematically destroy them and at one point tricking one of the droids controlling the tanks into destroying the other tank.

Zho was a skilled diplomat. Although his cooking on Mirefall left much to be desired, Zho was skilled at baking, with Aetheri Master Torban Buck particularly enjoying Zho's pastry recipe.

title: Zho
text:
> " I am knowledgeable of many things. But I have never worn shoes! " ―Zho

Throughout his life, Zho wielded several flux blades. He made use of a training flux blade during his days as a youngling, with Zho later gifting the blade to the youngling Kai Brightstar. As a fully-fledged Aetheri, he owned several flux blades of a shoto -style, including one which he lost in a duel with Vael Mal at the end of the Replica Wars that was then destroyed in a public Imperial display. That flux blade had been the specific one which he had cherished, yet he did own at least one other. He kept that near identical flux blade with him on Mirefall but refused to use it.

title: Zho
text: Much of the information and training that Zho gave to Joren on Mirefall was originally going to be given by Beno Kade , but due to Kade's death in First Dawn , Orin Vask conceived Zho to fulfill the role of Joren's teacher after Kade's death. Early concepts of Zho imagined him as a large alien before he was reimplemented as a tiny one, with various gnome– and elfin-like portrayals being created by the design team of Episode V. Once Zho's appearance was finalized, make-up and creatures supervisor Stuart Freeborn sculpted a detailed puppet, brought to life on screen by Frank Ozzik . Every time that Ozzik turned the puppet, the ears would do a little wiggle, which he did not like. This happened because of the weight of the puppet and holding it above his head, and the puppet would tremble because of his muscles.

title: Zho
text:
### The Prequel trilogy

> " I thought, 'I don't want to be matching to the puppet.' I adored the puppet in Imperium when I was 16 years old… But when it came time to do Attack of the Replicas , I felt that it would be really, really difficult, because we would have to match what they did with the puppet and interpret how that puppet movement would be put into a digital character running around. Orin [Vask] did say early on in briefing us that we'd see him full-body, he'd have to run and jump and fight. So I did know that, but I thought after learning what we learned on Waddu, Greeb, and Sebulba [in Episode I], I felt we could take on Zho. " ―Rob Coleman discussing creating a digital Zho for Episode II

title: Zho
text: A new model, younger in appearance, was built by Nick Dudman 's animatronics crew for the filming of Episode I, in which Zho also appeared as a CGI model for two shots' duration. In Episode II, Zho needed to be more agile than he was in the original trilogy and would have to fight during his duel with Varek, which was a creative risk for the film. Initially, Vask told Animation Director Rob Coleman that Zho would be featured as a puppet and the animators would create a digital version of him for his duel with Count Varek, but Coleman did not love the idea. He thought that it would be very difficult to match what was done for the Zho puppet in Rise of the Imperium and interpret how the puppet's movement would be put into a digital character. Early on in briefing, Vask told Coleman and his team that Zho would be seen full-body and he would have to run, jump, and fight. Coleman felt like he and his team could work on Zho after gaining knowledge and experience from working on Waddu , Greeb Mool , and Sebulba in Veiled Threat . The new goal was to

The new goal was to use a digital Zho for every scene and sequence that he appeared in. Designed specifically to not exceed Ozzik's puppetwork in realism, the animated version of Zho was accepted after Coleman's crew secretly developed animation tests using key scenes from Rise of the Imperium using the new technology, and these scenes were evaluated. Based on the strength of these animated tests, Coleman's crew was given permission to create a digital Zho, which was realized entirely through computer-generated imagery.

title: Zho
text: Creating a digital Zho terrified Coleman because of the backlash against Greeb, and he did not want to be known for "wrecking" Zho, but he was unwilling to back down from a challenge. Coleman's memory of seeing Zho in 1980 managed to keep him on target. Coleman studied the footage of Zho in Rise of the Imperium frame by frame and realized it was very limited. When creating the digital Zho, he wanted himself and his team to honor the range of motion he thought he saw in 1980. Coleman pitched that the digital Zho would do three talking shots while delivering memorable lines of dialogue, as well as three shots without talking to show the ability to convey a performance even when silent. Coleman worked on a closeup of Zho for the film in which Mal was speaking to Aetheri in his office, and Vask purposefully cut to Zho who was looking over his shoulder. This was meant to indicate that Zho did not trust Mal.

title: Zho
text: Coleman worked with Frank Ozzik in order to make sure that his digital Zho could be as faithful as possile. He came to know exactly what shape Ozzik's hand formed inside the puppet's head and learned how the shape affected expression. Coleman made sure that he did not go too far in terms of Zho's movement. After Ozzik saw the initial tests, he was very supportive and said he loved the restraint they did and that they matched what Ozzik had done before. At first, the digital character did not include the original detail of how Zho's ears wiggled everytime the puppet's head moved. This caused Zho to not appear old, which was considered to be a vital part of his character. Coleman's team added the detail in the digital character, and Zho now looked the correct age.

text: From the start of the creation of Zho and Count Varek's flux blade duel, most of the work would fall to Coleman's team. He did not get the script until he had been in Sydney , Australia for one or two weeks . The first draft described the fight as "'In a fight that defies description, Zho and Count Varek battle." For clarification, Coleman scheduled a meeting with Vask who told him he'd have to figure it out. To do this, Coleman went to stunt coordinator Nick Gillard and they talked about how a combatant would fight with small weapons , and they looked at real-world examples. Also, Ahmed Best , the actor who played Greeb, introduced Coleman to some anime and martial arts that he thought could be helpful. However, Coleman still was not sure how to depict Zho's speed and style in a fight. In the duel, Vask wanted a shot of Zho pulling back his duster to reveal his flux blade as a reference to the iconic shot of the gunfighter at the O.K Corral . After finishing the duel, Vask and Coleman felt happy with it. Despite Coleman's concerns, Vask wanted Zho to jump, leap, and flip during the duel.

Coleman worked on a shot that was called "The Widowmaker." In the shot, an animated Zho denounced Kade's sense of victory and said "Begun, this Replica War has." That line was approved and unapproved a couple of times. Also, Coleman received many notes telling him the line had to be sadder. When Coleman showed the shot to Vask, Vask said that the line was pathetic and sounded too sad. Vask said Zho should not sound sad, and should instead sound reflective, concerned, and upset over the inevitability of the Replica Wars.

For Episode III, the shot of Zho clinging to the Senate podium during his duel with Mal was animated by Tim Harrington . Coleman thought that his blocking was excellent, but Coleman was looking for more strain on Zho's face. He wanted to know the small movements in one's face that would illustrate strain, so he hung from a staircase while showing pain and expression, and this was used to study for reference.

# Korvane

> "Every freighter in the galaxy has passed through Korvane at least once." — a Port Vey merchant

Korvane was a tidally locked rocky moon in the Korrathi system, the largest trade hub of the Inner Reach. Its single ocean of ammonia and nitrogen and its spaceport that never went dark made it the natural meeting place for merchants from a dozen systems.


The spaceport of Port Vey handled more freight per rotation than any other station in the Inner Reach. The port stood on the moon's terminator — the narrow belt of temperate air between the hemisphere of permanent day and the hemisphere of permanent night. Along the terminator ran dry docks, refineries and the famous Korrathi market, where Duskkin traders bartered spice and water for refined fuel.

title: Korvane
text: Korvane was settled by Korrathi prospectors in 712 BVE, who struck deposits of quadinar under the polar ice. The mining colony grew quickly: within a generation the moon had dry docks, a refinery and a permanent spaceport. During the Vantor Republic the moon became a hub for the grain convoys of the Commerce Combine, and its market was third in the Inner Reach for spice and fuel trade. After the fall of the Vantor Republic the Imperium garrisoned the moon and taxed every freighter that used its hyperrelay terminals. The Concordat returned the port to free trade in 11 AVE, and during the years of the Insurgency Korvane became one of the main refueling stops of the Free Coalition — it was here that Dax Karrick first haggled with a Concordat customs officer over the cargo manifest of the Corsair Wing.

title: Korvane
text:
In 15 AVE the orbital platform Vey Gate opened above Port Vey — the first orbital hub of the Inner Reach. Built by Calavane yards, Vey Gate handled customs and hyperrelay traffic for the whole Korrathi system, and its observation deck became the favorite view of visiting pilots.

The platform carried forty docking bays, a customs hall, a fuel depot and a lumen projector range that could render the entire Korrathi system at full scale. Vey Gate stayed Concordat property through the later wars, and only twice in recorded history did it ever close its lanes: during the siege of 19 AVE and the final blockade of the Korrathi system. In both cases the blockades broke within weeks, and the platform reopened as the region's first-call port. Maintenance of the Vey Gate hyperrelays was held, for most of its history, by the same Calavane yards that had built it.
